DescriptionLong.0x000049BF:
The big winner of the 2015 Gran Turismo Awards at SEMA was this S30 Datsun Z, nicknamed the “Fugu Z.” The car was built by actor Sung Kang, known for his role in "The Fast and the Furious” movie franchise. When he purchased the car, it was a stock 1973 240Z, but it soon became something quite different and very special.

The "Rocket Bunny" body kit gives the reborn Z aggressive good looks, consisting of wide fender flares and stylish front and rear spoilers. Not just for show, the car comes equipped with a naturally-aspirated version of the RB26DETT engine, pulled from a Skyline GT-R. Thanks to some fine tuning, the inline-6 produces <220ps>, but feed it E85 IndyCar fuel, and that total jumps to more than <300ps>.

To handle this newfound power, a roll cage was installed to strengthen the body. Weight-saving measures were implemented to the car's dashboard and console, which were custom made by CarbonSignal.

The name of the car, “Fugu,” refers to the Japanese poisonous blow fish. Its organs are so toxic that anyone not taking proper precautions when handling the fish may die... and, we suppose, the same can be said about this car.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C0:
Introduced at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show, the DB11 represents all that is good about Aston Martin. It succeeds the popular DB9, which proudly represented the brand for 12 years.

The styling of the DB11 follows Aston Martin tradition, characterized by the brand's signature long nose and elegant wind-cutting profile. Aston Martin's Vice President and Chief Creative Officer, Marek Reichman, made sure the new coupe was instantly recognizable as an Aston, while imrproving aerodynamic efficiency. With airflow strategically guided around and under the body, the DB11 exhibits less lift at high speed and generates more downforce than its predecessor.

The DB11 is built on a new bonded-aluminum VH platform with a completely new design evolved from past models. Under the hood is a newly-developed twin-turbo 5.2-liter V-12. It produces <608ps> and <71.4kgm> of torque and comes mated to ZF 8-speed gearbox, allowing the super sports coupe to run to <100km/h> in 3.9 seconds and reach a top speed of <322km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C1:
Aston Martin's DB3S, based on the DB3 and developed under the guidance of David Brown, was a successful race car through the mid-1950s. In this era when not much separated race cars from sports cars, the DB3 was essentially a custom-built machine for the track, using many parts from the DB2.

The DB3S was a modernized version of the DB3, with a more curvaceous body for better aerodynamics, and an extra rigid and lighter body for better overall performance. The inline-6 engine started out life producing <166ps>, but then output was increased to <185ps>, and then to <228ps> and then ultimately to <243ps>. The car was a definite monster on the track, securing victories on both British soil as well as around the world.

Only 31 examples of the DB3S were produced. The car with vehicle chassis No. 1 received the Gran Turismo Trophy at the famous Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance in 2013.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C2:
The Aston Martin DBR9 GT1, built to compete in GT1 races, was based on the DB9 and named after the DBR1, the first DB series race car that finished 1-2 in the 1959 24 Hours of Le Mans.

With its chassis and body structure thoroughly reinforced, the DBR9 GT1 featured carbon fiber body panels (except the roof) and a completely stripped interior. Other weight-saving measures resulted in a car that tipped the scales at a lean <1100kg>, which is more than <600kg> less than the DB9 road car.

The car's aerodynamics were enhanced by way of a new front spoiler, side skirts, rear diffuser and wing. The 5.9-liter V-12 was tuned to raise its power from the <456ps>/<58.1kgm> of the DB9 to <608ps>/<71.4kgm>. The engine came mated to an Xtrac 6-speed sequential transmission.

The DBR9 GT1 won its debut race at the 2005 Sebring 12-hour event, and proved a menace on the track all the way until the GT1 category was discontinued at the end of 2011. In 2006, it won the team and drivers' titles in the ACO Le Mans Series, and took the FIA-GT manufacturers' title. In 2007 and 2008, it won the GT1 class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans two years in a row.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C3:
The original Lancia Delta was a family-oriented hatchback designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro. However, when Group B was phased out of the WRC, Lancia selected the Delta as the foundation for its new Group A contender. From that moment, the car’s destiny as a rally legend was sealed.

In 1987, Lancia equipped the Delta a high-performance turbocharged engine and a 4WD system, before setting it loose in the WRC. 
From that moment on, Lancia secured an unprecedented six consecutive WRC championships. However, maintaining its edge meant that it had to undergo a series of evolutions. Such is the life of a competition rally car.

By 1991, Lancia faced mounting pressure from its rival, Toyota. In response, it unveiled the ultimate iteration of the Delta at the Frankfurt Motor Show—the HF Integrale Evoluzione.


The Evoluzione sported a larger front grille and expanded hood vents, enhancing enhanced airflow for improved engine cooling and ventilation. This allowed the power of the engine to be increased from <200ps> to <210ps>.

To help the car's stability, the front and rear track were widened by <60mm>. 
This necessitated even wider blistered wheel arches, pushing the car’s overall width to <1770mm>. 
And, by shifting the 4WD torque distribution toward the rear, Lancia engineered the car to deliver a driving character closer to that of a rear-wheel-drive machine. The car also featured a spoiler mounted to the edge of the roof to further improve downforce. 

The Evoluzione made its WRC debut in 1992, playing a crucial role in extending Lancia's streak of dominance. Unfortunately, Lancia's parent company, FIAT, decided to withdraw the car from the WRC, bringing the Evoluzione’s competitive run to an abrupt end that same year.Y
DescriptionLong.0x000049C4:
The fourth-generation Mazda2, known as the Demio in its home market, was introduced in 2014.

It featured the company's "KODO" design philosophy, which implemented many traditional Japanese styling cues along with a sleek overall profile. The car came powered by the usual gasoline-engine options, but for this model, a 1.5-liter turbodiesel that Mazda dubbed "SKYACTIV-D" was added. This engine boasted the performance equivalent to a 2.5-liter gasoline engine, with <25.5kgm> of torque on tap for the 6-speed automatic model and <22.4kgm> for the 6-speed manual. The latter returned an impressive <30.0km/L> on the Japanese JC08 mode fuel economy test. Customers were so enthralled with the new diesel that more than 60 percent of the initial orders were for the SKYACTIV-D models.

There were three grades available for the diesel-powered cars. This included the base XD model, the XD Touring that included practical options such as LED lights and cruise control, and the XD Touring L Package, which included luxury options such as white leather seats and a leather bound steering wheel.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C5:
In 1999, the Lamborghini Diablo was given a minor exterior update that replaced the retractable headlamps with fixed ones. At the Geneva Motor Show of the same year, the ultimate road going limited-edition Diablo GT was unveiled. Based on the Diablo GT2, a racing car developed for the FIA-GT championships, Lamborghini modified this beast for the street.

The 6.0-liter V12, based on the GT2, produces <575ps> and <64.3kgm> of torque. Many body panels were replaced with carbon-fiber ones, resulting in a curb weight of <1490kg>, which is <40kg> lighter than that of the Diablo SV. Therefore, it was super quick and could reach a top speed of <338km/h>.

Keeping engine heat in check was a major issue, so Lamborghini engineers incorporated improved cooling and aerodynamic modifications, such as the special bumper spoiler that contained a larger oil cooler and vents in the hood to better discharge the extra heat. These upgrades and others came from the experience gained in fielding the Diablo GT2 race car; in other words, everything different about the Diablo GT came straight from the racing circuit.

Only 80 cars were produced, and the 80th car is on display at the Lamborghini Museum, at the company's Italian headquarters, in Sant'Agata. It is considered the "Ultimate Diablo," and to some, the ultimate Lamborghini.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C6:
Ferrari had experienced plenty of success in motorsports with its mid-engine layout machines, but in 1968, the company decided to finally release a road-going car incorporating this tried-and-true racing technology. The result was the Dino 206 GT, a beautiful Berlinetta with a flowing all-aluminum body and a <1987cc> aluminum V-6 under the hood, which marked a change from Ferrari's traditional use of V-12s. Another fact worth noting is the car was not marketed with the Ferrari name, being sold simply as the "Dino," as if it were a model from a different brand.

"Dino" was the nickname of founder Enzo Ferrari's eldest son, the engineer Alfredo Ferrari, who tragically died at the tender age of 24. The 65-degree DOHC V6 found in the car that bears his name was an idea he proposed while in the hospital. It proved successful in race cars from 1957 on, and part of the reason the Dino 206 GT was created was to homologate the F2 engine.

Receiving a makeover in 1969, the Dino GT became the 246 GT. Because of the high cost and difficulty to produce the aluminum body, the new one was made of steel, while the engine and block construction were now made of cast iron. To compensate for the increase in weight, displacement was increased to <2418cc>, with output and torque improved from <185ps>/<17.9kgm> to <195ps>/<23.0kgm>. Thus, the car achieved a top speed of <235km/h>. Another major improvement was a longer wheelbase that improved stability and handling performance.

In 1971, a Targa-top 246 GTS was added to the lineup. Along with the Berlinetta, a total of 3761 cars were produced until 1974.
DescriptionLong.0x000049C7:
Citroën's reborn "DS" brand, established in 2009, became a completely independent entity in 2015. This DS3 premium compact car, introduced in 2009, sported unique styling and superior quality, despite the fact that the platform and base mechanism were shared with the C3, which was introduced at the same time. 

The DS3 Racing car that was introduced at the 2010 Paris Motor Show was a special model developed by Citroën’s competition department. It came with a turbocharged 1.6-liter direct-injection engine from the DS3 Sport Chic whose power was increased from <156ps> and <24.5kgm> of torque to <207ps> and <28.0kgm> of torque. The body was also enhanced, as it sat <30mm> wider than the Sport Chic and <15mm> lower, via special shocks and springs. The car stopped as it good as it went, thanks to upgraded brakes with 4-piston calipers and larger diameter discs. Also, to differentiate it from other DS3s, the DS3 Racing wore sporty 18-in. wheels and came bathed in a flamboyant paint scheme.

Production was initially set at 1000 units worldwide, but it became so popular that 2000 additional cars were produced.u
DescriptionLong.0x000049C8:
The origins of Jaguar trace way back to 1922, when Sir William Lyons began looking for partners to produce a motorcycle with sidecar known as the “Combination.”

By 1961, Jaguar had become Britain's premier car maker, thanks partly to a beautiful 2-seat sports car called the E-Type.

The E-Type was the final model that Lyons was involved with. Inspired by the C-Type and D-Type race cars, the newest Jag sported a long, svelte body that sat low to the ground. It came in both fixed-roof and open-top versions.

The car came powered by Jaguar's trusty <3781cc> DOHC inline-6 with triple SU carbs, which also powered the XK series since 1949. The E-Type's version produced <269 ps> at <5500 rpm>. With a lean curb weight of <1219kg>, the E-Type was quick, running from zero to <100km/h> in 7.2 seconds and reaching a top speed of <210 km/h>.

Given its performance, the high £2,630 price tag at the time was extremely reasonable. In all, 7820 E-Types were produced through 1964, and of those, about 90 percent came to the United States.E
DescriptionLong.0x000049C9:
The Grand Turismo Awards take place every year during the SEMA Show in Las Vegas. In 2012, the GT crew awarded their 10th anniversary prize to a 1969 Ford Mustang customized by Eckert's Rod & Custom.

Based in Oregon, U.S., Eckert's Rod & Custom has worked on the restoration and customization of classic and muscle cars for more than 25 years. Its creation, called the Mach Forty, is a beautifully-restored first-generation Mustang Fastback, with plenty of added attitude underneath its sheet metal. Most of the flawless bodywork was completely rebuilt, and the floor, from the rear seats to the trunk, has been cut out to make room for an engine, making this Mustang a mid-engine sports car.

Ford's supercharged 5.4L V-8 was tuned to pump out <862ps> and includes a control fitted inside the cabin that allows the driver to adjust engine output from approximately <608ps> to <862ps>. To handle the substantial increase in power, the chassis has been thoroughly reinforced, and the Chevrolet Corvette C6's suspension and traction control system have been installed.

Sure, Eckert's Rod & Custom tampered with the Mustang's traditional front-engine/rear-drive formula, but in doing so, it created a car even the most ardent Mustang fan would love.9
DescriptionLong.0x000049CA:
The Enzo Ferrari is an ultra premium sports car with a limited production of 399 cars, built in commemoration of the 55th anniversary of Ferrari.

The Enzo was designed by Ken (Kiyoyuki) Okuyama, a Japanese designer in Pininfarina at the time. The highly aerodynamic body is reminiscent of F1 machines of the day. It is notable that not only the body panels, but most of the frame is built of carbon composites.

The 6-liter V12 engine was specially designed for the Enzo, and produces a massive <660ps> of power, and <67.04kgm> torque. The suspension is double wishbone in front and rear, and combined with Brembo carbon ceramic disc brakes, it can withstand full speed runs on the circuit. With its powerful engine and lightweight body, its maximum speed is in excess of <350km/h>.

Though it mounts the high power engine midship as in the F40 and the F50, it is also given gullwing doors, air conditioning, and a semi automatic transmission called the F1-matic. Measures have been taken against noise and vibration by mounting the engine to the subframe that is buffered by bushings, and it is designed to be more of a road than the F50, which was closer to a pure race car. E
DescriptionLong.0x000049CB:
The Super GT Series has been the most popular touring car racing series in Japan, even when it was operating under its former name, the JGTC (Japanese Grand Touring Championship). In 2007, new regulations for top-tier GT500 cars called for a skidplate measuring <30mm> to be added beneath the car in an effort to reduce cornering speeds.

This new rule hardly had an effect on the Honda NSX as it went on to win five of that year's nine races. The following season, while the NSX teams were allowed to use the same successful chassis as the previous year (thanks to a regulation that required the main frame be used two years in a row), the rules committee decided to allow other cars to catch up by imposing a <50kg> weight handicap to the NSX (this was reduced to <40kg> from Round 3 on). In addition, the committee imposed smaller engine restrictors for the cars, which slowed the NSXs down even more.

In response, Honda revised the specifications of its <3494cc> 32B V-6 for added throttle response, improved the car's aerodynamics, and made it even lighter.

There were five NSXs competing that year, and the EPSON NSX of Nakajima Racing was the only one running with DUNLOP tires, making them the odd man out when it came to data sharing with the other NSX teams.

Drivers Loïc Duval and Katsuyuki Hiranaka exceeded everyone's expectations, finishing 2nd in the eighth round at Autopolis, which was their highest placing of the year./
DescriptionLong.0x000049CC:
It was the rebirth of a legend. When the Jaguar F-Type bowed at the 2012 Paris Motor Show, it was evident from first glance that it was the spiritual successor of the celebrated E-Type, arguably the most beautiful sports/grand touring car ever made. The E-Type was discontinued in 1975, and while the XK Series carried on Jaguar’s grand touring duties, the F-Type was slated to carry on the company’s high-performance tradition.

The stylish car first came out as a convertible with an electric soft top, but almost exactly one year later, Jaguar unveiled the coupe version, which, not coincidentally, looked similar to the C-X16 concept car (the forbearer of the F Type shown almost simultaneously at the Los Angeles Auto Show and the Tokyo Motor Show), and the high-performance model of the series was the F-Type R Coupe.

The “R” designation stood for “Race,” so it came as no surprise that this model possessed a stronger engine, tighter suspension and more aggressive styling than the base F-Type. Under its hood resided a <550ps> 5.0-liter supercharged V-8, the base F-Type pumped out a “mere” <485ps>, which was still enough to make it one of the most powerful drop tops in the industry.

The F-Type R Coupe ran from zero to <100km/h> in a sprite 4.2 seconds, and reached a top speed of <300km/h>, restricted by a limiter. Its electronic controls such as the adaptive suspension and torque vectoring differential were also tuned for better performance. All this, and more, made the F-Type Coupe the consummate gentleman’s sports car, armed with a powerful engine, amazing handling and a high level of class.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.g

DescriptionLong.0x000049CF:
The W08 EQ Power+ was developed by Mercedes AMG Petronas Motorsport to compete in the 2017 Formula 1 season.

Mercedes made a full return to F1 in 2010 after a 55-year hiatus. It splashed onto the scene as among the top four contenders in that first year, and then showed marked improvement in the ensuing years. By 2014, Team Mercedes had conquered F1, winning both the Drivers and Constructor's titles from 2014 to 2016.

But because of new regulations in 2017, there were some initial minor problems. Drivers were struggling to establish their preferred setup, and although the car was fast in mid- to high-speed corners, it didn't fare as well on tracks with lots of low-speed corners. But leave it to Mercedes to overcome its issues.

The power unit reportedly produced approximately <950ps>, making it the most powerful in the field, which explained the car's excellent speed throughout the 2017 season. Drivers Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas achieved a fantastic 15 pole positions and 12 victories out of 20 races, giving Mercedes its fourth straight double titles.
DescriptionLong.0x000049D0:
The W08 EQ Power+ was developed by Mercedes AMG Petronas Motorsport to compete in the 2017 Formula 1 season.

Mercedes-Benz made a full return to F1 in 2010 after a 55-year hiatus. It splashed onto the scene as among the top four contenders in that first year, and then showed marked improvement in the ensuing years. By 2014, Team Mercedes-Benz had conquered F1, winning both the Drivers and Constructor's titles from 2014 to 2016. But because of new regulations in 2017, there were some initial minor problems. Drivers were struggling to establish their preferred setup, and although the car was fast in mid- to high-speed corners, it didn't fare as well on tracks with lots of low-speed corners. Still, the M-B overcame these issues in time for the start of the season.

The power unit reportedly produced approximately <950ps>, making it tops in the field, which explained the car's excellent speed throughout the 2017 season. Drivers Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas achieved a fantastic 15 pole positions and 12 victories out of 20 races, giving Mercedes-Benz its fourth straight double titles.
DescriptionLong.0x000049D1:
The F series is a line of full size pickup trucks sold by Ford since 1948. This is a model that has stayed on top of the pickup truck segment for over 40 years, and has also been the best selling car across all car categories for over 30 years in the United States.

The F-150 has always been the core of the series since being introduced in 1975. It is a model that has been the backbone of Ford throughout the years.

The F-150 Raptor is a special off-road model based on the 12th generation F-150, which started sales in the fall of 2008. It was developed by Ford's special vehicle development team "SVT" to be fit for racing in the desert and was added to the lineup in 2010.

The body is <18cm> wider with its enlarged fenders that house considerably thicker aluminum suspension arms supported by Fox Racing dampers, which are known to be the first off-road competition dampers to come equipped on a production car. The suspension travel in the front has been extended to <284.5mm> and <307.3mm> in the rear. The clearance under the car is also large, with an approach angle of 30 degrees and a departure angle of 22.7 degrees.

The engine is a 6.2 litre supercharged V8 producing <417ps> and <60.9kgm> of torque, and is combined with a 6 speed automatic transmission.|
DescriptionLong.0x000049D2:
F1 machines in the mid-80’s were characterized by a compact V6 turbo engine and their stoic, well cut appearance. The Gran Turismo F1500T-A is a machine that brings back the style still considered to be the best form in F1 history, with its own unique interpretation.

While maintaining the basic concepts from 30 years ago with a slightly forward cockpit and a simple aerodynamic package, this car also incorporates the performance of a front line formula racing machine.

The carbon fiber chassis is <4235mm> long, <2146mm> wide, and has a wheel base of <2718mm>. The 1.5 liter turbocharged V6 is symbolic of F1 engines from the 1980’s, and produces approximately <1000ps> at <11000rpm>.

The aerodynamic design of the wings and other components also follow the trends from the 80's, but as a result of increased cooling performance of the turbocharger and the engine, the opening of the air outlets on the side pontoons were minimized, improving the aerodynamics on the body sides.

Formula cars are a different type of beast compared to touring cars. Get a taste for Formula level performance with this machine.u
DescriptionLong.0x000049D3:
A very special Ferrari was announced by company founder, Enzo Ferrari, in July 1987. Dubbed the F40, this car was to mark the company's 40th anniversary, billed as Ferrari's first "street legal racing car."

Signore Ferrari spared no costs when building this dream machine. The F40's structure utilized a steel tube-frame in the same manner as other Ferrari road cars of the 1980s, but various internal and external chassis components were composed of carbon-fiber and Kevlar, the newest lightest, high-tech composite material available at the time.

The car's body panels were a structural part of the chassis, and its tube frame foundation was constructed from Kevlar and aluminum honeycomb sections, the preferred manufacturing method for racing cars at the time.

Powering the lightweight car was a twin-turbocharged, 3.0-liter DOHC V8 with a 90 degree bank angle, based on the power plant for the Ferrari's Group B 288 GTO; however, the one in the F40 had a larger displacement and altered boost pressures. As a result, the F40 produced an amazing <485ps> and <58.8kgm> of torque. The <1100kg> car could run to <100km/h> in about 4 seconds and reach a top speed of <324km/h>, making it the fastest production car in the world at the time.@
DescriptionLong.0x000049D4:
When one utters the phrase "entry-level cars," it's usually meant to describe an inexpensive automobile whose sole purpose is to get people from Point A to Point B. But when you're talking about Ferrari, all conventional definitions go out the proverbial window.

Replacing Ferrari's "entry-level" 360 Modena in 2004 was the F430. The car's styling was mesmerizing, with flowing lines influenced by the company's legendary Formula 1 racers and Le Mans prototypes of the 1960s.

Mounted amidships was a sweet-sounding V8 powerplant. Unlike the 350 Modena's engine, which evolved from that of the 1973 Ferrari 308 GT4 in 1973, the F430's 4.3-liter naturally aspirated unit was completely new. Output was impressive, as it was rated at <490ps>/<8500rpm>, eclipsing the output of the legendary F40's turbocharged V8. It came mated to a high-tech new twin-clutch transmission that allowed the driver to manually select gears via paddles on the steering wheel.

The F430's chassis was a heavily reworked version of the 360 Modena's that featured a frame composed of extruded and forged aluminum. Part of the structure was altered to meet new, more stringent collision safety standards, and the floor board was made of an exceptionally strong aluminum alloy used in aerospace called extra super duralumin. With available carbon-ceramic brake rotors and a top speed of <315km/h>, the Ferrari F430, whose base price was about $180,000, was perhaps the most desirable "entry-level" car in the world.5
DescriptionLong.0x000049D5:
As the successor to the amazing F40 sports car, the F50 represented the latest and greatest from renowned auto maker and race team, Ferrari. The car also commemorated the 50th anniversary of the company. The F50 became an instant classic, as only 349 units were built, following in the the tradition established by other limited-edition models, the 288 GTO and the aforementioned F40.

The basic philosophy behind the F50 was to produce a Formula One car for the road. And the sleek sports car was exactly that, realizing a long-standing dream of Piero Ferrari (the second son of Ferrari founder Enzo) of making a road car with an F1 engine.

Designed by Pininfarina, the F50 featured a carbon-fiber body and an open-air cockpit like that of an F1 race machine (although the F50 did come with a removable hard top for rainy days). Also mimicking F1 cars was the F50's chassis whose front suspension was mounted directly to the carbon monocoque tub, while the rear suspension connected directly to the gearbox. The V-12 engine was based on the power unit from the 641, Ferrari's 1990 F1 race car. For the F50, it was tuned for road use, such as increasing displacement from 3.5 to 4.7 liters for smoother power delivery and mating it to a 6-speed manual gearbox. Top speed for the F50 was rated at <325km/h> and its 0-<100km/h> time came in at 3.87 seconds, which far exceeded the best sports cars of its day.@
DescriptionLong.0x000049D6:
*The Nissan Fairlady Z was sold as the Nissan Z in markets outside of Japan.

Near the end of the 1960s, Japanese cars made a name for themselves on the international stage. One of these examples was the Datsun 240Z that was introduced in 1969. Yutaka Katayama, the president of Nissan North America at the time, convinced the Japanese brass that "now was the time for real sports cars," to challenge those from Europe. Thus, the Z was born.

Among the more notable Zs was the 432. While other Zs were equipped with the Type L engine, the 432 came equipped with the S20, a DOHC inline-6 lifted from the Prince R380. The "4" stood for 4 valves per cylinder, the "3" for 3 twin-choke carburetors, and "2" represented the engine's 2 camshafts. Output of the engine was rated at <160ps> and <18.0kgm> of torque.

This 432 also had a 432R racing spec model that sported a carbon-fiber hood for weight reduction. Only 30 of these cars were made.

A considerable amount of work went into making the 432. The S20 was known to be a delicate powerplant that only the Nissan mechanics at Oppama could get the most out of.  

On the other hand, the 2.4-liter Type L engine in the U.S.-spec 240Z was easy to work with, and its ability to provide plenty of torque throughout the rpm spectrum made it popular for racers. The 240Z performed well in safari races and notable off-road events such as the Monte Carlo Rally, as well as those on tarmac racing circuits.

Thanks to its high level of performance, the 240Z made it to Japan in 1971, marketed there as the Fairlady Z. A special version of the car called the 240ZG, referred to as the "G nose," added to the car's popularity, solidifying its place in the history books as one of the most popular and longest-tenured sports cars ever.
DescriptionLong.0x000049D7:
Nissan's legendary sports car, the "Fairlady Z," disappeared from the catalog lineup in the summer of 2000, but Nissan President Carlos Ghosn knew full well the importance of this car and had secretly given the go-ahead for the new generation model. In July of 2002, the new Z33 Z-car made its debut.

It shared its base frame and the V6 3.5-liter VQ35DE engine with the V35 Skyline, but it produced <280ps> and <37.0kgm> of torque. It also came with a 6-speed manual gearbox.

The new Z continued to evolve in the following years. One major advancement was made in January 2007, when the engine was changed to the new generation VQ35HR, improving power output to <313ps>. The intake manifold was completely redesigned, and the friction within the engine was reduced. By further improving the crankshaft section, the engine revved more freely. Also, the exhaust note was tuned to give off a deep and low sound, reminiscent of a V-8 engine. The designers added a power bulge to the car's hood to show the Z's extra power.

The engineers heavily modified the car's suspension, improving absorption of the road surface and delivering a flatter cornering character. These changes translated to better overall handling feel and enhanced race-track performance.m
DescriptionLong.0x000049D8:
When the sixth-generation Fairlady Z, the Z34, was introduced in December 2008, most people assumed that the car would be just a mildly updated version of the Z33 that revived the Z car in January 2002. The 370Z, as we knew it, appeared relatively the same; however, upon closer inspection, it became evident that this was an all-new car.

Built atop the E platform that also serves as the foundation of the Infiniti "Skyline" G37, the new Z featured an aluminum hood, door and rear hatch that kept the car's curb weight about the same as the previous vehicle (around <1500kg>). The new Z was nimble, thanks to a wheelbase that was <100mm> shorter and retuned suspension system that consisted of a double-wishbone setup in front and multilink at rear.

Under the hood was a more powerful engine, the VQ37VHR with VVEL. VVEL was a mechanism that varies the operating angle and lift of the valves for improved power and lower emissions. With <200cc> more displacement, the new V6 pumped out <336ps>/<7000rpm> and <37.2kgm> of torque that peaked at <5200rpm>. The engine came mated to either a quick-shifting 6-speed automatic transmission, or a revolutionary 6-speed manual gearbox equipped with the world's first synchro rev control mechanism. This system automatically adjusted engine rpm when downshifting, eliminating the need to heel and toe.

Thus, the Z34 became a true enthusiast sports car that even novices could drive effectively.
DescriptionLong.0x000049D9:
Daijiro Yoshihara, aka “Daichan,” a Japanese drift driver who was crowned Formula D champion in 2011, chose the Falken Tire / Turn 14 Distribution BRZ ’17 race car as his mount for the 2017 Formula Drift series.

The body of the car was based on the Rocket Bunny V3 aero kit, with various parts replaced with carbon. Packed with technology to boost its performance as a competition drift machine, the car featured an engine that needed to be seen to be believed. A massive 7.0-liter turbocharged V-8 packed into the cramped engine bay. It produced about <1000ps> through a MoTeC M800, making this an extreme machine able to drift faster and further than the rest.

The car was mated to a custom 4-speed transmission, with upgraded brakes that had 6-pot calipers up front and 4-pot calipers at rear. Although he was unable to win the 2017 championship, Daichan still managed to place 6th overall in his No. 9 car, always delighting the crowds and fans that came to cheer him on.1
DescriptionLong.0x000049DA:
Pontiac was the sporty upscale brand of General Motors, and the model which helped define the division in its heyday was an American muscle car called the Firebird. It was created to take on Ford's ultra-popular pony car, the Mustang.

Many variations of the Firebird were produced in order to compete against its famous rival, with Pontiac making the cars faster and more luxurious. The top model "Trans Am" was a car enthusiast's dream: the name of this top-of-the-line model, which ended up becoming more famous than the original "Firebird" name, was taken from the popular sports car racing series. The Pontiac Trans Am, with its giant Firebird sticker garnishing the hood, became a revered muscle car, and a classic American automotive symbol of the 1970s.

The final 1978 model of the second-generation series was available with both a 400 or 403 cubic inch V8. The big, high-compression 6.6-liter mill was an engine exclusive to Pontiac, and was not available in its pony car brother, the Chevrolet Camaro. The brass at Pontiac figured that instead of aligning the Trans Am with the Camaro, they were better off developing a special engine unique to the Firebird. Also, the car possessed a four-headlamp design, instead of the customary two, which differentiated it from the Camaro and other GM products.

The car was a great hit, and the Firebird Trans Am lives on in infinite lore as the car driven by Burt Reynolds in the movie "Smokey and the Bandit."
DescriptionLong.0x000049DB:
It was natural for Honda to offer a hybrid version of its popular compact vehicle, the Fit, for its lightweight nature made it an exceptional candidate to take full advantage of the company's excellent hybrid system. While the first-generation Fit Hybrid was a great hit, the second-generation model was even better, equipped with a completely new hybrid system.

The Honda IMA (Integrated Motor Assist) in the first generation model had a motor connected directly to the engine--using the engine as the main power source as the motor provided assist as necessary--but the second-gen Fit Hybrid separated the power units. Called the new Sport Hybrid i-DCD (Intelligent Dual Clutch Drive), this new system had a 7-speed dual-clutch transmission with a built-in electric motor that connected the motor to the gasoline engine, which prevented energy loss during regenerative power generation. Also, it allowed the vehicle to be driven in engine, Hybrid, or EV modes, depending on the driving conditions.

This i-DCD system combined with a 1.5-liter i-VTEC engine produced a combined output of <139.5ps>, offering powerful, sporty driving while also achieving the excellent fuel efficiency of <36.4km/l> in JC08 mode.

Aside from the hybrid system, the rest of the Fit was no different than any other third-generation model, with the choice of four trim levels, but the most sporty S package was the only one available with a paddle shifter.
DescriptionLong.0x000049DC:
Ford saw performance potential in its affordable sedan, the Focus, so it created the Focus ST, a souped-up version that made its debut in 1998. The third-generation Focus ST (the ST stands for Sports Technology) debuted at the 2010 Paris Motor Show equipped with a brand new engine.

The previous Focus ST came powered by a Volvo-based turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-5, but the new car featured an “EcoBoost” turbocharged direct-injection 2.0-liter inline-4 that boasted better fuel economy and reduced emissions. Despite being smaller by <500cc>, the new engine delivered <25ps> more power, up to <250ps>. While many models had moved on to 2 pedal transmissions, this stoic model only came with a 6-speed manual.

The car thrilled enthusiasts for years, and in 2014, in addition to a mild facelift, Ford engineers made some drastic changes under the sheet metal. They completely revamped the suspension system, changed the variable ratio of the power steering, updated the stability program, and installed a torque vectoring system. As a result, the new Focus ST’s boasted class-leading handling, impressing even hardened race car drivers with its quick reactions and road-holding ability. And with a price that undercut its rivals in the competitive C segment, the Ford ST is still the talk of performance-car aficionados, even at the tail-end of its model run.D

DescriptionLong.0x000049DE:
The Ford GT40 became an instant icon in the GT racing world by dominating the famous 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race, taking the top three spots on the podium in 1966 and winning the next four in a row. In celebration of Ford's 100th anniversary in 2002, the company elected to recreate the legend by producing the spiritual successor to the classic race car of the sixties, the Ford GT.

The concept model was presented at the 2002 North American International Auto Show, followed by the unveiling of the production car at the same show in 2004. Its beautiful styling closely resembled that of the original GT40, but the new machine came armed with the latest technological features. The car measured <457mm> longer and <102mm> taller than the original, but its larger size was effectively veiled by the stunning exterior styling.

Placed amidships, immediately behind the cabin, was a longitudinally-mounted supercharged 5.4-liter DOHC V8 that pumped out <558ps>/<6500rpm> with <69.13kgm> of torque at <3750rpm>. It came with a 6-speed gearbox. The new GT boasted remarkable performance, running from 0 to 60 mph (about 100km/h) in 3.3 seconds, while reaching a top speed of <330km/h>.

A total of 4038 Ford GTs were unleashed onto the streets during its three-year production run, and, by all accounts, this revived version of the GT40 will be just as collectable as the original.
DescriptionLong.0x000049DF:
As a stunning new take on a legendary racing car, the new Ford GT supercar was launched in the summer of 2004 to commemorate the company's 100th anniversary. As a reinterpretation of the classic 1960s GT40 that won four straight 24 Hours of Le Mans races, this new version featured the latest and greatest automotive technology. With that in mind, we decided to make a good thing even better by creating this Ford GT to contemporary Le Mans specs and calling it the Ford GT LM Race Car.

The powertrain remains the same as that which is found in the production Ford GT, a supercharged 5.4-liter DOHC V8 mounted amidships behind the seats. However, the <558 ps> output from the stock version has been boosted to a whopping <600 ps> in this race car model. A 6-speed manual race-spec gearbox has also been added.

The LM Race Car has the identical proportions as that of the stock Ford GT, measuring <4.61 m> from bumper to bumper and <1.95 m> wide. The chassis is an aluminum space frame design incorporating all of the latest automotive technologies, and the body is composed entirely of carbon-fiber. A large rear wing for increased downforce has also been added. The suspension system consists of a double-wishbone configuration fore and aft. The total curb weight is just 2535 lbs.
DescriptionLong.0x000049E0:
The original Ford GT, which was produced from 2005 to 2006, brought back the glory of the renowned GT40, whose exploits in the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the 1960s are now legendary. At the 2015 North American International Auto Show, Ford introduced the second-generation GT that boasted even more performance and technical savagery than its predecessor.

While the first Ford GT's styling strongly resembled that of the GT40, the new 2016 car featured a number of aerodynamic improvements that included an active rear spoiler and a large underbody tunnel that directed air from the side through to the rear. Underneath the sheet metal, there were aluminum front and rear subframes that provided a remarkably rigid body structure, while the body panels themselves were composed of lightweight carbon fiber.

Mounted aft of the cockpit was not the V8 of yore, but a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 that produced a whopping <656ps> and <76kgm>. It came with a 7-speed DCT transmission that sent the power to the rear wheels. This combination enabled the new Ford GT to run from 0 to 60 mph in a scant 3.2 seconds, while reaching a top speed of <348km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x000049E1:
The Toyota FT-1 is a "pure performance dream" concept model created by CALTY Design, the U.S. base of Toyota’s design network as a showcase for the future direction of Toyota sports car design.

Its exterior and interior design draws heavily on the Toyota brand’s long sports car tradition with influential vehicles such as 2000GT, Celica, Supra, and most recently, 86 (Model Name USA：FR-S, Europe：GT86).

The FT-1 concept’s purposeful yet elegant expression of functional beauty should not be viewed as precursor to a forthcoming Toyota production sports car. Rather, the bold and passionate design theme indicates a shift to a more exciting direction for the entire Toyota brand.

Dimensions:

Length: 4675 mm

Width: 1970 mm

Height: 1225 mm

Wheelbase: 2740 mm

The Toyota FT-1 debuted at the North American International Auto Show in January, 2014.

*The specifications for this car are a fictitious set created specially for Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x000049E2:
The Genesis Coupe is a sporty 2-door that shared a platform with the Genesis luxury coupe.

The Genesis Coupe was shorter than the sedan by <345mm>, with a wheelbase that was also shorter, by <115mm>. These dimensions, combined with the front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout and four-wheel independent suspension, gave the car excellent agility. The engine choices were a 3.8-liter V-6 or a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline 4. Thanks to the car's excellent power delivery and agile rear-drive handling, the Genesis Coupe quickly gained popularity.

A minor change was implemented in 2012 that gave the coupe sharper looks, but the focus was on increasing engine output across the board. Power for the 3.8-liter V6 was increased to approximately <350ps>, making it one of the most powerful cars in its class. Also, in addition to the previous 6-speed manual gearbox, a paddle-shift 8-speed unit was added as an option.

The high-performance model was the 3.8 Track. Springs, dampers and stabilizers were changed to race track-developed, heavy-duty parts, with an adjustable front camber and Torsen LSD. Also, Brembo four-piston calipers were added to the car, emphasizing its pure sport focus. In well-respected tests carried out by unbiased organizations, the Genesis Coupe easily outperformed class rivals.

DescriptionLong.0x000049E6:
When the time came for Volkswagen to create a successor to the legendary people's car, the Beetle, it came in the form of the Golf in 1974. Unlike the Beetle, however, the Golf had its engine up front powering the front wheels (FF), and this format would define the company's compact cars to this day.

The revolutionary packaging was a hit with the public, spurring VW to produce a number of variations on the Golf theme. Included among them was the GTI, which made its debut at the 1975 Frankfurt Motor Show.

Based on the 2-door Golf LSI, the GTI came powered by a 1.6-liter SOHC inline-4 whose compression ratio was boosted to 9.5:1 and featured Bosch fuel-injection. The end result was an engine that produced <110 ps> at <6100 rpm> and <14.0 kgm> of torque at <5000 rpm>. The car's handling saw dramatic improvements as well. The suspension was strengthened and counterbalanced, with custom shocks and springs that stiffened ride quality but improved the car's cornering nature. Also assisting in this department were 175/70R13 tires.

The Golf GTI enjoyed great popularity, and improved gradually over the years. In 1979, it received a 5-speed manual transmission, then in 1981 a 4-door model was added, and at the end of 1982, a 1.8-liter inline-4 was introduced. The Golf GTI set the standard for VW's compact cars to this day.
DescriptionLong.0x000049E7:
When the 7th-generation Golf made its debut in 2012, the car seemed more or less a carryover from the previous model; however, once Volkswagen revealed the changes made under the sheet metal, it was clear that the new Golf was a different breed altogether from its predecessor.

The platform was thoroughly refreshed, highlighted by a newly developed modular MQB system that significantly heightened driving performance, improved ride quality and increased safety. The Golf has long been considered the benchmark of the C-segment class, but the new version raised the bar even higher, leaving engineers from America, Japan and Korea scratching their collective heads.

In fact, the bar was raised so high that the sport-tuned Golf models were making sports car makers nervous. Both 3-door and 5-door GTIs possessed a high level of performance that could satisfy the most critical enthusiast. Under the hood was an intercooled-turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4, with the output improved from <210ps> of the previous GTI to <220ps>. This improved the 0-<100km/h> acceleration time of the car from 6.9 seconds to 6.5, and increased its top speed to <246km/h> from <240km/h>.

The new GTI shined in the handling department as well. Advancements in the “XDS” electronic control differential lock, which acts as a limited-slip differential, was improved to give the GTI super crisp turn-in response. The adaptive chassis control called “DCC,” along with the utilization of progressive steering, improved the Golf’s overall stability and cornering speed.

Also of note, the new GTI featured BlueMotion technology, a first for this model. Adding a brake energy recovery system and a start-and-stop mechanism, the new car was greener than before. Safety was also enhanced, thanks to a pre-crash brake system and lane assist.

The Golf GTI has always been known as a giant killer, and the new 7th-gen iteration embraced that role as never before.`
DescriptionLong.0x000049E8:
After 17 long years, the beloved Supra made its return, first as the race-ready GR Supra. Toyota's flagship sports car was co-developed with BMW, borrowing among other things the BMW Z4's superb inline-6 engine.

The 2-seat sports car made its first appearance at the 2018 Nürburgring 24 hour race a year before its release along with the slogan: To make even better cars. It entered the SP8T class in 2019 after its release.

With Masahiro Sasaki, Uwe Kleen, Herwig Daenens, and Morizo at the wheel, the GR Supra started the final race at the Ring from 99th place, but steadily made its way up the field as the drivers avoided a number of accidents at the beginning of the race. Eight hours into the contest, the car was involved in a slight crash, but fortunately for Toyota, damage was minimal and the car went on to finish in a respectable 41st place overall, and 3rd in its class.

Its outing proved that the GR Supra was a true sports car with a genuine race car heart.
DescriptionLong.0x000049E9:
The GR Supra Racing Concept, unveiled at the 2018 Geneva Motor Show, was a bold reimagining of Toyota’s legendary Supra—a sports car that had been out of production since 2002. With this concept, the nameplate returned for the first time in 16 years, reborn as a pure race car.

The car was developed by TOYOTA GAZOO Racing, the division responsible for the company’s motorsports activities and the GR sports-car series.

Its design followed the classic long-nose, short-deck form, with a front-engine/rear-wheel-drive, two-door coupe layout. The compact body was constructed from lightweight, high-strength carbon composite materials, the kind used in frontline racing. Large blister fenders, a rear wing, and a pronounced diffuser were added to deliver superior aerodynamics and high-speed stability.

The suspension, wheels, tires, and brakes were all racing-spec. The stripped-down interior included a dashboard with a rear-view monitor, competition seats, a race steering wheel with paddle shifters, and a full roll cage—all purpose-built for the track.

For a quarter of a century, the Supra had been beloved worldwide as “The Sports of Toyota,” leaving a powerful mark on motorsports history.
DescriptionLong.0x000049EA:
Toyota has long been a dominant presence in the World Rally Championships, consistently fighting for the series championship year after year. After building a number of classic rally race cars, the company will be introducing its newest off-road competition machine in 2021: the GR Yaris.

At first, it may not look that different from the production hatchback, aside from the super wide rear fenders, but under the skin beats the heart of a serious racer. Built on a combination of the TNGA GA-B and GA-C platforms, the extremely lightweight body possesses increased rigidity. Its flowing profile, characterized by the low carbon-fiber roof, optimizes airflow.

Under the hood of the RZ model is the G16E-GTS, a turbocharged 1.6-liter inline-3. Boasting the smallest size and lightest weight in its class, this unit produces 200 kW (<272ps>)/370 Nm (<37.7kgm>) and comes mated to a 6-speed manual transmission that sends power to all four wheels via a newly developed electronically controlled coupling type center differential. The RZ High Performance model is equipped with Torsen LSDs for both the front and rear differentials, for maximum traction.

This "First Edition" model, introduced alongside the GR Yaris in January 2020, was offered to those who pre-ordered the car. Among other things, it featured special forged aluminum wheels and was autographed by Toyota "master driver" Morizo, who is in fact Toyota CEO Akio Toyoda.
DescriptionLong.0x000049EB:
Maserati's GranTurismo S, not to be confused with this driving simulator of the same name, was unveiled at the 2008 Geneva Motor Show as the high-performance version of Maserati's handsome GranTurismo Coupe.

Although there wasn't much that visually separated the two cars, there were significant differences under the sheet metal; the most noteworthy of which being the drivetrain. For starters, the displacement of the DOHC V8 in the GranTurismo S was increased to <4691cc>, <500cc> more than in the base car. Combined with this revitalized engine was a state-of-the-art semi-automatic gearbox dubbed "MC Shift." MC Shift allowed drivers the choice between a smooth-shifting automatic transmission befitting a pure luxury car and a quick-shifting sequential manual where shifting is performed via paddles on the steering wheel.

And because it was a transaxle (with the gearbox mounted on the rear differential), the front/rear weight distribution was drastically improved, making the GranTurismo S a better handling machine.

Despite the two cars looking virtually identical, the GranTurismo S possessed a more athletic nature than the base car, while still delivering the luxury and elegance that has made the marque famous for nearly 100 years.b
DescriptionLong.0x000049EC:
The GT by Citroën announced at the 2008 Paris Motor Show, is a sports concept car in which Citroën and Gran Turismo collaborated for the first time.

The car attracted much attention as a new type of concept car, an expression of real and virtual. And it was in the spring of 2009, that a decision was made to run a racing spec version of this machine in the world of GT.

The exterior was designed by Takumi Yamamoto, the designer who created the original. Many sketches were sent to Polyphony Digital (PDI) day after day, and as a result, the original fenders were widened, and with the addition of air ducts and other aerodynamic parts, the design took an extremely aggressive turn.

Based on this, the details to make it more racing-car like was left to PDI. Details like the hood pins and tow hooks you would normally see on race cars, the valves for the air jacks, and the layout of sponsor stickers, were all set by PDI.

The other major piece of work left to PDI was the design of the interior. The motif was a modern jet fighter, and while being extremely high tech, it is balanced with the gritty feel of a real racing car.

All parts aside from the dashboard have been replaced, and the steering wheel and HUD (heads-up display) are functional in design as befitting a racing car, while still being as eccentric as the exterior. Though not changed in design, the dashboard is made of carbon, instead of copper.

The HUD displays things like speed, engine rpm, steering angle, and horizontal Gs.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.
DescriptionLong.0x000049ED:
The GT by Citroën announced at the 2008 Paris Motor Show was the first sports concept car created from a collaboration between Citroën and Gran Turismo. This approach succeeded in establishing an image of a new concept car that does not just end at the show floor. This is because a 21st century sports car imagined by Citroën is accurately expressed in both real and virtual forms.

Based on the GT by Citroën, the GT by Citroën Gr.4 is a race spec car modified for racing in the Gr.4 category.

To meet the Gr.4 regulations in which the range of modifications is limited, the exterior changes are minimal. However, because the original car is already very unique, its sense of presence is overwhelming. The armor-like front and rear fenders and the sharp visage of the fascia that remind the viewer of a medieval Japanese warrior’s mask, are maintained in this model.

The unique aspect of this car is that the modifications to make it a Gr.4 car were performed by none other than Takumi Yamamoto himself, who created the original design for the base car. The 6 variations of the livery and newly added rear wing express the intent of Yamamoto. The addition of required racing equipment such as hood pins, towing hooks, and air jack valves give the car the look of a serious circuit fighting machine.

The interior has also been modified for weight reduction, and the steering wheel and HUD are made in a functional design befitting of a race car. The dashboard material has been changed from copper to carbon, and the HUD displays speed, engine RPM, steering angle, and horizontal Gs to assist the assessment of the car’s state by the drivers on the track.

With its avant-garde styling and performance of a competition machine, the GT by Citroën Gr.4 is a groundbreaking combination of these aspects.
DescriptionLong.0x000049EE:
The GT by Citroën was a concept car created through a collaboration between Citroën and Gran Turismo. It was the hit of the 2008 Paris Motor Show, with many impressed by its avant-garde styling, penned by Citroën designer Takumi Yamamoto.

This super sports car came to life after numerous travels between Japan and France. It went from a show model to a running model, which we called the GT by Citroën Road Car. The major difference between the show car and road car was the former was an electric vehicle with a high-power motor, while the latter came powered by a mid-mounted V-8 engine.

The elegant exterior of the car was largely left intact. The slits between the rounded inner body and outer cowling effectively dissipate heat from the engine, keeping it cool. 

Also, the replacement of the heavy, high-capacity drive battery with a smaller gasoline tank made the car much lighter.

A sturdy rear cowl completely covered the engine bay, but it provided extra rigidity, which made the GT by Citroën an awesome handling machine. ~
DescriptionLong.0x000049EF:
The Ford Motor Company introduced the Mustang in 1964, a sporty coupe that would become an American icon. Back then, to raise its sporty image for better sales numbers, the folks in Dearborn, Michigan decided to enter the car in SCCA (Sports Car Club of America) racing.

According to the regulations, the homologation requirement for racing in the SCCA was 100, meaning that at least 100 units needed to be produced commercially to qualify for racing events; however, changes to the engine, suspension, or brakes were not allowed. In fact, the only thing that was permitted was weight reduction. Ford decided to create a special-edition production car with more power and performance than the base Mustang. It turned to Shelby American, led by legendary champion driver and automotive designer Carroll Shelby. Mr. Shelby delivered; in 1965, he presented Ford execs with the GT350, based on the Mustang Fastback.

Because the "production" car was built for the track, it included lots of racing technology, including a carbon-fiber hood replete with air intake, a stiff racing suspension, a performance limited-slip differential, and a transmission casing made from lightweight aluminum. What's more, it lacked rear seats, a heater, power steering, and sound proofing, making this pony car one lightweight yet loud and uncomfortable machine. The battery was mounted in the trunk for better weight distribution, and the spare tire was stored inside the passenger compartment for the same reason.

The engine was a tuned 4.7-liter OHV (289 cu in.) V-8 that was optionally available. It produced a whopping <306ps>/<45.6kgm>. This combination of brute force mixed with the agile chassis resulted in the car's domination of the SCCA, as the GT350 stood at the pinnacle of American road racing for three straight years.
DescriptionLong.0x000049F0:
In 1963, Ford attempted to buy Ferrari in order to improve its brand image through racing. The talks did not go well, to say the least. The deal didn't happen, and Henry Ford II went on a mission to beat Ferrari at its own game, expanding a collaboration with British race car constructor Lola Cars (to whom Ford was already providing engines) to develop a brand-new racing car.

In 1964, based on a race chassis designed by Lola, the Mark I was completed and the Ford GT was born. The commonly known name "GT40" was originally a nickname given by a reporter who was surprised by the low 40-inch height of the car.

A lightweight aerodynamic body of fiberglass was mounted on a steel monocoque chassis, powered by an all-aluminum 4.7-liter OHV V8 mounted amidships. The car made its debut at a 1964 Nürburgring race. Later that year, three Mark I's began the assault on Ferrari. The cars showed incredible speed at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, breaking the lap record and achieving the first run in Le Mans history over <186mph>, but the Fords failed to win due to reliability issues.

From 1965, Ford commissioned race activities to Carroll Shelby, and though the GTs again set new top speed and lap records at Le Mans, all of the cars were again forced to retire from the race. At the 1966 Le Mans race, 8 out of 13 Ford GTs in the race were advanced Mark IIs, with improved chassis and Shelby-made 7-liter OHV V8s. In addition to many other refinements, the power of the engines skyrocketed from <350ps> to <475ps>.

Mr. Ford himself came to the circuit to watch this race, and Ford not only achieved a much-sought victory, they dominated the podium with an incredible 1-2-3 finish. From 1966 through 1969, the Ford GT devastated the competition, winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans four years in a row.Y
DescriptionLong.0x000049F1:
The year was 1966, and Ford was on a roll, especially at the world's most famous endurance race, the 24 Hours of Le Mans. The company realized its goal of winning the historic contest on its third try, dominating the competition with the Ford GT Mark II. With their eyes set on winning future Le Mans races, the engineers from Ford began work developing a new race car in 1965, one that would eclipse the prowess of the GT Mark II. The GT Mark IV was built according to changes in Article J of the FIA vehicle regulation.

The new car possessed an aluminum honeycomb chassis, which replaced the previous car's steel monocoque one. The profile of the car was characterized by its long, low body that curved from the center section to the rear end. The side air intakes utilized NACA ducts for less drag. The car was subjected to intense wind tunnel testing, and as a result, the Mark IV was one of the most aerodynamically-proficient vehicles in the world.

Although the Mark IV's engine was carried over from the Mark II, its power was increased to <530ps>. The chassis was also updated. The result was a race car with an improved top speed of <347km/h> and a better overall stability than its predecessor. In 1967, the Mark IV won the 12 Hours of Sebring and claimed the checkered flag at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, beating its rival, Ferrari, by five laps. This victory marked the last time the Ford works team participated at Le Mans. The main reason for its departure was the adoption of a new rule in 1968 that restricted maximum displacement, which seemed directly aimed at the Ford GT because, simply put, the car was too fast for the competition.A
DescriptionLong.0x000049F2:
The Mitsubishi GTO was sold as the 3000GT outside Japan.

Introduced in October 1990, the GTO represented a bold statement from Mitsubishi, which hadn’t produced a flagship sports car in years. The name GTO, of course, paid homage to the legendary Galant GTO. Simply giving this new sports car that name signaled just how high expectations were within the company.

The styling was classic Mitsubishi of the era—bold, muscular, and clearly tailored to appeal to the U.S. market’s tastes. When viewed from above, the car’s distinctive bottle shape—narrowing noticeably at the doors—was striking. It was a design that turned plenty of heads back in the day.

But this car wasn’t just about looks. Beneath its exterior was a host of technical features that showcased the company's engineering prowess. The chassis was built around Mitsubishi’s cutting-edge All-Wheel Control philosophy—a key focus for the brand at the time. It boasted an impressive suite of advanced features, including full-time 4WD, 4-wheel steering (4WS), electronically controlled suspension, and ABS. It was also equipped with an active aerodynamics system in which the front and rear spoilers self-adjusted according to speed, and it possessed an active exhaust system that controlled exhaust sound. The GTO’s array of high-tech systems—combining electronic controls with variable, adaptive mechanisms—further added to its uniqueness.

The platform was based on the Diamante. Transversely mounted in front was the 6G72, a 3.0-liter DOHC V-6 offered in two grades: a potent twin-turbo or a naturally-aspirated variant. The turbocharged version unleashed <280ps> and <42.5kgm> of torque, while the naturally-aspirated one produced <225ps> and <28.0kgm>.`
DescriptionLong.0x000049F4:
This new Nissan GT-R was announced at the New York International Auto Show in April 2016, amid a fury of anticipation and hype. As the most significantly changed model since its introduction in 2007, the new R35 GT-R didn’t disappoint.

Changes to the car’s design was not only intended to make the car look better, but also designed to enhance its aerodynamic performance. The new, larger Vmotion grille highlighted the new freshened face, while a new lower, rigid hood resisted deformation at high speeds. The fenders and front bumpers were reshaped to provide more downforce.

The GT-R remained a monster when it came to performance. The engine, which was still built by hand by master craftsmen, had more power than before, with 565 HP at <6800rpm> and a maximum torque of 467 ft-lb on tap. Combined with an improved 6-speed dual-clutch transmission, the new GT-R was quicker and more responsive than the previous model in the mid-rpm ranges. Of course, to be considered the world’s best handling car, the cornering performance has also been improved.

With pavement-sticking all-wheel-drive handling, the new GT-R now wreaked havoc in a custom-tailored suit.

DescriptionLong.0x000049F7:
In the spring of 2014, Nissan Motor Company announced that it would enter the LPM1 hybrid class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans the following year with a race car wearing a GT-R badge. It would mark the return of "the Nissan prototype race car" after a 16-year hiatus—since the R391 in 1999. As if that wasn't newsworthy enough, Nissan revealed at the car's introduction in February 2015 that its new race machine, called the GT-R LM NISMO, possessed a front-engine/front-wheel-drive layout, a concept previously unheard of in prototype race cars.

The mastermind behind the GT-R LM NISMO is none other than Ben Bowlby, the man who created the DeltaWing and ZEOD RC race cars. By mounting the engine in the front, Bowlby claims that it opened up new design possibilities to maximize aerodynamics, thus making the car more efficient at higher speeds.

The body consists of a monocoque chassis and outer panels made of carbon fiber, allowing the car to tip the scales at a light <880kg>. Under the long front nose is a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter direct injection V-6 mated to an energy-recovery system.

The drivers of the car include homegrown talents, Michael Krumm and Tsugio Matsuda; GT Academy graduates Lucas Ordóñez and Jann Mardenborough; former F1 drivers Marc Gené and Max Chilton; and sports car drivers Alex Buncombe, Harry Tincknell and Olivier Pla.

Nissan will run two cars starting from the first round of the FIA World Endurance Championships, and enter three cars in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, with the sole purpose of grabbing the overall title._
DescriptionLong.0x000049F8:
The GT-R NISMO was introduced in 2014 as the high-performance version of the R35 GT-R. It delighted Japanese sports-car enthusiasts as soon as it appeared and remained unchanged until the summer of 2016 when an updated model finally arrived.

The 2017 GT-R NISMO featured structural adhesives that improved body rigidity. Under the hood, new GT3 turbines were added and the engine was slightly tuned, but output was kept at <600ps>/<66.5kgm>. While still a menacing handling machine, the new GT-R felt more civil on public roads, thanks to the Damp Tronic ECU incorporated into the car's suspension.

At first glance, the new GT-R looked similar to the outgoing model, but in fact, major improvements were made to the car's aerodynamics. The addition of rear spoiler and a front under spoiler and bumper with canard shaped fins on both sides resulted in <100kg> more downforce than the standard GT-R at <300km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x000049F9:
In 2012, Nissan introduced the GT-R NISMO GT3 into GT3 racing, a category that has now become the mainstay of GT races. Schulze Motorsport is a private team that fielded this car in the German ADAC GT Masters series.

In 2013, Gran Turismo game producer Kazunori Yamauchi collaborated with Schulze Motorsport for a fourth attempt at the 24 Hours of Nürburgring. The GT-R NISMO GT3 was updated to 2013 specs, and Polyphony Digital set up the car specifically for the Nürburgring using the simulation technology of Gran Turismo. In addition to Yamauchi, drivers taking the wheel included the two Schulze brothers, Tobias and Michael, as well as professional racer Michael Krumm.

Appearing like the production GT-R at first glance, the race car was converted from AWD to rear drive to meet FIA GT3 regulations. Fenders were widened to fit larger tires, and weight was reduced to <1300kg>. Engine output, brake performance, and aerodynamics were also upgraded. In qualifying for the 2013 race, car number 123 recorded the top time, a first for a Japanese car at the Nürburgring, but on race day, the team was plagued by a combination of red flags and mechanical problems. In the end, the 123 GT-R did not have a chance to show its full potential. There was a silver lining; however, the driving data gained from this racing effort significantly advanced the simulation engine of Gran Turismo.X

DescriptionLong.0x000049FB:
A new driving experience has been created through a collaboration between the Honda design team and Gran Turismo. What makes this possible is the Honda Project 2&4 powered by RC213V.

At the heart of this car that was born from a design competition project involving Honda’s 2-wheel and 4-wheel divisions, is a V-4 motorcycle engine. Thus, the car is a new form of fun mobility that combines the openness and agility of a motorbike with the dynamic performance of a 4-wheeled vehicle.

The working theme of the car's development was "'Exposure," and indeed, drivers of the vehicle can feel the sun and wind all around them, giving them an incredible sense of freedom.

Perhaps the most noteworthy element of the Honda Project 2&4 is the structure, which is a fusion of 2- and 4-wheeled vehicles powered by a motorcycle engine that's mounted amidships on an aluminum carbon composite backbone frame.

The combination of the <999cc> V4 engine producing <215ps> and the car's low <405kg> curb weight results in an incredible weight-to-power ratio of <1.88kg/ps>. The rear wheels are driven through a 6-speed DCT controlled with paddle shifters on the steering wheel. If you remove the assistant side body cowling it is also possible to add a passenger seat that makes it a two-seater.
DescriptionLong.0x000049FC:
The "Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo" midship-engined 2-seater coupe was born from a collaboration between the Honda design team and Gran Turismo.

This is a true sports model that takes to heart the Honda corporate spirit of "doing it because it's fascinating," and pursues the fun of driving as well as authentic realism befitting the "real driving simulator," Gran Turismo.

The "Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo" was the winner of the global design competition. For further design refinements after the competition, designers from both Japan and the US had their input in the process, with each applying their own unique strengths into project. The design progressed globally, with the quarter model built in the US, and the modeling data and hardware decisions made in Japan. Staff from each region were closely connected in the process, and the designers enjoyed participating in the project.

The "Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo" brings to life the design direction of Honda, "Human Centered Design". This is a human-centric way of thinking that is brought to life in the package design, where the position of the passengers, engine, and tires determines the shape of the car’s structure. The proportions of the car that makes it look as though it is about to propel itself forward, the clean cut body and the powerful front and rear fenders that spreads wide with air intakes, and wheels that combine function and beauty; all these things that are expected of a sports car, are expressed in the strong sense of presence emitted by the car.

Carbon fiber is utilized in many parts of the body, achieving a weight of just <899kg>. The <1998cc> engine is mounted midship, and combined with an L4 turbo and DOHC-VTEC, it produces <410ps> at <7500rpm>. This power is then efficiently transferred to the road through an 8-speed dual clutch transmission.

The aerodynamics simulations for the car of course involved wind tunnel testing, as it would be for a real life car. Through this process, the flow and exhaust of air passing through the body, underfloor, cabin, and engine room have been fully optimized.

The "Honda Sports Vision Gran Turismo" is a car that exemplifies Honda's "Power of Dreams," and is a car that we believe is a true to life machine that can be enjoyed by many.
DescriptionLong.0x000049FD:
Argentine businessman Horacio Pagani's background as a designer worked in his favor when he established Pagani Automobili in Modena, Italy, and then, in 1999, announced the company's first supercar. After all, this is a man who worked on the Lamborghini Countach 25th Anniversary.

His first model, the Zonda, was developed with another famous Argentine, legendary race car driver Juan Manuel Fangio, who served as an adviser. The car focused purely on driving performance. It was an extremely expensive and limited-production model, but it certainly proved its mettle on the track, even recording the fastest lap time at the world-famous Nürburgring in Germany up to that point. Highly regarded by many, it sold out immediately.

The Zonda's successor, the Huayra, made its debut in 2011. It was produced with a newly developed monocoque frame, combining carbon and titanium, and incorporated the gullwing doors that were carried over from the Zonda. However, in contrast to the sharp, edgy styling of the Zonda, the Huayra instead adopted beautiful, flowing lines. It was a vehicle that married high quality craftsmanship with top tier supercar performance; the mostly carbon-fiber body encased a luxurious interior, which combined leather, aluminum and carbon. In terms of aerodynamics, the four variable flaps in the front and rear of the car automatically adjusted downforce, while also serving as air brakes.

Under its hood was the same 6.0-liter, hand-built AMG V12 of the Zonda, but twin-turbochargers were added for more power. The Huayra produced <700ps> and <102kgm> torque, and was combined with a 7-speed sequential transmission. With a 0 to <100km/h> acceleration of 3.2 seconds and a top speed of <378km/h>, it was one of the fastest cars ever built.Q
DescriptionLong.0x000049FE:
The Lamborghini Huracán GT3 is the race version of the Huracán that was released as a successor to the Gallardo in 2014. It was developed according to FIA-GT3 specifications as the name implies, and was revealed for the first time in January 2015.

The development of the Gallardo was handled by Reiter Engineering, but the Huracán GT3 is developed by Squadra Corse, the internal competition department of Lamborghini. Italian race constructor Dallara engineering worked on the materials and aerodynamics of the body.

The hybrid chassis made from aluminum and carbon is the same as in the road car, but the body itself is much wider. Its aerodynamic effects are improved using a low front spoiler and splitter, an adjustable rear wing, and a large rear diffuser. These are in addition to the vents and louvers added on various parts to discharge and improve air flow. These additions have a side effect of giving the car a much more aggressive appearance than the road car.

The engine is also the same 5.2L V10 as in the road car, but the ECU is changed to a Bosch unit to make it more suited for actual operation in competition. The gearbox is changed from a 7 speed DCT to a 6 speed sequential, and to match the regulations, the drive train is modified from an all wheel drive to be a rear wheel drive. There are also 10 level settings for the traction control system and ABS.

The Huracán achieved a debut victory at the opening round of the 2015 Blancpain Endurance Series, but in addition to that win, it also achieved pole position in 3 rounds out of 5, and continued to show stable and fast performance throughout the series.'
DescriptionLong.0x000049FF:
Introduced at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show, the Huracán had big shoes to fill as it was labeled the successor to Lamborghini’s most successful model ever, the Gallardo.

Unlike Lamborghini models that came before it, the Gallardo, which enjoyed a successful 10-year run, possessed a compact body that made it more agile than past Lambos. Although slightly larger, the Huracán sported similar proportions, retaining the “agile” spirit that made the Gallardo so popular. That said, its styling theme inside and out was nothing like that of its predecessor. The Huracán’s exterior was simpler and neater, with more curves than the Gallardo, signaling a new design phase for the coach builder from Sant’Agata.

The structure of the car also evolved, from the Gallardo’s aluminum space frame to one composed of aluminum and carbon fiber. This resulted in a 10 percent lighter body with a 50 percent increase in rigidity. The engine, a fire-breathing 5.2-liter V-10 that produced <610ps> and <57.1kgm> of torque, came mounted amidships, and came mated to Lamborghini’s first 7-speed dual clutch gearbox.

Also, a new integrated drive control system called ANIMA was added to instantly switch the engine, transmission, the new Halidex 5 AWD system and handling characteristics from urban driving to hot laps on a race track. When unleashed, the Huracán could run from 0-<100km/h> in 3.2 seconds and hit a top speed of <325km/h>. With performance like that, no one dared to call this compact exotic car a “baby Lambo.”F

DescriptionLong.0x00004A01:
The HYUNDAI N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo was designed to embody the passion and spirit of "N," Hyundai’s high-performance sub-brand, in celebration of the company’s 50th anniversary in 2017. This exhilarating concept provides a glimpse into the company's future high-performance vehicles, highlighting the philosophy of "N," which delivers "the most thrilling winding road fun." 

While hybrid powertrains dominate today’s performance landscape, the N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo introduces a groundbreaking alternative—one poised to become the next major innovation in the automotive industry: the hydrogen fuel cell system. This cutting-edge system gives the concept sports car both eco-conscious efficiency and track-ready performance. With instant torque delivery, it transforms into an impressive cornering machine. 

While the high-performance fuel cell system was developed at the Namyang R&D Center—Hyundai Motors’ main engineering facility—the staff at Hyundai’s American Design Center took this cutting-edge technology and transformed it into a formidable powerplant, one that delivers the high performance worthy of the "N" badge. Also, Hyundai Motors’ Sound Design Research Lab developed a one-of-a-kind FCEV sport sound system, enhancing the emotional engagement of this high-spirited yet eco-friendly model. Equipped with this innovative technology, the N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo is a bold glimpse into Hyundai Motors’ high-performance future.

The N 2025’s powertrain is based on the world’s first mass-produced Hyundai hydrogen fuel cell from 2013. Its total output is 650 kW (<883ps>). The dual fuel cell stacks produce 500 kW (<680ps>), while the supercapacitor system adds another 150 kW (<204ps>) by harnessing regenerated energy during braking.
