DescriptionLong.0x00004A03:
BMW established the "i" line specifically to market its alternative-energy vehicles, including EVs and plug-in hybrids. The first example to be offered by the German company with the "i" designation was the i3 in 2013.

In a word, the i3's styling is futuristic, complete with a unique shape and clamshell doors. The car is just under <4m> in length, <1.8m> width, <1.6m> height, and weighs a mere <1195kg>, which is a testament to the engineers who made it a priority to keep the car's curb weight down. They accomplished this by extensively using carbon-fiber in the cabin and incorporating as much aluminum as possible in the chassis. The lithium-ion batteries are placed at the center of the vehicle to optimize handling balance.

The motor produces <170ps> and <25.5kgm> of torque, sending power to the rear wheels. The i3 runs from zero to <60km/h> in just 3.7 and to <100km/h> in 7.2 seconds. Top speed is rated at more than <150km/h>. Because electric motors can deliver peak torque instantaneously, the i3 feels like a supercar when you launch it from a standstill.

At full charge, the i3 possesses a <160km> range, and on the ECO PRO mode with minimal air conditioning and other power saving tricks, it can go up to <200km>. For those who may suffer from range anxiety, a 647cc 2-cylinder gasoline engine can extend the i3's driving range to a maximum of <300km>./
DescriptionLong.0x00004A04:
In March 1998, Subaru introduced the Version 22B-STi, based on the Impreza WRX STi Version IV. The “22” in its name signified the size of the engine, which came in the form of a turbocharged 2.2-liter flat-4. With a larger turbo, this boxer pumped out <280 ps> and <37.0 kgm> of torque, making it as fast as many European sports cars costing twice as much. The car’s biggest draw was its styling that featured wide-body fenders, making it look very similar to the WRC race car. The 22B’s production was limited to 400 units, but all of them were snatched up in a matter of months, despite a price tag of 5 million yen or about $50,000.

Not long after the 22B, Subaru took the covers off the STi Version V in September 1998. In addition to new aerodynamic parts on the exterior, the new STi received a new sport ABS to help stopping power.

In September 1999, the STi Version VI appeared featuring only modest changes that included a new front under spoiler, a reshaped rear spoiler and redesigned 16-in. alloy wheels. The competition model, the RA, came complete with mirror shells on the doors and sheeted rear quarter panels, designed to save weight. The STi Version VI marked the end of the GC-platform. What made this car especially noteworthy was that in its eight-year span, the WRX’s body style stayed generally constant, staying true to the original.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A05:
The Impreza WRX STi was first introduced in 1994 with the goal of winning the World Rally Chanpionships. Known as "GC8," which referred to its in-house chassis designation, the car met with success both on and off the track. In September 1999, the very last GC8, the WRX STi Version VI, made its debut.

Thanks to numerous improvements in the six years since the the GC8's debut, the engine's (EJ20) horsepower rating went from <250ps> to <280ps>, while the transmission, which was always considered a weak point of the car, was enhanced for quicker, more precise shifts and better durability. Aerodynamics, brakes and suspension were significantly upgraded, all maximizing the incredible potential of the GC8 chassis.

Of the three body types available for the Version VI, which included a sedan and station wagon, the most notable was the "Type R" coupe. Along with a rally-car styled exterior, it featured a driver-controlled central differential, an intercooler water sprayer, specially-tuned suspension system and an upgraded rear axle as standard equipment. The car was a virtual road rocket, weighing only <1260kg>, making it a fan favorite on the WRC circuit as well as a popular performance choice for enthusiasts. z
DescriptionLong.0x00004A06:
Infiniti made a big splash when it entered the luxury market in 1989. Its distinctive cutting-edge styling won it fans immediately, with vehicles such as the Q45, the G sedan/G coupe and the FX SUV. The brand continues to push the design envelope today, with products that include the Q50 and QX70.  

The Infiniti Concept Vision Gran Turismo is a project that started as an ambitious global competition to "design a pure Infiniti GT car." In the end, the winning entry was submitted by Infiniti Design Beijing. Part beauty and part beast, the car's powerful and sensual shape suggested that it was made for the track, something that the Chinese design team wanted to express.

The process of creating the design for the Infiniti Concept Vision Gran Turismo started with a simple sketch that was then refined digitally. After this process, the image was sculpted into a 3D model, and then further refined digitally once again. One of the designers said that his vision and inspiration was to capture the rise of the young generation and the essence of Asian creativity that always sought to break new ground. This desire to consistently be on the very edge of possibilities may one day result in this GT car taking on a real track. 

Needless to say, this project went beyond a mere design study and involved thorough examination of aerodynamic and engine performance. Power comes via a hybrid drivetrain. A naturally aspirated 4.5-liter V-8 gasoline engine, mounted aft of the front axle line, is mated to a transaxle. Also providing power is an electric motor, which provides a high level of instant torque. The use of a transaxle allows for an ideal front/rear weight distribution of 44/55, allowing you to drift the car when the need arises. Engineers with a high level of driving skill drove many virtual laps in this car to get the balance just right. As for aerodynamics, the underfloor airflow control, front and rear diffusers, and uniquely shaped rear spoiler enable this car to demonstrate high performance without compromising body design. In short, this is car that drives as good as it looks.q
DescriptionLong.0x00004A07:
The legend of the "Type R," which was designated to the highest-performance Honda vehicles began in 1992 with the NSX Type R; however, Honda decided to bring the brand to the masses by creating a lower-priced version, which came in the form of the Integra Type R in 1995.

The engine was based on the 1.8-liter B18 VTEC equipped in the Si. Redline and engine compression was increased using high-compression piston heads, high-strength connecting rods, and dual-valve springs. Each engine was assembled by hand, and what a piece of work it was. It produced <200ps>, which equals <111ps> per liter of displacement. The body was reinforced and, despite the use of heavy parts such as performance rods and a helical LSD, the car weighed <40kg> less, thanks to a smaller battery, the lack of soundproofing material, and lightweight aluminum wheels. The suspension was retuned for sharper handling, minimizing the car's tendency to understeer. 

When it was released to the market, this Integra Type R became the golden standard of high-performance front-wheel drive-cars.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A08:
The Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo has been developed from the ground up as a pure, all-electric race car that celebrates the beautiful designs from Jaguar’s illustrious racing heritage while providing an exciting glimpse into the future of Jaguar design and technology.

The state-of-the-art powertrain features powerful, light, compact electric motors and a lithium-ion battery pack developed from the race-proven technologies used in the Jaguar I-TYPE 4 Formula E car and the world’s first production battery electric vehicle race series – the Jaguar I-PACE eTROPHY championship.

Proportion is fundamental to the design of every Jaguar, and to enable the dramatic form of the Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo, the battery modules are packaged around the cockpit, contributing to the low center of gravity and near-perfect weight distribution.

Inspiration for the cockpit of the Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo, was drawn from the true icons in Jaguar’s rich racing bloodline: cars such as the revered C-, D-, and E-Type. Fused with a contemporary, driver-focused interior philosophy of pure, beautiful and intricate details, creating an ideal balance between analog and digital. Access via a powered roof hatch enriches the driver experience still further.

The car’s architecture is lightweight, simple, and dramatic, and is crafted from advanced and experimental materials and finishes. Sitting down low in the cockpit, the driver will feel enveloped by the car – echoing the feel of the three-time Le Mans-winning D-Type.

The perfectly-weighted controls, essential information displayed precisely in the driver's eye line, and a virtually seamless view of the road combine to deliver a precision racing experience. Features such as hologram technology add a further flourish. Looking out over the gracefully long bonnet of the Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo – a view that is unmistakably Jaguar – the player is fully immersed in the action.

Designed exclusively for Gran Turismo by Jaguar Advanced Design, players are taken on a journey into the future along with the designers for a purely digital yet visceral experience that will truly capture the imagination.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A09:
This GT-R, added to the Skyline (C10) line on February 1969, kick-started the glorious history of the brand, a few years after Nissan had taken over Prince Motors.

The car has since become a classic, going by the nickname "Hako-suka," which in Japanese means "box" and a shortened form of Skyline (suka-i-ra-in)," an obvious reference to its boxy overall body style.

Equipped with the S20 engine, a twin-cam inline-6 that was lifted from the famed R380 race car, the sporty GT-R model was made primarily for competition.

In fact, it was said that only the most skilled technician could perfectly adjust the high-tech valves and three carburetors to maximize the engine's potential. When it was tuned just right, the S20 had few equals, allowing the C10 Skyline GT-R to leave most of its rivals in the dust. The car also possessed excellent handling, thanks to its stable suspension system, with struts up front and a semi-trailing arm setup at rear.

The race version of the car was as dominant as there ever was. With famous drivers such as Moto Kitano and Kunimitsu Takahashi behind the wheel, the competition GT-R racked up 50 consecutive wins, making it one of the most successful race cars in history.C
DescriptionLong.0x00004A0A:
When Ferrari creates a “limited edition” model, the result is often something historic. In the past, now-legendary models such as the 288, GTO, F40, F50, and the Enzo Ferrari have rocked the exotic-car world, but the latest special-edition car from the revered marque will definitely go down in the annals of automotive history as the most special of them all: the LaFerrari.

In the same manner as its predecessors, the LaFerrari, introduced in 2013, represents grace, glamor and unprecedented performance, but two things in particular make this machine special. One of them is its carbon monocoque structure that’s composed of the same materials as Ferrari’s F1 machines, and built using the same processes. In comparison to the Enzo Ferrari, torsional rigidity of the LaFerrari is better by 27 percent, while beam rigidity has been improved by 22 percent. The car's other special feature is its hybrid drivetrain, a first for Ferrari. The 6.3-liter V-12 is tuned to <800ps> and matched to Ferrari’s HY-KERS system from F1 racing. The total output with the added <163ps> provided by the electric motor is rated at a whopping <963ps>, the most from any Ferrari road car…ever.

Also, the LaFerrari features an aerodynamics system that produces optimum performance by actively moving the front/rear diffusers, spoilers, and underbody in relation to driving conditions.

The performance specs include a 0-<100km/h> acceleration of less than 3 seconds, 0-<200km/h> acceleration of under 7, and a top speed of more than <350km/h>. At the Fiorano test track, the LaFerrari’s 1-minute-19.9-second lap was 5 seconds faster than the Ferrari Enzo and 3.1 seconds faster than the F12.

The production run of the LaFerrari was a mere 499 cars, and naturally, all of them have been spoken for, not surprising when you consider that there were more than 1000 inquiries to buy the super exotic three days after it was introduced.q
DescriptionLong.0x00004A0B:
April 10, 2015 marked the end of a legend when the final Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution was announced. All 1000 cars were sold out by August 20 of the same year.

The Final Edition Lancer Evo was based on the GSR with plenty of changes made throughout the vehicle to make it special. The power of the Evo's high-strung turbocharged 4-cylinder was raised to make an additional <13ps> and <0.7kgm> of torque to bring the total to <313ps> and <43.7kgm>. The High Performance Package included Bilstein dampers, Eibach springs and high-performance tires that came wrapped around 18-inch BBS dark aluminum wheels. The interior was highlighted by full bucket Recaro seats.

The Final Edition is basically another performance version of the Lancer Evolution X, but you won’t see the Roman numeral anywhere on its body. That’s because there will not be any more Evos after this model (no XI). Since its debut as a homologation model for a WRC race car in 1992, the Evo has been an icon for rally and performance enthusiasts all over the world, and it’s indeed sad to see this wonderful car go.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A10:
The Lancer Evolution took a major leap forward in August 1996, with the Evo IV. It completely redefined the model, starting with the 4G63 powerplant, which was flipped around 180 degrees in the engine bay and output was raised to <280ps> and <36.0kgm> of torque. But perhaps the noteworthy change was the introduction of the electronically-controlled AYC (Active Yaw Control) that replaced the mechanical LSD of previous models.

Building on the success of the Evo IV, the Evo V appeared in January 1998 with a slightly enlarged body to meet WRC specifications. The Evo V had more torque than its predecessor, rated to <38.0kgm>, and came with a new helical LSD for the front differential.

In January 1999, Mitsubishi introduced the Evo VI. While the car looked basically the same as the Evo V, there were significant differences under the sheet metal, including a refined engine and re-tuned suspension system. In January 2000, the first anniversary model was offered, as well as another special model that commemorated Tommi Makinen's four consecutive WRC championships. This special-edition model, limited to only 2500 units, featured a large front spoiler, a revised suspension stroke and quicker steering, among other things. It proved to be the final and ultimate example of the truly ground-breaking second-generation Lancer Evolution.*

DescriptionLong.0x00004A12:
In commemoration of Tommi Makinen's achievement of Drivers' Champion 4 years running from 1996 to 1999, The Lancer Evolution T.M. EDITION was sold in a limited run of 2500 cars. The model code was GFCP9A, and is sometimes nicknamed the Lancer Evo 6.5.

Compared to the Evo V, the Evo VI introduced in the beginning of the same year had a softer ride, due to the unpopularity of the previous suspension that was considered too hard for driving in the city. In addition, the front bumper shape had been revised for aerodynamic and cooling performance. The T.M. EDITION on the other hand was created in the image of a tarmac rally setup, and was equipped with a front bumper that omits fog lights for even better aerodynamics, and the harder suspension from the EVO V further lowered by another <10mm>. The steering gear ratio is also slightly quicker in this model.

By utilizing a titanium-aluminum alloy turbine and smaller compressors, its maximum torque of <38.0kgm> is produced earlier at <2750rpm>, rather than the usual <3000rpm>. It is also given red Recaro seats with a stitched TOMMI MAKINEN logo, special red meters, the same Enkei spoke wheels as the rally car, and a large exhaust muffler with a circular exit, rather than the original elliptical one.

The promotional image color of the body was red, and it was possible to select a special color package which had a black stripe running from the front fenders to the body sides.

This Evo was popular as a model that was further perfected, worthy to be crowned with the name of the undefeated WRC champion.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A13:
Introduced at the 2016 Geneva Auto Show, the LC500 luxury sports coupe represented the first F-segment model for Lexus.

The styling is nearly unchanged from the LF-FC concept vehicle revealed in 2012, which was penned at Lexus’ design studio in California. Its flowing lines and low hood give the LC500 a wind-cutting shape, and it features short front and rear overhangs that allow the engine to be placed aft of the front wheels, giving it a front mid-engine layout.

The LC500 was built on the newly developed GA-L platform. The body is composed of a combination of materials that include carbon fiber, aluminum and steel, which gives the sports coupe a highly-rigid yet lightweight character.

Under the hood is the same 5.0-liter naturally-aspirated V-8 found in the RC F and GS F that produces <477ps> and <55.1kgm> of torque. The engine comes mated to the first direct-shift 10-speed automatic transmission to be equipped on a passenger car.

The LC500 race car dominated its debut appearance in the GT500 class of the Super GT series in 2017, taking 1st to 6th place.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A14:
Already considered a classic among enthusiasts today, this compact car has become a favorite for drifters and has been featured in movies and comic books. The car has its roots from the Corolla/Sprinter, but when this model changed its layout to FF (front engine/front drive), the sporty version in the lineup, the AE86 or Corolla Levin/Sprinter Trueno, remained as a rear-wheel driver.

The "86" (or Hachi-Roku, as it was called in Japan) developed an immediate following because of its rear-drive layout, lightweight, excellent handling and affordable price tag. It came in two shapes: a 3-door hatchback and a 2-door notchback. The main difference between the Corolla Levin and Sprinter Trueno was the front end, where the former featured a horizontal grille and fixed headlights and the latter no grille and retractable headlights.

Providing power was the newly developed 4A-GEU, a 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4. This engine featured some of the day's most advanced technology, including EFI-D (Electronic Fuel Injection-Druck), which calculated fuel amount through a pressure sensor, and the T-VIS (Toyota Variable Injection System). This helped the 4-cylinder to produce <130ps> and <15.2kgm> of torque.

It revved freely and quick, and demonstrated excellent throttle response, making the car wonderfully controllable through tricky corners. The suspension, body and engine worked harmoniously together to provide real sports car attributes. It was this performance and personality that made the "86" loved by so many.M
DescriptionLong.0x00004A15:
For Lexus, the 2014 Super GT GT500 class was a historic season in which they fought hard for the class title until the very last race. And in 2015, Lexus added a new page to their ultimate challenge in the top category: They are planning an introduction of a car into the GT3 class, a class that is a gentlemen’s race but at the same time the ultimate international manufacturers’ championship. This comes from the hope of Lexus to fulfill the desires of gentlemen racers; to participate together with them in world class races in the car of their dreams.

With this background of Lexus’ involvement in racing, the LEXUS LF-LC GT “Vision Gran Turismo” was developed in reply to the passions of Gran Turismo fans, to compete in world class races with their dream car. The design and development of the car targets entry in races such as the Super GT and the Nürburgring 24 hour race.

For Lexus, the 2014 Super GT GT500 season was one to remember because it took home the championship in the very last race. In 2015, Lexus entered the GT3 racing class, where it battled in the world's foremost international championships.

The brand's amazing success in motorsports paved the way for the creation of the Lexus LF-LC GT “Vision Gran Turismo.” With this machine, Gran Turismo players were able to compete virtually in various world-class races in what can be called the quintessential gentleman's race car. 

The LF-LC GT "Vision Gran Turismo" is based on the LF-LC concept vehicle, which was shown at the 2012 North American International Auto Show and created by Calty Design Research. Thus, the LF-LC GT “Vision Gran Turismo” is a grand tourer that possesses both sculptured beauty and the highest levels of performance, with real world elements provided by Calty blended with the on-road prowess of Lexus Racing.  

Born from a passion for racing, the Lexus LF-LC GT “Vision Gran Turismo” is a car meant to probe the potentials of the ultimate Lexus race car._
DescriptionLong.0x00004A16:
In 2000, BMW redefined its super sports coupe, the M3, by placing a 3.2-liter DOHC inline-6 under its hood. Based on the E46 3 Series that underwent a full model change in 1998, the new M3 pumped out a fierce <343ps> at <7900rpm> and a hearty <37.2kgm> of torque at <4900rpm>. This meant that this amazing machine achieved more than <#100ps> per liter when the engine spun to its <7900rpm> redline. What really brought the motor to life was the M3’s new gearbox. Initially, it came equipped with a Getrag 6-speed manual, but later BMW added the SMG II, the company’s prize two-pedal (twin-clutch) semi-automatic transmission.

In developing the new M3’s chassis, BMW followed its credo of “the suspension must always be faster than the engine.” BMW engineers took the base E46 chassis and solidified each section, giving the car rock-solid stability throughout. The suspension was retuned to compensate for the M3’s added power.

In 2003, a lightweight version of this coupe was introduced, boasting even more performance than the base car, thanks mainly to a leaner body. The M3CSL tipped the scales at <1400kg>, about <100kg> less than the base model with the inline-6 pumping out <360ps> at <7900rpm> and <37.8kgm> of torque at <4900rpm>._
DescriptionLong.0x00004A17:
The M3 has represented the top-of-the-line model in BMW's popular 3-Series lineup since the very beginning. The car's performance is tuned by the company's M division, which specializes in taking stock BMW cars and making them virtually race ready. With the M3, tweaks have traditionally been performed on the engine, suspension and aerodynamic parts. The history of the M brand dates back to 1985, and the car represented here is the fourth-generation M3, based on the latest 3-Series Coupe, the E92.

The E92 M3 measured <4620mm> long, <1805mm> wide and <1425mm> high, and rode on a wheelbase of <2760mm>. Several years ago, the M3's engine evolved from a 4-cylinder unit to a 6-cylinder in order to keep up with the growing engine power of other performance cars, especially those that competed in touring car races. For this model, BMW took things even further by mounting a <420ps> 4-liter V8 under the hood.

The car's dimensions were larger than the previous model, but this M3 was lighter, thanks to a high-strength carbon-fiber roof, which helped in lowering the car's center of gravity, and aluminum for the suspension parts to reduce weight. As a result, the M3 tipped the scales at a lean <1630kg>.

Despite being created for the company's motorsports activities, the M3 came laden with the latest technology, including a 7-speed M DCT with Drivelogic (double clutch transmission), Variable M differential lock and M Dynamic Mode. /
DescriptionLong.0x00004A18:
While the first-generation BMW M3 (E30) was a special model created specifically to pass homologation requirements for Group A touring cars, from the second-generation and on, they were sold solely as high-performance models of the 3 Series. For the fourth-generation model (E92), two racing M3s that conformed to GT4 and GT2 FIA regulations were introduced. The GT2 car (which allowed more modifications), called the "M3 GT2," was the fastest M3 ever developed to date.

The street version of the E92 M3 was slightly larger than the previous model (E46) and <80kg> heavier at <1630kg>. To counteract the extra weight, BMW swapped the old M3 engine, a 3.2-liter inline-6, to a 4.0-liter V-8, which increased power output from <343ps> to a whopping <420ps>.

Using this car as the foundation, the M3 GT2 added carbon-fiber body parts, including the front and rear fenders, hood, trunk lid, and both bumpers, allowing the race-ready car to tip the scales at a lean <1245kg>. The GT2 is also <110mm> wider, and with a revised front bumper that incorporates air dams for better ventilation and intake, not to mention the addition of a large rear wing, the car possesses greatly improved aerodynamics. As for the engine, with a <30.1mm> restrictor installed, it produces more than <500ps> and <50kgm> of torque.

BMW entered this car in the ALMS and ILMC series in the 2010 race season. The car dominated the GT Class of the ALMS, and achieved overall victories at the Nürburgring 24 hour race as well as the ILMC Zhuhai 1000km.J
DescriptionLong.0x00004A19:
The first BMW M3 appeared in 1985, and it represented a high-performance version of the popular 3 Series (E30) that could also be used for touring car racing.

At first, the M3 only came in 2-door form, with wider treads and sporty fender flares. Also, front and rear spoilers were added, aggressive side skirts were installed and the angle of the C-pillar and rear window were revised to create a car that looked much meaner than the stock 3 Series. These body modifications also resulted in a better Cd of 0.38 (from 0.33). Under the hood was a special 2.3-liter DOHC inline-4 that produced <195ps> and <23.4kgm> of torque.

The race-spec model was introduced in 1987. From the onset, it dominated the DTM, winning five of the first 10 races. That same year, the M3 Evolution was released with even better aerodynamics and a <210ps> engine. In 1988, output was increased to <220ps> for the M3 Evolution II. In 1989 the final model of the E30 M3, called the M3 Sports Evolution, appeared, equipped with a larger engine (2.5 liters) that produced <238ps>/<24.5kgm>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A1A:
In the summer of 2013, BMW established the new “4 Series” line to separate the 2-door offerings of the 3 Series from the 4-doors. This meant that the extremely performance-minded M3 coupe now went by the name, M4.

While the name had changed, the spirit of the M3 was left totally intact. The M4’s exterior featured a menacing face with large air inlets in the front bumpers and a flowing roofline that hinted at the car’s awesome performance. When seen from its profile, the M4 is visually characterized by traditional BMW proportions—a sleek hood, long wheelbase and short front overhang. The characteristic M gill incorporated the Air Breather, which together with the Air Curtain within the front apron, served to ventilate the wheel arches and facilitate better airflow values.

Underneath the aluminum hood of the M4 was the M TwinPower Turbo engine. This turbocharged inline-6 produced <431ps>, which allowed the lean <1497kg>-car to go from zero to <100km/h> in just 4.1 seconds. Also, the combination of the active M differential, the adaptive M suspension, and the M specific DSC ensured that the M4 retained the handling prowess expected of all cars that wore the M badge.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A1B:
In the summer of 2013, BMW shuffled its lineup by placing the 3 Series coupe and convertible under the new 4 Series umbrella. This meant that the BMW M3 coupe was now known as the M4. Despite the name change, the car was still the same high-performance machine as before.

Underneath the aluminum hood with the slight bulge resided a twin-turbocharged inline-6 that allowed the car to run from zero to <100km/h> in just 4.1 seconds. This was possible, in part, because of the M4’s remarkably low curb weight of <1497kg>, which set new standards in its class. The M4’s lightweight nature also contributed to its agility, as did the car’s active M differential, adaptive M suspension, and the M specific DSC.

The M4 could be distinguished from other 4 Series models by its large air inlets in the front and the race-inspired low rear end. The characteristic M gill incorporated the Air Breather, which together with the Air Curtain within the front apron served to ventilate the wheel arches and facilitate better airflow. The rest of the M4’s design was defined by “customary BMW traits,” such as a sleek hood, long wheelbase and a short front overhang.

Whether it's called the M3 or M4, it doesn't matter. What's important is that this performance car will always be a favorite among enthusiasts because it's a true driver’s car.

This machine is a special model designed by Gran Turismo to recreate the image of safety cars used in races like the Moto GP.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A1D:
BMW introduced the race spec M6, dubbed the M6 GT3, at the 2015 Frankfurt Motor Show. The company announced that the car would participate in the FIA-GT3 class in 2016, replacing the Z4 GT3 that contested in the same category since 2010.

Despite being in the same class, the M6 GT3 is significantly larger than the Z4 GT3, measuring about <5m> in length and more than <2m> wide. Its wheelbase is not only longer than the Z4 GT3, but it's also <5cm> longer than the production model. This allows the M6 GT3 to be more stable at high speed and through corners than its predecessor.

The car's wide fenders, aerodynamic front and rear bumper, and high rear wing not only make the car look menacingly beautiful, they provide gobs of downforce, which is essential to a race car.

The M6 GT3 is very lean, thanks in part to a body that's made of mostly carbon fiber. The body structure has been reinforced, and the suspension has been totally tweaked from that of the production M6. Under the hood is a 4.4-liter V-8 with the Twin Power Turbo, with various reinforcements and modifications that results in <585ps>.

The M6 GT3 M Power, bathed in the red, blue and black colors of the BMW livery, has proved to be yet another shining example in a long line of successful BMW race machines.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A1F:
The Vision Gran Turismo project is the setting for the world's best automakers to develop concept cars for motorsports fanatics. The Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo pushes the boundaries at the intersection of technology and design. This is not your traditional Mazda but a vision of the future with a healthy dose of respect for the past. It’s the result of an unwavering pursuit of glory at the world’s most grueling endurance event, the legendary 24 Hours of Le Mans.

In crafting the Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo, the Mazda Design team masterfully fused agility with elegance. Its dynamic silhouette is drawn with sensual forms inspired by Mazda’s KODO design philosophy. Even the shape of the grille is an interpretation of the Mazda signature front end developed for its production vehicles. The stance of the Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo, reminiscent of the famed 787B that took overall victory at the 1991 24 Hours of Le Mans, is powerful yet graceful.

The Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo is engineered to be lightweight, featuring extensive use of carbon fiber, including a monocoque chassis, all wrapped in atmospheric white paint. Pair this with advanced drivetrain technology that delivers the pinnacle of power, efficiency, and durability, and the result is a remarkable power-to-weight ratio that surpasses most vehicles in its class.

The Mazda LM55 Vision Gran Turismo embodies Mazda’s vision for the future and its unwavering spirit to embrace challenges.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A21:
The McLaren F1 production car first made its appearance in 1991 as the king of all super sports exotics. The car was built by Formula 1 constructor McLaren and styled by lead designer Gordon Murray, who was assigned the arduous task of bringing to life company founder Bruce McLaren's dream of building a road-going automobile with the McLaren name.

The F1 sports car had scissor-type doors not unlike those of a Lamborghini Diablo. Its monocoque structure was extremely light, contributing to the car's weight of <1140kg>. The car was laden with so many special features that they are too many to list here, but one trait worth noting is the car's passenger seating arrangement. By positioning the driver's seat at the center of the interior and the two passengers on opposing sides behind the driver, an ideal lateral and vertical weight balance was realized. Even the trunk was positioned within the wheelbase to ensure optimal weight distribution. Mounted amidships was BMW's 6.1-liter V12 that pumped out <627ps>. Although other exotics of the day used forced induction, McLaren opted to keep its powerplant naturally aspirated for better overall response and driving ease.

Upon its release to the public, the McLaren F1 was hailed as the fastest road-going sports car in the world, one that was also quite practical as an everyday driver. Needless to say, many McLaren F1 owners wanted to race the car because of its incredibly high level of performance, prompting the company to produce the F1 GTR, a race version of the road car. The F1 GTR went on to enjoy a successful racing career that included wins in races such as the 24 Hours of Le Mans._
DescriptionLong.0x00004A22:
In 1991, McLaren unveiled its first true road car. It was conceived by Gordon Murray, who designed the company’s Formula 1 machines at the time, and the exterior of the car styling was penned by Peter Stevens, who designed the new shape of the Lotus Esprit. The collaboration resulted in a true masterpiece called the “F1.”

The monocoque body was formed from carbon composites, so it was extremely light, weighing just <180kg>, thus enabling the F1 to tip the scales at a lean <1140kg>. A 6.1-liter V12, made by BMW motorsports (the famous “M” division) produces <636ps> and <66.4kgm> torque. It helped power the car to an official record top speed of <391.0km/h> in 1998.

With the high demands of the racing world, McLaren developed a model with even more refined aerodynamics: the McLaren F1 GTR. Delivery started in 1994. From 1995, the McLaren F1 GTR entered the BPR Global GT Endurance series and won the championship, but they also had another significant victory that year taking the checker at the 24 Hours of Le Mans. In wet conditions that lasted nearly the entire day, the McLaren staved off the open prototype racers that were then said to have the advantage. In the end, car No. 59 (which was practically a McLaren works car) driven by Yannick Dalmas, JJ Lehto and Masanori Sekiya took the overall win.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A23:
Established in 1965, Formula 1 team McLaren has become one of the most recognized names in the glamorous sport, with an image almost equal to that of Ferrari. Whereas Ferrari branched out into manufacturing production cars, McLaren's activities were all race-oriented. That changed with the introduction of the McLaren F1, a car designed by Gordon Murray and powered by a BMW engine.

The concept of the F1 was a "Formula 1 race car for the road," and because it possessed such high levels of performance, its duties weren't restricted to only the public road. The car saw lots of action as a racer, partly because McLaren was promoting the racing version of the F1, the F1 GTR, as aggressively as it was the road car.

For the F1 GTR, McLaren added a front spoiler lip and rear wing to enhance downforce. BMW provided the car's V12, mounted amidships, with power rated at more than the stock version's <627 ps>.

To say that the F1 GTR's maiden race was a success would be a dire understatement. In the 1995 24 Hours of Le Mans, the F1 GTR won its class, as well as placing 3rd, 4th and 5th. It kept on winning all over the world and is still considered today as one of the greatest GT race cars in history.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A24:
The P1 GTR, introduced in 2014 to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the McLaren F1 GTR that dominated sports-car racing in the 1990s, was based on the "P1" hybrid super car that went on sale the year before. The main difference between the two was that the "GTR" version was created exclusively for the racetrack.

Although it may look like the road-going car at first glance, the aerodynamic efficiency of the P1 GTR is on an entirely different level, thanks to a larger front splitter, aggressive side skirts, and a massive rear wing.

Mounted amidships for both the P1 road car and the P1 GTR is a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter V-8 that produces <737ps>. Also powering the vehicle are <179ps> electric motors, which enable the P1 road car to boast an output of <916ps> and the P1 GTR to pump out <1000ps>.

In order to purchase a P1 GTR, you must first have a P1 road car in your garage. Production for the race car was reported to be 30 to 35 units. Those lucky few who got their hands on the P1 GTR were invited to participate in a circuit driving program hosted by McLaren. Well, it's a nice offer, considering you need to shell out a staggering 1.9 million GBP (about US $2.4 million) to buy the car.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A25:
McLaren established their road car department “McLaren Automotive” in 2010, continuing to release high performance cars into the world ever since. The McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo is a car developed by McLaren Automotive with an eye for 2030 and beyond.

Gran Turismo series producer Kazunori Yamauchi was also involved in development of this car. It brings to life the future of McLaren, while staying true to the design pillars and principles that were established, by being committed to putting the driver first. Within the main structure of the cabin, the driver resides in a motorcycle-like driving position. This enables an extreme cabin-forward design, by giving the driver an ability to clearly identify the apex of the corners as they turn. The teardrop shaped canopy covering the driver carries on the tradition of McLaren roadcars, helping to provide this excellent field of vision.

Mounted behind the cabin is McLaren's 4-Liter V8 Twin Turbo engine. This drives the rear wheels, while the “pods” housing the front wheels contain high output electric motors which drive the front wheels. The overall combined output of the car reaches <1150ps>.

The aerodynamics of the car is also very innovative. The body of the McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo is optimized so that the body itself generates peak aerodynamic performance, by minimizing individual components that would adversely affect aerodynamics. Rather than actuating surface panels in its active aerodynamics system, tiny aperture covers around the air inlets on key surfaces will open, producing drag and downforce. As a result, the number of moving parts in the system was reduced to help keep weight to a minimum. With McLaren being the pioneer who first implemented carbon fiber into F1 racing, this machine also utilizes carbon fiber components throughout the car, which achieves a curb weight of just <1000kg>.

The McLaren Ultimate Vision Gran Turismo will be available in three liveries: Performance, Ulterior, and Noir. We hope you will take the opportunity to experience this sensory overload, combining incredible sound with awe-inspiring acceleration.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A27:
The 3-door model of the third-generation Mégane that was introduced in 2008 was on a totally different level from its 5-door hatchback stablemate.

The high-performance version of this 3-door coupe, tuned by Renault Sport Technologies, is the Mégane Renault Sport. It was first shown at the 2009 Geneva Auto Show, and reached the public in 2010.

Mounted in a body that wore special aerodynamic parts was a dedicated 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 with a twin-scroll turbocharger, producing <250ps> and <34.7kgm> torque. The engine was mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox.

The most notable component of this car was the chassis. Renault Sport, which develops cars for one-make and rally racing, created two different types of chassis for this car. One was tuned for road use, while the other was a “Chassis Cup” spec that also took into account on-track racing. Both utilize a double-axis strut system that allows load to remain at the centers of the front tires regardless of the up/down movement of the suspension. Because of this, the car’s cornering speed was said to be the quickest ever for a front-wheel drive.

In 2011, Renault introduced a 500-car limited edition model called the Mégane Renault Sport Trophy, featuring an increased power output of <265ps> as well as 19-inch wheels. This car was taken to the Nürburgring for a time trial, and set a front-engine/front-wheel-drive record of 8 minutes, 7.97 seconds!9

This special edition to commemorate the 15th anniversary of Gran Turismo is based on the third-generation Renault Mégane. The concept car was unveiled at the Geneva show in the spring of 2008, and the official debut was at the Paris Motor Show in the autumn. Completely different from the second-generation model, and renewed with a stylish, sporty form, it was well received by enthusiasts from all over Europe. This latest generation of the one-make race machine was dubbed the Mégane Trophy V6.

As with all one-make Mégane race cars since the first generation, Renault Sport was in charge of machine development. The third-generation car adopted the same method as that of the second-generation machine, building it into the style of a DTM machine with significantly enlarged fenders that functioned as radical aerodynamic devices front and rear. The few parts shared with the production car include lamps, door mirrors and the emblem on the front. The designers performed a remarkable job retaining the general look of the base car, making it unmistakable as a Mégane from any angle.

The powerplant, mounted low in a vehicle weighing just <955kg>, is paired with a Renault Sport-tuned 3.5-liter Nissan V6 that delivers <360ps>/<39.8kgm> through a 6-speed, manual gearbox. Suspension is the classic coil and damper formula, the body is made of FRP, not carbon, in order to reduce the cost for racers – the only people who get to purchase this iconic machine.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A2B:
The AMG-GT3, which made its debut at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show, was based on the AMG GT road car. It served as the replacement to the SLS AMG GT3 that had competed in races all over the world since 2011.

The AMG-GT3, built to FIA-GT3 specifications, looked meaner than its road-going counterpart, thanks to a special vertical-latticed grille, wide front and rear fenders, a low front splitter, large canard wings, and a rear wing carried over from the SLS AMG GT3. Also, the rear diffuser was much larger than that of the previous GT3.

The engine was swapped from the twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 of the road car to a naturally-aspirated 6.3-liter V-8 that powered the SLS AMG GT3. This powerplant was mounted low on the car's aluminum space frame, which was a tad smaller than that of the SLS AMG GT3. This meant that the new race car was lighter, with a curb weight under <1300kg>, and more nimble, thanks in part to a shorter wheel base.

The car took to the track in 2016 in various GT3 races around the world. At the 24 Hours of Nürburgring, it took the top four spots in its very first year of competition.

HTP motorsports of Germany, one of the top teams running the AMG GT3, found itself consistently in the championship hunt with the Mercedes race car in the Blancpain GT series. It won the Budapest and Silverstone rounds in 2016, as well as having finished 2nd place overall in the Nürburgring endurance race.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A2C:
After the exotic Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG was discontinued in 2013, the AMG GT was created to fill the void. But calling the AMG GT the direct successor of the SLS AMG wouldn’t entirely be accurate as the GT was slotted slightly lower than the SLS, and it didn’t feature the car’s trademark gull wing doors.

However that isn’t to say that the cars were not alike. The new AMG GT featured a long nose and stout rear deck like its predecessor, and its body was constructed over a rigid aluminum space frame. The engine was mounted just aft of the front axle, and a 7-speed semi-automatic transaxle was placed at the rear, helping the AMG GT achieve an ideal 47:53 front/rear weight distribution.

Under that long hood resided the compact M178, a twin turbocharged <3982cc> V-8 developed specifically for this car. Customers had the choice of going with the standard engine tune that provided <460ps> and <61.2kgm> of torque, while those with insatiable performance appetites could opt for the upgraded version that delivered <510ps> and <66.3kgm> of torque. The high output engine came in the AMG GT S, and it allowed the super sports car to run to <100km/h> in a scant 3.8 seconds and reach a top speed of <310km/h>. The standard AMG GT was by no means a slouch, as it reached <100km/h> in 4.0 seconds and hit <304 km/h> in full stride.

The rear-wheel-drive sports car came equipped with an LSD, along with electronically controlled variable dampers and a drive select system that featured a race mode, which was appropriate because the AMG GT was pretty much a race car in street-car clothes.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A2E:
Vision Gran Turismo is a project in which the world's auto makers and global brands develop a concept car for the fans of "Gran Turismo". The car that crowns the opening of this innovative collaboration is the Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo.

The design team of Mercedes-Benz incorporated the image of a large cat on the hunt, incorporating both agility and graceful elegance in the design. The characteristic body with its sensual contours is reminiscent of traditional Mercedes-Benz sports car proportions. Even the shape of the front grille is a reinterpretation of the wide Mercedes-Benz sports car grille with central star. Its shape is reminiscent of the legendary 300 SL racing car which won the third Panamericana race, known for being one of the toughest long distance races in the world.

With an aluminum spaceframe body and components in carbon fiber, the material of choice in motor racing, the Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo tips the scales at only <1385kg>. The AMG V8 biturbo engine delivers an exceptionally agile response to even the smallest movements of the accelerator. It develops 430 kW (<585ps>) and a maximum torque of 800 Nm (590.4 ft-lb). With its ultra lightweight body, the weight-to-power ratio calculates to an amazing <2.4kg/ps>. In addition, anyone can experience its breathtaking performance thanks to its AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT 7-speed sports transmission, which is systematically configured for outstandingly dynamic performance.

The sound of the car is another point to be noted. The powerful howl emitted by this engine was composed by sound specialists at AMG. The sonorous exhaust note and engine sounds are tuned perfectly to awaken the excitement of a racetrack wherever you are.

The double wishbone suspension on the front and rear axles reflects a long-standing racing experience at Mercedes-Benz. The electronic differential lock ensures the ideal traction for the powered rear wheels. The AMG ceramic high-performance compound brake system guarantees excellent deceleration.

Experience for yourself the exquisite concept sports car presented by Mercedes-Benz.W
DescriptionLong.0x00004A2F:
”Vision Gran Turismo” is a dream project in which leading international brands develop concept cars for Gran Turismo and its fans. And the car which kicked off the project with its stunning debut in November 2013, was the “Mercedes Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo”.

The creation by the Mercedes-Benz design team is a sensual gull-winged sports car designed in the image of a hunting feline. The car is elegance personified, infusing elements that show the 130-year legacy of Mercedes Benz perfectly with futuristic sports designs such as the LED front grille, an ultra lightweight body and an exhaust system that is integrated with the tail lights.

And for the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo”, there is also a separate version that is optimized for the competitive racing scene of Gran Turismo. This is the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo Racing Series”.

The immediately noticeable difference with the original version is the fixed rear wing. Despite the increase in drag this creates, the aerodynamic device was utilized in favor of more downforce on high speed circuits. The side mirrors using CCD cameras were returned to conventional mirrors, and the rear brake light is decorated with the “Gran Turismo” logo for a touch of racing flavor.

And of course the non-visible elements have also been stepped up. The AMG 5.5 liter V8 Twin Turbo has been raised to <600ps>, and the 7 speed dual clutch transmission has been optimized for transmission performance rather than ride comfort; now changed to a sequential transmission with dog links. Though the original is already extremely light at <1385kg>, equipment for utility and comfort have been omitted to reduce the weight down to <1300kg>. Lowering the ride height even further, the center of gravity has also been lowered for better circuit performance.

The balance of ultimate elegance and competitive performance. This is another breed of the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo”, waiting to pounce on its prey.m
DescriptionLong.0x00004A30:
”Vision Gran Turismo” is a special project where leading international brands develop concept cars for Gran Turismo and its fans. And the car which kicked everything off with was the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo," that first made its appearance in November 2013.

The Mercedes-Benz design team created a sensual gull-winged sports car designed in the image of a hunting feline. The car is elegance personified, infusing elements that reflect the 130-year legacy of Mercedes-Benz with futuristic sports design cues such as the LED front grille, an ultra lightweight body and an exhaust system that is integrated with the taillights.

There is also a separate version that is optimized for the competitive racing in Gran Turismo called the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo LH Edition," which is distinguished by a fixed rear wing that provides gobs of downforce on fast straights. The CCD camera side mirrors were returned to conventional mirrors, while the brake lights are adorned with the “Gran Turismo” logo.

For the race car, output for AMG's twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter V-8 was raised to <600ps>, and the 7-speed dual-clutch transmission was optimized for fast gear changes, featuring sequential shifting with dog links. And while the road car tips the scales at a lean <1385kg>, the race car comes in at a fighting <1300kg>, thanks to the removal of all creature comforts. Also, thanks to a lower seating position, the car's center of gravity was improved for superior circuit performance.

Whichever version you happen to choose, one thing for certain is that the “Mercedes-Benz AMG Vision Gran Turismo" represents a balance of ultimate elegance and competitive performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A31:
In the latter half of the 1990s, famed sports car manufacturer BMW purchased the branding and manufacturing rights to the MINI brand and resurrected the MINI Cooper in 2001.

This new MINI was a bit larger than the classic model of yesteryear, measuring <3655mm>, <1690mm> and <1455mm>, overall length, width and height, respectively. But BMW kept the car's spirit intact, thanks to quirky styling cues that were reminiscent of the original 1959 model. These included a "cute" face, highlighted by large round headlights and a square front grille and boxy silhouette.

The performance-oriented version in the new MINI lineup was the Cooper S. The power plant in the standard MINI was the "Pentagon," a 1.6-liter SOHC inline-4 developed in cooperation between BMW and Chrysler, while the Cooper S got an intercooled supercharger bolted on to its power plant—the large air intake on the model's hood being a dead giveaway of forced induction.

The supercharger accounted for an additional <54ps> and <7.26kgm> of torque over the stock engine, for a grand total of <170ps> and <22.45kgm>. It came mated to a slick-shifting 6-speed manual gearbox. This made the Cooper S one of the most fun to drive FF (Front drive, Front engine) compact cars in the marketplace.

It was a testament to the German company that effectively instilled the car's British heritage into the new MINI Cooper.1
DescriptionLong.0x00004A32:
The MINI Clubman Vision Gran Turismo, created from the inspiration of the MINI's success in motorsports, was designed strictly for the track. It's powered by a <395ps> engine that sends this <1050kg> vehicle from zero to <100km/h> in a mere 3.5 seconds. Top speed is rated at <290km/h>, with the right gear ratios. Power is transferred to all four wheels via a 6-speed sequential race gearbox. The suspension system consists of McPherson struts in the front and HA3 dampers at the rear, all of which are fully adjustable and ensure excellent cornering ability.  

The MINI Clubman Vision Gran Turismo sits low to the ground, with the wheels positioned outside the body, resulting in go-kart-like agility. Adjustable carbon diffusers are placed in the front and rear, while large vents behind the wheel arches regulate air flow to cool the engine and brakes. The split rear spoiler and fully enclosed underbody enhance the sophisticated aerodynamics.

The car MINI design has familiar touches, such as the hexagonal front grille, elliptical headlights with implied racing-design stickers, and rally stripes on the hood and roof. Quick release hinges on the hood and tank and the small sliding window on the side reveal that this is not your oridinary performance car.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A33:
Since its debut in 2000, the 147 had served as Alfa Romeo’s entry-level model, but in 2008, the 3-door MiTo took over this role in the lower B-segment.

The "Mi" in MiTo stands for Milan, where Alfa Romeo's design studios are located. The "To'" refers to Turin (Torino in Italian), where the car was manufactured. And the word "mito" in Italian translates to "myth" or "legend," adding a layer of meaning to the name.

One size smaller than the 147, the MiTo was crafted at Alfa Romeo’s design center. The car's overall styling, particularly the front and rear, invoke the spirit of the 8C Competizione. Alfa Romeo fans embraced the MiTo’s appearance, which they felt exuded an ideal balance of charming, classic styling and modern, cutting-edge aesthetics.

While the MiTo shared components with the FIAT Grande Punto, it was tuned to deliver the unmistakable flavor of an Alfa Romeo. When it was introduced, many hailed the MiTo as the best in its class, praising its blend of responsive handling and exceptional controllability.

Under its hood resided a turbocharged 1.4-liter DOHC inline-4. The 1.4 Sport model, which came with a 6-speed manual gearbox, produced <155ps> and <23.5kgm> torque. The MiTo sprinted from 0 to <100 km/h> in 8.0 seconds and hit a top speed of <215 km/h>, making it among the sportiest cars in its class.,
DescriptionLong.0x00004A34:
Mitsubishi Motors, a company with a spectacular history in races like the Dakar Rally and World Rally Championships (WRC), has developed a special concept model for Vision Gran Turismo: This is the “Mitsubishi Concept XR-PHEV EVOLUTION Vision Gran Turismo”.

In the development of this special concept model, Mitsubishi Motors introduced their design team, Advanced Vehicle Research and Development Group, and Aerodynamic Engineering Development Group into this project in the same process they would normally follow to plan and develop real motorsports vehicles.

The styling of the car follows the basic concepts of the “MITSUBISHI Concept XR-PHEV” shown at the 2013 Tokyo Motor Show, while pouring in know-how gained from years of motorsports experience into its every detail. As a result, the concept was evolved into a stoic racing machine.

The “Athlete Form” design concept was advanced further, emphasizing the driving features aggressively. The iconic front grille is a study of next generation Mitsubishi SUV identity, and the shape that forms a wedge starting from the triple diamond mark is designed in the image of an athlete at crouching position on a starting line, evoking an intense image of tension and potential.

Applying advanced development technology from the Plug-in Hybrid EV System, the spontaneous power of the motor and powerful torque of the engine is transmitted through an 8 speed dual clutch transmission (DCT) to drive the 4 wheels. Its overwhelming drive performance is controlled precisely with the S-AWC vehicle dynamics control system that distributes the drive force optimally to the 4 wheels, producing a handling characteristic that moves the car exactly as the driver desires. In addition, the carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) body reduces weight and greatly contributes to its agility, and the downforce produced by the aerodynamic form of the front and rear diffusers produces excellent cornering performance. The large diameter 20 inch aluminum wheels gives an impression of a tough suspension system, and the powerful appearance of the front and rear fenders is in the image of toned muscles of a powerful athlete.

We hope you enjoy this special concept model, packed with the sports spirit of Mitsubishi Motors.>
DescriptionLong.0x00004A35:
Automobili Lamborghini was founded in 1963. Following the development of the 350 GT and 400 GT, Lamborghini unveiled the TP400 in bare chassis form at the 1965 Turin Motor Show. At the Geneva Motor Show the following year, they revealed the Miura P400, now adorned with a stunning body styled by Marcello Gandini, then Chief Designer at Bertone.

The Miura adopted a mid-engine layout, housing a <3929cc> V-12 behind the rear bulkhead. It was a landmark model for Lamborghini—their first true supercar—delivering <350ps> and <37.5kgm> of torque. With its revolutionary layout and design, it propelled the Lamborghini name into the international spotlight.

The development of the Miura brought together several remarkable individuals. Its chassis was the work of Gian Paolo Dallara, who would go on to found Dallara Automobili, now a powerhouse in the world of racing car design. Paolo Stanzani, the brilliant engineer who would later lead the creation of the Countach, also played a key role in the project.

It is believed that three prototypes of the Miura P400 were built between its Geneva Motor Show debut and the start of full production. The earliest prototype reportedly lacked the distinctive louvre over the rear cowling. These initial cars were later updated to production specifications and sold as standard Miura P400 models.

The Miura line would eventually evolve into the more powerful S and SV versions, with production continuing through to 1973. A handful of rare SVJ models also exist, crafted in homage to the legendary Jota.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A36:
The first high-performance model for the iconic Mini Cooper was the "S". The Mini, which was manufactured as a compact car for the everyman by BMC (British Motor Corporation), wasn't only extremely civil - able to accommodate four passengers - it was extremely fun to drive, thanks in part to its sports-car-like handling.

Together with the Cooper Car Company, which won the 1960 F1 Constructor’s Championship, BMC created the new Mini Cooper and the sporty Mini Cooper S. These models were equipped with twin carbs and disc brakes, features seldom seen in compact cars at the time.

What made the 970 "S" special was its larger engine, whose displacement was increased to <970cc> resulting in a hearty <66ps>. This change was made so the Mini Cooper could race in certain classifications. (The standard <848cc> engine produced <34ps>.) Although the 970 "S" found success on the racetrack, only 963 examples were built since it made its debut in 1964, making it the least produced Mini Cooper model ever.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A37:
Since 2008, Nissan's entry in the GT500 class of the Super GT Series was the R35 GT-R. The car initially came with a 4.5-liter V-8 (VK45DE), then switched to a 3.4-liter V-8 (VRH34A/VRH34B) in 2010. In 2014, it sported yet another new powerplant: a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 with direct injection (NR20A), independently developed in the same manner as Toyota and Honda.

Because of new regulations in the Super GT Series for the 2014 season, where the weight and center of gravity of the monocoque had to mimic those of DTM machines, the GT500 GT-R underwent major changes under its skin. These changes continued all the way to the 2016 season.

In 2014, four teams competed with the new GT-R, and the Motul Autech team of Tsugio Matsuda and Ronnie Quintarelli brought home the series championship that year. The following year saw them repeat the feat bringing home the Driver Championship and the Constructor Championship to Nissan for the second straight year. The streak came to an end in 2016 when, despite winning the first two races of the season, they ended up in 3rd place in both the Driver and Constructor championships.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A38:
Following in the footsteps of the McLaren F1 with its ultimate performance, and the SLR McLaren with Mercedes Benz, the third McLaren supercar was given the name MP4, as if to remind one of its relationship with F1 machines. As with the revolutionary MP4 F1 car that introduced carbon composite bodies to F1 racing back in 1981, the major point of note in this car is the one-piece carbon composite "mono-cell" tub utilized in its structure. The weight of the mono-cell alone is just <80kg> and contributes greatly to weight reduction. In the front and rear of the mono-cell is an aluminum frame to which the engine and suspension are assembled.

The midship-mounted engine is a 3.8-liter V8 twin turbo, with a maximum output of <600ps>. The displacement and power specifications may perhaps appear to be surprisingly modest for a McLaren road car. However its performance is nothing short of incredible, as its boasts a top speed of over <320km/h>, 0-<400m> (400m) acceleration of approximately 11 seconds, and a 0-<200km/h> acceleration of less than 10 seconds, giving it a performance level equal to or greater than the Ferrari 458 Italia.

The 7-speed dual clutch system is given the name "Seamless Shift Gearbox," much like F1 machines, and incorporates six preset driving modes. The electronically controlled suspension is set up as a 4-wheel double wishbone configuration, and it is also notable that the front-rear-left-right dampers are connected hydraulically for ride comfort.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A39:
The second-generation MR2, which arrived in 1989, represented the all-new version of the AW11, Japan's first mass produced mid-engine sports car. Toyota wanted to broaden the appeal of its two-seater to the general public, so it made the car larger. To compensate for the added mass, Toyota increased power. The 4A-G, a 1.6-liter inline-4, was swapped in favor of the 3S-G, a 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4, which produced <165 ps> in naturally-aspirated form and <225 ps> when turbocharged. Unfortunately, with the new engines, the handling characteristics of the AW11 worsened, as the car exhibited a tendency to oversteer. As a result, in December 1991, the chassis was completely revised in the updated SW20 II model.

Things dramatically improved, even more so in 1994 with version III that featured more power via a stronger turbocharger; <245 ps> and <31.0 kgm> of torque. The naturally-aspirated model also saw an increase in performance going to <180 ps> and <19.5 kgm> of torque. In June 1996, the IV added a helical LSD, as well as standard fare ABS. In December 1997, the V introduced the VVT-i (Variable Valve Timing-intelligent) to the naturally-aspirated engine that was now pumping out <200 ps> and <21.0 kgm> of torque. With all these improvements, the SW20 became one of the most popular sports cars of its day, outshining the AW11, the model that started it all.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A3A:
The Lamborghini Murciélago made its debut at the 2001 Frankfurt Motor Show as the flagship for the renowned Italian maker. It had big shoes to fill for it was succeeding the legendary V12 supercars, the Countach and Diablo as the company's top model. The Murciélago, along with the V10-powered Gallardo introduced at the 2003 Geneva Motor Show, represented a new era for Lamborghini, which blossomed under Audi AG's umbrella.

Five years later, at the 2006 Geneva Motor Show, Audi took the veils off a new, even meaner version of the Murciélago, the LP640. The “LP” in its name stands for Longitudinale Posteriore (longitudinally rear mounted), while the numerical designation refers to its <640ps> (640ps). Actually, the “LP” designation is a traditional one for Lamborghini, dating back to the days of the Countach. As mentioned earlier, the power of the car was <640ps>, up from the stock Murciélago's <580ps>. It came from a 6496 cc DOHC V12 that transferred the power to all four wheels. The car's performance was nothing short of extraordinary, going from zero to <100km/h> in 3.4 seconds and reaching a top speed of <340km/h>.

The styling of the Murciélago and Gallardo were penned by Luc Donckerwolke, and for the LP640, that original design was fine-tuned, resulting in an edgier supercar-like shape. The most notable differences between the stock Murciélago and the LP640 were the front and rear diffusers and the integration of the exhaust tips within the bumper. The scissor-type doors opened upward, providing a family lineage to the Countach and Diablo. The LP640 lineup included an open-air roadster and a lightweight, high-performance limited-edition model called the LP670-4 SuperVeloce.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A3B:
America’s premier pony car celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2014, and Ford celebrated this occasion by introducing the all-new sixth-generation model. Unlike previous versions of the Mustang that were only available in limited markets, Ford decided to share the wealth and marketed the new car to more than 120 countries.

The designers at Dearborn took extreme care in styling the new Mustang, making it appear more aggressive than any model before it, but making sure that it would still be instantly recognizable as a Mustang upon first glance. The engineers took the same tack, giving the car a great balance of efficiency and power. They brought back the inline-4 of Mustangs past, but after bolting on a turbocharger, the base 2.3-liter engine pumped out a hearty <314ps>/<32.6kgm> to the delight of sports car fans worldwide. However, the star of the show was the thundering Mustang GT's 5.0-liter V-8, which people expected from a powerful American muscle car. It didn’t disappoint, delivering a whopping <441ps>/<40.8kgm>, making it among the most powerful Mustangs ever.

The new pony car also featured a fine-tuned fully independent suspension system (previous models came with a rear beam axle). It was clear to see from this rebirth of the modern-day pony car that the Mustang was no longer only an American icon, but an international one.

It didn’t disappoint, delivering a whopping <441ps>/<40.8kgm>, making it among the most powerful Mustangs ever.

The new pony car also featured a fine-tuned fully independent suspension system (previous models came with a rear beam axle). It was clear to see from this rebirth of the modern-day pony car that the Mustang was no longer only an American icon, but an international one.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.B regulations by Gran Turismo.J
DescriptionLong.0x00004A40:
In the postwar era, American cars were widely seen as large and expensive, but that perception shifted dramatically in the early 1960s with the debut of the Ford Mustang in 1964. With its sporty attitude and impressive performance—offered at an affordable price—the Mustang immediately won over the American public. It became a financial triumph for Ford Motor Co., and its popularity only grew in the years that followed.

In 1969, Ford gave the Mustang a major redesign, but it retained its signature long nose and short rear deck. Otherwise, nearly everything else about the car changed so dramatically that many saw it as a completely new machine. The updated Mustang was larger but kept its core structure and layout.

It was during this refresh that the formidable Mach 1 arrived in 1969. Launched as part of the Mustang’s fastback lineup known as the "SportsRoof," its sweeping roofline didn’t just enhance aerodynamics, it inspired sports-car designers around the world.

Ford offered a wide range of engines under the Mustang’s hood, from high-powered big-block V-8s capable of matching race cars in performance to more accessible options. The most common was the small-block 351-cubic-inch V8. In its 1970–1971 Ram Air configuration. It produced an impressive <304ps>, making the 351 Mustang one of the quickest and most thrilling street cars of its time.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A41:
In its 80 year history, Nissan has participated, and succeeded, in nearly every form of motorsports imaginable. Its specialty has been in the grand-touring category where the company has continually produced championships after championships, with cars such as the 510 and 300Z. What's more, because these cars were based on production versions, anyone could drive the road-going versions of them on public roads with remarkable comfort and safety. Nissan is now looking to the future and has imagined a new type of performance machine, one that we're calling the "NISSAN CONCEPT 2020 Vision Gran Turismo".

Through the magic of digitization, the design and development processes of automobiles have been undergoing a revolutionary change in recent years. Designers now work in a world where they can share their expressions and insights instantaneously. Their visions and ideas can also be realized virtually, and on this occasion, the designers at Nissan decided to turn to Gran Turismo to visualize their concept. The car you see here was penned by young designers from Nissan Design Europe, based in the UK, and when the final product was shown to the young engineers on the engineering side in Japan, they excitedly inputted their technical evaluations and simulations.

The car is characterized by a unique 2+2 profile based on Nissan's touring cars that have competed all over Europe. It features prominently shaped fenders that act like wings, providing gobs of downforce at high speed. The air enters the front side inlet and travels through the inner side of the wheels, before it is drawn out in an accelerated manner. This allows the body to cut through the air like a hot knife through butter. The air flows over the roof and off the rear deck without creating excessive turbulence behind the car. If you examine the airflow over the car, you will realize that despite its boxy shape, it's configured much like a prototype race car.

The rear wing automatically rises and lowers, depending on the speed of the car. At a speed of <300km/h>, it generates more than <400kg> of downforce. The underbody also takes cues from a race car to ensure excellent aerodynamics.

Powering the car is a high-performance hybrid FR-4WD system with a turbocharged V-6 engine and three electric motors. The high-output motors produce instant torque to all fnur wheels and keeps the acceleration going until the gasoline engine takes over. The torsue vectoring of the individual front motors combine with the active suspensioy to deliver razor-sharp handling, even at high speed.

The NISSAN CONCEPT 2020 Vision!Gran Turismo, the product of vnnnon and tochniqal imagination, is definitely a car that fe hope becomes a remlnty in the near future. Of it does, then our driveng future looks very wrignt indeed.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A42:
The Acura NSX became an icon after only several years on the market, and although it was gone in 2005, it was hardly forgotten. To the delight of performance-car enthusiasts everywhere, Honda introduced a concept of a second-generation car in 2012, and then gave us a production version of it at the 2015 North American International Auto Show.

The new NSX came in the form of a mid-engine supercar that combined aluminum, high tensile steel and other advanced materials in the chassis, covered by a lightweight carbon-fiber body. The engine, mounted behind the cockpit, came in the form of a twin-turbo V-6 with a dry sump, mated to 9-speed dual-clutch transmission with a built-in motor. There were also electric motors powering the front wheels to make the new NSX an all-wheel-drive machine. The AWD system, called the Sports Hybrid SH-AWD, allows torque vectoring that controls deceleration as well as drive force, enhancing the car’s ability to corner.

The NSX also featured an Integrated Dynamic System that possessed four modes—the lowest one allowed driving with electric power alone at low speeds, while the highest one combined the gasoline engine and electric motors to provide the highest performance, intended for use on the racetrack.
