DescriptionLong.0x00004A46:
Beginning in November of 1992, the first-generation NSX Type R was available over the course of a limited three-year-period run, and then became an icon. Seven years later, a new NSX-R was shown as a concept car at the 2001 Tokyo Motor Show, reviving the legend. Not long after, the NSX Type R once again became available to the public when it went on sale in May of 2002.

Why such a long period between Type R models? With the base NSX's performance threshold already so high, engineers elected to wait for new cutting-edge automotive technology to incorporate into their creation rather than just carry over pre-existing packages.

Special emphasis was placed not on the engine, which was addressed when the second-generation NSX's power plant had its displacement increased and was fitted with a new 6-speed manual transmission, but in the area of aerodynamics. The work done in this area resulted in a rare feat for a commercially available vehicle: a shape that not only produced negative lift but generated downforce.

In order to achieve this newfound aerodynamic efficiency, a newly-shaped hood and rear wing were created; lightweight carbon-fiber was used unsparingly in these vital components. The final result was a new NSX Type R that became the first street-legal road car to lap the famed Nürburgring course in less than 8 minutes, an unheard of feat for a full-fledged production car at the time.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A47:
The NSX proved to be a major hit with both automotive enthusiasts and the media alike, but the limited-edition NSX Type R (NSX-R) that went on sale in Japan in November 1992 took Honda's mid-engine sports car formula to the extreme limits. This ultimate sports car was so well received that the "R" designation eventually made its way into the lineup of Honda's more mainstream cars, namely the Civic and Integra.

Honda's engineering philosophy for its Type R vehicles followed two main principles: "less weight" and "increased rigidity." In the case of the NSX, this meant removing the car's air-conditioning unit and sound system hardware, not to mention all of its sound absorbing insulation. Other changes included installing lightweight seat and wheels. The result was a lean performance machine that tipped the scales at a low <1230kg> (the stock NSX weighed <1350kg>), improving the Type R's weight-to-power ratio from the base car's <4.82kg/ps> to <4.39kg/ps>.

Complementing its new lean body was improved structural rigidity that came via additional bracing throughout its aluminum monocoque chassis. Stiffer shocks and springs on the suspension system were also key contributors. Overall, the Type R behaved like an entirely different animal when compared to the base NSX, especially on the racetrack where the car belonged. Less than 500 NSX Type Rs were produced during the car's limited three-year run, with all of them now considered collector items by many Honda fans.e
DescriptionLong.0x00004A48:
Taking center stage at the 2008 Paris Motor Show was a special camouflaged sports car from noted supercar manufacturer, Aston Martin. This car would ultimately become the now legendary One-77, named thus because its production run was limited to a mere 177 units. The car made its official introduction at the 2009 Geneva Motor Show.

At first glance, the One-77 was obviously an Aston Martin, as it possessed the styling cues of other modern high-profile Aston models, namely the DB9 and DBS. That said, the One-77 did sport a unique, more exotic shape that gave it better aerodynamics than its stablemates.

Developed from the ground-up, the One-77’s chassis was a joint effort by Aston Martin and Multimatic. It combined a carbon monocoque tub with handmade aluminum panels, while the suspension featured an inboard double-wishbone geometry that was similar to those of many race cars.

Cosworth helped with the engine. Starting with the company’s 6.0-liter V12, displacement was increased to <7312cc>, which resulted in a whopping <760ps>/<76.5kgm>…the highest output of any normally aspirated engine to date. What’s more, all this displacement and extra power came in a more compact package. Because the actual size of the engine decreased by 25 percent when compared to the 6.0-liter, Aston Martin engineers were able to mount it <100mm> lower than usual and nearly <260mm> behind the front axle. This provided a low center of gravity and excellent front/rear weight distribution, which made the One-77 one of the best handling production cars in the world.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A49:
The Pantera, a product of the former Italian sports car maker De Tomaso, featured plenty of American engineering under its svelte, exotic bodywork. Co-developed by Ford, under the supervision of then-vice president, Lee Iacocca, the Pantera was meant to rekindle Ford's fire for exotic cars, which was first established by the Ford GT40. To give the car a more European flavor, Iacocca brought in Alejandro de Tomaso to join the project.

Ford wanted to sell the Pantera in large numbers and in order to do so, Iacocca knew it needed to have a low price tag. So despite the expensive, exotic looking bodywork, designed by Tom Tjaarda of Carrozzeria Ghia, it came equipped with a Ford V8 that was suited for mass production.

The mid-engine Pantera made its debut with a 5.8L OHV V8 351 with a CDI that produced <335ps> and <45kgm> of torque, providing both power and performance equal to or better than its rivals of the day. While it was not powered by its own engine like cars from other Italian brands, it was a project that made perfect sense, taking the best of both worlds from the American and Italian car industries.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4A:
A steel pipe frame with simple mechanisms. A tiny seat and exposed engine. A racing go-kart is often seen as the most basic form of a race car. However, these karts can be quite complicated, coming in a number of shapes and sizes; some, like the Shifter Kart featured here, are virtually mini versions of formula cars.

The Shifter Kart is basically the same as a standard racing kart, but the major differences are that the former is equipped with a 6-speed transmission and front brakes. The gearbox is combined with a dry clutch, requiring the driver to operate the clutch whenever stopped, including after a spin. Gear-shifting is usually accomplished by pushing or pulling a lever next to the steering wheel. Depending on the gear ratios, top speed can reach up to <200km/h>, so Shifter Karts are often raced on full-size auto circuits.

The front brakes are primarily to control this high-speed range, but they also allow changes in brake balance between front and rear, which in turn changes control characteristics. A Shifter Kart can be set up with much more precision than a standard kart with only rear brakes.

The Shifter Kart is a full-fledged race machine, used to train top drivers. Drive one and feel for yourself the level of performance. It is sure to change your opinion about these tiny machines.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4B:
Nissan originally conceived the Skyline GT-R R32 as a Group A race car, but when Group A racing went defunct, Nissan found a new series for its prized car, the All Japan Grand Touring Championship (JGTC). The GT-R later underwent a full redesign as the R33, and performance of this new car on the track was impressive to say the least. However, as Nissan's main rival, Toyota, started contesting with a faster version of the Supra, and Honda added more heat when it joined the series in 1997, the GT-R was losing its grasp on JGTC dominance.

Although Nissan took both the Drivers' and Constructors' championship titles in 1998, the company switched to the new R34 in 1999 as the foundation for its race car. The new GT-R rode on a <55mm> shorter wheelbase than the R33, making it more agile than its predecessor. Also a shallower oil pan and the fuel tank relocated inside the cabin accounted for better weight distribution.

The new revived GT-R found itself in far fiercer competition than anticipated, and didn't score its first win until the fourth race of the season.

The GT-R was unable to log a second win that year, but collected enough points on the strength of its reliability to give Érik Comas, driving the Pennzoil NISMO GT-R, the Drivers' championship title for the second year in a row before the final race was even run.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4C:
In 2008, the Nissan GT-R made its heralded return to the Super GT Series in Japan. As the GT-R made the headlines, Lexus was quietly making significant improvements to its entry in Japan's most popular racing series, the SC430.

The SC430 did not fare well in the Super GT series the previous year, as it was aerodynamically inferior to the competition, the result of a compact body with front and rear overhangs that were too short to provide acceptable levels of downforce. However for 2008, Lexus lengthened the overhangs, giving the car much improved aerodynamics than the previous year. The result was a sleek, fast race car that flourished on high-speed race tracks.

Despite winning only one race during the entire season (at the Fuji International Speedway) by the ZENT CERUMO team, the Lexus SC430 GT machine took home the overall championship, thanks to the consistency of the Petronas TOM's team. The combination of a good long-term strategy and a reliable, fast car proved to be the right formula in winning the series title that year.!
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4D:
On May 30, 1916, Peugeot won the legendary “Indianapolis 500 Mile Race” with its L45 race car. One hundred years later, we pay homage to that achievement by bringing you the Peugeot L500R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo. 

Filled with the latest technology, the L500R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo features sharp styling cues and an incredibly low profile. With even the bulge that covers the cockpit kept to a minimum, the car stands a mere <1m> tall. The tail section was inspired by the old L45 race car, ending in a streamlined shape with three distinctive rear lamp claws similar to that of the 3008, which is a Peugeot design cue today.

The cockpit utilizes a near-future user interface, with two holograms displaying a variety of information to the driver. Unlike the L45, the L500R is a single seater—the navigator has been replaced with a virtual navigator in this concept.

The L500R is powered by a 1.6-liter 4-cylinder turbocharged engine and two electric motors. Total output is <500ps> and maximum torque is <74.43kgm>. Utilizing the latest lightweight materials, the car weighs only <1000kg>. All this allows the Peugeot race car to run from 0-<100km/h> in 2.5 seconds and to the <1000m>-mark in just 19 seconds.

Peugeot has participated in many forms of motorsports all over the world, including the 24 Hours of Le Mans, WRC and Rally Raids. This innovative machine represents the company’s spirit and passion for competition.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4E:
On May 30, 1916, Peugeot won the legendary “Indianapolis 500 Mile Race” with its L45 race car. One hundred years later, we pay homage to that achievement by bringing you the Peugeot L500R HYbrid Vision Gran Turismo. To celebrate the release of Gran Turismo Sport, Peugeot decided to develop the L500R even more, creating the L750R HYbrid, a competition model with even more performance. 

What mainly separates the L750R from the L500R is its power unit. By raising the rev limit of the turbocharged 1.6-liter inline-4 to <10000rpm>, output has been increased to 580 brake horsepower. And when you combine that with the 170 brake horsepower coming from the electric motors, you get a total output of 750 brake horsepower. 

The L750R basically wears the same body as the L500R, but with improved aerodynamics. A large splitter has been added to the front, and the airflow of the underfloor has been further optimized. A rear wing has also been added to increase downforce. The L750R weighs <175kg> less than its stablemate, tipping the scales at <825kg>. This has improved the car’s 0-<100km/h> acceleration by 0.1 second, to 2.4 seconds.

Peugeot took the incredible L500R race car and refined it even further to create a truly remarkable machine that conveys the company’s passion and spirit for competition.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A4F:
When PEUGEOT designers and PEUGEOT SPORT engineers teamed up to create an exceptional super car the result was PEUGEOT Vision Gran Turismo.

This racing car, specifically designed for the Anniversary Edition of Gran Turismo 6, brings together the major elements of a hyper-efficient endurance car. Boasting a radical style, the PEUGEOT Vision Gran Turismo stands out with its almost absent aerodynamic elements and its air-rending monolithic figure. Its design allows an aerodynamic support directly generated by the car bodywork, which reaches a mere 1.04 m (<1.04m>). 

The PEUGEOT Vision Gran Turismo focuses on the driver. Behind them, in a rear central position, the 3.2L V6 turbo engine delivers its 875 ch (<887ps>) to the four permanent driving wheels, sized 22-inch at the front and 23-inch at the rear, via a mechanical 6-speed transmission.

Combined with the car's lightness <875kg>, and its ideal mass distribution (48% at the front and 52% at the rear), the ultra-direct steering makes it the perfect ride to face up to the challenges of Gran Turismo. Its acceleration is exceptional thanks to its 1 kg/ch (1 kg/HP) weight/power ratio and its deceleration is just as formidable thanks to its 4 ventilated carbon discs with a diameter of 380 mm (15-inch) on the front, and 337 mm (13-inch) on the rear. 

Are you ready to add your name to PEUGEOT SPORT’s great list of victories on every track of the world?

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A52:
The third-generation Prius, introduced at the 2009 North American International Auto Show, did not simply improve the environmental characteristics of its predecessor, it significantly raised the bar in terms of sportiness and the all-important fun-to-drive factor.

While the overall body style of the new Prius was defined by sharp lines and angles, making the vehicle more aerodynamic and better looking than the outgoing model, it also had a vastly improved drive system. A larger 1.8-liter engine was installed and more than 90 percent of the hybrid system was redesigned. And yes, it was more fun to drive than any Prius before it.

With an increase in the popularity of "green" vehicles in the global marketplace, the new Prius shattered its sales target goal of 10,000 units per month by selling 18,000 soon after its release. It continued to top the new-car sales chart for the next six months, all the way up to November 2009. Naturally, it was awarded Japan's Car of the Year for 2009.

The new Prius came in three trim levels of L, S, and G, with the G being the most luxurious, fitted with leather-wrapped steering and smart entry system.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A53:
When Audi introduced AWD technology to the World Rally Championships (WRC) in 1981, it changed the face of rally racing forever. Having all four wheels provide grip and traction over off-road courses gave its cars a distinct advantage over the competition. That was validated in 1982 when the company won both the Manufacturers Title and the Drivers Championship. The following year, an Audi driver won the Drivers Championship and in 1984, the company claimed both titles yet again.

The race car at the center of this amazing run was the Sports quattro. In the fall of 1983, Audi sold 200 of the 2133cc turbocharged inline-5-powered Sports quattros for Group B homologation. In the 1985 Tour de Corse, an improved version of the car, called the Sports quattro S1, also known as the Sports quattro E2 in some countries, made its debut. The car's engine was basically a carryover from the previous car, incorporating some improvements such as a misfiring (anti-lag) system, but output was increased to a staggering <600ps>. The big change came to the transmission, a 6-speed semi-automatic with a clutch sensor in the shifter. Later that year, it was also given a revised body with front spoilers and large front fenders that improved the car's aerodynamics and made it look meaner. Along with rear fenders incorporating air inlets, plus a rear wing, the car by this time had matured into the ultimate rallying quattro.

During this time, Audi also modified a WRC-spec Sports quattro S1 to hill-climb specifications and entered it in the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb. The result: Overall wins and track records in 1985 and 1987, with Michèle Mouton and Walter Röhrl behind the wheel, respectively.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A54:
The Audi R18 is a LMP1 class race machine developed by Audi to compete in the FIA World Endurance Championships (WEC).

The first appearance of the race machine dubbed the “R18” was in 2011. This later evolved into the “R18 Ultra” in 2012, and “R18 e-tron quattro” from 2013-2015, continually evolving over its years in competition. The Audi R18 is the successor to this series, but while it carries over the R18 name, this was a very different machine from the past iterations, developed from scratch.

First, the aerodynamics were greatly revised. The front center section looks like a very narrow version of the high nose section of an F1 machine. Between this and the left and right fenders there is a wing, also like that of a formula car. The shapes of the front and rear fenders were also changed, with positions and sizes of the wheel housing air outlets changed as well. This car had a very different style from that of the previous R18 e-tron quattro.

Another major difference is the engine. While still a 4L turbocharged diesel, the regenerative energy storage device was changed from an electric flywheel to a lithium-ion battery, and the amount of regenerative energy discharge was increased from 4MJ to 6MJ. The output of the front MGU was also greatly increased from 200 kW (<272ps>) to 350 kW (<476ps>)

In the 2016 World Endurance Championship Series, 2 cars were entered from Audi Sport Team Joest. The R18 raised constant good results by winning 2 races, placing 2nd in 5 races, and 3rd in 2 races. Ultimately they achieved a respectable 2nd place in the Constructors point rankings for the year. However Audi decided to withdraw from the World Endurance Championship Series at the end of this season.0
DescriptionLong.0x00004A55:
The Audi R18 TDI is a prototype race car developed by Audi to run in endurance races such as the famed 24 Hours of Le Mans. This model takes its heritage from a series of diesel-powered race cars such as the R10 in 2006 and the R15 in 2009. However, the major difference compared to previous Audi LMP1 machines is that the car features a closed body again for the first time since the 1999 R8C.

While the previous R15 produced <600ps> from its 5.5-liter V10 turbo powerplant, the R18 produces <540ps> from a 3.7-liter turbocharged V6. The closed-body design was utilized to alleviate this loss of power by improving aerodynamics. The necessity for these changes was due to the car's chief design directive: to incorporate a futuristic hybrid system, which required the car to be as light as possible. This was the main reason for choosing a lighter V6 over a more powerful V8, the cylinder count of which was perfectly allowed by race regulations. The body is, of course, a carbon monocoque, and even the gearbox housing is made of carbon fiber, to save weight. Much thought was also given to designing the 120 degree V6 that mounts a single turbo between the cylinder banks; in doing so, Audi was able to lower the center of gravity and increase airflow on both the intake and exhaust sides of the engine.

The car's racing debut was in the second race of the LMS (Le Mans Series) in May 2011. In the pinnacle of the series—the 24-hour race—the car from Team Joest, driven by Benoît Tréluyer, André Lotterer and Marcel Fässler achieved the ultimate goal, an overall win.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A57:
On August 21, 1989, after a 16-year hiatus following the legendary "Kenmeri" GT-R, the iconic GT-R badge made its triumphant return as part of the eighth-generation Skyline series.

Powering the car was the freshly developed RB26DETT, a twin-turbocharged 2.6-liter DOHC inline-6. Equipped with ceramic turbochargers, the engine delivered <280ps> and <36.0kgm> of torque, while being packed with motorsports-bred technology, including six individual throttle bodies, sodium-filled exhaust valves, and a reinforced cylinder block. The drivetrain featured the groundbreaking ATTESA E-TS system—an electronically controlled, torque-split 4WD system engineered with a clear focus on one goal: enhancing cornering performance.

The suspension employed Nissan’s unique multilink setup at both the front and rear, working in harmony with the brand’s Super HICAS 4-wheel steering system. Aluminum calipers were introduced to the braking system, with 4-pot opposing pistons in front and 2-pot opposing pistons at the rear.

Nissan resurrected the GT-R name with one clear mission: to dominate Group A racing. After pouring its cutting-edge technology into this machine, it became an unstoppable force on the circuit, going on to win race after race.

The company introduced several special variants that pushed the GT-R’s performance even further. This included the limited-edition Nismo model, followed later by the V·Spec and V·Spec II.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A58:
When the new ninth-generation SKYLINE sedan, the R33, was introduced in August 1993, one model was conspicuously missing from the lineup: the GT-R. The R32 GT-R was still being sold at dealerships (all the way through November 1994), and Nissan engineers were working overtime to create a car that surpassed the R32. The car was finally unveiled at the 1993 Tokyo Motor Show, but fans still had to wait until January 1995 for it to hit dealerships.

Many had their doubts whether the R33 could surpass the awesome performance standards set by the R32, but it not only met everyone’s expectations, it surpassed them, proving this in a television commercial called “Minus 21-second Dream.” It showed the R33 running the famed Nürburgring race course 21 seconds faster than the R32.

Under the R33’s hood, which was now made of aluminum along with the front fenders, sat the RB26DETT, but this one was more refined. It pumped out a whopping <280 ps> at <6800 rpm> and <38.2 kgm> of torque at <4400 rpm>. Gear selection was performed through a 5-speed manual gearbox that sent power to all four wheels via Nissan’s ATTESA E-TS all-wheel-drive system. Also included in the handling mix was an active LSD, strut-tower bar and powerful ABS-equipped Brembo brakes.

To commemorate its entrance in the famed 24 Hours of Le Mans race, the LM Limited was introduced in 1996./
DescriptionLong.0x00004A59:
The much anticipated R34 was unveiled in January 1999, armed with a total new approach to styling and technology. The new GT-R was a bit smaller than its predecessor, with a slightly shortened overall length and wheelbase. The new chassis, whose structural rigidity was increased dramatically, made for a car more adept through tight corners. The R34’s exterior styling was based on form over function with all the elements designed to help the car’s aerodynamics, including providing massive amounts of downforce at high speed.

For the engine, the RB26DETT saw significant improvements, including the refinement of the ceramic turbocharger that generated less friction. The 2.6-liter inline-6 was more efficient than before and produced more torque, rated at <40.0 kgm>. Horsepower remained level at <280 ps>, the maximum allowed for JDM cars at the time. The ATTESA-E-TS all-wheel-drive system efficiently managed torque between the four wheels. The R34’s steering system was also tweaked to exhibit more sharpness.

The high-performance V-spec model featured an active LSD (Limited-Slip Differential). The V-spec II, introduced in October 2002, got a carbon-fiber hood with NACA ducts. A better riding version of the GT-R arrived in May 2001 in the form of the M-spec.

As a final hurrah for the R34, in January 2002, Nissan unveiled the most potent GT-R ever, the Nür, whose name was derived from the famous Nürburgring race course in Germany.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5A:
The Audi R8 sports car, whose foundation was based on the "Le Mans quattro" concept car shown in 2003, was a special supercar not only because it was the company's first exotic, but because it was named after the prototype race car that successfully won several consecutive championships at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The body incorporated Audi's ASF technology (Audi Space Frame), a space-frame structure made of aluminum. This helped the weight of the body and shell of the car to weigh a mere <210kg>. Audi cut no corners when it came to quality; most of the body was built by hand, and an X-ray inspection device was used to check all welds at the micron level. The center section of the rear spoiler rose at speeds above <100km/h>, improving the car's aerodynamics at high speed, while dissipating heat from the exhaust when the car was sitting still.

The 4.2 FSI engine, mounted behind the cockpit, is a direct-injection 4.2-liter V8 that produces <420ps>. The power is transferred to all four wheels via the "quattro" all-wheel-drive system, which has now become a hallmark of Audi. A viscous-coupling unit utilized for the center differential distributes 10 to 35 percent of the drive force to the front wheels.

Audi poured all of its latest technology into this supercar, implementing the Magnetic Ride system, which included dampers that utilized magnetic particles, and the R-Tronic gearbox that shifted using hydraulic pressure.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5B:
The Renault R8 Gordini was a sports model released in 1964 as a high-performance version of the compact "8" sedan. The legendary Amédée Gordini tuned the car at Renault’s special request.

The base 8 was full of advanced technology, such as a newly developed five-main engine and class-first disc brakes on all wheels. Gordini took maximum advantage of these tech innovations. The <1108cc> engine, already offering superior revving and endurance characteristics, was an excellent foundation for "The Sorcerer" to build upon. The addition of a cross-flow head with sub-combustion chambers and dual twin-choke carburetors increased engine output to <95ps> without any increase in displacement.

In 1966, the R8 Gordini 1300 was announced, with an actual displacement of <1255cc>. This car pumped out <103ps> and its innovative 5-speed gearbox helped boost top speed by <5km/h> to <175km/h>. The R8 Gordini dominated the Tour de Corse and many other races for three years in a row starting in 1964. From 1966, the world's first single-make series, the "Gordini Cup," became the training ground for French racers and produced many top professional drivers, making this car an icon of the 1960s French motorsports scene. The car is still popular with enthusiasts and collectors who love the distinctive "lunch pail" styling of the R8 Gordini.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5C:
The Audi R8 generated one of the most successful GT3 race cars ever, in the form of the R8 LMS and R8 LMS Ultra. When it came time for a new production R8 to be introduced, in March 2015, Audi took this opportunity to improve the R8 GT3 car, most notably in the safety department.

The second-generation R8 LMS featured crumple zones in front and rear, the “PS1” Audi Protection Seat from LMP machines, and a roof escape, the first ever for GT machine. With all the new safety measures, the new R8 LMS actually exceeded the safety standards of FIA-GT3 regulations for 2016.

The car’s performance was also improved, starting with aerodynamics. The new race car boasted an underbody that was almost completely flat, and came with an enlarged diffuser. Even the air circulation within the cockpit was engineered to minimize wear on the driver.

Despite the fact that the race car shared 50 percent of the parts with its production car sibling, the R8 LMS was a much meaner animal. The R8 LMS was built using the same spaceframe as the production model, but it weighed <25kg> less, thanks to new lighter materials used in the chassis. The powerful V-10, which came off the same line as the production car’s engine, was significantly retuned, and the suspension system was completely replaced. Also, the car’s 6-speed gearbox and traction control were newly developed.

The new R8 LMS made its debut at the Nürburgring 24 Hour Race, and to the surprise of almost no one, it took the overall win in the race.)
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5D:
In the 1980s, Group C represented the most competitive arena for GT racing, prompting Nissan engineers to develop a strong engine for this class: a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-8. This powerplant found a home inside the engine bay of a new, sleek race car called the R89C, which

was co-developed with the British company, Lola.

The R89C waged war in the European World Championships, the American IMSA and the All-Japan GT Championships, as well as the 24 Hours of Le Mans. As Nissan began development on its own chassis to house the powerful engine, those plans were scrapped when the FIA revised the regulations for the Group C class, prohibiting turbocharged engines. So while Nissan began development of a new Group C car for race series abroad, it refined its racer for Japan, where the regulations remained unchanged. The R89C eventually made way for the R92CP. With <900ps> on tap, the car's revised VRH35 engine allowed it to reach <400km/h> on the front straight at Fuji Speedway, generating 3.5 tons of downforce. An even more powerful version was tuned for Le Mans, which pumped out <1200ps>.

The new race car was most successful in Japan, winning all six All-Japan Championship races it entered.C
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5E:
The NSX CONCEPT-GT was Honda’s entry into the GT500 class of the Super GT series, competing from 2014 to 2016. It was based on the NSX concept car unveiled by Honda in 2012, which previewed the forthcoming production model of the new-generation NSX. The concept employed a hybrid powertrain that combined a mid-mounted V-6 engine with electric motors.

Like other GT500 machines, the NSX Concept GT was built under the 2014 regulations that aligned with DTM technical standards. Unlike its rivals, however, it featured a midship-mounted turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 with direct injection—developed within a unified format across manufacturers. It also incorporated a hybrid system similar to the production car. However, to prevent the system from providing an unfair advantage, a minimum weight was imposed, and strict limits were placed on both the electric assist output and energy usage.

While the car faced numerous challenges during its debut season in 2014, performance improved significantly in 2015. In 2016, however, Honda encountered supply issues from its battery manufacturer, forcing the team to compete without the hybrid system. The Raybrig NSX CONCEPT-GT was one of the standout cars in this program. In 2014, with Takashi Kogure and Hideki Mutoh at the helm, it finished 11th in the team rankings. In 2015, driven by Naoki Yamamoto and Takuya Izawa, it climbed to an impressive 3rd place in the series standings. However, 2016 proved difficult for all Honda teams, with the season ending in a disappointing 12th place.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A5F:
While German luxury carmakers have traditionally defined the luxury sports coupe market, Lexus decided to join the fray with a svelte version all its own called the RC F. Introduced at the 2014 North American International Auto Show, the RC F is the sportiest entry of the RC line—the letter “F,” which references Fuji Speedway, is added to all of the brand’s high-performance models.

Under the hood is a 5.0-liter V-8, the same powerplant found in the IS F, with new titanium valves, forged connecting rods, newly designed cylinder heads and custom exhaust system. They combine to help the engine produce <456ps>/<53.0kgm>, which is <33ps> and <1.5kgm> more than the IS F. It comes mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission that performs lightning-quick shifts via paddles near the steering wheel.

The Sports Mode of the VDIM, which centrally controls vehicle dynamics, has been refined for the racetrack, and most of the electronic devices have been updated. The RC F features the first torque-vectoring system in the world to be incorporated into a front-engine/rear-wheel drive car. This system allows drivers of all levels to enjoy the RC F’s excellent handling balance and overall performance.

With the exception of the limited-edition LFA supercar, the RC F is the sportiest model to ever come from Lexus.\
DescriptionLong.0x00004A60:
While Lexus ran an RC F-based race car for the VLN and Super GT Series in 2015, it was allowed to compete with this particular car without

having to adhere to homologation requirements. The RC F GT3 Prototype made its debut in Round 9 of the VLN series and won the SPX class, which allowed specially permitted entries.

This prototype race car was developed with the intent of eventually providing a GT3 machine to race teams around the world. Starting out as an RC F, the entire car was altered dramatically to ensure competitiveness and reliability in GT3 races. Weight was significantly reduced and the body drastically stiffened; the front and rear fenders were swapped to improve aerodynamics; and power from the 5.0-liter V-8 engine was increased to <540ps>. Ultimately, the car was homologated and introduced as the Lexus RC F GT3 in 2017.

The following year, the new race car was delivered to Emil Frey Racing in Switzerland, which took part in the development of the RC F GT3. Participating in the GT Open Championship of Europe, the team won four of 14 races and placed 3rd for the season.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A61:
When Lexus introduced the RC luxury sports coupe in 2014, it also included a high-performance version in the lineup called the RC F, which served as the foundation for the RC F GT3 race car.

Created to compete in GT3 races around the world, the RC F GT3 was developed at the same time as the production RC F. The original V-8 engine was converted to have a dry sump lubrication system, and displacement was increased to 5.4 liters. Mated to a 6-speed sequential gearbox, the race engine produced <500ps>. Although it looks larger than the production car because of its wider fenders, the RC F GT3 tipped the scales at a lean <1300kg>.

Starting in the 2017 season, the RC F GT3 waged battle in the American IMSA series (GTD category), the European International GT Open series, and the Japanese Super GT series (GT300 class), where it performed admirably.

In the International GT race at Silverstone, the RC F GT3 grabbed its first victory. Then in Japan, it won for the first time in the Super GT series, taking the checkered flag in the second-round race at the Fuji Speedway.

The RC F GT3 prototype represented here is a car that was built for performance evaluation before the RC F GT3 acquired homologation. This car won the ninth race of the VLN (Nürburgring Endurance Series) on October 8, 2016, running without a paint job and its carbon-fiber body fully exposed. The car here, though, wears the livery of Emil Frey Racing, a top Swiss team that competes in the International GT Open.X

While the RC F’s appearance is similar to that of the base model, Lexus designers incorporated subtle-yet-functional details that help improve performance. These include air outlets on the engine hood and at the rear end of the front fenders. On the trunk is a variable rear spoiler that changes angles automatically according to speed.

With the exception of the limited-edition LFA supercar, the RC F is the sportiest model to ever come from Lexus.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.O
DescriptionLong.0x00004A63:
At the Peugeot booth of the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show, there was a concept car displayed with flowing lines: the “308 RCZ”. This sports car was notable for its wide and low silhouette, with a cabin offset forward due to its midship layout. From the center of the roof to the rear glass, a double-bubble design was utilized, giving it a unique style.

This was a design study based on the 308, but it gathered a lot of attention, with many fans wanting to see the car actually produced. To answer their call, the car was finally released in 2010 with a style that was virtually unchanged from the prototype. It was named with no 308 designation but simply as the “RCZ”.

The engine is a 1.6-liter inline 4-cylinder turbo, with two models producing <156ps> and <200ps> respectively. The <200ps> version is given an engine that becomes more lively as the engine RPM becomes higher, and a suspension system carried over from the original 308 series is made stiffer for sports driving. The combination gave the car a level of performance that provided a fulfilling sports driving experience.

Then in 2012, the RCZ underwent a minor change. This was mostly a stylistic change with the opening of the grille made smaller, the addition of a black light unit and LED position lights, and the overall facelift of the front end, giving it a chic style and appearance.

The GT Line is a grade model added from 2015, with a special front grille, double exhaust pipes, 19-inch wheels, and red stitched black leather interior for a sportier look.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A68:
*The Eunos Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5 in Europe and as the Mazda MX-5 Miata in the U.S.

The Eunos Roadster captured the imagination of the world as soon as it made its appearance in September 1989. We know it better as the Miata, and it revived the category of the lightweight convertible sports car, bringing the classic genre back into the limelight. With a compact body, rear-wheel-drive and a simple, and yet straightforward 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4, the Eunos Roadster was as fun to drive as it was good-looking.

It came powered by the 1.6-liter Type B6-ZE that produced <120 ps> and <14.0 kgm> of torque. The suspension system consisted of double wishbones at all four corners, while the brakes were discs at both the front and rear.

Mazda wanted to make sure that its new creation acted like part of the driver's body, going wherever the driver wanted in an effortless way. Thus, the phrase "rider, horse, one body" was adopted as its guiding principle.

In August 1993, a new engine, the 1.8-liter DOHC Type BP-ZE, was placed under the hood, with the output increased to <130 ps> and <16.0 kgm> of torque. The next round of changes came in August 1995 when the final gear ratio and flywheel were modified, thus creating the 1800 Series 2. Mazda produced 531,890 units through the end of 1997, setting a world record for production of a 2-passenger open vehicle, an achievement recorded by the Guinness Book of World Records.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A69:
*The Eunos Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5 in Europe and as the Mazda MX-5 Miata in the U.S.

This original car created by "Gran Turismo" is based on the 1989 Mazda Eunos Roadster (NA Special Package). The following is the description of the base model:

The Eunos Roadster captured the imagination of the world as soon as it made its appearance in September 1989. We know it better as the Miata, and it revived the category of the lightweight convertible sports car, bringing the classic genre back into the limelight. With a light and compact body, rear-wheel-drive and a simple-yet-straightforward 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4, the Roadster was as fun to drive as it was good-looking.

It came powered by the 1.6-liter Type B6-ZE that produced <120ps> and <14.0kgm> of torque. The suspension system consisted of double wishbones at all four corners, while the brakes were discs at both the front and rear.

Mazda produced 531,890 units through the end of 1997, setting a world record for production of a 2-passenger open vehicle, a fact recorded by the Guinness Book of World Records.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6B:
One look and almost anyone in the world can recognize Mazda’s sporty convertible sports car that's proved so popular that it made its way into the Guinness Book of World Records. While it goes by different names throughout the world, the Roadster in Japan, the MX-5 in Europe and the MX-5 Miata in the US, we’ll refer to it simply as the MX-5 here.

The fourth-generation MX-5, codenamed “ND,” was introduced at the New York Auto Show in April 2014. It was obvious from this “display only” model that the car possessed all the attributes to make it great, returning to the formula that made the first-generation model so successful. It was going to be lighter than the outgoing model, with most of the heavy components, including the driver, focused at the center of the chassis.

When the final exterior and interior design of the MX-5 was revealed simultaneously in the US, Japan and Europe in September of the same year, driving fans were excited. The new MX-5 looked sleek and sexy, sitting low to the ground with a wide stance. The car, slightly smaller than the previous model, was more in line with the first generation car. It measured <3915mm> long, <1735mm> wide and <1235mm> high, and rode on a <2310mm>-wheelbase. It tipped the scales from <990kg> to <1060kg>, depending on the grade model.

Powering the compact roadster was a <1496cc> DOHC inline-4 that delivered <131ps> and <15.3kgm> of torque. It came mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox or an automatic transmission with a torque converter. The combination of the lightweight package, peppy engine and manual gearbox made the “ND” one of the most rewarding cars to drive on the planet, and it reminded everyone of how enjoyable top-down motoring can truly be.

*The Mazda Roadster was sold as the Mazda MX-5 in Europe and the Mazda MX-5 Miata in the US.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6C:
Renault Sport has been transforming Renault cars into exclusive high-performance machines for many years. The division created the R.S.01 in the summer of 2014 to participate in a one-make race series, especially for its fan base of hardcore enthusiasts.

The R.S.01 illustrates the deep working partnership between Renault and Nissan. Its carbon monocoque chassis was co-developed by Renault and Dallara, while the exterior styling was executed by a Nissan designer. The car measures <4710mm> from bumper to bumper and sits <2000mm> wide. It tips the scales at a lean <1100kg>, making it quick and agile. Nissan was also responsible for providing the power unit, a Nismo-tuned VR38DETT from the Nissan GT-R. The twin-turbocharged V-6 produced <550ps> in the R.S.01.

Renault Sport also produced another version of this race car called the R.S.01 GT3. As the name suggests, it met FIA's GT3 homologation rules. Because of this, the GT3 version wasn't as hardcore as its stablemate, with steel disc brakes rather than carbon and less engine power. However, because the GT3 category has become the most popular category in sports car racing, it presents an ideal opportunity for the R.S.01 to showcase its amazing potential for all the world to see.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6D:
Created for a special one-make race series introduced in 2015 called the “World Series by Renault”—the successor to the Mégane Trophy—the Renault Sport R.S.01 was a limited-edition competition machine that defined the term “pocket rocket,” thanks in part to a power unit straight from the Nissan GT-R. itself.

Utilizing a carbon monocoque developed together with Italian race car constructor Dallara, the Sport R.S.01 was extremely lightweight, tipping the scales at a lean <1100kg>. Power was supplied by Nissan’s twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter V-6 found in the Nissan GT-R, which was further tuned by NISMO. The engine, mounted amidships, produced more than <500ps> and <61.2kgm> of torque. It came mated to an SADEV 7-speed sequential gearbox that helped the car reach a maximum speed of more than <300km/h>.

In November 2015, Renault introduced a GT3 version of this car at the Paul Ricard Circuit in France, developed for the FIA-GT Championships. The R.S.01 GT3 had to be tamed considerably to meet GT3 regulations, so a restrictor was added to the engine to decrease power. Also, the brakes were changed from carbon ceramic to steel discs. To meet the minimum weight specified by the FIA, more than <50kg> of ballast was added to the chassis, and the aerodynamics were also revised. All the changes just confirmed how potent the original was.[
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6E:
The MAZDA RX-VISION is a concept car introduced at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show. Based on Mazda’s "KODO - Soul of Motion" design theme, the car represented Mazda's attempt to create the most beautiful FR sports car in the company's history. It came powered by the next-generation rotary engine called "SKYACTIV-R."

Back in 1967, Mazda overcame numerous obstacles to produce the first commercial rotary engine in history. It powered the Cosmo Sport and then was fitted to a number of other Mazda cars, including the RX-7, and even those that raced. In 1991, the four-rotor Mazda 787B became the first Japanese car to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The MAZDA RX-VISION GT3 CONCEPT expresses the design beauty of form following function in a race machine. To meet the performance requirements of the Gr.3 category, the design was inspired by the 787B, specifically the 4-rotor powerplant, now equipped with SKYACTIV technology. This new rotary engine was mounted in a lightweight body to achieve unprecedented performance.E
DescriptionLong.0x00004A6F:
Created to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Toyo Kogyo (Mazda), the RX500 concept car was introduced to the world in 1970. It featured the company's revolutionary rotary engine, which made its debut in the Cosmo Sport three years prior, and an unforgettable bullet-shaped body that focused on aerodynamics.

The designers of the car experimented with several different versions of the RX500, including a coupe with a beautiful rear section and a race car with a rear wing, but opted to go for the car you see here because of its superior Cd (drag coefficient) value of 0.31. In terms of styling, the car was truly before its time; for example, its upswing doors were introduced before those of the Lamborghini Countach.

The powerplant, mounted amidships in a steel-tube space frame, was a 10A rotary engine built for the company's Spa 24 Hours race car and produced more than <250ps>. It came mated to a 4-speed manual gearbox from the RX87 Luce Rotary Coupe. Top speed was expected to exceed <250km/h>, and the brake system featured 4-piston calipers and 4-wheel ventilated discs, which represented cutting-edge technology for that time, as only a very few racing cars boasted a similar set-up.7
DescriptionLong.0x00004A70:
By the time the second-generation RX-7, the FC3S, arrived in October 1985, Mazda had firmly established the model as a competent rotary-powered sports machine. Although the new model was shorter than the previous car, it was wider and slightly taller, resulting in a 200-kg weight increase. The newly designed 13B Wankel did more than compensate for the extra mass, as the turbocharged 654-cc powerplant produced <185ps> and <25.0kgm> of torque. To keep the rear end more secure, Mazda incorporated semi-trailing arms and lateral rods for the rear suspension that featured a toe control hub.

An even purer sports version of the car was introduced in August 1986, called the Infini. This limited-edition model was a two-seater, and featured, among other things, BBS alloy wheels, firmer shocks and an aluminum hood. The Infini name would make an appearance seven times, each time representing the sportiest version of the model, before production of the FC3S ceased in 1991.

Mazda made significant tweaks to the RX-7 in 1989, when it matched a new independent twin-scroll turbocharger to the 13B as well as raising the engine's compression ratio. The result was a power increase to <205 ps> and <27.5kgm>. The final Infini model saw the power of the 13B raised to <215 ps> and <28.0kgm>. A convertible model was added to the lineup in 1987, which proved popular in the U.S., especially with women.h
DescriptionLong.0x00004A71:
Arguably, one of the purest sports cars to come from Japan is the third-generation RX-7 (FD3S) that was introduced in 1991. Gone was the name "Savanna" that graced previous models, replaced by the moniker, ɛ̃fini RX-7. The FD3S was wider than the FC, and significantly lighter at <1200kg>, thanks to the aluminum used for the hood, double wishbone suspension, and spare-tire jack.

New life was breathed into the 13B Wankel via new twin sequential turbochargers. The rotary engine produced <255ps> and <30.0kgm> of torque. With each passing year, the FD improved, with dramatic improvements in body rigidity and ABS. The weight-to-power ratio of the lighter Type S was <4.90kg/ps>, making it the fastest RX-7 to date.

The FD3S continued to evolve. Body rigidity, the computer, and ABS were upgraded. The Type I, created in 1991, led to the Type II, Type III, and the Type VI in 2000. Available only in the Japan market was the limited-edition Type RZ, the first Japanese car equipped with 40/45 low-profile tires. This was followed by the Type R Bathurst R in 2001 that came equipped with self-leveling shocks.

The 13B got an upgrade in 1996 and produced <265ps>. In 1998, after Mazda refined the engine's cooling system, the two-rotor Wankel was able to produce the maximum <280ps> allowed for JDM cars at the time. This allowed the Type R to boast a weight-to-power ratio of <4.50kg/ps>, which put it in the same league as the exotics. In August 2002, the RX-7 Spirit R was introduced as an anniversary model and became the last one in the series. After 25 years of delighting sports car fans around the world, the RX-7 was discontinued.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A72:
The S-FR was a concept car that the company claimed to “provide perfect control in an entry model, allowing the driver to enjoy interacting with the car in its everyday use.”

One look at the body, and the connection to the Sport 800 was obvious by its long nose and rounded body, but the lines and general design of the car had been updated to incorporate modern styling cues.

The only specifications Toyota released for the car were its measurements. It rode on a <2480mm>-wheelbase, while its overall dimensions were <3990mm>, <1695mm>, and <1320mm>, length, width and height, respectively. The four-passenger vehicle possessed a front/rear weight distribution of 50/50 with two passengers on board. The gearbox was designated as a 6-speed manual.

At the 2016 Tokyo Auto Salon, Toyota displayed the S-FR Racing Concept. Based on the S-FR, it featured a number of carbon fiber aerodynamic parts, including fender flares, front spoilers, canards and a large rear wing. Toyota showed that its exciting new concept was sporty enough to become a track-only model if customers so desired.m
DescriptionLong.0x00004A73:
The Toyota made a splash at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show when it unveiled the S-FR. The sporty car was compact, measuring only <3990mm> in overall length and sitting <1695mm> wide. It weighed a mere <980kg>, which meant that this stylish car with the long nose and short rear deck was quick and fun to drive. Despite the fact that Toyota said it had no plans to produce the car, it nonetheless generated quite a bit of interest from the show goers.

The race version of this car, called the S-FR Racing Concept, was introduced at the 2016 Tokyo Auto Salon. This concept vehicle sported flared fenders, increasing the S-FR's width by <20mm> on each side. Other visual enhancements included a large air outlet on the hood, carbon-fiber front spoiler, rear wing, side skirts and rear diffuser. The end result was a car that appeared to be a serious GT racing machine.

While the road-going S-FR's overall height was <1320mm>, the race car sat <50mm> lower, at <1270mm>. Underneath sheet metal, the suspension was lowered and most likely stiffened, while the front brakes utilize drilled disks and horizontally opposed 4-pot calipers.

No details regarding the engine were offered, and there was no mention of it actually going on sale.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A74:
The Nissan Silvia, called the 240SX in the States, had a loyal following since it was first introduced in 1988 because of its extremely sporty nature and head-turning good looks.

The most popular version was the 5th-generation model, which many felt was the best looking in the car's lineage. Produced from 1988 through 1993 and dubbed the S13, the stylish coupe was also heralded by the media, garnering Japan Car of the Year honors for 1988. It would eventually go on to become the best-selling Silvia ever. The top-of-the-line version was the K model, powered by Nissan's CA18DET, a turbocharged DOHC inline-4 that produced <175ps>/<6400rpm> and <23.0kgm> of torque at <4000rpm>.

From the driver's seat, the engine felt much more powerful, thanks mainly to the car's lean curb weight of <1140kg>. Its straight-line prowess and finely-tuned suspension that included a compliant multilink setup at the rear made the FR (Front drive/Rear engine) sports coupe a true driver's car that was capable on both winding roads and the open highway.

In February 1990, a Diamond Select Edition was added to the lineup. This special model offered an array of optional features that included automatic climate control, aluminum wheels and a rear spoiler, allowing prospective owners to tailor their car toward either a grand tourer or pure sports car.*
DescriptionLong.0x00004A75:
Tapped as the savior of the brand, the seventh-generation Silvia made its debut in January 1999 amid the S14's struggle in the marketplace. Returning to basics, the S15 came with a more compact body, one more like the popular S13. This was Nissan's way of saying that the new Silvia wasn't intended to be luxurious, but very sports minded.

Under the hood was the same SR20 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 that powered both the S13 and S14, only it was more refined than ever. The naturally aspirated variants produced <165ps> and <19.6kgm> of torque, while the turbocharged version pumped out <250ps> and <28.0kgm> of torque. The S15 was offered in two main trim levels: the naturally aspirated Spec S and the turbocharged Spec R that boasted a weight-to-power ratio of <4.96kg/ps>.

Retaining key components of the S13 and S14 chassis, Nissan drastically increased body rigidity, which improved handling. The S15s also received a helical LSD.

To broaden the car's appeal even more, a convertible version of the Spec S, called the Varietta, was introduced in 2000. However this year also marked the beginning of the end for the Silvia because it wasn't able to meet Japan's exhaust emission standards for 2000. Production of the S15 stopped in August 2002, marking the end of the 38-year Silvia dynasty that started in 1965.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A77:
The Honda S2000 was a revolutionary car that symbolized the company’s future direction in sports cars. It possessed technology that trickled down from its deep association with motorsports, thus, the S2000 was like a Formula 1 car for the road, from its high-revving engine to its engine-start button. The S2000’s true roots came from Honda’s S series from the 1960s. The S500, S600 and S800 were the S2000’s forefathers, all two-seat convertible sports cars with FR (Front engine, Rear drive) configurations.

The S500, released in 1963, embodied Honda’s philosophy of the engine and suspension working together harmoniously for maximum results and pleasure. Honda revived this philosophy for the modern age and instilled it into the S2000. Every component of the car was custom-built, including the super-rigid open monocoque “X-bone frame” chassis. The engine was as race-oriented as they came in a production car. The F20C, a 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 featured an amazing 9000-rpm redline, with power rated at <250ps>. It also boasted excellent fuel economy. Mated to the engine was a sturdy 6-speed manual gearbox whose throws were short and well-defined. In July 2000, the S2000 Type V was added to the lineup, featuring the VGS system that electrically controlled the steering ratio according to speed and turning angle. Aerodynamics and suspension were reworked in 2007, giving birth to the Type S with enhanced drivability on winding roads.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A78:
While kei-cars aren’t necessarily known to be fun to drive, there are a few exceptions, such as the Honda S660, which was introduced to the Japan market in 2015. This super compact convertible was the spiritual successor to the popular Honda Beat that was discontinued back in 1996.

Like the Beat, the new S660 sports a mid-engine layout. The exterior is characterized by an entirely new look, with sharp lines and smooth curves. Ultra-high-tensile steel comprises 60 percent of the car, including the center tunnel, side sills and side frame. The rear subframe is composed of die-cast aluminum. All this helps keep the S660’s curb weight down to a low <800kg>, while maintaining the twisting rigidity that surpassed even that of the S2000.

The roof is a variation of a targa top, where only a portion of it can be removed. The soft top can also be rolled and removed, to be stored in a box under the front hood.

Powering the S660 is a turbocharged <660cc> DOHC inline-3 that produces <64ps> and <10.6kgm> of torque. It comes mated to a close-ratio 6-speed manual gearbox or a paddle-shift CVT with sports mode. Stopping the car are disc brakes at both front and rear.

The suspension consists of struts at all four corners. A torque vectoring system reduces understeer by slightly applying the brakes on the inside front wheel. Thanks to the lightweight and the S660’s remarkable chassis, it’s one of the best handling cars, kei or otherwise, in the world.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A79:
Having dominated the world of two-wheeled racing at the Isle of Man TT, World GP, and more, Honda moved into to the world of four-wheeled cars in 1963. The company's first example was an ultra compact, two-seat sports car called the S500. Soichiro Honda, the founder of Honda Motors, shocked the world by building a sports car from scratch.

But this decision made sense because it was easier for a motorcycle manufacturer to to build a sports car than a sedan because it was much simpler in structure. So the company utilized all the know-how they gained in producing motorcycles into building the S500, a car that lined up with the company's already-established sporty image.

After the debut of the S500 in 1963, Honda produced the S600 the following year, equipped with a more powerful engine. That was followed by a special fastback coupe that performed well in racing. Back then, and even today, the world had never seen a car that could rev up to <10000rpm> in stock form. Two years later, the S800 with an even larger engine was added, and when the improved S800M made its appearance, the Honda sports car had finally come into its own, now equipped with a true automotive 4-wheel suspension system.

Starting with the S800, the Honda Sport series featured an exceptionally short shifter, only <10cm> in length, which allowed effortless shifting from the low seating position. Delivering a true sports car experience and driving feel, these cars would become popular classics the world over."
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7A:
Spearheaded by Swiss car constructor Sauber, the C9 appeared in 1988 as a Group C car. Beginning in 1986, Mercedes-Benz began supplying Sauber with Group C engines, and two years after that, Mercedes-Benz officially announced Sauber as its motorsports partner, forming a partnership committed to building GT race cars. This marked the first time since 1955 that Mercedes-Benz built GT race cars, ever since a big accident at the 24 Hours of Le Mans forced the company out of motorsports.

The Sauber Mercedes-Benz C9 met with success immediately, earning pole position in the opener for the 1988 WSPC (World Sportscar Championship) and going on to win five of 12 races that year. In 1989, Mercedes-Benz replaced the turbocharged 5.0-liter SOHC V-8 with a 4-valve version that increased power to <720ps>. The restyled C9 looked imposing, bathed in silver paint and was christened with the nickname "Silver Arrow," a reference to the legendary Mercedes-Benz (and Auto Union) Grand Prix cars during the Golden Age of Racing.

That year, the Silver Arrows finished 1-2 at the World Sportscar Championship at Suzuka Circuit and 2-3 at Dijon. At the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Silver Arrows finished 1-2, and another car finishing 5th. In 1988, with seven wins in eight races, Jean-Louis Schlesser became the Drivers' Champion and Sauber took the team title.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7B:
Thanks to its sporty and stylish nature, the Volkswagen Scirocco became a popular 3-door model in the 1970s and 80s; however, it ultimately faded into automotive oblivion by the early 1990s. Just when we thought we heard the last of the Scirocco, it made a triumphant return in 2008 as a hot new hatchback based on the popular VW Golf platform.

The new Scirocco continues where the last one left off, offering plenty of sport for the economy-minded enthusiast. Its turbo-/supercharged 1.4-liter TSI engine gained high praise for its performance when it debuted in 2008, but the following year, an even better powerplant was introduced under the hood of the hot Scirocco R. This car was so impressive that it won its class in the Nürburgring 24-hour race two years in a row.

The Scirocco R's lowered ride height and wide body hinted at its high-performance nature: it wore special side skirts and a roof spoiler reminiscent of the successful Nürburgring race car. Its suspension and brakes were greatly improved, and the 2.0-liter TSI direct-injection turbocharged engine produced an impressive <256ps> at <6000rpm>—the same as the Golf R. But while the Golf R utilized 4-Motion all-wheel drive, the Scirocco remained front-wheel drive to keep its weight low. As a result, it is <120kg> lighter than the Golf R at <1410kg>.

With its dynamic engine sound, sharp cornering capability and convenient utility, the Volkswagen Scirocco is the rare car that fulfills every boy racer's heart for spirited driving while also serving the role as everyday commuter.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A7D:
The Nissan 180SX — sold as the Nissan 240SX in the U.S. and the 200SX in the EU — was created as the Silvia's sister hatchback model in March 1989. This car, sporting retractable headlights and a glass hatchback, was overshadowed by the coupe at first—despite sharing the same powerplant, a 1.8-liter DOHC inline-4 that came available only with a turbocharger. But as time went on, people recognized the true value of the stylish fastback and sales began to climb.

The engine received an upgrade in 1991 to the SR20DET, the same 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 in the normal Silvia with output rated at <205ps> and <28.0kgm>. This prolonged the 180SX's life span because its production run was initially slated to end alongside the S13 Silvia; however, thanks to the popularity of the 2.4-liter 240SX in the U.S. (that possessed the same body shape of 180SX), Nissan elected to keep the compact rear-drive coupe around.

In 1996, the first normally-aspirated 180SX, the Type S, was added to the lineup. Without forced induction, the Type S lacked the acceleration of the hotter version. This made the car a favorite among tuners, who took things into their own hands, giving the car their own dose of power and beefing the chassis up accordingly. This paved the way for a new 180SX, one that featured the Silvia's front end, making the two cars virtual clones of each other; it was dubbed the "Sil-Eighty."
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7E:
The concept version of the Mercedes-Benz Vision SLR was unveiled at the North American International Auto Show in Detroit in 1999. It was the talk of the town, and everyone wondered if Mercedes-Benz was indeed going to build this supercar. The answer came at the 2003 Frankfurt Motor Show when a production version of the car was displayed. As the name suggests, the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren was built alongside McLaren Automotive of Formula 1 fame.

The SLR McLaren was a supercar of the highest order. It featured a carbon-fiber unitized body, ensuring low weight, which, by the way, was a lean <1768kg>, more than <200kg> lighter than the SL 55 AMG. Under its hood sat a supercharged 5.5-liter V8 with dry-sump lubrication that produced a whopping <625ps> at <6500 rpm> and <79.6kgm> of torque from <3250 rpm> to <5000 rpm>. The SLR had the same 5-speed automatic that the SL used, but added sport, comfort and manual settings.

The brakes featured SBC (Sensotronic Brake Control), a brake-by-wire system, with carbon-ceramic discs at all four corners. The front calipers were 8-pot Brembos while the rears, also Brembo, had 4 pots. The suspension system consisted of double wishbones at all four corners.

The SLR boasted an amazing weight-to-power ratio of <2.8kg/ps>, which allowed the car to accelerate from zero to <100km/h> in 3.8 seconds. Top speed: a cool <334 km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A7F:
The SLS AMG, with gull wing doors that paid homage to the classic 300 SL, bowed at the 2009 Frankfurt Motor Show. This exotic sports car, built from the ground up by AMG, made its debut in Japan in September of the same year, but not at an auto show or a Mercedes-Benz dealership; rather, it was featured in the "Gran Turismo" booth at the Tokyo Game Show.

Many considered the SLS AMG to be the successor of the SLR McLaren, but the body structure of the two cars were quite different. The SLS AMG did away with the costly carbon monocoque body of the SLR McLaren and instead came with an all-aluminum platform. The sacrifice in weight savings was nominal as the aluminum monocoque frame weighed only <241kg>, allowing the SLS AMG to tip the scales at a lean <1600kg>. This is quite impressive for a car that stretches more than <4600mm> from front to rear.

Mounted just aft of the front axle was a new 6.3-liter V8 with dry-sump lubrication, dubbed internally as the M159. It produced <571ps>/<6800rpm> with a peak torque of <66.3kgm>/<4750rpm>, and came mated to a newly developed 7-speed DCT (dual clutch transmission) in a trans-axle layout. Of note, the driveshaft and torque tube were composed of carbon fiber.

The car featured five driving modes: "Comfort," "Sports," "Sports Plus," "Manual," and "Launch Start." Mercedes-Benz claimed that the SLS AMG could sprint from zero to <100km/h> in 3.8 seconds, and reach a top speed of <317km/h>. Thanks to a front/rear weight distribution of 47:53 and a sport-tuned suspension, the SLS AMG could handle with the best of them. Fifty years after the first 300 SL rolled off the line, the SLS AMG marks the rebirth of M-B's ultimate sports car, one graced with elegant styling and great performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A80:
In 2009, the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG was introduced at the Frankfurt Motor Show.

This supercar was developed independently by AMG, the high-performance development arm of Mercedes-Benz also responsible for the company's motorsports activities. The car sparked a worldwide sensation, thanks to its incredible high performance and gull winged doors that were reminiscent of the historic 300SL.

Mounted front amidships within the all-aluminum space frame was the M159, a tuned 6.2-liter V8 based on the AMG 63 series engine. Producing <571ps>/<66.3kgm> of torque, and combined with a Getrag 7-speed DCT, it went 0-<100km/h> in 3.8 seconds and hit a top speed of <317km/h>.

The SLS AMG GT3 was a racing car based on this SLS AMG, modified to comply with FIA-GT3 regulations. The front and rear bumpers and side sills have been modified and an adjustable wing was added in the rear. The front/rear fenders were widened, and a cooling duct was incorporated to the hood. Aside from being fully functional, the styling is notably more aggressive. Its engine is shared with the production SLS, but although there are no official figures, it is said to have been massaged to exceed <600ps>.

The transmission was swapped for a racing-style 6-speed sequential gearbox with paddle shifters. Composite brakes were fitted with a competition-level ABS, the steering was made direct ratio, and the car was given a special adjustable suspension.

This machine competed from the beginning of 2011, and out of the 101 races it contested, it won 25 times.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A82:
With its compact and lightweight body, the Toyota Sports 800 was one of the most admired sports cars of its day. It made its debut in 1965, and represented Toyota's first production sports car. Known in Japan as the "Yota-Hachi" a vernacular phrase for "Toyota Eight," it also was the first Japanese car to feature a targa top and removable roof panel.

As a sports car, it was cleverly designed. It aimed for simplicity rather than complicated mechanics, so many parts came from its popular boxy passenger-car, the Publica. The Yota-Hachi was smaller than the Publica, with an overall length of <3580mm>.

The engine was a <790cc> flat-2 with two carburetors helping it to produce <45ps>. Although it wasn't as powerful as other sports cars, its lean <580kg> curb weight allowed it to behave like a true performance machine on the road. The FR (Front engine, Rear drive) exhibited adequate punch off the line and was able to reach <155km/h>, performance comparable to cars with <1500cc> engines.

Thanks in part to the Publica's wide tread and low center of gravity, the Sports 800 demonstrated exceptional agility on the twisty stuff, with sharp turn-in response and near neutral handling balance. Its main rival was the Honda S800, and oftentimes, the Sports 800 battled the little Honda on both road and track.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A83:
The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo is an uncompromizing, unrestricted single-seat mid-engine, all-wheel-drive vehicle.

Its main powerplant is a nearly flat, 144-degree 6.98-liter V-10 that produces more than 1000 hp, supported by a pneumatic sub-unit. With four levels of assistance, the pneumatic power unit uses regenerative braking to compress air and store it into two pneumatic cylinders, then releases it when it’s required. This unit is also used for the suspension system.

The handling dynamics of the Tomahawk are enhanced by a continuously active aerodynamic system that deploys multiple pneumatically driven elements, including a rear wing and a secondary front splitter. The Tomahawk’s aerodynamic system reacts to inputs provided by a forward scanning laser system that detects surface changes in front of the car. The computer controls anticipate changes in vehicle ride height, pitch and yaw to adjust the splitter accordingly. The exhaust of the V-10 is routed to the rear diffuser. This accelerates underbody flow at the rear of the car and creates a blown diffuser effect that increases downforce with no negative effect on drag. 

The GTS-R is the lightest and race-ready version of the Tomahawk concept. The extreme g-forces resulting from its immense power output, its extremely lightweight nature and enhanced handling are more than what the human body can handle unassisted. Therefore, the driver requires a special racing suit that pressurizes the body to maintain blood flow to the brain. This G-suit uses excess pressurized air from the pneumatic power system, allowing it to quickly react to increasing g-forces. 

The Tomahawk GTS-R’s aerodynamics are enhanced with a dual-element version of the active rear wing. The upper element is stored beneath the lower element when it’s not in use or during high-speed straightaway speed. DescriptionLong.0x00004A85:
The SRT Tomahawk Vision Gran Turismo is a near-future supercar created by Dodge's in-house tuning department, SRT (Street and Racing Technology). This mean machine features next-generation automobile technologies that includes high-tech materials throughout the chassis and a road-surface-sensing active aerodynamics system. Providing the muscle is a 1000-hp V-10 engine mated to pneumatic power units.

This version is based on the race spec GTS-R, the lightest model in the series. After overhauling the body, the stock car’s active aero parts were scrapped in favor of a fixed rear wing and an aero fin mounted aft of the cockpit. 

To reduce weight, the pneumatic power units were removed, while the engine was tuned to produce <703ps>. The power train layout has also been changed from all-wheel drive to rear-wheel drive to comply with regulations. 

While it is no longer capable of extreme speeds that transcends the limits of the human body, its superb handling and aerodynamic control remain intact. In endurance races, this model will no doubt put great fear into your opponents.(

DescriptionLong.0x00004A87:
At the 1970 Turin Motor Show, Bertone unveiled a striking concept car called the Stratos Zero. With its radical wedge-shaped profile and a front windshield that doubled as the door, the vehicle was conceived purely as a design study. But even then, Bertone described it as a mid-engine concept. Following the show, development began in collaboration with Lancia, which was in search of a new rally car to succeed the Fulvia.

Marcello Gandini was tasked with refining the concept into a production-ready model. Drawing inspiration from the shape of the Stratos Zero, he created an angular body that echoed its otherworldly name: Stratosphere. Thus, the legendary Lancia Stratos was born.

The Stratos featured a robust welded steel monocoque chassis clad in lightweight fiberglass panels. Mounted behind the seats was the same 2.4-liter DOHC V-6 engine found in the Ferrari Dino 246 GT.

Its performance potential was evident in its dimensions: an exceptionally short wheelbase of just <2180 mm> and a wide rear tread of <1457 mm>. This configuration delivered razor-sharp handling and extremely sensitive response. For those who could master its traits, the Stratos offered extraordinary performance that translated into rally dominance, ushering in a golden era for Lancia on the world stage.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A88:
Vision Gran Turismo is a revolutionary project established for car enthusiasts all over the world. The car provided by Subaru for this dream project, where the world's car manufacturers and brands develop concept cars in the game world, is an ultimate sports car carrying Subaru's concept car motto "VIZIV"; Vision for Innovation. The car is called the "SUBARU VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo".

Inheriting the design language of Subaru's "SUBARU VIZIV 2 Concept" revealed at the March 2014 Geneva show, the Subaru design team have added dynamic and solid shapes to the model. Its shoulder line extends from the front hexagonal grill all the way to the rear. Its tough-looking body seems as though it was carved from hard, solid metal. And with blister fenders extending its shape three dimensionally outward, it visually expresses Subaru's pursuit of a safe and enjoyable driving experience. Its large diffuser, the roof integrated rear spoiler, and its shooting brake silhouette, which accounts for aerodynamic performance, will surely stand out among others in the game.

Thorough weight reduction was a focus in the design of the body structure, and carbon materials have been utilized everywhere. As a result, the vehicle weight was held down to <1380kg> despite being equipped with heavy batteries and motors. And propelling the lightweight body is Subaru's legendary 2 liter horizontally opposed engine that has been fully tuned with years of motorsports experience. The direct injection turbocharged engine that has been powered up with revised restrictor diameters is combined with one high-power motor in the front and two in the rear, which achieves a total system power output of <600ps> and 800 Nm (<82kgm>) of maximum torque. By independently controlling each of the motor outputs, turning ability while cornering is drastically improved, while the torque vectoring lamps built into the fenders visualize its movement. Thus, as with any other Subaru, the car is made controllable for anyone driving it, regardless of its extremely high performance levels.

Experience the "SUBARU VIZIV GT Vision Gran Turismo," a car that delivers Subaru's ideals of confidence and driving pleasure through an unprecedented aggressive design and extreme levels of performance.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A89:
Using the popular Celica XX, which made its debut in 1981, as the foundation, Toyota decided to embark on making a true sports car that would challenge the best examples from Europe. And after much research and development work, the company introduced the Supra in 1986.

Intended mainly for the North American market, the Supra featured a double-wishbone suspension at all four corners, a first for the company since the 2000GT. The rear differential utilized a subframe to deliver sporty handling and a comfortable ride.

The new Toyota sports car was large for a coupe, measuring <4620mm> long, <1690mm> wide and <1310mm> high. It initially came powered by the 7M engine, a 3.0-liter turbocharged unit that produced <230ps>, with a twin-turbocharged <185ps> 2.0-liter inline-4 and normally-aspirated versions added later (<105ps> and <140ps>). But the most noteworthy Supra was the 3.0 GT Turbo A, which appeared in 1988. This model became the foundation for a race car that competed in the Japan National Touring Car Series. It used a 3.0-liter turbo engine that produced <270ps>., and it wore the same <1745mm>-wide body as the North American-spec model, with low-profile tires and improved suspension.

In 1990, this power plant was replaced by the 1JZ-GTE in the 2.5GT Twin Turbo R. The new engine cranked out <280ps>, which was the maximum allowed for JDM cars at that time.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8A:
It was in 2002 when Toyota's popular high-performance sports car, the Supra, was discontinued to the dismay of hardcore fans all over the world. And ever since, people wondered if Toyota was secretly planning to bring the car back. Well, wonder no more because an all-new production version made its eagerly-anticipated debut at the 2019 North American International Auto Show.

The reborn sports car comes equipped with a twin-turbocharged inline-6 that powers the rear wheels. The development of the car was headed by chief engineer Tetsuya Tada, who was also in charge of creating the renewed Toyota 86. The working theme of the car was "Numbers are one thing, feeling is what matters." And by the looks of it, the Toyota team remained true to those values. The new Supra features an optimal 50:50 front/rear weight distribution and a low center of gravity, while possessing ideal sports car proportions, highlighted by a wide stance and short wheelbase. Thanks to the powerful engine, lightweight body and solid chassis, the car can shred a winding road with the best of them.

The new Supra will also star in the virtual world as Gran Turismo Sport has been charting the development progress of this car from day one, offering gamers a true representation of how this exciting sports car drives.
