DescriptionLong.0x00004A8C:
Toyota took its flagship sports car, the Supra, in an entirely new direction when it introduced the second-generation variant in May 1993. This was evident from the car's unique exterior styling that featured a long nose, large fixed rectangular headlights and slim taillights on a round rear. It looked nothing at all like the previous model, or anything else on the road for that matter. It sat <120mm> wider and <100mm> shorter. Inside the cockpit was a snug 2+2 layout with the dashboard wrapping around the front-seat occupants.

There were two engines offered, a naturally aspirated and turbocharged version of the 2JZ. The base 3.0-liter DOHC inline-6 produced <225ps> while the turbocharged one cranked out <280ps>. A race version of this engine is said to produce <400ps> to <500ps>, so it was far from reaching its potential in the Supra, though many aftermarket tuners managed to reach that figure and beyond. The engines came mated to a 5-speed manual, 4-speed automatic or a new Getrag 6-speed manual gearbox.

The Supra's suspension consisted of double wishbones at all four corners, tuned to provide maximum cornering prowess. Thus, ride quality was on the stiff side, but this FR (Front engine, Rear drive) car possessed the best handling in its class.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8D:
The Suzuki Swift Sport is a model that is based on the second-generation Swift, their model aimed for the global market. The European model is a 3-door body, but in Japan it is also offered in a 5-door body.

Its development was performed mainly in Europe, and was based on the production model rather than a prototype. Though this delayed the release timing to be later than the model change, this European development was imperative to perfect the level of tuning on the car. For the same reason, it was subjected to numerous tests, under a large variety of road conditions.

One merit for developing in Europe was that they gained the partnership and support of Teneco. Their knowhow gained from their Monroe brand helped to perfect the driving performance of the Swift Sport.

The engine is a 1.6-liter normally aspirated engine, combined with forged pistons and VVT, and tuned for driving in the high rpm range.

In a minor change in 2007, the maximum power did not change but the rev limit was increased from <7000rpm> to <7500rpm>. And by introducing cross ratio gears for the 5-speed MT, its power can now be more effectively applied and appreciated. It is also equipped with an ESP, a feature which is becoming more common among European cars, and the overall performance of the car has been improved. The interior also used to have many red accents, but this has been reduced for a more mature, chic atmosphere.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8E:
The Taycan is Porsche’s answer to the question of sustainable mobility, their first fully-electric vehicle.

A sports sedan that combines sports performance with everyday usability, its electric all-wheel-drive system uses 2 electric motors mounted on the front and rear axles, with the rear-motor encompassing a revolutionary 2-speed transmission allowing unparalleled acceleration and efficiency at high speeds.

Both the Turbo and the Turbo S models normally output 460 kW (<625ps>), but with the overboost feature engaged the output of the Turbo model is boosted to 500 kW (<680ps>), and the Turbo S cranks out a staggering 560 kW (<761ps>). This incredible power output is enabled by the first 800-volt power unit to be seen in a production car, which successfully achieves greater efficiency while drastically reducing charging time.

And of course no effort has been spared in producing dynamic handling. It features Porsche’s superior active suspension management and torque vectoring technology, controlling these systems in sync to provide the best possible driving experience under all driving conditions. Taycan’s technical advances also extend to its user interface, enabling media and air-conditioning to be operated directly through its intuitive voice control system.

The Taycan carries forward Porsche’s historical lineage while signaling a new era of automobiles. Truly a model in which heritage meets the future.O
DescriptionLong.0x00004A8F:
In 2006, Tesla Motors introduced its open-air, 2-seat electric car (EV), the Tesla Roadster. At this time, many car companies were still figuring out how to make electric cars viable in the marketplace. Delivery of the Lotus Elise-based sports car began in 2008, and by 2012, all 2500 units were sold.

The company's second model, a 5-door sedan introduced in 2009, was called the Model S. It was a much larger vehicle than its predecessor, being somewhere between a Mercedes S-Class and E-Class in terms of size.

Designed by Franz von Holzhausen, formerly with Mazda's North American Design Center, the Model S featured a sharp nose and short front and rear overhangs, giving it a sporty stance and a luxurious demeanor. The interior featured environmentally-friendly materials, including 100-percent recyclable PET plastic and no-lead Italian leather. Taking center stage was a large 17-inch touch screen monitor on the center dash that acted like a computer, including having 3G wireless capabilities that allowed continuous connection to the internet.

Providing the power was a liquid-cooled 9-inch motor with lithium-ion batteries that were mounted under the car’s floor to ensure a low center of gravity. The battery pack came in three different configurations, with the most expensive one offering a total driving distance of <483km> and producing a whopping <416ps>. All versions could be charged via a household outlet, compatible with 110V, 220V and 440V types. The total charging time was four hours when using a 220V charger, and only 45 minutes when using a 440V charger.

The Model S was among the quickest performance sedans in the marketplace, with a 0-to-60-mph time of 4.4 seconds. It indeed offered the best of both worlds: a clean-burning luxury sedan with sports car performance.u
DescriptionLong.0x00004A90:
The 86 GRMN is a factory-tuned version of Toyota's popular 86 sports car. The "GR" in GRMN stands for Gazoo Racing, which is Toyota's factory race division, and "MN" stands for "Meister of the Nürburgring". Gazoo Racing has participated in the classic Nürburgring 24 hour race since 2012, where it won its class twice with the 86. The 86 GRMN represents the fruits of the company's racing experience at the historic track.

For this special race car, the chassis was stiffened significantly, and the center of gravity was lowered by adding a carbon-fiber roof, hood, and trunk lid. Also, the rear windows were composed of polycarbonate plastic, which is significantly lighter than glass. Aerodynamic parts such as the front spoiler and rear wing were specifically developed to induce downforce, and the car was further lightened by becoming a 2-seater, with special Recaro bucket seats and a small diameter steering wheel.

Mechanically, the intake and exhaust components were replaced, and the friction of the internal parts were reduced to improve response and power in the high RPM ranges. As a result, both power and torque were increased from the standard model, by <19ps>/<1.2kgm>, respectively. The 86 GRMN's engine ended up producing <219ps>/<7300rpm> and <22.1kgm>/<5200rpm> of torque, and came mated to a close-ratio 6-speed gearbox.

The suspension system consisted of specially-developed dampers and springs, while the tires were developed specially for this car by Toyota and Bridgestone. The brakes featured opposed 6-pot monoblock calipers in front and a 4-pot setup at the rear.

Limited to only 100 units, the 86 GRMN was indeed a special car, and everyone seemed to realize that fact right away. Despite having a price tag that was double the price of a standard model, Toyota received more than 3000 orders for the 86 GRMN.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A91:
The 86 signaled a return to the classic front-engine/rear-drive sports-car segment for Toyota. Introduced in 2012, the 86 was essentially a modern-day version of the classic Corolla/Sprinter AE86 from the 1980s.

Unlike its predecessor, the new 86 came equipped with a boxer-type engine - a 2.0-liter flat-4 - that gave the compact sports car a very low center of gravity, thus better agility and handling response on both road and track. In 2016, the 86 received its first minor update, which included more spot welds to enhance the rigidity of the body and a revised front spoiler for better aerodynamics. The power of the 6-speed manual version was raised to <207ps>/<21.6kgm>, while Sachs dampers were offered as optional equipment for all trim levels.

The GT "Limited" version is the top-of-the-line model, which featured high quality materials such as leather and alcantara in the cabin, resulting in a more mature overall character.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A92:
The FT-86 Concept was introduced in 2009 to the delight of Japanese sports car enthusiasts everywhere. The exciting front-engine/rear-drive sports car was developed by a collaborative effort between Toyota and Subaru, and it rekindled the spirit of the legendary Toyota AE86. In 2011, the production version of the FT-86 made its long-awaited debut at the Tokyo Motor Show.

The "FT" (Future Toyota) designation was dropped, going simply by the name Toyota 86. The new-generation "Hachi-Roku" (86 in Japanese) featured a profile similar to that of the FT-86 II Concept shown at the 2011 Geneva Motor Show. The sleek body adopted Toyota's "Aero Handling" concept, which was the company's advanced aerodynamic philosophy.

Under the hood was a naturally-aspirated 1998cc DOHC flat-4, or "boxer" engine, mounted aft of the front axle. It produced an even <200ps> at <7000rpm> and <20.9kgm> of torque at <6600rpm>. The power was transferred to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual gearbox or a 6-speed automatic transmission with paddle shifters. Its ideal 53:47 front/rear weight distribution allowed for true sports car handling, with some models getting a limited-slip differential for even more precise cornering. Another reason for the car's amazing agility was because its center of gravity was located in the same place as many exotic supercars, sitting only <460mm> off the ground. The car was also lightweight, tipping the scales at <1230kg>.

Tuning firms, such as Modelista and TRD, offered plenty of customization for the 86, and they showed us that it made for a excellent starting point to build a race car. In sum, the 86 was a lightweight sports car that truly catered to the young car enthusiast of its day.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.!

DescriptionLong.0x00004A94:
Following the excitement of the FT-1 release in the Gran Turismo 6 game, the CALTY design team from Toyota’s North American Design branch has taken their dream one step further in creating the ultimate race car, the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo.

The designers’ original intention in designing the FT-1 was to unabashedly appeal to the die hard car enthusiasts. In the same way, the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo is designed for die-hard Gran Turismo fans. The designers focused on keeping the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo authentic for the virtual race tracks of the game, to maximize their driving pleasure.

Because the bones and architecture of the FT-1 already lent itself to cooling and downforce through “function-sculpting,” the Vision version just needed to be enhanced as a pure racing car. The designers closely studied race tracks and race cars, and applied their research into the styling. A deep sense of rawness is evident in the FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo, due to its purely function-driven design aesthetics. The fenders and tires are wider for extreme grip on the track. The enlarged air intakes provide increased cooling, and a larger rear wing and additional front canards have been added for even more downforce. The rear diffuser has been enlarged with multiple vertical fins, and is moved further back for cleaner airflow.

The FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo looks and feels the way it performs, so the driver can speed through the race tracks with the same sensations and thrills of real racing.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004A96:
Already considered a classic among enthusiasts today, this compact car has become a favorite for drifters and has been featured in movies and comic books. The car has its roots from the Corolla/Sprinter, but when this model changed its layout to FF (front engine/front drive), the sporty version in the lineup, the AE86 or Corolla Levin/Sprinter Trueno, remained as a rear-wheel driver.

The "86" (or Hachi-Roku, as it was called in Japan) developed an immediate following because of its rear-drive layout, lightweight, excellent handling and affordable price tag. It came in two shapes: a 3-door hatchback and a 2-door notchback. The main difference between the Corolla Levin and Sprinter Trueno was the front end, where the former featured a horizontal grille and fixed headlights and the latter no grille and retractable headlights.

Providing power was the newly developed 4A-GEU, a 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4. This engine featured some of the day's most advanced technology, including EFI-D (Electronic Fuel Injection-Druck), which calculated fuel amount through a pressure sensor, and the T-VIS (Toyota Variable Injection System). This helped the 4-cylinder to produce <130ps> and <15.2kgm> of torque.

It revved freely and quick, and demonstrated excellent throttle response, making the car wonderfully controllable through tricky corners. The suspension, body and engine worked harmoniously together to provide real sports car attributes. It was this performance and personality that made the "86" loved by so many.M
DescriptionLong.0x00004A97:
Known in Japan as the "Hachi-Roku" (Eight-Six), the popularity of the AE86 Levin/Trueno platform has not diminished in the more than 25 years since it first appeared. The Trueno here is of special interest—it is owned by Shuichi Shigeno, the author of "Initial D," a very popular comic book series in Japan in which the AE86 plays a pivotal role.

While chassis rigidity was improved by beefing up some body panels in key areas, the car's overall stock curb weight was reduced by about 100 kg, thanks to installing a carbon composite hood in place of the much heavier stock unit.

The AE86 enjoyed a long and varied tuning history, from carburetor conversions to superchargers to turbo kits. The method chosen for our car is perhaps the most common of AE86 upgrades: conversion to a 4-barrel throttle body. Further upgrades like high-compression pistons and a high-lift camshaft helped bring out the famous engine's character even more, imparting it with an exciting power curve where engine response felt sharp and the torque delivered generously with increasing revs.

A powerful MoTeC engine control unit was utilized for superior control, enabling the engine to attain a <210ps> maximum output, which is very close to the physical limits under normally aspirated tune. The exhaust system made use of an HKS manifold and Trust muffler to extract the most performance from the engine... plus it sounded really nice.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A98:
The TS030 hybrid prototype race car waged battle in the 2012 24 Hours of Le Mans and the WEC (World Endurance Championships) as one of the first hybrid-powered machines to step onto the international motorsports stage.

As its name suggests, the TS030 succeeds the TS010 and TS020, Toyota's awesome race cars that competed at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the 1990s. What sets the TS030 apart from its predecessors is its hybrid powertrain.

The THS-R system (Toyota Hybrid System-Racing) was developed by Toyota's production hybrid development team and the East Fuji Research Lab's motorsports department. The car utilizes a newly designed naturally-aspirated 3.4-liter V8 and a Denso motor unit built into the rear gearbox. Power is stored in an electric double-layer capacitor.

The drivers of the TS030 were Alexander Wurz, Nicolas Lapierre and Kazuki Nakajima. For the 24-hour race, a second car, driven by the formidable lineup of Anthony Davidson, Stéphane Sarrazin and Sébastien Buemi, was added.

At its first Le Mans race, the TS030 ran at the top of its class, but was forced to retire due to accidents and problems. However, the car made up for its shortcomings in the WEC. Of the six races the TS030 ran, it won three times, took three pole positions, and set four fastest laps. And although the car didn't partake in every race of the series, it still managed to take 2nd overall at the end of the WEC season.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A99:
The TS050 Hybrid was Toyota’s prototype race car, developed in 2016 to compete in the LMP1 class of the FIA World Endurance Championship, which included the legendary 24 Hours of Le Mans. Two years earlier, in 2014, Toyota had claimed the series championship with the TS040 Hybrid. By 2015, however, the team finished the season in 3rd place, prompting Toyota to design the TS050 from scratch to reclaim the top.

Like its predecessor, the TS050 was an all-wheel-drive hybrid, employing MGUs at both the front and rear wheels. But the powertrain switched from the naturally-aspirated 3.7-liter V-8 to a twin-turbocharged, direct-injection 2.4-liter V-6. Its supercapacitor system was replaced with a high-power lithium-ion battery, specially developed for racing and capable of rapid energy storage and deployment. The total system output stood at <1000ps>, equal to the TS040’s, but torque was significantly boosted thanks to turbocharging.

Further refinements included a more compact front MGU, which enabled aerodynamic redesigns to channel airflow more efficiently under the car, further sharpening its performance.

Toyota Gazoo Racing fielded two TS050 Hybrids in the World Endurance Championships. One car was piloted by Kazuki Nakajima, Sébastien Buemi, and Anthony Davidson, while the other was shared by Kamui Kobayashi, Stéphane Sarrazin, and Mike Conway. In 2016, the Kobayashi entry demonstrated blistering pace and remained in contention for the Drivers’ Championship, but in the end, the team concluded the season ranked 3rd in the Manufacturers’ standings.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9A:
Audi was hesitant at first in producing a compact 2+2, but when the TT concept was greeted enthusiastically at the 1995 Frankfurt Motor Show, the company went to work in making the car a reality, and the TT 1998 bowed to a waiting public.

The base engine was a <180ps> 1.8-liter DOHC inline-4, the same engine that powered the A3 and A4. But the choice for enthusiasts was a retuned version with dual intercoolers that pumped out <225ps>. Because of the compact size of the TT, it was one of the most nimble cars in the marketplace. Built on the A3's platform, with the wheelbase shortened <9cm>, the TT displayed excellent cornering balance with a slight penchant for understeer. The choice for enthusiast was the all-wheel-drive version because of a more neutral turning character, helped in part by the car's double wishbone rear suspension.

The TT's popularity was increased even more by an attractive convertible version in 2000 and the addition of a 3.2-liter DOHC V-6 in 2003. With <250ps> on tap and mated to the company's revolutionary DSG twin-clutch semi-automatic gearbox, the TT became the luxury 2+2 of choice for discerning enthusiasts.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9B:
The TT Cup is a purpose-built race car developed by quattro GmbH, based on the Audi TT. It was engineered specifically for the Audi Sport TT Cup, an exclusive one-make racing series launched in 2015.

While the road-going TT Coupé featured aluminum in its outer panels and upper frame, the Cup car took weight reduction even further with the use of carbon fiber in parts of its body shell. Stripped of comfort amenities, it tipped the scales at <1125kg>, more than <100kg> lighter than the lightest production version.

Both front and rear fenders were widened to accommodate 260/660R18 tires. 
Aerodynamics were further refined with specially designed low-profile front and rear bumpers, while a large adjustable rear wing added significant downforce.

Under the hood resided the familiar 2.0-liter TFSI inline-4, the same engine used in the production model in Germany. While the base output remained at <31ps>, the TT Cup car featured a push-to-pass system. With the press of a button, drivers received a temporary boost of <30ps>, encouraging bold overtakes and keeping the racing fiercely competitive. It was paired with the same 6-speed S tronic dual-clutch gearbox found in the road-going TT.

The front axle was fitted with an electronically controlled Haldex hydraulic limited-slip differential, allowing the driver to fine-tune the locking ratio directly from the cockpit.

Although positioned as an entry-level racing series, the Audi Sport TT Cup often served as a support race for the prestigious DTM. Its popularity soared in 2016, when the series attracted a total of 125 participating drivers.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9C:
When the third-generation Audi TT bowed at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show, the design direction stayed consistent with the first two generation models, meaning it still possessed a sporty, round look. Still, a new front fascia, highlighted by a one-piece grille and R8-like headlights, ensured that this was not the same TT as before.

Despite riding on a <37mm> longer wheelbase than its predecessor, the new TT’s overall length was shortened by <8mm>, making it slightly smaller. Its compact size accentuated the car’s amazing agility, provided in part by a new, lighter Audi Space Frame, which helped decrease the curb weight of the third-gen car by <50kg>.

The TTS sports model came with a turbocharged 2.0-liter TFSI inline-4 tuned to produce <314ps> and <38.7kgm> of torque (specs of the German-market model). The powerplant came mated to a 6-speed manual gearbox that sent power to all four wheels via Audi’s renown quattro system. With the lighter body and increased engine output, the new TT was faster than before, racing from zero to <100km/h> in a scant 4.7 seconds and reaching a restricted top speed of <250km/h>. The Audi Magnetic Ride variable damper system came as standard equipment, while a dual clutch semi-automatic S Tronic transmission with launch control was available as an option.C
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9D:
Toyota decided to go after Ford and Chevy in the heartland of America by offering a large pickup truck called the Tundra to the North American market.

The Tundra struggled at first, as it was smaller than its competition, and unable to sway die-hard Ford and Chevy fans from ditching their F-150s and Silverados. So for the second-generation model which was introduced in 2007, Toyota made its truck even bigger and dropped a larger engine into it. While it wasn't enough to dethrone the American brands, it was a great success in the marketplace.

In 2014, the bodywork was made more aggressive, and in 2015 the “TRD Pro” version was introduced. Tuned by TRD, Toyota’s motorsport arm, the new truck performed significantly better on rough roads, thanks to TRD coils and Bilstein dampers that improved the stroke characteristics of the suspension.

The TRD Pro disappeared from the Tundra lineup afterward, but returned again in 2019. Based on the Crewmax 4x4 with a 5.7-liter V8, the suspension was further tuned with Fox dampers, and its sporting character was enhanced with equipment such as a new hood scoop and BBS wheels.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9E:
TVR, a name derived from the first name of founder Trevor Wilkinson, is noted for making high-performance specialty cars, British coachworks style.

The company's first production car, the Grantura, made its debut in 1958, and featured the skillful combination of components from existing production cars such as Volkswagens and Austin Healeys, wrapped in sporty, head-turning body styles.

Another model was the Tuscan, that, despite its racing struggles in the 1960s, was resurrected in 2000, armed with a bevy of new features. The 2-seat, 2-door car didn't share the styling of its predecessor. It came equipped with a detachable roof, making it look as good as a convertible as it did as a coupe.

Its eye-catching exterior, highlighted by a wild face, made the car look big, but in fact, the car possessed modest dimensions. Its overall length, width and height measured <4235mm>, <1810mm> and <1200mm>, respectively, while the wheelbase was stretched to <2361mm>. The Speed 6 got its name from the number of cylinders in the engine.

Two inline-6s were available; a 3.6-liter model and a 4.0-liter model. The latter featured the day's latest racing technologies, including dry-sump lubrication. Output was rated at <365ps> and <42.86kgm> of torque, and when this power was coupled with the car's lean <1100kg> body, the Speed 6's acceleration was impressive, to say the least. It sprinted to <100km/h> in less than 4.0 seconds, making it one of the quickest cars of its day.
DescriptionLong.0x00004A9F:
The Volkswagen created by Dr. Ferdinand Porsche had a plethora of ideas packed in the small bodies, as well as infinite possibilities. The cars were developed into a variety of variants, from off-road cars for battlefields, to sports cars like the Porsche 911.

This Sambabus is an example of its transformation into a van with a large luggage space. Because the engine is mounted in the rear in the same manner as the old Volkswagen Beetle, the nose is extremely short. And because of the flat horizontally opposed engine, the floor of the luggage room is not very high. This is an example of the Volkswagen mechanism proving its superiority, in attaining the maximum space in a minimum body size.

The actual height of the car is relatively low at less than <1600mm>, and it is said this is because they did not want to raise the air resistance with a high height. Still, because the floor of the car was very low to the ground, it had more space than its rivals, and it was also very high in cost performance. Its small turning radius thanks to its short wheelbase, and the versatility of its compact size also gave it a lot of advantages as a commercial van.

The round headlights and the rounded front end design was practical but humorous, and is often used as a motif of other custom cars. Volkswagen is well aware of the important image of the Sambabus, and has already introduced this in taller wagon concept cars.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA0:
Established just north of Milan, Italy, in a town called Monza in 1919, Carrozzeria Zagato became one of the most heralded coach-builders of its day. It was primarily known for producing lightweight car bodies that borrowed technology from aircraft manufacturing. Alfa Romeo, which had been producing sports cars since before World War II, met with amazing racing success with Zagato-built bodies. This collaboration continued even after the war, and together they went on to create many significant cars that have now become part of automotive history.

One of the notable examples was the TZ introduced in 1962. The TZ, whose name stands for Tubolare Zagato, was a road car that could also double as a race car. It featured an aerodynamic aluminum body on a steel tubular space frame, helping it to weigh in at a lean <660kg>. Supplying the power was a DOHC 1.6-liter engine from the Giulia that produced <112ps> at <6500rpm>.

Unlike the original TZ, the 1965 TZ2 was a pure race car, with a production run of only 10 to 12 units. Rumor has it that many original TZ owners preferred a pure race version of their cars, so they returned them to the factory to be refitted as the TZ2.

What differentiated the TZ2 from the TZ was its fiber glass body that made it <40kg> lighter. It also sported a lower nose and roof that resulted in better aerodynamics. Its engine was also upgraded using the same twin-ignition head from the GTA. The result was 170 HP at <7500rpm> and a top speed of <245km/h>, up from the TZ's <215km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA1:
One of the most visually stunning race cars on the planet is the Aston Martin V12 Vantage GT3, which has been competing on the international motorsports stage since 2012, after replacing the vaunted DBR9/DBRS9.

The GT3 race car is based on the flagship in the Aston Martin lineup, the V12 Vantage, which first made its appearance in 2009. The production model came equipped with a 5.9-liter V-12 that produced <517ps> and <58.1kgm> of torque, which was stuffed into a light and sturdy body that allowed it to run from 0-<100km/h> in 4.2 seconds and reach a top speed of <305km/h>.

For the race car, Aston Martin tuned the engine to <600ps> and torque was increased to <71.4kgm>. Also, the stock gearbox was swapped out for an XTrac sequential transmission with paddle shifters. After shedding unwanted weight to a lean <1250kg> while establishing an ideal 50:50 front/rear weight distribution, the V12 Vantage GT3 was ready to rock.

The car’s exterior looks a lot meaner than the road-going car because of FIA GT3 regulations that called for a gigantic front spoiler lip, huge rear wing and larger fenders.

The race teams around the world that purchased the V12 Vantage GT3 were impressed from its first year on the circuit. In 2012, the Aston Martin race car piled up 18 wins and 30 podium finishes. In 2013, it scored 17 wins and 34 podium finishes, which just went to prove that the car ran as good as it looked.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA2:
After a long five-year absence from the marketplace, the third-generation Vantage finally made its appearance in 2005. Before, the Vantage was a high-end sports car that touted supercar performance, but the new version was positioned at the bottom of Aston’s lineup with a competitive price tag.

Referred by some as “the baby Aston,” the new front-engine/rear-wheel-drive Vantage set its sights on the Porsche 911, hoping to lure buyers away from the popular German 2+2. Therefore, high performance was made a priority. The Vantage sported the graceful design DNA of the DB7, and it was built atop a bonded aluminum space frame called the VH platform (also found on the DB9). Thanks to this new lightweight chassis, the new Vantage tipped the scales at a lean <1570kg>, which was <400kg> lighter than the previous model.

The Vantage came powered by a 4.3-liter V-8 that shared the same block as the powerplant in Jaguar XK. The engine initially produced <385ps>, but gradual improvements kicked the power up to <406ps> in 2007. In 2008, the V8’s displacement was increased to 4.7 liters, which resulted in even more power at <426ps>. In 2011 power output peaked at <436ps> for the Vantage S model.

The top-of-the-line Vantage S not only received the high-output engine, but it had a sportier suspension via stiffer dampers, springs and bushings. Also, a quicker steering gear ratio gave the Vantage S race car-like handling, giving its rival, the Porsche 911, all it could handle on the racetrack.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.4 regulations by Gran Turismo.,

DescriptionLong.0x00004AA4:
When Lamborghini introduces a limited-production car to celebrate its 50th anniversary, you know that it’s bound to be special, and very exclusive. Well, the company from Sant’Agata, Italy didn’t disappoint when it unveiled the multi-million-dollar Veneno, a super car whose clientele was restricted to a mere three people.

The Veneno was based on Lamborghini’s flagship, the Aventador, which featured an exterior design that looked like it came from another planet. However, there’s a reason for its bizarre looks, as precision aerodynamics had been implemented into the body to ensure optimal performance. The “V” shaped nose suggested that Formula 1 technology had made its way into the car design. Combined with a high-mounted variable rear-wing, a gigantic rear diffuser, and a shark fin that extended from the roof to the rear, the Veneno possessed gobs of downforce that kept it glued to the pavement through high-speed corners.

Also keeping the Veneno stable was a full-time 4-wheel-drive system and an F1-type pushrod suspension system that made it one of the cars with the best handling of all time. Providing the punch was a 6.5-liter V-12 that came mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox. With <750ps> on tap and a lightweight carbon-fiber structure that made it <125kg> lighter than the Aventador at <1450kg>, the Veneno sprinted to <100km/h> in 2.8 seconds and reached a top speed of <355km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA5:
It is one of the most fabled marques in the history of the automobile. Ettore Bugatti’s cars were so technologically advanced in the 1930s that they remained quite competitive in numerous racing categories... for about two decades. Imagine a contemporary Formula 1 team or sports car trying to make that claim. But the new Bugatti Veyron created by German car maker Volkswagen was without question the single greatest supercar of the modern era.

Its quad-turbo, 8.0-liter, W-16 engine produced a mind-numbing <1001 ps> at <6000 rpm>. Its transmission was an ultra-smooth, quick-shifting 7-speed DSG developed exclusively to the Veyron. Its performance numbers were downright scary, with a 0-<100 km/h> time of 2.5 seconds and a 0-<300 km/h> dash in 16.7 seconds. Its braking was also impressive, coming to a stop from <100 km/h> in a distance of <31.4 m> and only 2.3 seconds.

Then there’s the price: 1 million Euros (about $1.4 million).

The Veyron was capable of such high speed, said to be over 250 mph, that the vehicle’s ride height and rear wing angles changed in three positions: standard, top speed, and handling mode. To enter the top speed mode enabling speeds of over <375 km/h>, a special separate key needed to be inserted when the car was at a standstill.

Everything about the Veyron, its price, performance, limited quantity and top speed, was completely over-the-top. That’s why it rested atop the pinnacle of the super exotic car universe when it went on sale./

DescriptionLong.0x00004AA7:
The Dodge Viper evolved into its 3rd-generation model at the 2012 New York Motor Show. With the appearance of this iconic American sports car, the development of a GTS-R competition model was also announced, and it became clear that the Viper would return once again to the 24 Hours of Le Mans and the American Le Mans series after a 10 year hiatus. The Viper GT3-R is a GT3 machine created for private teams, based on the GTS-R works machine.

In the development of this machine, SRT, the high performance car development division of Dodge, and Riley Technologies, a major racing constructor in the U.S., worked together to instill the car with their know-how for victory.

The traditional long nosed, short deck body had improved aerodynamics with a flat bottom and the addition of a wing. Weight had also been reduced to <1295kg>. The 8.4-liter V10 with a dry sump was powered up to <680ps> (507kW) unrestricted, and this power was transferred with a X-Trac 6 speed sequential transmission. It was also equipped with 6 piston front/4 piston rear brake calipers with large diameter discs for stopping power.

The Viper GT3-R was priced at $459,000, with orders received from the latter half of 2013. Its level of performance was already proven in various GT Car races in the U.S. and other parts of the world.b
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA8:
Dodge introduced the Viper concept in 1989 to an awe-struck public to show that Chrysler was capable of producing something that could dethrone the Chevrolet Corvette as America's sports car. America's supercar war officially began in 1992 when Dodge released the 2-seat convertible to the public.

The Viper was as raw as sports cars came, with a loud, powerful engine and wide, menacing body that reminded many of the Shelby Cobra. For some, the car was too over-the-top. Dodge, hearing these comments, produced a fixed-roof version of the Viper called the GTS in 1996. At the same time, a race version of the GTS was also introduced, called the GTS-R. The GTS-R was created to contest in the world's GT races that included Le Mans and the 24 Hours of Nürburgring.

The GTS didn't just get a fixed roof, but also got more power. The massive V10 under its long hood now produced <456ps>, as opposed to <400ps> in the RT/10 roadster, which made the car quicker off the line.

The aerodynamic shape created by the fixed roof accounted for a better top speed, one that eclipsed the RT/10's top speed of <165mph> at <185mph>. The GTS's handling was also sharper, thanks to the car's added structural rigidity. The FR (front-engine, rear-wheel-drive) sports car set record-breaking slalom and skidpad records, thanks in part to its meaty tires.

The original Viper was a nostalgic and primitive-feeling sports car. However, with the release of the GTS, the Viper joined the ranks of the supercar.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AA9:
For years, Americans had only one real sports car, the Chevrolet Corvette. That all changed when the Dodge Viper arrived on the scene in 1991. The two became immediate rivals, and in a classic battle of one-upmanship, both Chevrolet and Dodge kept trying to outdo one another in an all-out performance race. As a result, both cars became such formidable sports machines that their on-road and on-track prowess eclipsed high-priced European supercars of their day.

In 2012, Dodge kept the tradition going with a new model that would transcend the others that came before it. The 3rd-generation Viper was tuned by the folks at SRT, Chrysler's high-performance factory tuning division. They kept the spirit of the American supercar intact, but raised the performance level so high that even Chevrolet engineers were scratching their respective heads. Built on the square steel space frame as before, this Viper featured aluminum cross bracing that improved rigidity by 50 percent. Also, thanks to the extensive use of lightweight materials such as carbon fiber, the car weighed <45 kg> less than the previous model. The heart of the Viper, the massive 8.4-liter V10 powerplant, received new pistons, as well as a new intake, exhaust and engine management system, allowing it to produce <649ps> and <83kgm> torque. The upper grade GTS was equipped with active suspension.

The new specs allowed the Viper to hit a top speed of <330km/h>, higher than most race cars. When you consider that the price of the 2013 model was still under the $100,000 mark, it's easy to see why many people, even today, regard the Viper as the best bang-for-the-buck supercar of all time.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AAB:
When the original Dodge Viper was introduced in 1992, the sports car world immediately took notice. Its sleek body, mean-looking design and powerful V-10 engine put it on par with the most exotic cars of its day. The breed improved in 2003 with the arrival of the second-generation model, and in 2006 a new model joined the lineup: a hard-top version called the SRT10 Coupe.

The SRT (Street and Racing Technology) in the car's name refers to Chrysler/Dodge's specialty sports division in charge of spicing up the company's vehicles. For the new Viper, it took its 8.3-liter OHV V10 and tuned it so it would produce <517ps> and an asphalt-shredding peak torque of <73.96kgm>, much more powerful than before.

The crew at SRT also improved the Viper's handling, by lowering the curb weight and testing it on the demanding Nürburgring circuit, not just to take the "America's Sport Car" moniker away from its main rival, the Chevrolet Corvette, but to challenge the likes of Ferrari and Lamborghini, which it succeeded in doing on the world stage.

Though its unique exterior tends to grabs everyone’s attention first, the Dodge Viper remains one of the most powerful and fastest sports car in history.p
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAC:
The Volkswagen Type 1, better known as "The Beetle" and "The Bug," can arguably be called the most universally loved automobile in history. "The People's Car," as it was known in Germany when it was introduced in the late 1930s, was designed by none other than Dr. Ferdinand Porsche.

The Type 1's most distinctive design features were its cute-looking round silhouette and air-cooled 4-cylinder rear-mounted engine (rear engine/rear-wheel drive layout). This engine would be the predecessor found in a long line of Porsche cars, featuring a flat or Boxer layout. Perhaps most remarkable of all was its production volume and longevity: 21 million cars were produced from 1938 all the way up to 2003.

The Volkswagen 1200 was the official name of the model manufactured in the mid-1950s to the late 1960s powered by a 1.2-liter 4-cylinder engine. Of these, the 1966 model is of particular interest to many VW fans and car collectors. This was the last Beetle to use a 6-volt battery to power its electrical system and was nicknamed the "6-Volt" in some countries.

From 1967 on, the electrical system was updated to a 12-volt system, and the car featured upright headlights, making it look more modern. The <1192cc> engine mounted in the 1200 first appeared in 1954. A <1285cc> version appeared in 1965 and a <1493cc> was offered in 1966. The engine did get a few improvements over the years, as horsepower was increased from the initial <34ps> to <40ps> in its late years.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAD:
Talk about your super exclusive exotic cars. After creating the One-77 in 2009 that was limited to a production run of 77 units, Aston Martin introduced the Vulcan at the 2015 Geneva Motor Show, which unlike the One-77 was intended only for the race track, but like its predecessor extremely limited in production. Only 24 cars were made available.

The Vulcan was built around a full carbon-fiber monocoque and body, with a front-engine/rear-wheel-drive layout. Under its hood was Aston Martin’s signature naturally-aspirated V-12, whose displacement was raised to 7.0-liters and tuned to pump out <811ps>. It was mated to an XTrac 6-speed sequential transaxle. Power was routed through a magnesium torque tube and carbon fiber drive shaft. And like a true race car, it featured a push-rod-type suspension with variable shock absorbers. It also sported carbon ceramic brake discs and driver-adjustable ABS system. The traction-control system could also be adjusted by the driver to fit his or her tastes.

Every part of the car has been optimized for lightness and strength, as it tipped the scales at a lean <1350kg>. This gave the Vulcan an amazing weight-to-power ratio of <1.66kg/ps>. A
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAE:
Volkswagen developed a new sports car for the digital world when it unveiled the 2-seat “GTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo." The designers and engineers injected the DNA from the legendary GTI into this car, before further refining the car's design and performance. The car came equipped a 503-hp VR6 TSI engine that was mated to a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox. Power was transferred to all four wheels via VW's 4MOTION four-wheel-drive system. Thanks to a whopping 665 Nm (<67.8kgm>) of torque, this car provides amazing acceleration, while its handling was tuned specifically for the “Gran Turismo” race tracks.

The body of the “Supersport” was aerodynamically optimized through numerous features. The front-end, for instance, was fine-tuned, with the designers placing the vertical light modules further outboard. They are now connected by a spoiler element to underscore the width of the GTI and enhance its visual presence. The air flow through the body was enhanced with a large air inlet that boosts aerodynamic performance at the front. The airstream flows past the front wheels and is practically sucked out of the wheel arches in order to cool down the brake discs. The hallmark GTI honeycomb structure adorns all the air inlet and outlet openings.

Aerodynamics and cooling are just as important in the strengthened rear section: downstream of the roof spoiler, a rear wing creates the necessary downforce to keep the rear end stable. An aerodynamic feature on the roof ensures that the airflow to the rear wing is ideal. Furthermore, air flows through the rear wheel arches in order to optimally dissipate the thermal energy produced during braking. The flat rear lights have been visually adapted to the extraordinary flat and dynamic proportions of the rear end.

Like the “Roadster,” the “Supersport” was also fitted with 20-inch GTI alloy wheels. The multipiece GTI wheels were refined further to a five-spokes design finished in ultralight carbon fiber. Between the wheels, the two classic GTI stripes can be found above the side sill, an homage to the Golf GTI I. The same applies to the hallmark black film around the edges of the rear window, which is finished in a carbon-fiber look. A helmet compartment and a racing tank have also been built into the car. The “GTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo” comes in io four colors: Reflex Silver, Gran Turismo Red, Lapiz Blue and Oryx White.

On digital pacetracks around the world, the unmistakably charismatic looks of the new “PTI Supersport Vision Gran Turismo” is sure to catch more than a few stares and make tie competition nervous.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AAF:
Based on successful GTI DNA, Volkswagen Design has developed a highly distinctive supercar: the “GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo”.

The design owes much to the successful history of the GTI: style-defining design elements from the various GTI generations illustrate the extraordinary evolution of this vehicle. Boasting a visionary design, the Roadster promises an immediate driving experience – the extreme acceleration can be experienced directly through the low-cut windscreen.

Powered by a 3.0 twin-turbo VR6 TSI engine, the "GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo" delivers <510ps> with an enormous torque of 665 Nm (<67.8kgm>). The 7-speed dual-clutch transmission with sports programming ensures phenomenal acceleration and fast gear-shifts on the racetrack. 

An aerodynamically optimized front and rear spoiler, together with an integrated diffuser element at the rear, achieve the required downforce for excellent road-holding. Fitted with 20-inch wheels in size 235/35 (front) and 275/30 (rear), the massive torque can be transferred reliably to the track via 4 driven wheels. The supercar features ventilated ceramic brakes, <380mm> in diameter at the front and <356mm> at the rear.

The "GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo" is presented in a bright, intense Gran Turismo Red, a modern interpretation of the classic GTI red.

The result is a fascinating and exceptionally dynamic extreme sports car with a sophisticated design for the racetrack in which players can gain a unique impression of what it’s like to drive in the GTI world.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.V
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB0:
The alluring "GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo," created by Volkswagen Design, embraces the successful history of the GTI in its flowing lines. The style-defining design elements from various GTI generations illustrate the rich history of the model, and you can tell by just looking at it, notably the low-cut windshield, that this roadster promises great fun and excitement behind the wheel.

Powered by a 3.0 twin-turbo VR6 TSI engine, the GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo delivers 503 HP with a hearty helping of 665 Nm (<67.8kgm>) of torque. The 7-speed dual-clutch transmission with sports programming ensures phenomenal acceleration and fast gearshifts on the racetrack.

An aerodynamically optimized front and rear spoiler, together with an integrated diffuser element at the rear, combine to generate gobs of downforce. Fitted with 20-inch wheels that are shod with 235/35 front and 275/30 rear tires, the all-wheel-drive sports car stays glued to the driving surface in all types of conditions. Stopping power is provided by ventilated ceramic brakes, <380 mm> in diameter at the front and <356 mm> at the rear.

The "GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo" is presented in a bright, intense Gran Turismo Red, a modern interpretation of the classic GTI red.

The result is a fascinating and exceptionally dynamic extreme sports car with a sophisticated design for the racetrack that appropriately conveys what it's like to drive in the GTI world.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB1:
While traditionally known as the Subaru Impreza WRX, the rally-inspired compact sports sedan became simply the Subaru WRX in the fall of 2013, but everything that made this model one of the most exciting machines in the world remained intact.

The WRX was built on the platform of the Levorg, a Japan-market-only station wagon. After seriously reinforcing the body structure, Subaru engineers went to work on the engine and chassis, putting much of their focus on the high-performance STI. They wanted to make sure that the WRX STI and the WRX S4 were completely different models, the former meant for the performance enthusiast, while the latter catered to grand touring fans. While the STI and S4 looked similar, everything from the engine to the steering mechanism was different.

For the STI, the engineers dropped the EJ20, a turbocharged 2.0-liter flat-4, into the engine bay. This powerplant produced <308ps> and <43.0kgm> of torque, routing the power to all four wheels via a 6-speed manual gearbox and Subaru’s excellent 4-wheel-drive system that featured a driver-controlled center differential. It was this 4WD system that made all WRX STIs so special. It included both an electronically-controlled and mechanical LSD—a Helical LSD controlled the front wheels, while a Torsen LSD was installed for the rear.

The WRX STI defined the “point and shoot” nature of compact sports cars of its day, thanks in part to its quick and precise hydraulic power steering system and custom-tuned suspension. On either road or dirt, the WRX STI had very few equals.

*This model was specially tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations by Gran Turismo.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AB5:
In June 2016, a Subaru WRX STI set a new record for 4-wheeled vehicles in the Time Trials at the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy race.

The competition, which has been a part of the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy since 1907, gained notoriety for the daring motorcycle racers who ripped through the island's roads at reckless speeds. One lap of the course measures <60.7km>, with more than 200 corners and no escape zones. There are sections where vehicles reach speeds in excess of <200km/h>. With an elevation change of roughly <400m> and a slick tarmac, this is arguably one of the most dangerous courses in the world.

The record-setting WRX STI was prepared by Subaru of America, which had been participating in the event since 2011. In that first year, the company set the fastest speed record of 19 minutes 56 seconds in an Impreza WRX STI, and in 2014, it broke that record with run of 19 minutes 15 seconds using a VAB series WRX STI, a model that became separate from the Impreza.

For 2016, Subaru returned with VAB WRX STI, but this time, the car featured engineering from STI, Subaru’s motorsport division, and styling/manufacturing support from Prodrive of the UK; the very group who had dominated the World Rally Championships (WRC) with Subaru. The car's turbocharged 2.0-liter flat-4 turbo was tuned to produce more than <600ps>, with further refinements such as a DRS built into the rear wing.

As a result, with former rally driver Mark Higgins behind the wheel, Subaru cut two minutes off of its previous record, with a time of 17 minutes 35.139 seconds and an average speed of <207km/h>.

DescriptionLong.0x00004AB7:
The first sports car developed by Austrian motorcycle manufacturer KTM made its debut at the 2007 Geneva Motor Show. Its name X-BOW was pronounced "Crossbow," inspired by the weapon of the same name. What's more, the car was styled in the image of a crossbow itself. It's a 2-seater, with no doors or windows... in fact, there are no comfort or luxury items to speak of. It certainly is, however, street legal.

The car was styled by Kiska Design, who also designed KTM's 2-wheeled machines, so the chassis features a motorcycle-like design. The X-BOW is a mid-engine vehicle with a carbon monocoque structure, which was co-developed by Dallara, a top race car chassis designer. A pushrod type double wishbone suspension is mounted front and rear, giving it the setup like that of a pure racing car. It possesses a flat bottom and a large diffuser at the rear end that generates <200kg> of downforce at <200km/h>. This helps allow the car to register an insane 1.5g in lateral acceleration.

There is nothing on or in this car other than what is required to go really fast. Inside the simple cockpit, there is a single display that serves as the instrument panel. Mounted behind the seats is Audi's turbocharged direct injected 2.0-liter TSFI engine that produces <240ps>/<31.6kgm> of torque. It propels the <790kg> car from 0-<100km/h> in an amazing 3.9 seconds. Even in standard trim, the X-BOW rivals the performance specs of some respectable supercars. The top-of-the-line "R" model gets the same engine, but power is boosted to <300ps>/<40.8kgm>. And with an upgraded suspension to accompany the extra power, it's as fast as—perhaps faster—than many race cars around a track.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB8:
The fan car project that started with the collaboration between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo continued even after the release of Gran Turismo 5. Adrian Newey, the chief technical officer of Red Bull Racing, and Gran Turismo series producer Kazunori Yamauchi further refined the concept of the "fastest racing car on earth, untouched by any and all regulations," and pursued the optimization of the design even further. What came as the result, was the X2014 series announced at the end of 2013 in Gran Turismo 6.

The entry level model for beginners to the X series is the X2014 Junior. A conventional aerodynamic, compact body is matched to an equally compact naturally aspirated <2000cc> inline 4 cylinder engine that produces approximately <250ps>. This is an optimal machine for learning the basics of driving a formula car, with high grip and high downforce characteristics.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AB9:
The fan car project that started as a collaboration between Red Bull Racing and Gran Turismo continued at full speed after the blockbuster release of Gran Turismo 5. Red Bull Racing’s Chief Technical Officer Adrian Newey and Gran Turismo Producer Kazunori Yamauchi continued to refine their premier concept of creating the fastest race car on earth, no holds barred.

The result was the groundbreaking X2014 series, announced at the end of 2013 in Gran Turismo 6.

The X2014 Standard, the mid-range model of the X2014 series, features conventional suspension and aerodynamics, without the axial flow fan and ground-effect skirt of the X2014 Fan Car that serves as the flagship of the lineup.

The X2014 Standard features the same streamlined front and rear wheel covers and glass canopy as the Fan Car, but to achieve the desired downforce, the Standard gets a dual-plane front wing. The contour of the rear floor has also been optimized for this configuration.

Downforce is governed by the universal rules of racing aerodynamics — increasing as the inverse square of vehicle speed. The engine is a 2.0-liter turbocharged
V-6, a liter less than the Fan Car but still delivering a massive <810ps>. When piloting this version of the X2014, the driver must keep in mind that the downforce available during cornering changes greatly as speed increases and decreases.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABA:
Imagine a race car that can unleash its full unbridled potential, free of any restrictions or regulations. That's exactly what Gran Turismo and Red Bull did when they created the X2010, followed by the X2014 a few years later. This project of creating the ultimate performance machine was updated for the 2019 FIA Gran Turismo Championship, and thus, the X2019 Competition was born.

Based on the X2014 Standard, the X2019 Competition features a front wing and a slightly modified rear end that produces less downforce to minimize aerodynamic changes to the car during close battles. The rear wheel covers have been altered to allow fast tire changes. Under the hood, the turbocharged 2.0-liter engine was swapped for a naturally-aspirated 3.0-liter powerplant, equipped with a more conventional throttle system to provide a more attractive exhaust note.

The X2019 Competition will be painted in the national colors of the Nations Cup finalists and will no doubt bring added excitement to this year's championships.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABB:
When the all-new R35 GT-R made its debut in the Fall of 2007, it was obvious that Nissan intended its supercar to go racing. The company didn't waste much time making its official announcement. Only a month after the GT-R went on sale, Nissan told the Japanese press that the new GT-R would compete in the Super GT Series, the most popular race series in Japan, perhaps all of Asia.

Specifically developed with 2009 vehicle regulations in mind, this race-ready Nissan GT-R featured an innovative construction design that centered on the cabin. While its overall appearance was similar to that of the production GT-R, the race car was a completely different animal.

The engine was a 4.5-liter V8 based on the VK45DE, the power plant in the Fairlady Z GT race car from the previous year. It was reported to produce more than <500ps>.

In competition, the number 23 Xanavi Nismo GT-R piloted by Satoshi Motoyama and Benoît Tréluyer, showed incredible performance from the opening round of the car's maiden season, winning the first two races. In the end it won a total of three races, good enough to bring the team the drivers' title in 2008.

In all, five GT-Rs competed in the Super GT series that year. The GT-R finished 1-2 in the opening round at Suzuka, and won a total of seven out of that year's nine races, meeting, and perhaps exceeding, the expectations of Nissan and GT-R fans all over Asia.@
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABC:
When it comes to racing, there may not be any other marquee around with a richer historical heritage than Jaguar. Back in the day, Jaguar won the 24 Hours of Le Mans from 1955 to 1957, with the now legendary D-Type taking the checker three years in a row. The company's activity as a works team ended in 1956, but there were those within the company that still had a passion for racing. These men continued to develop racing cars, and one in particular was intended to succeed the D-Type. This car was dubbed the XJ13 and was completed in 1966. It was Jaguar's first mid-engine race car.

The body was similar to the road-going E-Type, often considered one of the most beautiful road cars in history; however, within the engine compartment sat a 5.0-liter DOHC V12 that pumped out <502ps>. This engine would serve as the basis for the company's 12-cylinder engines for years to come.

The engineers had high hopes for the XJ13 in actual competition, but the management team at Jaguar wasn't keen on seeing it race, and along with the fact that company brass wanted to keep the V12 engine a secret, the XJ13 project was canceled. It's too bad really, because the car was said to be the most beautiful in Jaguar's history. Although it never made it onto any racetrack, one car was actually produced, but it was severely damaged during filming of a promotional clip for the E-Type. Since then, the car has fortunately been restored to its original splendor.t
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABD:
In the golden era of racing, Jaguar was a force to be reckoned with, especially at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, where the classic marquee won five times from 1951 to 1957. And then, Jaguar took a long break, not returning to the Sarthe Circuit until 1986 when the company re-emerged with the Group C race car, the XJR-6, developed by TWR (Tom Walkinshaw Racing).

Designed by noted Formula 1 designer Tony Southgate, the XJR-6 was a bit different from other Group C cars in that it did not have a turbocharged powerplant. Most teams opted with small displacement turbocharged engines to improve fuel-efficiency, but Jaguar went with pure power, in the form of a naturally-aspirated 6.5-liter V-12, which grew to 7.0 liters in the XJR-9, which produced about <700 ps>.

The XJR-9 competed with perennial powerhouses such as Nissan, Toyota, Mercedes-Benz and Porsche at the 1988 24 Hours of Le Mans. The XJR-9 took the checkered flag, with Jan Lammers, Johnny Dumfries and Andy Wallace sharing the driving duties. It was a historic moment for Jaguar, which returned to glory at the famed French circuit after a long absence.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABE:
The car that won the Gran Turismo Trophy at the 61st Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance in 2011 was this 1960 Plymouth XNR Ghia Roadster.

The designer was Virgil Exner, the legend who led the golden years of Chrysler in the 1950s and 1960s. The XNR Ghia Roadster, which inherited his name in abbreviated form, was actually built by Carrozzeria Ghia, a company that Exner had close ties with.

Plymouth represented the entry-level brand for Chrysler, but that didn't stop Exner from incorporating technology into his creation that had trickled down from Chrysler's involvement in NASCAR. This concept car was made as the future of sports cars that would rival cars like the Chevrolet Corvette and Ford Thunderbird.

By far, the most striking feature was its asymmetric styling. From the air intake in the car's nose to the flow from the headrest to the rear, it's Exner's interpretation of aerodynamic styling that characterized 1950s racing. The cockpit's right side is covered with a tonneau cover which makes the car appear to be a single-seater at first glance, but there actually is a seat hiding under the cover, making it a fully-fledged 2-seat sports car.

The prominent fins on the sides of the body were actually a shared design feature from the Valiant, the car on which the concept car was based. Although its overly avant-garde styling ultimately proved too much for the market, thus prohibiting the car from making it to mass production, the XNR did manage to make major shockwaves in the car design realm at the time and gave a glimpse into the depth of American Automotive History.
DescriptionLong.0x00004ABF:
*The Nissan Fairlady Z was sold as the Nissan 300ZX outside Japan.

The Z32, appearing in 1989, was the first complete transformation for the Fairlady Z. It came in a wide, flat body, turning 180 degrees from the narrow, long body designs that lasted 3 generations. It was sized as a global sports car, not restricted by the size classes of the Japanese market.

Its steering characteristics were changed drastically. As soon as the steering wheel is turned, the nose slices into the corner, and the wide tread gave it a high level of potential. This Z opened new doors as a cornering machine, while maintaining its performance as a GT. Again, the Z dropped European thoroughbreds into a hole of despair.

At the heart of this car was a compact V6 with a low center of gravity. Even though it is an FR, it was given a front midship layout with the engine located as far back as possible, to make the front/rear weight distribution close to 50:50. Aiming for the global market, the engine size was fixed at 3 liters, and producing <230ps> in the NA, and <280ps> in the twin turbo, its performance decorated the end of the 20th century. Its suspension used advanced designs as well, and even features like an ABS that does not transfer shock to the brake pedal, were things that went beyond the usual standards of the time.

In 1992, a convertible model was added to the lineup, and was greatly welcomed in its main market of California.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC0:
The FIA-GT racing versions of the E85/E86 BMW Z4 were immensely popular with race teams, especially privateers.

The second-generation E89-based GT3 machines started racing in 2010. Because the production Z4 was only sold as a convertible starting in 2009, the GT3 race car was converted into a coupe by omitting the opening and closing mechanism of the power hard top. A large front spoiler and rear wing, along with flared front and rear fenders provided gobs of downforce without any added weight. The hood, roof, wing, and the front and rear fenders were made of carbon fiber, making the car <300kg> lighter at <1200kg>.

Under the hood, the Z4’s stock inline-6 was swapped in favor of the E92 M3’s fire-breathing 4.0-liter V8 that came mated to a 6-speed sequential gearbox. The ECU of this engine was reprogrammed to produce <480ps>. New competition-grade ABS brakes provided the stopping power, and the front axle was redesigned for added performance and durability.

The 2011 model pushed the envelope even further as the fenders were widened and the entire body was upgraded to improve the car’s aerodynamics. Also, engine displacement was increased to 4.4 liters, bumping power up to <515ps>. The 6-speed sequential gearbox was updated to incorporate paddle shifters.

The transformed Z4 GT3 won two races in the FIA-GT3 championships in 2011, and in the two 24-hour races at the Nürburgring and Spa, it placed second overall. The car showed, and continues to show, superb performance in races with high levels of competition.
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC1:
Announced in 1999, the Z8 was a luxury open-top sports car that took its roots from the legendary BMW 507 of the 1950s (of which only 252 cars were ever made). The car drew additional attention when its gorgeous sheet metal was revealed for the first time, as the Bond car in the 19th "007" movie, "The World is Not Enough."

While the Z8 is a production car, it was positioned as a very special model in the BMW lineup, and they spared no expense in its creation. The basic structure of the car starts by combining an extruded aluminum space frame with aluminum paneling, an expensive undertaking that requires precision craftsmanship. The long-nose, short deck layout, electric soft top, and retro-modern style employing a variety of classical details, is the work of legendary designer Henrik Fisker who would later work on the Aston Martin DB9, before going on to create his own hybrid car company.

Its design motif is consistent through to its interior, recreating the metallic interior panels of the 507 with composite panels and center gauges. Meanwhile, fine leather is utilized unsparingly to create an interior fit for the very best of luxury cars. Mechanically, it borrows its engine from the high-performance E39 M5 sedan, a 4941 cc V8 producing <400ps>/<51.0kgm>, and also shares the 6-speed manual transmission, front MacPherson strut and rear integral-arm aluminum suspension. Because the car is <150kg> lighter than the E39 M5 at <1630kg>, 0-<100km/h> is a brisk 4.7 seconds, which made it the fastest BMW of its day.E
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC2:
Inspired by the aerodynamic designs of great prototype endurance race cars, the ISO Rivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo is a contemporary gentleman driver’s sports car designed specifically to compete at the highest international levels. Virtually-built using realistic volume and base measurements, the ISO Rivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo evokes a fierce attitude and raw emotion through its sensorial coachwork proportions: low center point of gravity, voluptuous fenders and sleek, elegant lines.

Historically, ISO Rivolta became famous among sophisticated, international clients in the 1960s and 1970s for its innovative approach in marrying Italian design with an American powertrain, thus producing excellent and reliable performance cars. These classic Iso sports and racing cars participated in some of the world’s greatest sports car competitions, such as the 12 Hours of Sebring, 1000 km of Nurburgring, and 24 Hours of Le Mans. The marque bearing the mythological Griffin logo also joined Formula 1 in the early 1970s through a partnership with Marlboro, and successfully competed at the hand of legendary professional drivers Jacky Ickx, Gjis Van Lennep and Arturo Merzario, to name a few.

Zagato, a design atelier with 98 years of experience, has collaborated with many famous automotive brands and is renowned for creating iconic, competitive sports cars in limited numbers. Zagato Vice President of Design Nori Harada pays tribute to ISO Rivolta with the creation of the new ISO Rivolta Zagato Vision Gran Turismo to honor ISO Rivolta’s racing heritage and passion for performance. Once again the Griffin will compete against the Ferrari, Lamborghini and other motorsports titans, this time in the virtual world of Gran Turismo.V
DescriptionLong.0x00004AC3:
Italian car manufacturer Pagani Automobili came to fame in 1999 when it introduced the Zonda, a very limited-edition super car for the extremely wealthy, at the Geneva Motor Show that year.

The company founder and president, Horacio Pagani, who once worked for Lamborghini and assisted in the design of the Countach anniversary model, set out to create a hand-made machine that would surpass all others in performance and styling. Many would agree that he did just that with the Zonda.

Looking like a Group C race car for the road, the Zonda C12's body was completely made of carbon fiber, helping the car to weigh in at an incredibly lean <1250kg>. Providing the power was a mid-mounted AMG V-12 engine that produced <394ps>.

There were a few variations of the Zonda after its initial release. This car, the Zonda R, was one meant strictly for the racetrack, like the Ferrari FXX. In this version, the AMG V12 was tuned to produce <750ps> and <72.4kgm> of torque, all managed by a 6-speed sequential gearbox. In order to raise stability on the racetrack, the car's wheelbase was lengthened and its tread width was extended. Also, a large front spoiler and a rear variable wing were added to improve downforce. According to Pagani, the Zonda R could accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in just 2.7 seconds and reach a top speed of <350km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x00005137:
To many, the 300 SL name represents Mercedes-Benz's classic sports coupe that first appeared in 1954, but the 300 SL moniker actually originated with a prototype race car built by the company for its factory team.

Codenamed W194, the 300 SL race car featured an aluminum tube frame and improved versions of the engine and suspension from the W186 300. It weighed just <870kg>, and the inline-6 was tuned to produce <172.4ps>.

This very car, chassis number 194007/52, went out and won the 1952 24 Hours of Le Mans on its debut race, then two months later, after having its roof removed to cut <100kg> from its racing weight, took the checkered flag at the 24 Hours of Nürburgring.

Naturally, its success on the race track convinced the execs at Mercedes-Benz to create a production version, which we now know as the "Gullwing 300 SL."
DescriptionLong.0x00005138:
Making its debut in 1975 was the successor to the very popular Ferrari Dino 246 GT called the 308 GTB. This svelte sports car represented one of the first of a long line of V-8-powered mid-engine Ferraris that would the exotic-car genre for years to come. 

The wedge-shaped exterior was penned by Leonardo Fioravanti of Pininfarina, who was responsible for a number of Ferrari designs from the late 1960s to the early 1990s. 

Under the sheet metal, the 308 GTB was equipped with a 3.0-liter DOHC V-8, the same powerplant as the Dino 208 GT4, which produced <255ps>. In 1980, new emissions regulations brought output down to <215ps>, but two years later Ferrari increased it back up to <240ps> after it adopted a 4-valve system for the engine. The new car was called the 308 GTB Quattrovalvole. In 1977, a targa top GTS was added to the mix, setting the stage for the 328 that was introduced in 1985.
DescriptionLong.0x00005139:
The 356, Porsche's first mass-produced car, made its debut in 1949 and immediately revolutionized the compact sports-car genre. An updated version of the original model called the 356A appeared in 1955 and again in 1959. 

The 356A featured a rounded windshield, soft padding above the interior panels, and a horn at the center of the steering wheel. Performance of the car increased every year, ultimately leading to the 1500 GS Carrera and the 1500 GS GT Carrera, which were limited-production models billed as the GT3 of their day.

Powering the 356A was a slightly detuned version of the 4-cam engine found in the 550 Spyder race car. The road-going 1500 GS Carrera produced <100ps>, while the track-ready 1500 GS GT Carrera pumped out <110ps>. Both cars were offered as a coupe, cabriolet, and speedster.

Of particular note is that the 1500 GS Carrera was the first to go by the "Carrera" name, which has now become synonymous with Porsche.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513A:
Before World War II, Alfa Romeo was a small automotive manufacturer that specialized in creating race machines and upscale road cars. The most notable model from this era was the 8C that appeared in 1931. 

The name 8C actually refers to the company's 8-cylinder powerplant. Designed by renown engineer, Vittori Jano, this water-cooled engine featured the latest technology of its day, including dual overhead cams (DOHC) and a hemispherical combustion chamber. The 1937 8C 2900B, the last in the 8C line, had 2.9 liters of displacement and came equipped with twin superchargers, enabling the engine to produce <180ps>. Two different versions of the chassis were available, with varying wheelbases, allowing customers to choose a number of different body styles from their favorite Carrozzerias.

The Alfa Romeo 8C 2900B Touring Berlinetta is a gorgeous coupe created by Carrozzeria Touring, utilizing the company's Superleggera (Superlight) technology. Thanks to its engine, it boasted race car performance, making it one of the most heralded super sports cars of its day. Rumor has it that only five of these cars were ever produced.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513B:
In 1989, Porsche introduced the Type 964, the third-generation version of the popular 911. While the car featured approximately 80 percent new parts, it nevertheless stayed true to the elements that defined all 911s before it. What was different about this one was that the first model offered, the Carrera 4, came equipped with a new 4WD system originally developed for the vaunted 959. The lighter 2WD version of the 964, called the Carrera 2, came a year later in 1990.  

All Type 964 911s came powered by an air-cooled flat-6, mounted aft of the rear wheels, with 3.6 liters of displacement. The Type 964 produced <250ps>/<31.6kgm>.

The Carrera RS was a performance model based on the Carrera 2, with a more rigid body structure and less weight (lighter by <120kg>). Power was upped to <260ps>, making this model a monster on the race track. A turbocharged 911 would appear later, with the top-of-the-line Turbo S delivering a whopping <381ps>.c
DescriptionLong.0x0000513C:
The Porsche 911 entered its fourth generation in 1993 with the introduction of the Type 993.

The most noticeable change was a significantly lower nose that flattened the peaks of the front fenders and swept the headlights rearward. The rear fenders were widened, among other revisions, giving the car an entirely new look. The rear suspension was also redesigned with a multilink setup to improve handling.

The base engine was a 3.6-liter flat-6 carried over from the previous Type 964 and tuned to <272ps>. With the succeeding 911 (996) moving to water cooling, the 993 became the last air-cooled flat-6 911.

The most powerful version of the Type 993 was the Carrera RS, released in 1995. Its engine was enlarged to a <300ps> 3.8-liter unit, body rigidity was increased, and weight was reduced by removing the rear seats.

The lineup also included the Carrera RS Clubsport, which featured track-oriented modifications such as a large front spoiler, a rear wing and a welded roll cage.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513D:
As its name implies, the 911 GT1 Strassenversion was the "street version" of the 911 GT1, a race car developed to compete in grand touring races between 1996 to 1998. Because the FIA required that every GT1 race car needed to be based on a production car with at least 25 units produced, Porsche homologized the 911 GT1 into the vehicle you see here.

Introduced in 1996, the 911 GT1 race car used the Type 993 chassis converted into a mid-engine layout. Power came from a twin-turbocharged 3.2-liter flat-6 that produced <640ps>. A year later, the production version of the GT1 was released wearing the front fascia of the Type 996, but possessing the same basic architecture of the race car.

The engine was relatively unchanged, but power was decreased to <544ps> to meet European emissions standards. Still, the race car-converted-into-street car was remarkably quick, thanks to its lean curb weight of <1100kg>, which allowed the 911 GT1 Strassenversion to run from zero to <100km/h> in a scant 3.7 seconds and reach a top speed of <308km/h>.!
DescriptionLong.0x0000513E:
The Porsche 917 Living Legend is a hyper car inspired by the legendary Porsche 917 racer, which brought the manufacturer the first overall victory in the 24 Hours of Le Mans back in 1970.

Developed in 2013 by a small team of engineers and designers in Weissach, the 917 Living Legend was simultaneously a tribute and spiritual successor to the legendary Porsche racer. Inspired by the signature proportions of the original, the 917 Living Legend was all about celebrating the car that brought the Le Mans title to Stuttgart.

Under the sheet metal, the 917 Living Legend featured the latest technology of its day, including lightweight materials such as carbon fiber, which was used for the chassis. Powering the car was a turbocharged 8-cylinder engine that pumped out about <1014ps>, while the suspension system, based on the 918 Spyder, provided remarkable handling at all speeds.

With updated aerodynamics, the car could reach <300km/h> on long straights, making the 917 Living Legend a true reincarnation of the legendary Porsche race car.
DescriptionLong.0x0000513F:
The Porsche 917K, a prototype race car developed by Porsche to compete in Group 4 sports-car racing, was essentially the 917 with a shortened body. After the debut of the 917 in 1969, Porsche introduced the shorter model, calling it the 917K (the "K" stood for "Kurz," which means "short" in German). The standard, longer car was then called the 917LH. 

The car's space-frame chassis was composed of aluminum alloy pipes that weighed just under <50kg>. A carbon-fiber body covered a mid-mounted <4494cc> flat-12 engine that produced <600ps>. And with a curb weight of about <800kg> and enhanced aerodynamics — downforce was increased by sloping up the rear edge of the short tail body, while the front tip was squared off — the 917K was a monster on the straights.

In 1970, it dominated the international manufacturer’s championship winning 7 of 10 races, and also brought Porsche its first victory in the Le Mans 24 Hour race.
DescriptionLong.0x00005140:
Introduced in 1971, the A112 Abarth is widely regarded as the original hot hatch. Built on the ultra-compact Autobianchi A112 platform, the A112 Abarth was a nimble 3-door hatchback, measuring just <3230mm> in length and <1480mm> in width.
