Called the 205 Turbo Evolution 2, they possessed a lighter frame, an improved engine, and a large rear-wing and became known as one of the monsters of Group B.

The 205 Turbo Evolution won seven out of the 12 Group B races in 1985 and six out of 13 in 1986, taking home both the manufacturers' and drivers' championship titles both years. However, its amazing run lasted until the end of 1986 when the FIA decided to discontinue the Group B category. Still, the car had made its mark and definitely carved out a place in the annals of automotive history.
DescriptionLong.0x00008209:
The Mazda RX-VISION was first shown at the 2015 Tokyo Motor Show. Billed then as the company's Rotary Sports Concept.

Based on Mazda's KODO design philosophy, the car was a visual tour de force, with smooth flowing lines and proportions befitting a spiritual successor of the RX-7 and Eunos Cosmo. A bit of mystery surrounded what was under its hood.

All that was disclosed was that it was Mazda's next-generation Skyactiv-R rotary engine.

The catchphrase included the words, "a dream to hopefully achieve one day." That the company still had plans for a future rotary engine was made clear with this machine.

Gran Turismo Sport players had an exclusive chance to sample its prowess in the virtual world in the form of the RX-VISION GT3 Concept.
DescriptionLong.0x000084A7:
Since its release in 2018, the ZC33 Swift Sport has been praised by automobile enthusiasts as an extremely sporty and fun-to-drive hatchback. The credit here went to the car's lightweight highly rigid body structure, a responsive turbocharged 1.4-liter engine and excellent handling character. 
 
Unveiled at the 2020 Tokyo Auto Salon, the "KATANA Edition" concept offered a peek into what future Swift Sports may look like. The car borrowed the spirit of Suzuki's high-performance sports bike, the Katana. Because Suzuki specializes in building both cars and motorcycles, this is a vehicle that could be created by only a few manufacturers in the world.
 
The designers used the Suzuki Swift as a base, but added the front and rear bumpers that had design elements from the Katana. The exaggerated fender flares widened the car further. The interior featured burnt titanium-colored panels that simulated a hot exhaust to create the look and feel of a sports bike. Additionally, both the interior and exterior came with red accents and Katana logos throughout.
 
In addition to the two-tone silver-and-matte black design on the show car, five other color variations were added. "Candy Daring Red" was the same color as the limited-edition Katana bike that was sold in January 2021. Only 100 examples of that bike were made.
 
This special version featured in Gran Turismo has been slightly modified in design and specification to compete in Gr.4 racing. Among the changes were an enlarged front spoiler, a new unique GT wing designed to reflect the shape of the Katana's seat cowling and the addition of a roll cage.
DescriptionLong.0x00008BD5:
Suzuki is one of a small number of manufacturers to produce both cars and motorbikes. First introduced 20 years ago, the GSX-R/4 sports concept was developed as the amalgamation of its 2- and 4-wheeled sports vehicles. It featured the high-performance engine from the company's "Hayabusa" flagship sports bike mounted amidships on a lightweight aluminum-framed car body. The GSX-R/4 has also appeared in previous Gran Turismo titles.

And now, the latest rendition of the Hayabusa engine returns with Suzuki's latest developments in electrification and lightweight construction methods in the Suzuki Vision Gran Turismo.

The car sports a front-engine/rear-wheel-drive layout with the new Hayabusa <1340cc> engine mounted just aft of the front axle. The gasoline engine is combined with two electric motors that drive the front wheels and one that powers the rear. Total output is rated at 318kW (<432ps>) and 610 Nm (<62kgm>) of torque peaking at 3000 rpm. And thanks to Suzuki's lightweight construction methods, the 2-seat convertible tips the scales at a lean <970kg>. 

The exterior design combines the DNA of Suzuki's sporting heritage seen on the Swift Sport. The GSX-R/4's long nose is reminiscent of the company's Cappuccino "kei car." The interior design possesses the aesthetics of a motorcycle and expresses the joy of driving in a modern pure sports fashion.
DescriptionLong.0x00008BE3:
Kei vehicles are unique to Japan, where they serve an important role in the country's automotive culture. The vehicles must adhere to many restrictions, mainly in size and engine displacement, but that hasn't stopped many manufacturers to create some amazingly fun-to-drive sporty examples.

Once such car is the Daihatsu Copen, a convertible that can be considered a genuine sport car. The second-generation model, which appeared in 2014, featured a D-Frame body and came powered by a turbocharged 3.0-cylinder engine, complete with variable valve timing. It also had what the company called the Dress-Formation system that allowed body panels to be easily removed and replaced to change the look of the car.

Using this car as a base, the COPEN RJ Vision Gran Turismo was created to explore the full sporting potential of kei cars. RJ stands for "Racing Jacket," which refers to the car's sporty exterior. The car indeed has the look of a warrior dressed for battle with an oversized front spoiler, rear wing and diffusers. The car's aggressive fender flares adds to the car's "let's get down to business" nature.

By law, the engine's displacement remains <660cc>, but boost pressure has been increased to allow the 3.0-cylinder to produce <149ps> and <20.6kgm> of torque. Also, curb weight has been reduced to just <600kg>, giving the car the acceleration pop of bigger sports cars.

In the 1960s, Daihatsu competed in motorsports with the classic P-5. The COPEN RJ Vision Gran Turismo is meant to carry on that fighting spirit.
DescriptionLong.0x00008BE5:
The Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo Roadster is an all-electric single-seater which combines a race-proven, state-of-the art powertrain with a taut, sculpted form inspired by the iconic, timeless Jaguar D-type.

Following the success of the original Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo Coupé and Vision Gran Turismo SV endurance racer, the Gran Turismo Roadster is designed to bring gamers the pure, visceral driving experience of an open-cockpit Jaguar sports car powered by three electric motors generating a total power output of more than <1000ps>.

The flowing surfaces, dramatic lines and perfect proportions of the first two Jaguar Gran Turismo Vision cars are instantly recognizable, but in place of a deployable canopy is a swept-back aero screen directly in front of the driver. Behind, a modern interpretation of the fin synonymous with the three-time Le Mans-winning D-type, is aerodynamically optimized using the latest computational fluid dynamics tools to be deployable at speed for enhanced stability with minimal drag.

The fin also features one of the beautiful details found on the Roadster, here in the form of a Union Jack etched into the fin itself, and subtly illuminated by LEDs. The theme continues with the hand-crafted leather straps on the front fenders and iconic roundel lights in the grille.

The Jaguar Vision Gran Turismo Roadster’s dramatic, driver-focused interior combines lightweight, luxurious materials and finishes with stunningly intricate details. Looking out onto the gracefully long hood, gamers will be fully immersed in the action._
DescriptionLong.0x0000923D:
The ZR1 is the ultimate-performance version of the Chevrolet Corvette. The seventh-generation C7 Corvettes already had an impressive lineup that included the sporty Z51 and the powerful Z06, but in 2018, as the generation neared its end, the mightiest C7 of all was released in the form of the ZR1.

The ZR1 featured a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 called the LT5. It was similar in construction to the <659ps> LT4 engine in the Z06, but a larger supercharger and the addition of GM's first dual-injection system allowed it to pump out an impressive <765ps> and <98.8kgm> of torque, which represented a 10-percent increase in output.

The car's aerodynamic parts were developed in conjunction with Pratt & Miller Engineering, known for building racing Corvettes for GT competition. Every component of the car was designed for performance. For example, two different rear wings were developed for the ZR1, one for maximum speed and the other for the fast lap times. When the car was optimized for maximum speed, it was capable of reaching <345.8km/h>.!
DescriptionLong.0x0000923F:
The G70 is a sports sedan developed as part of Hyundai's high-performance Genesis brand. A standard D-segment vehicle, it was released in 2017 and intended as an entry-level model.

Despite sharing most of its features, including the platform, with the KIA Stinger (KIA are also part of the Hyundai group), the G70 was designed from the ground up as a luxury sedan.

Three engines were made available for the G70: a twin-turbocharged 3.3-liter V-6, a turbocharged 2.0-liter gasoline turbo, and a 2.2-liter diesel turbo. The twin-turbo V-6 was capable of <370ps>. Like the other cars in the Genesis lineup, rear-wheel drive and AWD versions of the G70 were offered.

The G70's styling was an instant hit, widely praised for its elegant outline. In 2020, however, the car underwent a major redesign, intended to make it more similar to the luxurious G90 and G80. As a result, the G70 looked more polished and even more striking.

In 2021, a shooting brake model, based on the sedan was produced for the European market. Its stunning style made it an instant hit.c
DescriptionLong.0x00009241:
In April 2021, Hyundai's new premium brand, Genesis, unveiled its Genesis X concept, the brand's interpretation of how GT cars could look in the future. 

The front fascia features the shield-shaped crest grille that has become the brand's signature design element. Two lines stretch from the grille to past the front wheel arches and reappear again at the rear of the car to form the taillights. This new-generation example of car styling is part of Genesis calls its "Athletic Elegance" design language.

This car was more than a concept, as Genesis also created a racing edition for Gran Turismo that was inspired by the Genesis X. The Genesis X Gr.3 is a serious Gr.3-spec machine designed to compete in Gran Turismo's fierce championship competition.

The X concept was originally designed as an electric vehicle, but the Genesis X Gr.3 is equipped with a conventional gasoline engine. Thanks in part to forced induction, it produces <550ps>. To house the race car's larger tires, the body was widened to <1992mm>, while aerodynamic improvements were added to the underside. Also, a larger rear wing helps make this machine look race-ready. 

A combination of luxury and performance, the Genesis X Gr.3 is a radical new type of Gr.3 machine, the likes of which have never been seen before.p
DescriptionLong.0x00009243:
The G70 is a sports sedan developed as part of Hyundai's high-performance Genesis brand. A standard D-segment vehicle, it was released in 2017 and intended as an entry-level model.

Despite sharing most of its features, including the platform, with the KIA Stinger (KIA are also part of the Hyundai group), the G70 was designed from the ground up as a luxury sedan.

Three engines were made available for the G70: a twin-turbocharged 3.3-liter V-6, a turbocharged 2.0-liter gasoline turbo, and a 2.2-liter diesel turbo. The twin-turbo V-6 was capable of <370ps>. Like the other cars in the Genesis lineup, rear-wheel drive and AWD versions of the G70 were offered.

The G70's styling was an instant hit, widely praised for its elegant outline. In 2020, however, the car underwent a major redesign, intended to make it more similar to the luxurious G90 and G80. As a result, the G70 looked more polished and even more striking.

In 2021, a shooting brake model, based on the sedan was produced for the European market. Its stunning style made it an instant hit.

This particular car is a special tuned model, designed to comply with Gran Turismo's Gr.4 racing regulations.
DescriptionLong.0x00009345:
In September 2020, Nissan unveiled a new prototype Z car. Its design was reminiscent of the original 240Z (S30) that appeared in 1969. A few months later, Nissan announced that it would be building a production model scheduled to hit the market in North America in 2022. While the new Z would utilize the same platform of the previous model, sharing much of the same basic construction, everything else would be completely new. 

The new Z features a complex mix of tradition and cutting-edge technology. The exterior follows on from the S30's iconic long nose, while dynamic touches like its undulating character lines and LED headlights make it look fresh. It also utilizes the latest developments in cooling and aerodynamic performance.

The previous generation's naturally aspirated engine was replaced by the powerful VR30DDTT, a twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 found in the Skyline 400R that produced <405ps>/<6500rpm> and 475 Nm (<48.4kgm>)/<1600rpm>-<5600rpm> of torque.

This powerplant was mated to a 9-speed automatic with manual mode or a traditional 6-speed manual. To keep the car's curb weight in check for the automatic-gearbox model, the engineers opted to use a magnesium alloy transmission case. Also, the front and rear dampers featured monotube construction that improved response and an advanced launch control system that ensured the car left the line with aplomb. This is the first time Nissan offered such a system on its rear-wheel-drive models.

Can this classic sports car survive in an industry increasingly moving towards automated driving and electrification? Time will tell, but we think it will not only survive but flourish._
DescriptionLong.0x00009BB1:
Subaru began competing with the original BRZ in the GT300 class of the Super GT series in 2012. In 2016, it was one of the top teams in its class with some incredible performances on track. However, in the fall of 2020, the second-generation BRZ premiered in North America, which meant that a brand-new race machine was developed for the 2021 season.

As with the previous model, the engine was developed by STi and the body by R&D Sports. The vehicle as a whole was developed as an orthodox evolution of the previous model, carrying over many elements such as the basic structure and EJ20 engine.

The already aerodynamically superior second-generation BRZ were further improved by adding details developed from the previous model. The car's cornering characteristics were also enhanced through an overhaul of the weight distribution that included changing the position of the third damper.

Takuto Iguchi and Hideki Yamauchi both continued their roles as the drivers for the new model for the 2021 season. The new BRZ showed incredible potential from the start, taking pole position in 4 of the 8 races for a glorious champtionship victory. Subaru had been competing in domestic GT racing since the 1997 All Japan Grand Touring Championship, but this was their first such achievement./
DescriptionLong.0x00009BB2:
A collaborative effort between Subaru and Toyota resulted in the front engine/rear-wheel-drive Subaru BRZ and Toyota 86. In 2020, the second-generation versions (ZD8) of these identical twins were released.

A new platform was adopted, featuring a number of improvements from the previous models. The entire chassis adopted Subaru's inner frame construction, which provided more rigidity and reduced weight. The combination of Subaru's flat-4, also called a boxer engine, with Toyota's direct-injection technology was carried over from the previous car. One big change to the new car was that the engine's cylinder bore was enlarged, increasing displacement from 2.0 liters to 2.4 liters. As a result, output was raised to 173 kW (<235ps>)/250 Nm (<25.5kgm>), making the car faster and more pleasant to drive. The transmission was either a 6-speed manual or 6-speed automatic, with the automatic-equipped model coming with the EyeSight driver assistance system as standard equipment.

The car featured here is the "S," the high-end model with improved interior and exterior, including 18-inch wheels, ultra suede and leather combination seats and an 8-speaker car stereo.
DescriptionLong.0x00009D53:
With the LMP1-class TS050 Hybrid, TOYOTA GAZOO Racing captured two consecutive titles in the 2018–2019 and 2019–2020 World Endurance Championship seasons, along with three straight victories at Le Mans. But from 2021 onward, new regulations shifted the top level of competition to the LMH class. To meet these new conditions, Toyota developed the GR010 HYBRID.

As a completely new design, the GR010 differed from the TS050 in many ways, most notably in its powertrain. The engine went from a <500ps> twin-turbocharged 2.4-liter V-6 to a <680ps> twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6. Meanwhile, the <500ps> electric motors powering both front and rear wheels were replaced by a <272ps> system driving only the front wheels. The result was a 4-wheel-drive configuration that relied on electric power at the front and engine power at the rear.

For the 2021 season, Car No. 7 was driven by Mike Conway, Kamui Kobayashi, and José María López, while Car No. 8 was piloted by Sébastien Buemi, Kazuki Nakajima, and Brendon Hartley. That year, Toyota secured its fourth consecutive Le Mans victory—and sixth overall—marking a triumphant start to the new Hypercar era.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A042:
The world's largest hill climb race, the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb, is held every summer on Pikes Peak Highway near Colorado Springs in the United States.

The <20km> course covers an elevation difference of <1440m>, from <2862m> to <4302m> above sea level. It consists of 156 corners ranging from tight <60km/h> hairpins to <200km/h> sweeping high speed curves. Also, the temperature difference between the starting point and the finish line can be as much as 20 degrees. All these make for extremely harsh conditions for any race car.

The Suzuki V6 Escudo Pikes Peak Special was a machine developed specifically to compete in this environment. It was built around a newly designed aluminum space frame,  with the engine relocated aft of the front axle line to improve the car's front/rear weight distribution. The engine itself was tuned dramatically; the 2.5-liter V-6 came fitted with twin turbochargers, enabling it to pump out <995ps> and <95kgm> of torque.

Plenty of mass was taken out of the car. It tipped the scales at a lean 800kg. Helping to keep this lightweight vehicle planted to the road surface was a massive front spoiler and rear wing, both developed through extensive wind-tunnel testing. These modifications changed the production Escudo into a fearsome beast.

The car was driven by Nobuhiro "Monster" Tajima, who boasted seven consecutive wins in the All-Japan Dirt Trial Championships.  He began competing at Pikes Peak in 1988, and in 1995, he became the first Japanese driver to take the overall title at Pikes Peak. His race car then was the Suzuki Twin-Engine Escudo.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A043:
This car is the Gr.3 version of the Suzuki Vision Gran Turismo, a lightweight sports car combining the sporting philosophies of Suzuki's 2- and 4-wheel machines. This model highlights the company's racing prowess and has been extensively tuned to meet Gr.3 regulations.

The base Suzuki VGT features a hybrid powerplant, combining the <1340cc> Hayabusa engine with three high-powered electric motors. While the base car was all-wheel drive, the Gr.3 machine takes the form of a front-engine/rear-wheel driver with two 4-cyclinder Hayabusa engines bolted together, making it a <2680cc> V-8. With twin turbochargers providing extra muscle, this amazing engine produces <586ps> at an astoundingly high <10000rpm>.

Compared to the base model, the design aesthetics have been altered to provide increased downforce that comes via an enlarged front spoiler, rear wing, air ducting on the hood, and front and rear diffusers. Also, plenty of carbon fiber has been used to keep the car's weight minimal.

The livery represents a vivid representation of Suzuki's passion for motorsports, featuring graphics using Metallic Triton Blue and Metallic Mystic Silver, Suzuki's motorcycle race team colors.A
DescriptionLong.0x0000A1BD:
Every August in the U.S., the world’s most stunning automobiles from across automotive history gather for the prestigious Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance. In 2014, the Gran Turismo Trophy—just one of the many coveted awards—was claimed by this Maserati A6GCS/53 Spyder, chassis No. 2078.

The A6 nameplate referred to a series of 6-cylinder race cars Maserati developed between 1947 and 1956. The GCS variant was built for sports car championship competition and initially took the form of a two-seat version of the classic cigar-shaped Grand Prix racers. But in 1953, following a shift in regulations, coachbuilders began to craft their own bodies for the car’s tubular frame.

Chassis No. 2078 was one such creation, graced with an elegant Spyder body penned by Carrozzeria Fantuzzi. Its <170ps> engine came from none other than Gioachino Colombo. During the 1954 season, this car competed as part of the Maserati works team, racking up five class wins and three overall victories.u
DescriptionLong.0x0000A1BE:
The Hakosuka GT-R, which gets its nickname from "Hako" (square) and "Suka" (Skyline), took Japanese motorsports by storm and ended its illustrious career in 1972. But the legend of the Skyline refused to die, and fans continued to hope for its return many years after.

Their hopes became reality in 1982 when Nissan created a Silhouette Formula car based on the sixth-generation Skyline 2000RS, powered by a 4-valve DOHC engine that had not been in the lineup since the "Kenmeri" GT-R. (Ken Meri was a nickname that came from the car's commercials.) This was the Skyline Super Silhouette.

The Super Silhouette racecars were pure race cars that maintained the silhouette of production models. These cars were active in the Fuji Super Silhouette Series, which began as the supporting race for the Fuji Grand Champion Races in 1979, but the Silhouette Series soon became more popular than the main Grand Champion event.

The Skyline Super Silhouette is one of the most iconic cars from this series, with a look that is far from ordinary, to say the least. Sporting a chin spoiler that extends far forward of the car that nearly scrapes the tarmac, it also had fenders expanded to extreme levels at both the front and rear and a large rear wing. It came powered by a turbocharged 2.1-liter 4-cylinder race engine called the LZ20B. It often spit flames out of its exhaust, which was located just below the left door, making it an awesome presence on the track, completely mesmerizing car enthusiasts and race fans.

In the hands of legendary driver Masahiro Hasemi, it competed in the 1982 to 1984 seasons with eight wins to its credit. Because of regulation changes, it was active for three seasons, accounting for 19 races. People still refer to this car as the "extraordinary" Skyline, and it is still fondly remembered to this day.*
DescriptionLong.0x0000A33F:
The first-generation Pontiac GTO, which was introduced in 1964, was a big hit and is credited for the boom in street-legal muscle cars. The second-generation model followed in 1968 with a more stylish fastback style and decent performance. It wasn't enough to prevent the GTO from losing its king-of-the-hill status to its increasingly impressive rivals, however.

Keen to rectify this situation, in 1969, General Motors released a new GTO known as "The Judge." The standard sports package wore an exclusive logo and stripe decals, and powered by a 6.6-liter V-8 "Ram Air 3" engine that was said to be capable of more than the advertised <366ps>. It was mated to a Hurst shifter. The car had a heavy-duty suspension system, wide tires, and a rear spoiler. Despite all this, it only cost $332 more than the standard GTO. In terms of both performance and sheer presence, it outdid its rivals and attracted plenty of attention.

Muscle cars such as the GTO started to disappear when strict emissions regulations were introduced a couple of years later.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A341:
Porsche has competed in many sports-car races with the 911, which was one of the most popular models in its production-car lineup. The company eyed going racing with another of its production cars in 2015, when it introduced the Cayman GT4. The Cayman was a mid-engine model that possessed performance levels comparable to the 911, and the GT4 was created specifically for motorsports.

The Cayman GT4 had the same combination of 3.8-liter flat-6 and 6-speed manual gearbox used in the 911 Carrera S. In fact, it actually outdoes the 911 with <385ps> of power.

Some parts from the 991 GT3 were used for the brakes and suspension of the Cayman GT4, thus reducing ride height by <30mm>. The 2-seater also came with a distinctive lip spoiler and a fixed rear wing.

The choice of optional extras included a roll cage, fire extinguisher, and a 6-point seatbelt, making it clear from the start that this was a car designed for the track.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A460:
The S14 Silvia made its debut in October 1993 as the successor to the hugely successful S13 model, and with a new larger body, Nissan hoped to continue on the car's previous success.

The S14 sat <1730mm> wide compared to the S13's <1690> and the track was also enlarged. The new car stretched <30mm> longer at <4500mm> and <5mm> taller at <1295mm> than the outgoing model. The softer lines of the body really enhanced the wider nature of the car's body. The K trim level came with 16-inch wheels as standard, further adding to it visual flair.

Under the hood was a retuned version of the S13's SR20 engine. The K model came with an intercooled turbocharger that helped pump out <15ps> more than the previous generation at <220ps>/<28.0kgm>. The naturally-aspirated Q and J trim levels produced <160ps>/<19.2kgm>. The basic suspension geometry was carried over from the S13, featuring front struts and a multilink system at rear. The car was also available with Super HICAS electronic rear wheel steering.

The S14 placed an extra focus on luxury to increase its appeal as an FR coupe, but when Japan's financial bubble burst in 1991, the coupe market shrank, and the car lost its appeal. To revitalize the model, Nissan released a facelift model in 1996 with an extensive redesign. The exterior's soft image was tightened up with scowling headlights and a large real spoiler for a sharper and more striking appearance. 

The S14 Silvia was sold in North America as the 240SX and in Europe as the 200SX.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A461:
Starting in 1948, Porsche built its reputation as one of the world’s premier automotive manufacturers by creating elegant, well-engineered lightweight sports cars. These cars were not defined by extreme horsepower, but instead were characterized by a highly efficient power-to-weight ratio combined with timeless, functional design.

The Porsche Vision Gran Turismo follows in this tradition while expressing the company's take on the future of the sports car. It merges elements of the iconic design of historic Porsche sports cars with the company's storied race machines. The car also possesses hints of the record-breaking 919 Hybrid, as well as Porsche's first electric sports car, the Taycan.

Exterior and interior design flow seamlessly together, providing drivers with the feeling of being one with the car when inside the cockpit of the state-of-the-art carbon monocoque chassis. The glass dome places them into the surrounding natural environment. 

The Porsche Vision Gran Turismo’s dual electric engine layout delivers 820 kW (<1114ps>) of power and a maximum torque of 1,090 Nm (<111kgm>). An innovative active aerodynamic system dynamically reacts to all driving situations to enhance the car’s performance, thus making the car perfectly suited for the demanding corners and high-speed segments found on tracks like the Nürburgring Nordschleife or on alpine roads.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A462:
As the threat of global climate change looms ever closer, automotive manufacturers are pushing forward with electrification to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. Volkswagen was one of the first companies to take up the challenge. The company introduced its ID brand in 2020, which included a radical performance machine that showed the awesome performance potential of electric vehicles. This car was the ID.R prototype race car.

The ID.R's body was constructed of carbon-fiber, with oversized wings placed on the front and rear to produce maximum downforce. At <5.2m> long, the car was relatively large, but weighed less than <1100kg>. The dual-motor 4WD system produced 500 kW (<680ps>) / 650 Nm (<66.3kgm>), allowing for a 0-<100km>/h acceleration time of just 2.25s. These performance statistics rivaled those of race cars with internal combustion engines.

In the real world, the ID.R competed in numerous motorsports events around the world and produced amazing results. At the 2018 Pikes Peak Hill Climb, driver Romain Dumas set a record of 7 minutes 57 seconds, the first ever run to break the 8-minute barrier. At the Nürburgring Nordschliefe, the ID.R set the record for fastest lap by an EV at 6 minutes 5 seconds. At the Goodwood Festival of Speed, the car became the first to ever finish the legendary hill in less than 40 seconds with a record of 39.9s.

Since the birth of the automobile, people have been enamored with the pursuit of speed. The ID.R is proof that even in the age of electrification, this fascination lives on.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A51E:
The C10 Skyline, more commonly known as the Hakosuka, was succeeded by an all-new model in September 1972. The new car, designated C110 , came to be known as "Kenmeri" because its commercials featured a couple of models named Ken and Mary. The car was an instant hit, thanks to its attractive styling and excellent performance. The Kenmeri also included the four round headlights that defined previous Skylines. 

The top-of-the-line GT-R was added to the Kenmeri lineup in January 1973. This car was designated inhouse as KPGC110, and it came equipped with the same legendary engine as its predecessor, the S20 inline-6. Output remained at <160ps> and <18.0kgm> of torque, as did the front strut and rear semi-trailing arm suspension, but the new 4-wheel disc brakes were an improvement over the previous model.

The car's dimensions were <4460mm> in overall length, with a width of <1695mm> and height of <1380mm>, not much different than the Hakosuka.

The Kenmeri GT-R should have won many races, but it wasn't able to compete because of stringent emissions regulations. You see, the S20 inline-6 was virtually a pure race engine, which meant it could not adhere to the new emissions laws. So, Nissan made the difficult decision of shelving the Kenmeri after only three months and 197 units produced, without it ever having raced. The GT-R name would lay dormant for another 16 years, until it returned in the form of the R32.J
DescriptionLong.0x0000A51F:
Released in 2015, the fourth-generation ND MX-5 received worldwide praise for its return to the original concept of "Jinba Ittai," which translates to "rider and horse, one body." This essence was especially apparent in the NR-A trim level, which was intended for track use. 

The NR-A first made its appearance on the second-generation NB MX-5, catering to those who enjoyed driving their sports cars on the track. The concept proved popular enough for Mazda to include an NR-A in the ND lineup. 

The section of the frame that connects the transmission to the rear differential was upgraded for the ND NR-A, along with the driveshaft, LSD and differential case. The size of the radiator and brake rotors were increased, and the suspension adopted height-adjustable dampers made by Bilstein. Another useful feature was the Multi-Information Display that allowed the driver to get vital stats through switches on the steering wheel.

This 2022 model has further improvements, including a new Kinematic Posture Control system that stabilizes the rear end of the car. The options list also features racing equipment such as roll bars and bucket seats, which come especially useful for hot-lapping sessions.

The NR-A is the ideal track car for weekend warriors because of its excellent and predictable handling, with power delivery that's just enough to make things fun and exciting.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A5FF:
The BMW 2 Series coupe is a popular high-performance rear-wheel-drive compact car. The BMW M2 Competition is the extreme version that fills the same engine compartment with a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged inline-6 "S55" engine from the M3 and M4.

What you'll notice first is the car's captivating bodywork. With its bulging over fenders, the exterior is the embodiment of speed. Although it measures only <4475mm> in length, it's actually about the same size as the E36 M3. Whether in the city or on winding backroads, the car displays an incredible sense of control, as if it was an extension of the driver's body.

The S55 engine delivers a maximum power output of <410ps> with <56.1kgm> peak torque. Even up against BMW's long history of high-performance inline-6 engines, this model has an exceptional high-revving nature, and as the boost builds its explosive power emerges.

No compromises have been made to the running gear either. To reduce unsprung weight, the aluminum suspension components have been specially tuned for spirited driving. Meanwhile, the torque vectoring "Active M Differential" ensures the car turns exactly where you want it to.

Now that the M3 and M4 have moved to a higher segment, this car may be the ideal expression of BMW's "Ulitmate Driving Machine."
DescriptionLong.0x0000A600:
The Sierra was a relatively standard family car with an aerodynamic hatchback body produced by Ford Europe from 1982.

But in 1985, the impression of car enthusiasts regarding the Sierra took a big turn. This was because the famed Cosworth added the Sierra RS Cosworth to the selection, known affectionately as the "Cossie" among enthusiasts. The Sierra RS Cosworth was powered by a 2.0-liter inline 4 tuned to <206ps> with DOHC and a turbocharger. The chassis was reinforced, and the exterior was upgraded with fender extensions and a large rear spoiler.

A year later, power was further increased to <227ps>, and a 500-unit limited Sierra RS 500 Cosworth was added to the lineup, with an engine reinforced for race use and better aerodynamic details.

And, of course, all of these improvements were developed for touring car racing. From 1988 to 1990, the Sierra won a number of series championship titles in the international Group A category in countries such as Germany, UK, Australia, Japan and New Zealand.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A601:
The S14 Silvia made its debut in October 1993 as the successor to the hugely successful S13 model. Armed with a new larger body Nissan hoped to continue on its previous successes.

The S14 is <1730mm> wide compared to the S13's <1690> ,and track width was increased. The new model is also <30mm> longer at <4500mm> and <5mm> taller at <1295mm> for an overall larger body. The softer lines of the body design make the wider stance stand out the most. The K's grade model also featured 16-inch wheels as standard.

The engine is a retuned version of the S13's SR20 series. The highest grade K's model features an intercooled turbocharger and produces <15ps> more than the previous generation at <220ps>/<28.0kgm> with the naturally aspirated Q's and J's models producing <160ps>/<19.2kgm>. The basic suspension structure was carried over from the S13, utilizing front struts and a multilink setup at the rear. The car was also available with the Super HICAS electronic rear-wheel steering system.

In 1996, Nissan released a facelift model with an extensive redesign. The exterior's soft image was tightened up with scowling headlights and a large real spoiler was added for a more sharp and striking appearance.

The "Aero" model featured here was added to the Q's and K's lineup in the spring of 1995 as the top-of-the-line model. The exterior features unique bumpers along with front and rear spoilers. The interior received a leather wrapped steering wheel, a new shift knob and white gauge faces. These changes proved to be popular with drivers, and the grade was continued on the facelift model.

As the number of affordable rear-wheel-drive coupes dwindled through the 1990s, the S14 Silvia can be considered a very important car for carrying that design DNA into the next generation. It was also popular overseas where it was sold in North America as the 240SX and in Europe as the 200SX.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A608:
The Ferrari Vision Gran Turismo is the first Ferrari single-seater concept car dedicated to the world of virtual motor sport, with a spectacular and futuristic design founded in the Prancing Horse's unequalled racing heritage. The Ferrari Vision Gran Turismo draws its inspiration from the fascinating world of Ferrari's hugely successful 1960s and '70s sports-prototypes. Below hyper-modern bodywork and dramatic proportions, the car hides the DNA of masterpieces such as the Ferrari 330 P3 and the 512S. It is a nod to the past, yet a powerful hint of the future of endurance racing.

The Ferrari Vision Gran Turismo's architecture is crafted around an advanced aerodynamic design and is equipped with the same engine architecture that powers the Ferrari 499P. Here, though, the engine has been made more extreme to develop no less than 1,030 CV (<1030ps>) at <9000rpm>, with an additional 240 kW (<326ps>) available through three electric motors, one on the rear axle and one on each of the front wheels.n
DescriptionLong.0x0000A6A6:
The Chiron is a super sports car unveiled by Bugatti in 2016. This limited production model was introduced as a follow-up to the Veyron, with only 500 units available worldwide.

The exterior featured large C-shaped lines that encircled the cabin and also served as air intakes. The body possessed an accentuated centerline inspired by the Type 57 Atlantic Coupe that increased straight-line stability.

The carbon-fiber chassis provided the same level of rigidity as an LMP1 race car and housed the Veyron's quad-turbo 8.0-liter W-16 engine, which was extensively tuned to produce <1500ps> and <163.1kgm> of torque.

The car ran from 0-<100km/h> in 2.5 seconds, and a pre-production prototype was able to reach a maximum speed of <490.48km/h>.

In 2018, the Chiron Sport was introduced with an improved chassis weighing <18kg> less than the original. In 2019, the limited edition "Chiron Sport 110 ans Bugatti" was released to celebrate the 110th anniversary of Bugatti. Only 20 of them were made.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A6A7:
The car often called "America's sports car," the Chevrolet Corvette, saw a drastic change to its layout in 2019. That year came the eighth-generation iteration, which had its powerplant mounted behind the cockpit, making it the first MR Corvette in its history. 

The new engine location was evident upon first glance of the car. The Corvette's iconic long nose is now absent, as the cabin was moved far forward, resulting in proportions of a classic mid-engine sports car. Without an engine, the front section serves as a luggage compartment to go along with luggage area behind the engine that's big enough to store a small golf bag.

The car's V-8 engine is a new-generation small-block LT2 developed from the previous generation model C7's LT1 engine. With 6.2 liters of displacement, it produces <502ps>/<65.0kgm> and also features fuel saving features like cylinder deactivation. The only transmission available for the new Corvette is an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic with paddle shifters allowing drivers to select gears manually. The suspension system consists of double wishbones at all four corners with a height adjustable capability to tackle various road surfaces and for aerodynamic purposes.

The driver-centered cockpit features a multifunctional infotainment system with an 8-inch touchscreen. With the engine bay moved to the rear of the cabin, the new generation Corvette has shown itself to be a contender with exceptional performance in GT car racing.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A6A8:
When it comes to front-wheel-drive cars, Citroën has few equals, and the DS can be considered the company's masterpiece, which came laden with the most cutting-edge technologies of the day.

The DS first appeared at the 1955 Salon de l'Automobile. While many other manufacturers were still producing cars in the pre-war style, the DS represented a stunning vision of the future. With its avant-garde aerodynamic body and revolutionary hydropneumatic suspension system, it was nicknamed the "flying saucer." Development was led by André Lefèbvre, while the comparatively large <4.8m> long body was the work of Italian designer Flaminio Bertoni, who also worked on the classic 2CV.

With such a forward-thinking design, the DS remained relevant for a long period of time. Along with various equipment and engine upgrades, the car was produced for 20 years. In 1964, the "Pallas" grade that included luxury interior and exterior fixtures was added to the lineup. In 1967, a slight facelift gave the car four round headlights that replaced the two-light scheme. 

The DS 21 Pallas, produced from 1969, came powered by a <116.7ps> 2.1-liter engine. The large seats and spacious interior remained, and the lightweight car accelerated briskly.

While originally conceived as an everyday passenger vehicle, the DS was also loved as a government vehicle, ambulance and even a taxi. It is one of the most important French cars in automotive history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A6A9:
After capturing the double title of Driver and Constructors championships with the ST185's brilliant showing in 1993, Toyota introduced the new ST205 Celica the following year, searching for even more victories in the WRC.

Although the new Celica was bigger than its predecessor, it had better weight distribution with a longer wheelbase and wider track. The TTE works team was involved in the car's development from the very start, providing key contributions to overall aerodynamic and cooling performance.

The Celica was scheduled to appear at the 1994 1000 Lakes Rally, but because of unexpected delays in undercarriage development, it spent the 1994 season running trial races.

The Celica participated as a full-time entrant in the 1995 WRC season, battling with the newly improved Subaru Impreza. Driver Didier Auriol scored the first win for the car in the fourth round at the Tour de Corse. Although Toyota continued to experience problems with its super strut suspension, the team continued racing and making improvements throughout the season to overcome the handicap.

In the seventh round at Catalonia, the Celica was found to be in violation of the intake restrictor diameter regulation and was stripped of all points for the season. In a show of opposition to the decision, Toyota ended its participation in the WRC, which resulted in the ST205's run in the series to be limited to just one season.

Although it was only active for a short time, this machine's unmistakable silhouette imprinted itself on the hearts of many fans. When discussing Toyota's rally cars, this is one that must be mentioned.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A827:
Italdesign, founded in 1968 in Turin, Italy, has designed and engineered more than 300 production cars and 100 concept vehicles, many of which have been displayed the world's most important auto shows. More than a few cars designed by Italdesign are featured in Gran Turismo.

Some Italdesign creations have gone on to become famous movie cars, such as the DeLorean DMC 12 featured in the hit film trilogy "Back to the Future," and who can forget the Lotus Esprit that turned into a submarine in the James Bond feature "The Spy Who Loved Me?"

The Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo continues the endearing relationship between Gran Turismo and Italian automobiles. Inspired by the 2013 mid-engine compact GT called the Italdesign Parcour, this concept machine features cutting-edge technology and four different chassis settings—track, snow, off-road and urban—thus, it's at home on both the race track and off-road trails.

The car comes powered by two 200 kW (<272ps>) electric motors mounted up front, and a V-10 engine placed amidships that produce a combined 910 kW (<1237.3ps>), allowing the EXENEO VGT to reach a top speed of <380km/h> and a zero-to-<100km> acceleration time of 2.5 seconds. The EXENEO also has a 7-speed gearbox, Individual Wheel Drive (IWD) and KERS recovery system. To ensure maximum stability, an intelligent suspension system adapts automatically to different types of terrain.

The crystal sphere cockpit was developed around the driver. A carbon-fiber and aluminum tape envelope the driver and engine as a "xenium." This Latin word translates to "gift for the guest," and what a gift the Italdesign EXENEO Vision Gran Turismo is.

DescriptionLong.0x0000A8B2:
Honda has always been at the forefront of innovation. This dates back to the company's early days, a precedent established by founder Soichiro Honda. An example of its technical prowess was its Formula 1 race car in 1964. Called the RA271, it featured an aluminum shell over a space frame body and a 1.5-liter V-12 engine mounted transversely in an unusual fashion amidships. Unfortunately, the car did not fare well in its debut season.

The following year, Honda radically changed the RA271, resulting in the RA272. The RA272E engine was a more efficient version of the previous V-12 with lighter components. The construction of the rear suspension was changed from an inboard to an outboard setup, which allowed the weight to be reduced from <525kg> to <498kg>, signifying a drastic decrease. The drivers for the new, improved Honda race car were Ronnie Bucknum, in his second year, and new arrival Richie Ginther.

At the start of the 1965 season, the extra power from the RA272's engine showed great potential, but the car suffered from poor stability. The team opted to skip Round 7's German Grand Prix to address the issue. The engineers moved the engine <100mm> rearward, while also making adjustments to the body, suspension and exhaust.

In the final race of the season—Round 10's Mexican Grand Prix—the RA272 finally showed its true potential. After starting in 3rd place, Ginther grabbed the lead and stayed there until the finish, giving Honda its first F1 victory. Teammate Bucknum finished 5th.

Since then, Honda has won many F1 races and several championships, and it was the RA272 that started it all for the forward-thinking Japanese car manufacturer.
DescriptionLong.0x0000A8C2:
Introduced in 1973, the 911 Carrera RS 2.7 was the first model in the long history of the Porsche 911 to feature the RS badge. The "RS" stands for "Rennsport," which is translated as "racing sport" in English. As its name suggests, this sports car was developed as a homologation model for the FIA's Group 4 category.

Mounted at the rear is a 2.4-liter engine from the base model 1973 911 S, but displacement was increased to 2.7 liters, which in turn upped power to <210ps>. The front end was modified to house an air dam that fed into an oil cooler. The tail section of the car featured the iconic duck-tail spoiler as standard fare, and the fenders were stretched to make room for wider rear tires.

The Carrera RS 2.7 came in three grades: Touring, Sport and Racing. Of note, even the luxury-oriented Touring model weighed less than <1100kg>.

The car was originally produced in a limited homologation run of 500 units; however, because it sold out almost immediately, Porsche increased production to 1,580 units.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AA88:
The year 2019 marked a pivotal time of reform for the German Touring Car Championship (DTM). The series adopted the new Class 1 regulations, including the downsizing of engines, allowing for the possibility of shared race events with Japan's Super GT Championship.  

Audi's entry in this new arena was this RS 5 DTM, powered by a brand-new engine. While the exterior retained the familiar look from the previous season, beneath the body, the naturally-aspirated 4.0-liter V-8 was replaced with a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 engine. This change resulted in a dramatic reduction in weight and improved weight distribution, while also delivering more than 600 hp, far exceeding the output of its predecessor. It was a completely new machine on the inside. 

Audi entered six of these RS 5 DTM cars in 2019 through its factory DTM teams. With additional support from customer teams, the Audi RS 5 DTM was a dominant force on the grid. Among this impressive lineup, one car stood out above the rest: Car No. 33, piloted by ace driver René Rast. From the opening rounds, the car proved unstoppable, clinching victory after victory. In the final race at Hockenheim (Race 2), it achieved a pole-to-win finish, besting fellow Audi driver Nico Müller. Audi Sport Team Rosberg, with Rast at the helm, also claimed the team title, making car No. 33 a historic double-title winner. 

The final round at Hockenheim was a special mixed-class event featuring Japan's Super GT500 cars, and an interleague exhibition race followed in Japan. However, the emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic led to Audi's withdrawal from the DTM. With one of its key manufacturers stepping away, the Class 1 regulations were retired after just two seasons.

Despite its short lifespan, the Audi RS 5 DTM stands as a shining representation of the ambition and innovation embodied by Class 1 regulations and has become a vital part of motorsports history. m
DescriptionLong.0x0000AA8A:
This MAZDA3 represents the fourth-generation model of Mazda's C-segment passenger car first released in November 2018. Back then, it was called the Axela in Japan, but with this model, it went by the moniker "MAZDA3" all around the world. 

Like its predecessor, this MAZDA3 came in both fastback and sedan versions, but thanks to the company's "KODO" design language, the character of the car became more refined. The shape of the fastback was especially impressive, with the delicate form of the body panels beautifully expressing the subtle transition of light.

Powering the car was a new SKYACTIV engine. The base MAZDA3 models came with a 1.5-liter and 2.0-liter direct injection gasoline engines. There was a 1.8-liter turbo diesel powerplant and a 2.0-liter "Mild-Hybrid" (M-Hybrid) version that came a little later. The M-Hybrid was powered by the SKYACTIV-X engine that introduced proprietary spark-controlled compression ignition, a revolutionary technology that suppressed carbon emissions without relying on expensive solutions like the Urea-SCR.

The X Burgundy Selection was a special model with a burgundy interior on the Grade X model. Equipped with wine-colored leather seats and dashboard, this special model exuded a classy, uniquely mature aura.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AAA1:
At the 1983 Frankfurt Auto Show, Porsche introduced the "Gruppe B" concept model. This was a design study of an all-wheel-drive race car that was being developed for competition in the top "Group B" category of the WRC that started in 1982.

Two years later, in 1985, the road going version of this model was unveiled. Called the Porsche 959, it adopted the basic structure of the Porsche 911 and was packed with revolutionary technology. The engine was a <2850cc> twin-turbocharged horizontally-opposed 6 cylinder, with a maximum output of 450 horsepower. It came mated to a 6-speed manual transmission.

The most noteworthy feature of this car was its electronically controlled all-wheel-drive system that actively managed the drive ratio between the front and rear wheels according to the conditions of the road surface. Also, it was possible to select a drive mode that matched the current driving condition. The 959's all-wheel-drive system was truly revolutionary in that it provided not only excellent stability at high speeds, but also convenience for the user. 

Only 292 examples of the Porsche 959 were produced for Group B homologation, but because of the termination of the Group B category, the race version never made it to the WRC. But it did go on to set great records in competition, even winning the overall title at the Paris-Dakar Rally, which is considered one of the most grueling races in the world.

Many of the technical innovations of the 959, including the all-wheel-drive system, saw their way into the company's other production cars, such as the 911. The Porsche 959 still enjoys a high level of respect and popularity today and remains a very important part of automotive history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AAA3:
The minivan is a popular automotive category in Japan. It has become a highly competitive segment with each manufacturer vying to outdo the other. But the one vehicle that has held the undisputed title of the ultimate premium minivan is the Toyota Alphard. 

Since its introduction in 2002, the Toyota Alphard redefined the category with its classy styling and smooth, quiet ride quality. Its highly premium nature has made it a popular limousine for transporting VIP guests in Japan.

The third-generation Alphard that bowed in 2015 was a refined version of its predecessor. Of note was the "Executive Lounge" luxury version that redefined the vehicle's second-row seating. Unique to the Executive Lounge were the "Executive Lounge Seats," which were one size larger than the seats of the base model, equipped with heating and ventilation as well as a folding mini-table. The quality of the leather and stitching was a major point of focus by Toyota, and the result was a high level of comfort and convenience that were comparable to a first-class airline seat.

A minor model change was performed in 2017, with output of the Alphard's 3.5-liter V-6 being increased from <280ps> to <301ps>. The transmission was also optimized with more gears, going from a 6-speed automatic to an 8-speed. Also, the Alphard's structural rigidity was enhanced, making its ride smoother and more stable than ever before.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AAA5:
Shortly after its establishment in the 1950s, Porsche quickly rose to prominence in global motorsports with the 356 and its purpose-built mid-engine derivatives like the 550 Spyder. 

One of the key milestones that carried this legacy forward was the 1963 Porsche Carrera GTS. Also known by its development code, the 904 GTS, it was developed in response to the evolving World Sportscar Championship regulations.  

In the 1950s, the championship featured low-volume, pure racing machines. However, the regulation changes of 1961 shifted the focus to mass-produced sports cars. To compete in the GT Class, manufacturers had to meet a homologation requirement of producing at least 100 units. 

Porsche responded with the Carrera GTS, engineered around a ladder-frame chassis better suited for small-series production. It was then wrapped in a lightweight fiberglass-reinforced plastic (FRP) body. This combination was a first for the company. Styling was led by Ferdinand Alexander Porsche, grandson of company founder Dr. Ferdinand Porsche. His design gave the car its low, clean lines that remain iconic to this day. Mounted in a mid-engine layout was an air-cooled flat-4 engine, though the chassis was versatile enough to accept 6- and even 8-cylinder units for competition use. 

From its debut, the Carrera GTS proved its capability with victories in storied events like the Targa Florio, as well as class wins at endurance races including the Nürburgring and Le Mans. In 1964, it went on to dominate the GT Class Championship.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AB80:
The Mercedes-AMG GT3 was based on the Mercedes-AMG GT sports car that was unveiled to the public at the Paris Motor Show in 2014. This FIA (Federation Internationale de l'Automobile) homologated GT3 race car appeared on the international motorsports scene in 2016.

This updated 2020 model was introduced in 2019 with a focus on further reducing running costs as a customer race car. Improvements like a more durable engine and better protection for the radiator through a redesigned front end helped keep the costs of running a GT3 car more affordable for privateers. 

The car's aerodynamics were improved through the addition of a front splitter and winglets, as well as a large wing and diffuser at the rear. The engineers also reduced the car's weight by using carbon fiber anywhere and everywhere possible.

The lower portion of the front grille was significantly widened, and the front and rear lights were updated. Although it retained the distinctive design of the previous model, many details on the car were updated to match the refreshed production model. Y
DescriptionLong.0x0000AB81:
In spring 2023, Japan's top formula race series, Super Formula, saw the debut of the new Dallara SF23 race car.

The SF23 uses a number of new technologies from the "SUPER FORMULA NEXT50" motorsports sustainability project headed by Japan Race Promotion, the organizers of Super Formula.

The body of the SF23, based on the SF19 introduced in 2019, uses bio-composite materials produced by the Bcomp company. This allows a 75-percent reduction in CO2 emissions through the raw materials and construction processes while keeping the same weight and body rigidity as the previous carbon-fiber shell. 

The car's tires are provided by Yokohama Rubber, which have also been developed for sustainability and are composed of sustainable materials such as naturally derived polymers and recycled rubbers. Although the Yokohama Carbon Neutral Racing Tires use 33-percent of sustainably sourced materials, they achieve the same handling levels as before. Equipped with these new tires, the SF23 becomes the ideal carbon neutral racing machine as outlined in SUPER FORMULA NEXT50.

To achieve another of the campaign's goals, which is to increase the entertainment value of the Super Formula races, the aerodynamics of the SF23 went through a complete overhaul. The new body allows drivers more opportunity to show off their skills in close quarters than ever before. As for the engines, the teams continue to choose between a Toyota or Honda powerplant.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AB82:
