DescriptionLong.0x0000AB83:
In 1988, Jaguar showed a prototype of a super sports machine at the British International Motor Show called the XJ220. In 1991, it unveiled the final production version of the car at the Tokyo Motor Show. The XJ220 received its name from its maximum speed, which was 220 mph, the highest ever at the time for a commercially marketed car.

Jaguar entrusted production of the XJ220 to Jaguar Sports, a joint venture with TWR, which developed the Jaguar Group C car and was in charge of its race team. The prototype engine was a naturally-aspirated V-12, but the XJ220 that was shown in Tokyo came with a twin-turbo 3.5-liter V-6 engine from the XJR11 Group C car. The chassis was crafted from composite aluminum honeycomb and carbon Kevlar, not unlike that of a serious race car. Under the body, a panel that produced serious ground effects was added, again, just like a Group C racer. Setting the car apart from the race machine was a luxurious interior that was finished with the finest materials around, in the same manner as the company's notable luxury cars.

In 1993, Jaguar entered the XJ220 into the GT class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Taking the wheel were David Coulthard, David Brabham, and John Nielsen, who teamed up to successfully complete the endurance race and win in its class...or so everyone thought. A month later, the XJ220 was disqualified due to an exhaust violation, and its result was stricken from the books.

Later, the XJ220 was entrusted to the famous Team Chamberlain race team and continued to participate in GT races including the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
DescriptionLong.0x0000ACEC:
The first generation Giulia was marketed from the 1960s to the 1970s and proved to be a huge hit for Alfa Romeo. The Giulia was available only as a 4-door sedan when it went on sale in 1962, but a coupe version was added to the line up in 1963. This first coupe was called the Sprint GT.

It was designed by a young Giorgetto Giugiaro, who was with Carrozzeria Bertone at the time. The car's body consisted of smooth lines and soft curves, with a characteristic edge at the front. The beauty of the car has made it popular among classic-car enthusiasts to this day.

The Giulia Sprint GT came powered by a 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4. Producing <106ps> and <14.2kgm> torque, it propelled the lightweight <950kg> body to a top speed of <180km/h>.

The car was extremely popular with driving enthusiasts because of its compact lightweight body, which translated to exceptional handling and acceleration. All of this allowed the Giulia Sprint GT to overcome the test of time, being produced until 1977.L
DescriptionLong.0x0000ACED:
The SEMA Show takes place every year in November in Las Vegas, Nevada. At the world’s largest automotive aftermarket festival, Gran Turismo handpicked standout vehicles for its prestigious Gran Turismo Awards. In 2018, the "Best of Show" honors went to the 1971 Ford Maverick, created by Greening Auto Company (GAC).

The Maverick was originally an affordable compact coupe built on the Ford Falcon chassis. GAC transformed the Maverick into a monster hot rod that blended extreme performance with street-friendly drivability.

The exterior's lowered ride height and flared fenders immediately turned heads, but the real showstopper was found under the hood. In the engine compartment resided Ford's famous 7.0-liter small-block Windsor V-8. Packing not one, but two turbochargers, GAC claimed the engine unleashed a staggering <1216ps>. But it wasn't all about raw, unadulterated power—adjustable engine control logic allowed for the car to cruise comfortably around town.

In the spring of 2019, this Maverick took on a top speed challenge, setting a record of 202.748 mph (approximately <326km/h>). This car was truly a rare masterpiece where nostalgia and cutting-edge technology seamlessly blended together.
DescriptionLong.0x0000ACEE:
Nissan's BNR32 Skyline GT-R was created to win touring car races. Armed with the RB26DETT engine with displacement meeting Group A specifications, this all-wheel-drive grand tourer had all the ingredients that went into a high-performance sports machine, including a 4-wheel steering system. 

As was expected, a GT-R NISMO version appeared in its second year of production in the form of a Group A homologation model with a limited production of 500 cars.

Compared to the standard GT-R, the GT-R NISMO was equipped with fins above the front grille that increased airflow into the engine room for cooling, as well as air inlet openings in the front bumper. To improve aerodynamic characteristics, the rear end of the side sills had protectors that directed airflow around the rear tires. A small rear spoiler was also added to improve downforce, while the turbos were changed from ceramic to metal. The exhaust manifold was specially redesigned for this car, and to reduce weight the A/C, audio system, and rear wipers were deleted, making the car <30kg> lighter than the base model.

The GT-R NISMO won the top touring car class in Japan, as well as many other famous endurance races throughout Asia, Europe and in Australia. Its mere presence was enough to cause havoc at Group A races all over the world.M
DescriptionLong.0x0000ADDC:
The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution, launched in September 1992, took the compact body of the production Lancer sedan and implemented components used in the Galant VR-4 WRC race car. Thus, the Lancer Evolution was a rally machine in the guise of a passenger sedan. 

At the heart of the "Evo" was the 4G63, a turbocharged 2.0-liter DOHC inline-4 that pumped out <250ps> and <31.5kgm> of torque at the time of its debut. With the incredible power delivered to all four wheels, the car had amazing traction and was already much faster than any other model in its class.

One year after its creation, in December 1993, an improved Lancer Evolution II was introduced with power increased to <260ps>. The tires were also changed to 205/60R15, while modifications to the wheelbase were also implemented. At about this time, Japanese fans began referring to it by a new nickname, "Lan-Evo."

Then came another "evolution" in January 1995, when the Lancer Evolution III was introduced. It featured a drastically modified body style that resulted in better aerodynamic performance. With a larger grille and an enhanced rear spoiler, it now had the powerful look of a vehicle focused on competition.

The compression ratio of the 4G63 power unit was raised to 9.0, improving output to <270ps>. Enhancements were also made to the suspension, and these changes greatly improved the car's already excellent handling character. At the time, the base Lancer model was about to receive a full model change, and it was rumored then that the Evo III could be the last Evo.G
DescriptionLong.0x0000ADDD:
Few car companies possess a rich and profound history like that of Aston Martin. Founded 110 years ago, the British car company, known for its beautiful and powerful road and race cars, recently produced the Valkyrie, developed in collaboration with Formula 1 constructor Red Bull Racing.

The design started from an idea for an innovative road car devised by Red Bull Racing's designer and aerodynamics expert, Adrian Newey, who took his proposal to Aston Martin where chief designer Marek Reichman took notice. In 2016, the project began in earnest as the "AM-RB 001," the letters standing for Aston Martin and Red Bull. The car was unveiled at the 2017 Geneva Motor Show as the AM-RB, along with its official name, the Valkyrie.

Production versions of the Valkyrie were first seen in 2021, taking form as a uniquely shaped hypercar that incorporated F1-derived aerodynamics combined with Aston Martin's design language. The front of the car featured a spoiler that directed air through Venturi tunnels in the underbody, generating massive downforce at high speed. Inside the teardrop shaped cockpit, the driver and passenger sat with their feet elevated ala an F1 car.

Extensive use of lightweight materials was implemented, including the carbon-fiber body. Even the Aston Martin nose emblem was made lighter, crafted from aluminum measuring only 70 microns wide. As a result, the car tipped the scales at roughly <1000kg>, achieving an astonishing power-to-weight ratio of <1.0kg/ps>.

Mounted aft of the cabin is a hybrid power unit that combined a naturally-aspirated 6.5-liter V-12 Cosworth engine with a KERS (Kinetic Energy Recovery System). The total output of the system was rated at <1155ps>, putting the car on par with top category racing machines.

Only 150 units of the coupe version of the Valkyrie were offered at US $3 million, and they sold out almost immediately. Then came the "AMR pro," a Le Mans style competition model, and an open-top "Spider" version. Whatever model you chose, one thing for sure was that the Aston Martin Valkyrie remains one of a handful of hypercars to boast the performance levels of an LMP1 machine.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AF31:
Gazoo Racing (GR), Toyota’s high-performance brand, had drawn on its motorsports experience to create the ultimate hot hatch, the GR Corolla.

The goal for this car was to deliver exceptional performance, ready to take on any rival. The base chassis of the Corolla Sport had its front track widened by <60mm> and the rear by <85mm>, enhancing cornering ability. To further increase rigidity during hard cornering, 349 additional structural spot welds were applied.

The powerplant was the same turbocharged 1.6-liter 3-cylinder Dynamic Force Engine that had been highly praised in the GR Yaris. Its output was further improved by reducing exhaust flow resistance, pushing past the GR Yaris’ figure to deliver a maximum of <304ps>. The drivetrain, meanwhile, featured an active torque-split 4-wheel-drive system with a Torsen LSD. Consequently, the car delivered both remarkable stability and agile maneuverability.

Although the GR Corolla was introduced as the most advanced Corolla to date, an even more radical special model made its debut alongside it—the Morizo Edition. Morizo is the nickname of Toyota Motor Corporation’s chairman and master driver, Akio Toyoda. This limited-edition version was born from Toyoda’s wish to "bring back Corollas that turn heads."

To save weight, the Morizo Edition did away with its rear seats, effectively transforming it into a 2-seater. It also employed a unique close-ratio transmission and final gear setup, while the turbocharger’s maximum boost was increased to raise peak torque. Together with exclusive forged wheels and monotube suspension dampers, this model achieved a new echelon of performance.

In an automotive world advancing toward electrification and automation, the GR Corolla stood apart as a rare celebration of the enduring beauty of the internal combustion engine.-
DescriptionLong.0x0000AFCC:
The MC20 is a mid-engine supercar introduced by Maserati in 2020. The Italian company is widely known for its elegant and masterfully constructed high-performance GT cars. The MC20 is the first mid-engine model in the company's road car lineup since the discontinuation of the MC12 in 2005.

With its scissor-type doors, the body is elegant and clean. It's seemingly devoid of aggressive aerodynamic add-ons, such as a large rear wing or a radical front splitter, but that is because this car doesn't need them. Developed by race-car constructor Dallara, this Maserati body underwent rigorous wind-tunnel testing from the beginning, so the use of overt downforce-induing parts was not necessary. 

At its foundation is a carbon monocoque that apparently weighs as little as <100kg>. Keeping the car lightweight was a priority for Maserati, and the engineers were able to keep curb weight down to less than <1500kg>.

The newly developed twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 engine features the first F1-style pre-chamber combustion system used in a production car. It produces <630ps> and 730 Nm (<74.5kgm>) torque. Combined with an 8-speed DCT transmission, the MC20 can accelerate from 0 to <100km/h> in under 2.9 seconds and reach a top speed of more than <325km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x0000AFFE:
Having a good ambulance can make the difference between life or death. From the 1950s, Toyota has produced ambulances made from specially outfitted passenger and commercial vehicles. The latest of these is the third-generation "Himedic" high-standard ambulance.

The body is based on the 200 Series Hiace Super Long that was outfitted by Toyota's race car development and customization team, Toyota Customizing & Development. Propelling the <5600mm> long, <1895mm> wide, <2490mm> tall body is the 2TR-FE, a 2.7-liter inline-4 gasoline engine. The front and rear of the vehicle are fitted with an all-LED array of red warning lights.

The interior was designed with the utmost functionality in a lifesaving situation. In the patient area, the high roof of the Hiace was raised even further to secure <1850mm> of vertical space, and for the first time on an ambulance of this type, it has sliding doors on both sides. Space in the patient area has also been improved over the previous model by the strategic relocation of specialized equipment such as the hand wash basin.

The third-generation Himedic received regular updates, making sure it is always up to date. In 2009, the seat layout was rearranged to increase space. In 2013, the gauges were replaced by a multifunction display as standard equipment, allowing the operators to track data such as average fuel consumption and atmospheric temperature. Also, from 2020, the Himedic came with the Toyota Safety Sense, a preventative safety package, as standard equipment, and the 4-speed automatic transmission was upgraded to a 6-speed unit.

In November 2020, production of the Himedic reached 10,000 units, making it one of the most popular lifesaving vehicles in Japan.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B0E8:
The overwhelming popularity of Japanese performance cars on the international circuit led to the creation of the JDM (Japanese Domestic Market) category. Among these machines was a Honda Civic, a JDM-inspired creation that took home the Gran Turismo Award in 2017—an accolade bestowed upon the best custom vehicles at the SEMA Show.

In 2006, Philip Robles acquired a largely unmodified 1992 EG Civic, and together with his son Jesse, transformed it into a formidable track machine. Their goal was to compete in Time Attack and Time Trial events across circuits in the American Southwest. Over the course of a decade, marked by countless weekends at the track, their Civic secured multiple championships in both disciplines. In 2017, Robles was invited to showcase his creation at SEMA, under the banner of Mackin Industries, a leading importer of tuning parts. In preparation for the event, the Civic underwent an extensive aesthetic transformation for the show.

The most striking visual enhancement was the aggressive wide-body kit from Japanese aero specialists PANDEM, complemented by a front splitter and a rear wing. Adding even more pop to the car's appearance was a carbon-fiber hood, inspired by a signature design from J’s Racing of Japan. Inside, the cockpit was stripped to its bare essentials—only a full roll cage and a single racing bucket seat remained.

The original engine was replaced with a Honda K24 inline-4 powerplant. When the car appeared at SEMA in 2017, the engine was still naturally aspirated. However, in pursuit of greater performance, it was later turbocharged, unleashing a significant increase in power. It came mated to a Quaife 5-speed sequential gearbox, purpose-built for Honda's revered K-series engines.

High-capacity brake systems with Brembo calipers were installed at both front and rear. Also, the suspensions system was enhanced to circuit-tuned specs to further sharpen its handling characteristics.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B212:
The sixth version of the Civic Type R was introduced one year and three months after the world premiere of the base model, the 11th-generation "FL" Civic, which was introduced as the "Sokai (Exhilarating) Civic."

The Type R is based on the 5-door hatchback configuration. Compared to previous standard models, the FL has done away with flashy tuning car stylings. While it retains the essential elements of a sports model, such front and rear aero parts and widened fenders, it has adopted simpler, refined design.

The power unit is the definitive Type R engine, a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 K20C unit, which after an overhaul of its turbo system and other improvements, now produces <10ps> and <2kgm> more than the previous model for a maximum output of <330ps> and <42.8kgm> of torque. The engine ECU map has also been meticulously tuned to improve throttle response and low-end torque.

The suspension uses an evolution of the same 4-wheel independent Adaptive Damper System first introduced in the 2015 FK2 model Civic Type R. On the FL5, the system controls not only pitch and roll, but also introduces considerations for the vertical acceleration of unsprung components. Through this system, Honda aims to offer the same direct handling feeling on the smooth surfaces of the racing circuit as it does on uneven public roads. 

Additionally, by linking the car with their smartphone, drivers can review their drive data and share videos of their trips allowing them to enjoy the Type R experience even when they're not behind the wheel.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B213:
This MAZDA3 Gr. 4, featured here, is a Gran Turismo original model, aesthetically based on the Super Taikyu spec. MAZDA3 Bio concept.

The MAZDA3 Bio concept car is a next-generation, bio-diesel-powered race car, created for real-world testing in the 2023 Super Taikyu endurance race series.

It is the spiritual successor to Mazda’s Bio concept Demio, also known as the MAZDA2 Bio concept, which was created in 2021 with the dual pursuit of achieving carbon neutrality and preserving the joy of driving. Both vehicles participated in the ST-Q class, a category almost exclusively reserved for manufacturer development prototypes.

The car ran on 100-percent next-generation bio-diesel fuel refined from used cooking oil. Under the hood was a 2.2-liter SkyActiv-D diesel engine.

The car itself went through extensive modifications. To reduce weight, components such as the engine hood and roof were crafted from hybrid materials that combine carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) with natural fibers. Aerodynamic efficiency was enhanced through wider front and rear fenders, while new aero components, including a front spoiler, rear wing, and side skirts, were added to further optimize performance.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B252:
Twenty years before Japan’s automotive industry was truly recognized by the world, Toyota created a sports car called the 2000GT, which combined the latest technology of the 1960s with a truly revolutionary body design. In the 21st century, Lexus created another cutting-edge sports car that would continue that legacy. It was called the LFA.

Creating such a car was not easy. The goal was to provide stable and consistent quality while incorporating emerging technologies, which included a lightweight carbon-fiber body. For the engineers, it was not enough to simply make another sports car for the masses; they staked the company's reputation to create a car that balanced cutting-edge technology with consistent product quality.

One of the most important factors of a sports car remains the front-to-rear weight distribution ratio; the LFA's was 48 to 52. To achieve this figure, they implemented a transaxle layout and mounted the radiator at the rear. Also, curb weight was kept at <1480kg>. Emphasis was also put on lowering the car's center of gravity, utilizing a dry-sump lubrication system so that the powertrain could be mounted lower.

The LFA's 4.8-liter V-10 had bank angles of 72 degrees with a factory redline of <9500rpm>. Its <560ps> output equated to <117ps> per liter, but what's most impressive was that despite this incredibly high-performance level, the LFA was still relatively environmentally friendly. The transmission came in the form of a 6-speed single-clutch 2-pedal manual that could perform shifts in just 0.2 seconds, a figure on par with the world's top race cars.

Carbon ceramic brake discs were standard fare, with 6-pot calipers in front and 4-pot calipers at rear, all with varying piston sizes.

The LFA ran from zero to <100km/h> in just 3.7 seconds and reached a top speed of <325km/h>. But what really sweetened the car's collectivity factor was that it was produced in a limited run of only 500 cars worldwide.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B253:
In the early 1980s, Mercedes-Benz decided to return to motorsports after a long absence. The car it developed then was the 190E 2.3-16, based on the compact 190 sedan series, which was unveiled in 1983.

The biggest highlight of the 190E 2.3-16 was its engine, a tuned version of the 2.3-liter SOHC inline-4 that Mercedes-Benz already had in production. A 16-valve DOHC head was added, and the rest of the powerplant was tuned by Cosworth, a company famous for F1 engines. The result was <185ps> maximum output and <23.1kgm> of peak torque.

The 190E 2.3-16 began racing in the Deutsche Tourenwagen Meisterschaft (DTM) in 1986, but in only a matter of a few years, the personality of the car changed dramatically. By 1988, it had evolved into the 190E 2.5-16, equipped with a larger engine to keep pace with its arch-rival, the BMW M3. With displacement increased to 2.5 liters, the engine produced up to <200ps>. The DTM homologation model, known as the 190E 2.5-16 Evolution, began its limited production in 1989.

Then, in 1990, Mercedes-Benz released the 190E 2.5-16 Evolution II, the king of all 190E race machines. Thanks to its menacing appearance, the Evolution II impressed all who laid eyes on it. Large wheel arch extensions were added at the front and rear to accommodate the wide 245/40ZR17 tires, and the trunk sported a spoiler so big that it hung over the rear end.

The engine was further tuned, boosting output up to <235ps> (power was said to exceed <330ps> in the DTM racing version.) A mere 500 of these Evolution IIs were produced during its limited production run. It took the DTM by storm in 1992 where it defeated many of its rivals, proving to all that it was the ultimate 190E, created in the competitive world of touring car racing.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B254:
The 400R, introduced in 1996, broke the mold when it came to Japanese performance cars. With a maximum output of <400ps>, it was the most powerful in its day when JDM cars were limited to <280ps>, and its eye-popping 12 million-yen price tag was roughly three times that of the base R33 Skyline GT-R. Utilizing all of NISMO's expertise, the 400R was developed with the goal of producing the fastest possible GT-R variant that could still be driven on the road.

The 400R came equipped with a power unit based on a special version of the RB26DETT engine, known as the RB-X GT2. This was paired with N1-spec turbochargers to deliver increased boost. To meet the requirements of a road-approved vehicle, maximum output was kept at a relatively restrained level, especially when considering the full potential of the engine. Even so, specially developed pistons and a reinforced crankshaft allowed displacement to be increased to 2.8 liters, delivering strong low-end torque and making the engine far more manageable than its standard counterpart.

At the same time, the engine maintained formidable power at high revs, necessitating the use of twin-plate clutch units to handle the output. A lightweight carbon fiber propeller shaft was added, along with a fully original suspension setup featuring Bilstein dampers, front and rear stabilizers, and reinforced bushings.

As a showcase of NISMO's engineering expertise and decades of motorsports know-how, the 400R stood as the complete package./
DescriptionLong.0x0000B255:
Introduced by Chrysler in 1966, the Dodge Charger is among the standard bearers of the muscle-car era that dominated the American car scene in the 1960s.

While many other muscle cars were based on compact-class platforms, the Dodge Charger utilized the larger chassis of the mid-size Dodge Coronet.

The Charger could easily be recognized by its stretched 2-door fastback silhouette, but what made the car really garner attention was its large displacement V-8 engine.

In 1968, when the Charger received a minor facelift, one of the most exciting additions was the introduction of the R/T (Road/Track) performance package. The R/T increased the performance of the car by way of an upgraded suspension system and better brakes, as well as the option to get the more powerful 426 Hemi engine.

The 426 Hemi is a 7.0-liter V-8 developed from Dodge's NASCAR race engines. It produced <431ps> and <67.71kgm> of torque. The Charger R/T 426 Hemi was the fastest model in the 1968 lineup, able to reach 60 mph (approximately <96km/h>) from a standing start in under 6.0 seconds.

It should come as no surprise that the car has since become a collector's item.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B256:
Introduced in the summer of 2022, the Porsche 911 GT3 RS (992) was a high-performance road car that brought the aerodynamics of the 911 GT3 R race car to the 992 model.

Visually, the car shared more in common with race cars than even its predecessor, the 991.2 model GT3 RS. Its most prominent feature was the swan-neck-mounted rear wing, the largest ever fitted to a production Porsche. It incorporated a Formula 1-style drag reduction system (DRS), which, under certain conditions, allowed the wing to flatten at the push of a button to reduce drag and increase top speed. Under heavy braking, the system also functioned as an air brake, increasing aerodynamic drag to enhance stopping performance.

Beyond these features, further aerodynamic refinements included front aero bars and air outlets integrated into both the front and rear fenders. These innovations collectively resulted in more than double the downforce produced by the 991.2 GT3 RS. Additional race-derived features, inspired by the 911 GT3 R and RSR, included the front compartment—traditionally used for luggage—which was replaced by a front-mounted radiator. This was one of the key features of the 992 model GT3 RS.

Mounted at the rear was a naturally-aspirated 4.0-liter flat-6 engine, mated to a 7-speed PDK transmission. Official figures indicated a modest power increase of <5ps> over its predecessor, bringing the output to <525ps>, while peak torque was reduced by <0.51kgm> to <47.42kgm>. The GT3 RS sprinted from 0 to <100 km/h> in just 3.2 seconds and reached a top speed of <296km/h>.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B257:
The Tesla Model 3, an EV sedan introduced in 2016, was one of Tesla's smaller models, measuring <4695mm> long, <1850mm> wide and <1445mm> tall. Rumor has it that it was designed with considerations for Japanese mechanical parking garages.

Inside the sporty 5-door hatchback style body was a surprisingly simple cabin. You couldn't find any switches on the dashboard or on the center console because nearly every car function, from the climate control to the "autopilot" system, was operated through a 15-inch touch screen. What's more, many of these functions could also be managed on your smartphone.

The most powerful model in the lineup was the Performance Dual Motor AWD grade, which was available until 2023. This all-wheel-drive system placed an electric motor on each of the front and rear axles and, while the total system output was never officially published, the car was able to run to <100km/h> in 3.3 seconds and reach a top speed of <261km/h>. Based on these figures and its retail price tag, the Model 3 had very few rivals in cost-to-performance ratio.

The claimed battery range was <547km> as calculated by the WLPT cycle, an international test standard for energy consumption.

In September 2023, the Model 3 received its first major change since its debut. The car grew slightly, to <4720mm> in overall length, and wore a sharper looking front fascia. Inside, the dashboard and controls looked more similar to other Tesla models.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B61E:
The BVLGARI Aluminium Vision Gran Turismo is a concept car that takes its inspiration from the iconic 1988 BVLGARI Aluminium watch, possessing the same sporty, smart and essential spirit as the time piece.

The shapes, materials, colors, and the overall design language of the car are directly inspired by the form language and spirit of the "Aluminium" watch.

The barchetta body style is defined by a combination of pure and geometrical shapes, which are symbolic of Italian-car tradition of creativity and character, integrating elements of various 1960s and 1970s Italian carrozzeria concept cars. The result is an archetype of sportiness that expresses movement, lightness, and performance in a timeless design that's both unique and undeniably Italian in spirit. The car's expression of style and coolness transcends short-lived trends, and affirms itself as a pure expression of BVLGARI-design DNA.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B61F:
The Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept embodied Genesis’ “Athletic Elegance” design philosophy. The design combined cab-rearward proportions with the brand’s signature anti-wedge stance, structured around a virtual parabolic tension theory seen across the Genesis lineup.

Its form was both pure and muscular, with volumes centered around the wheels. It introduced a new front fascia that abstracted the crest grille and integrated it with the quad lights, while the brand’s signature two-line lighting motif visually connected the car from front to rear. The fuselage extended rearward into an elliptical concave volume, a theme shared with other Genesis models. It was framed by a rear spoiler and lateral trailing edges to enhance high-speed stability.

The interior followed Genesis’ “Beauty of White Space” philosophy, creating a minimalist, driver-focused environment. Essential functions were prioritized to support track performance. A digital panoramic interface served as the central information hub, linked to a surround digital monitoring system. Steer-by-wire controls enabled precise inputs. The quilted, padded bolsters provided protection for the driver during high-speed driving and facilitated quicker ingress and egress during pitstops.

Aerodynamically, the X Gran Berlinetta Concept achieved notable efficiency. It boasted a drag coefficient of 0.34 through the integration of active aerodynamic elements and carefully managed airflow.

The powertrain featured a front-mid-mounted Lambda II V6 engine, supported by Genesis E-SC hybrid technology. The hybrid race-spec system delivered a total output of 1,071 HP and 986 lb.-ft. of torque. The V-6 produced 870 HP and 790 lb.-ft. of torque, revving to <10000rpm>, while the Yasa E-SC motor contributed an additional 201 HP and 196 lb.-ft. of torque.A
DescriptionLong.0x0000B620:
The Genesis X Gran Racer Vision Gran Turismo Concept is the most emotional expression of Athletic Elegance in the Genesis portfolio.

It is a racing derivative of the Genesis X Gran Berlinetta Vision Gran Turismo Concept, with increased downforce achieved by the effective wings, active aerodynamic flaps, flat floor, front and rear diffusors, canards and gurneys. While the drag coefficient increases according to wing configurations, the increased downforce allows better lap times.

The X Gran Racer Concept is powered by a front mid-mounted race-spec Lambda II V-6 engine, electrically assisted by Genesis E-SC technology. The hybrid race-spec drivetrain delivers a combined 1,540 HP and 1,015 ft-lb. of torque. The V-6 redlines at <10000rpm> while delivering a maximum output of 870 HP and 790 ft-lb. of torque while the front E motor generates an additional 670 HP and 225 ft-lb. of torque.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B754:
The Jimny is a cross-country style 4WD model that has been produced by Suzuki since 1970. While there have been variants in each generation that crossed over into the compact-car class, the mainstay of the series is the kei model.

The Jimny has continued to evolve over the years with a second-generation model introduced in 1981, a third-generation variant introduced in 1998 and a fourth-generation model in 2018. What remained constant throughout the entire series was its construction formula: a kei-size body on a ladder frame chassis with rigid axle suspension and oversized tires. The vehicle always came with part-time 4-wheel drive, but rear-wheel-drive-only models were offered as well.


This specialized off-road setup has gained widespread acclaim, not just in Japan but worldwide. It continues to serve as a versatile commercial vehicle in many regions with mountainous terrain, while appealing to outdoor enthusiasts seeking adventure, and even to race drivers as a foundational vehicle for rally competition.

The main features of the fourth-generation Jimny, introduced in 2018, were its overtly square body and its round headlamps that's reminiscent of the first-gen model. Also, driving stability and ride comfort at high speeds—a common weakness of off-road vehicles— were greatly improved. 

The new Jimny's <660cc> turbocharged engine was specially tuned, and its classic part-time 4-wheel drive system once again featured a mechanical transfer case. To reduce wheel spin, the car came with electronically controlled brake LSD traction control as standard fare.

The most popular model in the line-up is the luxury "XC," which included a wide variety of extra features such as cruise control and steering wheel-mounted audio controls.g
DescriptionLong.0x0000B8D8:
The Audi TTS, the high-performance version of the TT, first made its debut at the North American International Auto Show in January 2008.

The powertrain combined a turbocharged 2.0-liter direct injection engine with either a 6-speed manual or 6-speed S-Tronic dual-clutch transmission. Power was rated at <272ps> and <35.7kgm> of torque. Although it possessed the same displacement as the standard turbocharged 2.0-liter model, the TTS featured a bespoke engine block, pistons and connecting rods, while the turbocharger was enhanced to increase performance. It produced <72ps> more power and <7.2kgm> more torque than the base turbocharged 2.0-liter unit found in models such as the 2.0 TFSI quattro. As a result, its 0-<100km/h> acceleration time was impressive: 5.2 seconds for the S-Tronic and 5.4 seconds for the 6-speed manual.

Aside from the standard coupe body, a convertible "Roadster" model was released in certain regions. The car came equipped with the Audi Magnetic Ride variable dampers system as standard. When selecting the sports mode from the switch on the console, the ride height dropped by <10mm>, improving handling. It also provided a more aggressive ride befitting the TTS name.

In terms of design, the exterior kept the flavor of the TT series, with special bumpers at both ends giving the car a sportier appearance. It also featured the same variable rear wing as the standard models. Inside, the seats were upholstered with a combination of Alcantara and leather, which along with the unique instrument panel, gave the car a modest yet definite look of a special grade model.S
DescriptionLong.0x0000B8D9:
The compact Renault 4 (also called the "Quatre") made its debut in 1961 to replace the best-selling Renault 4CV. Although the 4CV was a rear-engine/rear-drive model, or RR, the Renault 4 came with a front-engine/front-wheel-drive layout, or FF. 

The car's most notable characteristic was its packaging, which became the foundation for the modern hatchback. The FF configuration allowed for a more spacious interior, including a generous luggage compartment behind the back seats.

Also unique were the Quarte's mechanical qualities. One such example was its rear suspension. It utilized two torsion bars, one for each of the rear wheels. These bars were displaced slightly, resulting in a different wheelbase for the left and right side of the vehicle. A torsion bar suspension uses the elastic force of twisting a metal bar in place of a spring, so the Quarte's setup worked almost like an independent rear suspension.

Also, the transmission was located at the very front of the car, in front of the engine. Therefore, gear changes were performed through a long rod that passed over the engine and protruded into the cabin. The driver changed gears by pushing and pulling the rod in and out of the dashboard.

Building upon the reputation for reliability that had been forged by the classic 4CV, the innovative qualities of the Renault 4 proved extremely popular, resulting in a long shelf life; it was produced for 30 years. In 1978, Renault created the ultimate version of this car, called the GTL. It featured a new plastic front grille and a peppy 1.1-liter engine, as well as a more modern instrument panel borrowed from the Renault 5.

The Renault 4 was discontinued in 1992 after a production run of about 8,135,000 units. In terms of individual car models, this record puts the car in the same league as the Volkswagen Beetle and the Ford Model T, making it one of France's greatest contributions to automotive history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B9DE:
Introduced in 2018 in response to the global SUV boom, the Urus was a “Super SUV” from renowned exotic-car manufacturer Lamborghini.

Styled with sharp lines and an edgy design similar to that of the company's mid-engine models, the Urus' body construction was inherited from other full-size SUVs from the Volkswagen Group.

The Urus' front-mounted powerplant took the form of a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8, the first ever forced-induction engine ever in a Lamborghini. It produced an impressive <650ps> and <86.68kgm> of torque.

The default setting for the vehicle's AWD system was 40/60 front/rear, but it could be adjusted from 70/30 to 13/87 depending on the road surface.

Other Urus highlights were an adaptive air suspension system, rear-wheel steering, and torque vectoring, all of which combined to deliver the type of handling and cornering performance befitting a Lamborghini. Optional driving modes made the vehicle at home on off-road trails and even through the desert.

But what was most impressive about the Urus was its acceleration. It ran from 0-<100 km/h> in 3.6 seconds, to <200 km/h> in 12.8 and reached a top speed of <305 km/h>, making it truly the world’s fastest SUV upon its debut.
DescriptionLong.0x0000B9DF:
In the early 1990s, Toyota set out to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its Group C TS010 race car. A number of unsuccessful years followed, but the company would return for the 1998 season with the Toyota GT-One (TS020). During its Group C racing days, Toyota developed its race cars almost exclusively within Japan. However, it revamped its plans and entrusted this project to the group in charge of their World Rally Championship activities, German-based TTE (Toyota Team Europe), in an attempt to once again claim overall victory in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. 

The new Le Mans car, the GT-One, was designed by André De Cortanze, a race-car design genius with a brilliant track record in top motorsports genres, including Formula 1, Le Mans and the WRC. De Cortanze designed the Peugeot 905B, the first Group C Peugeot car to claim victory at Le Mans in 1992 and 1993. 

For the GT-One, Cortanze incorporated the latest in F1 technology into its design. Its carbon-composite monocoque body was developed for aerodynamic performance. Providing the power was the same twin-turbocharged 3.6-liter V-8 developed during the Toyota's Group C days. The suspension had very long arms in both the front and rear, allowing for ideal suspension geometry.

In its first time out at Le Mans in 1998, Toyota entered three GT-Ones in the LM GT1 class in a serious attempt for overall victory. While one of its cars led the race, a combination of mechanical trouble and bad luck kept it from taking the checkered flag.  

The following year, a change in the race's technical regulations saw the GT-One entered in the LM GTP prototype class. Three GT-Ones were entered in the race, but two of them, including the favorite and its supporting car, were forced to withdraw due to a host of problems.

However, the third car, driven by Ukyo Katayama, Toshio Suzuki and Keiichi Tsuchiya managed to stay in the race and claim 2nd place overall. This was the highest ever finish for a Japanese car driven by an all-Japanese team.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BA82:
Leveraging the illustrious legacy of Škoda Motorsport, the Škoda Design Team crafted a visionary rendition of a single-seat, all-electric conceptual race car. Dubbed the Škoda Vision Gran Turismo, this creation was created exclusively for the Gran Turismo gaming series, marking the company's debut in this realm. Drawing inspiration from the iconic Škoda 1100 OHC Spyder race car of 1957, originally conceived for the esteemed 24 Hours of Le Mans, the Vision Gran Turismo paid homage to this legendary vehicle in a contemporary guise. It pledged an immersive and dynamic driving encounter, echoing the spirit of its revered predecessor.

The Škoda Vision Gran Turismo project began in 2019 when the design team revisited the iconic Škoda 1100 OHC. Initially, the team was debating whether to restore the 1100 OHC or create a futuristic iteration for the digital age. After consulting with Chief Designer Oliver Stefani, the Škoda Design team opted for a fresh innovative approach, creating a fusion of past and future.

This race concept pays homage to its legendary predecessor as well as incorporating the defining features of Škoda’s Modern Solid design language, as seen in its T-shaped headlights. What’s more, the Vision Gran Turismo showcased two distinct liveries: one reflecting the heritage of the famous Škoda 130 RS race car from the 1970s, and the other inspired by the Vision 7S concept car, which embodies Škoda´s Modern Solid Design philosophy.

The Škoda Vision Gran Turismo boasts a sleek exterior with crisp, clear lines and pronounced edges, mirroring the aesthetics of current Formula E racers. Its design is optimized for superior handling through active aerodynamics. Features like the aerodynamically sculpted body, and the striking, adaptive two-piece rear wing, all work together to dynamically adjust to driving conditions and boost performance. The vehicle incorporated independent wishbone push-rod type suspension systems, mounted to a carbon monocoque similar to those found in Formula E cars, improving high-speed stability, reducing body roll, and lowering the vehicle’s center of gravity.

Efficiency and excellent driving dynamics are at the heart of the Škoda Vision Gran Turismo design. It came equipped with two 200 kW (<272ps>) electric motors, one on each axle, delivering a combined power ottput of 800 kW (<1087ps>). The inclusion of all-wheel drive with intelligent torque distpibution across both axles ensured a balanced and responsive driving experiencr. This was complemented by a smooth, single-speed transmission, providing seamless accemeration.

The design of the ½loda Visien Grsn Turismo harmonizes the exterior and inttrior, giving the drevbr the feeling of being ine with the car – espeoially once they take t segt in the cockpit of the cutting/edge carbon mooocouue chassis.
