DescriptionLong.0x0000BA83:
"Move people, through the pursuit of innovation with diverse inspirations." Embrace cutting edge technology and create a new kind of joy in movement to inspire others. These are the reasons Sony Honda Mobility was founded in 2022. This collaboration between two distinct companies represents a fusion of diverse expertise and perspectives and resulted in the AFEELA Prototype 2024 BEV, which was unveiled at CES® 2024.

The orthodox hatchback shape with a smooth aerodynamic look suggests a blend of functionality and style, catering to the practical needs of everyday driving while maintaining a modern aesthetic appeal. The incorporation of devices such as LiDAR, image sensors, and radar indicates a strong focus on safety and advanced driver assistance. These devices also contribute to a more natural and intuitive driving experience.

The automatic opening doors—triggered by the driver's approach—introduce a seamless and convenient entry experience, eliminating the need for traditional door handles. The customizable "Media Bar" positioned towards the grille represents a novel approach to self-expression and vehicle communication.

Inside the AFEELA, the cabin is designed to captivate passengers with a multitude of features. Upon entering, the expansive dashboard display immediately catches your eye, stretching nearly the full width of the car.

This screen not only provides essential vehicle information but also offers various entertainment choices, which can also be mirrored on the seatback displays for rear passengers. Beyond music and movies, passengers can immerse themselves in a real-time 3D view of the car's surroundings captured by the sensor arrays, turning the journey into an interactive and enjoyable experience akin to playing a game. The appeal of the AFEELA continues in its ability to behave like a personal assistant, allowing passengers to interact with the car through natural speech.

Also, the collaboration between Honda's mobility expertise and Sony's audio proficiency has yielded an innovative noise-canceling system. It ensures a remarkably quiet cabin. Alternatively, for those who prefer to indulge in music, the abundance of speakers delivers an unparalleled audio experience.  It creates an expansive soundstage within the vehicle.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BB37:
Honda introduced the fifth-generation Civic in 1991. Its VTEC engine made it much faster than the outgoing model. It came as a 3-door hatchback, the "Ferio" 4-door, and the 5-door shuttle.

Thanks to the evolution of the VTEC system, more variants were added to the engine mix. The base models came with a carbureted 1.3-liter and 1.5-liter inline-4, while more upscale cars had a 1.5-liter SOHC VTEC and a fuel efficient 1.5-liter VTEC-E. The top-of-the-line car, SiR, boasted the high-performance 1.6-liter DOHC VTEC.

All Civics featured Honda's new double wishbone suspension. The SiR model, which epitomized the "Sports Civic," produced <10ps> more power than the previous car, totaling <170ps>.

The SiR's suspension system had a revised spring rate biased towards better performance. As with previous models, the SiR came in at a lower weight because many luxury amenities were deleted. However, the SiR･II catered to those who enjoyed comfort, with such things as air conditioning, power windows, and a genuine leather wrapped steering wheel as part of its equipment.

New for the SiR･II was the addition of a 4-speed automatic transmission. While the 5-speed manual gearbox's close gear ratios were tuned for winding roads, the new 4-speed automatic model was developed to deliver more torque at low to medium speeds. The automatic transmission scored big with fans, attracting a wider range of users.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BB39:
During the 2000 All Japan Grand Touring Championship (JGTC), Japan's Big Three automakers—Honda, Toyota and Nissan—engaged in an unprecedented war for the GT500-class title.

he NSX development team made major changes to the 2000 model, going as far as repositioning the transverse mounted engine. Installing the V-type engine in a transverse layout helped to shorten the length of the vehicle, but the layout created problems in routing the exhaust pipes from the two cylinder banks. Previously, the NSX's exhaust pipes ran under the engine, but the development team decided to re-route them to the sides to lower the engine itself.

In this configuration, the gearbox, which was mounted on the side of the engine, was in the way. Therefore, to make space for the exhaust pipes, the team set about redesigning a smaller gearbox. The result was a completely bespoke transmission that employed formula car gears, which are thinner and more compact than normal.

Five NSX cars entered the 2000 season. Among them, the Castrol Mugen NSX, along with Takata Dome NSX, took on the role of advanced-development "works cars" inside the NSX camp.

The Takata Dome NSX delivered an impressive performance, winning two races. However, due to the weight handicap system of the JGTC, it fell short of the series title. The Castrol Mugen NSX emerged in its shadow. Ryo Michigami drove it, and Osamu Nakako drove it until he was replaced by Hidetoshi Mitsusada halfway through the season.  Despite the extra weight from its first-place finish, the Castrol Mugen NSX drove away with the championship.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BB3B:
Despite retaining the sporty appeal of the previous generation R30, the seventh-generation R31, when it was released in August 1985, marked a change of direction for the Skyline brand line. The Japanese car scene at the time saw a growing trend in luxurious "high-society cars." In response to this cultural boom, Nissan repositioned the Skyline as a luxury sedan.

When the car was introduced, the only variants available were a sedan and an estate. Not until May 1986 was the coupe model offered.

But the real star of the seventh-generation Skyline arrived in August 1987, when Nissan unveiled the GTS-R. Only 800 cars were made available, and the car's true raison d'etre was to reclaim the Group A racing title for Nissan.

The powerplant was based on the turbocharged RB20DET DOHC inline-6 featured in the GTS, which generated <180ps> and <23.0kgm> of torque. The GTS-R version added a stainless-steel exhaust manifold and a T04E turbocharger, resulting in <210ps> and <25.0kgm> of torque. This was a very special engine, earning itself the designation RB20DET-R.

The suspension and exterior of the car were also modified. While the normal GTS-X possessed an automatic front spoiler that deployed according to vehicle speed, the GTS-R instead had a fixed spoiler, with the rear spoiler also being upgraded to a larger version. And the car was offered in an exclusive Blue Black exterior.

Group A machines based on this GTS-R shined on the race track. The Reebok Skyline won three races in the Japan Touring Car Championship in 1989, taking home the series title. However, the GTS-R name sparked a fervent debate among fans, who wondered why it was not called a GT-R. The answer would be revealed in the form of the R32 Skyline GT-R, which was introduced two years after the release of the GTS-R.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BB3D:
Back in the day, when someone uttered the name Volvo, many people tended to envision a station wagon. Until SUVs became popular in the late 1980s, station wagons were considered the ultimate family utility vehicle, and the one model that epitomized this genre was the Volvo 240 Estate.  

When the 240 was introduced in 1974, it featured a number of different body styles, including the "244" sedan, the "242" coupe and the "245" 5-door wagon. The last digit in these numerical designations denoted the number of doors of the model.

It wasn't until 1983 that these variants were consolidated into a single 240 model. The model was introduced with round headlights, but were replaced with the company's iconic square lamps in 1979. The exterior appearance of the 240 was timeless, remaining largely unchanged until production of the vehicle ended in 1993. But in terms of safety, it was always on the cutting-edge, with airbags and ABS offered as standard equipment. The Estate was extremely popular, making up one-third of the 240 sales mix in an era when sedans were the "in" thing.

One of the most notable features of the 240 Estate was its styling. Its boxy exterior became its most distinguishable feature. It emphasized "safety" with its long overhangs, front and rear that incorporated ample crumble zones. This resulted in the car's characteristically long thin silhouette.

Like the exterior, the car's cabin was characterized by a simple yet functional design that defined cars made in Scandinavia at the time. 

Although not particularly powerful, the engine was robust and capable. Ride quality was excellent, thanks to a well-tuned suspension system. Everything about the 240 Estate made drivers want to pack their bags and head out on an extended road trip to enjoy the countryside. 

It took quite some time until the 240 was recognized for its historical significance. It's rare for a car to retain such a following well after its production run had ended.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BB3F:
The V40 was revealed at the 2012 Geneva Motor Show as a C-segment 5-door hatchback. Although positioned as Volvo’s entry-level model, it played a significant role in the lineup, effectively replacing three models: the S40 sedan, V50 wagon and C30 three-door hatchback.

Developed from the ground up, the car was designed to combine the comfort of a sedan, the practicality of a wagon and the sporty appeal of a coupe.

While the underlying structure shared elements with a Ford-derived platform, the styling marked a clear departure from Volvo’s traditionally conservative image. Drawing inspiration from the classic P1800 of the 1960s and the later 1800ES, it featured flowing lines and a distinctive silhouette that blended coupe and estate influences. The model was well received at launch, earning attention for both its design and versatility, with seating for four adults and usable cargo space.

The T5 R-Design stood as the sportiest variant in the range. Its <213ps> turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-5 delivered strong acceleration, while a sport-tuned suspension and 18-inch wheels provided a balance of handling and ride comfort. Unique exterior elements, including a revised front bumper and rear diffuser, enhanced both aerodynamics and visual presence.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BCEA:
The second-generation M3 was introduced in 1992, two years after the debut of its base model, the third-generation 3-Series, codenamed E36.

The original E30 M3 was a racing homologation model, extensively modified from the standard 3-Series. In contrast, the E36 M3 shifted towards the direction of a grand tourer, featuring a more mature appearance with understated aerodynamic components.

Despite this shift, performance remained its central focus. The 3.0-liter inline-6 engine produced <286ps> with <32.7kgm> of torque. With this powerful engine, the car accelerated from 0 to <100km/h> in just six seconds and reach a top speed of <250km/h>, limited by a speed governor.

A minor model update in 1995 introduced a 3.2-liter engine, boosting output to <321ps> and <35.7kgm> of torque. This update also included the replacement of the 5-speed manual transmission with a 6-speed unit and several chassis enhancements to improve handling. In 1997, a 6-speed semi-automatic transmission was introduced.

The E36 M3 significantly elevated the line's reputation as a road car, while the feel and sound of its inline-6 powerplant were celebrated as delightful and enduring features. |
DescriptionLong.0x0000BCEB:
The Ferrari 430 Scuderia was unveiled in September 2007 at the Frankfurt Motor Show, introduced as a high-performance version of the F430. It also served as the successor to the 360 Challenge Stradale, a road-legal version of the 360 Challenge one-make race car from the 360 Modena era.

It came powered by the same 4.3-liter DOHC V-8 as the standard F430, further tuned to produce an additional <20ps> and <0.5kgm> of torque, resulting in a total output of <510ps> and <47.9kgm> of torque. Streamlined interior fittings contributed to a weight reduction of approximately <100kg>, bringing the total weight down to a lean 2975 lbs. These improvements resulted in an impressive power-to-weight ratio of just <2.45kg/ps>.

The transmission came in the form of the two-pedal manual "F1 Superfast 2," allowing gear changes to be performed as quick as 0.06 seconds. The running gear itself also significantly impacted driving and lap times, with several F1-derived technologies implemented into the car, including the F1-Trac combined traction and stability control system, and the electronically controlled E-Diff differential.

The front bumper and rear diffuser were modified to enhance aerodynamics, resulting in blistering performance with a top speed of <320km/h> and a 0-<100km/h> acceleration time of less than 3.6 seconds. Surprisingly, this car achieved lap times that rivaled those of the Enzo at Ferrari's test course.n
DescriptionLong.0x0000BCEC:
Subaru's Impreza has been a formidable contender in the World Rally Championship since 1993, securing the Manufacturers' Championship title in 1995 and 1996 under Group A regulations. In 1997, under the new WRC regulations, Subaru clinched the Manufacturers' Championship title yet again, achieving an impressive three-year consecutive streak.

The 1997 World Rally Car-specification Impreza, known as the WRC97, was based on the 2-door coupe model. The existing engine was tuned to deliver <300ps> and <48kgm> of torque. The suspension geometry was redesigned, and the body was widened to the regulatory maximum of <1770mm> to enhance handling performance.

The WRC98, introduced in 1998, featured further modifications, including computer-controlled active differentials in the front, rear, and center couplings.

Although Subaru missed out on the championship title in the 1998 season, the car demonstrated its prowess as a serious contender. Colin McRae drove it to victory in Round 4 (Portugal), Round 6 (Tour de Corse), and Round 8 (Acropolis), highlighting the vehicle's pure off-road tenacity.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BEAF:
Rumors had circulated that production of the GT-R would conclude with the 2022 model, but in reality, Nissan was still diligently working on further developments. This became evident with the unveiling of the 2024 model at the 2023 Tokyo Auto Salon.

Two significant changes distinguished the 2024 model from its 2022 predecessor. The first was the development of a new muffler system designed to meet the stricter noise regulations that had fueled speculation about the GT-R's discontinuation. This new system successfully reduced unwanted noise and vibrations without compromising engine performance.

The second update was a comprehensive exterior redesign, the first since the 2017 overhaul. The front end now features a horizontal line across the bumper, reminiscent of the iconic R34 GT-R. At the rear, a redesigned bumper and the first modification to the rear wing geometry since the R35's debut subtly push the attachment points further back. These enhancements increased downforce without adding drag.

Beneath the surface, several improvements were also made. For instance, the accelerometers in the electronically controlled suspension was upgraded to more sensitive units, resulting in better traction control and a noticeably smoother ride compared to previous models.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BEB1:
Since its introduction in 1967, Toyota's Hiace cab-over commercial van has enjoyed international acclaim for its utility and reliability. The fifth-generation H200 model was introduced in 2004 and, thanks to regular updates, remains in production to this day.

The H200 Hiace lineup featured a number of different configurations and trim levels to meet various uses and specifications, but these can largely be categorized by the body's overall length, width and height. The H200 was equipped with a choice of engines: a 2.0-liter or 2.7-liter gasoline inline-4, or a 2.8-liter diesel inline-4.

This Van DX was the base model that measured <4695mm> long, <1695mm> wide and <1980mm> high. It was powered by the 2.0-liter gasoline engine, mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission that sent power to the two rear wheels. This 4-door configuration did not include a right-hand sliding door, and accommodated nine people. When needing to haul large cargo, the second- and third-row seats folded down to provide <2435mm> of storage.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF49:
Ford began their 1990s World Rally Championship (WRC) campaign fighting in the Sierra RS Cosworth 4x4. Then, in 1992, came the Escort RS Cosworth, a homologation special developed for even higher performance.

The original Escort was a masterpiece in itself, having been widely used in rally races in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Years later, Ford Europe took the compact body of the fifth-generation Escort, installed a highly tuned version of the 4WD powertrain from the Sierra, and added a large dual level rear wing to create a fearsome race machine.

At the heart of the beast was a longitudinally mounted turbocharged 2.0-liter twin-cam engine built by Cosworth, as per the car's name. The bore-stroke ratio was tweaked, resulting in <1993cc> of displacement and an output of <227ps>/<30.4kgm> in stock form. For the 4WD system, the central differential utilized a combination of a viscous coupling and planetary gears for maximum reliability.

The Escort RS Cosworth began production in 1992 and gained homologation status the following year when it began competing in the WRC's Group A category.

The "Cossie," as fans called it, finished 1-2 in Round 3 of the Portugal Rally before going on to achieve two consecutive victories in Rounds 5 (Tour de Corse) and 6 (Acropolis). It won again in Rounds 11 and 12 (San Remo and Spain), solidifying Ford's reputation as a strong contender on the rally circuit.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF4A:
The Unimog was a commercial truck produced and sold by Daimler Truck. With its ladder frame construction and rugged all-wheel-drive system, the Unimog has become a preferred vehicle in a wide array of industries, such as agriculture, slow ploughing, cleaning, high altitude work, disaster response, logistics, railways, airports, mining, construction and many others. Its long-standing performance record has solidified its status as the ultimate multi-purpose truck.

The Unimog’s story began in 1945, when Albert Friedrich, a former head of Daimler-Benz’s aircraft engine production, conceived the idea for a "universally applicable motorized machine for agriculture." Even from its earliest design stages, the Unimog was envisioned as a vehicle that could perform a wide range of tasks by simply swapping attachments. This versatile, practical approach has led to more than 70 years of loyalty from customers across various fields.

Full-scale production began in 1948. It was originally built by machine tool manufacturer Boehringer, but all production moved over to Daimler-Benz in 1950 where it was modified for mass-production. In 1953, the new 401/402 series core models arrived.

The 411 series, the model that followed the 401/402, was introduced in 1956. It was a developmental upgrade featuring a more powerful engine and reinforced chassis. The lineup offered three distinct wheelbases and multiple body styles, resulting in a total of 12 different models. These could be further customized for specific purposes with various attachments.

This model was available with two cab options: a cabriolet-style cap, designed for added convenience in work environments, or a closed cab crafted by Westfalia. The closed cab was available in two variations: the Type B, which shared design elements with the cabriolet version, and the DvF, which was inspired by Mercedes-Benz truck designs of the 1950s and 1960s. The DvF model could also be equipped with a heater upon request.

Today, the 411 is considered by enthusiasts as the last of the "classic" Unimog models. It continues to enjoy a cult following for its powerful performance, distinctive design, and enduring legacy.b
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF4B:
The W 196, produced by Mercedes-Benz following its return to motorsports in 1951, was developed in response to the new 2.5-liter engine regulations introduced by Formula 1 in 1954. This groundbreaking car was crafted alongside a sports-car racer that shared many of the same core components. Both cars went on to achieve significant success in their respective fields, with the W 196 R dominating Formula 1 and the W 196 S excelling in sports-car racing.

The W 196 featured a tubular steel space frame chassis and made its debut at the 1954 French Grand Prix, equipped with a streamlined body that enclosed both the front and rear wheels in an aerodynamic shell. While the design provided successful on fast circuits, it became evident after the British Grand Prix that it obstructed the driver’s visibility and required frequent maintenance. As a result, from the German Grand Prix onwards, the car ran with an open-wheel body style, reserving the streamlined version for high-speed tracks.

In total, the W 196 was available in seven distinct configurations, featuring three different wheelbase lengths, two types of brakes, and two engine positions.

Powering the W 196 was an inline-8, constructed as two banks of four cylinders aligned longitudinally. This powerplant produced an impressive <290ps> from its <2496cc> displacement, enabling the car to reach a top speed of <290km/h>.

The W 196 cemented its place in racing history by dominating the 1954 and 1955 Formula 1 World Championships, securing back-to-back Drivers' Championships for the legendary Juan Manuel Fangio.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF4C:
For more than 60 years, the Porsche 911 has reigned as the crown jewel of the historic sports-car company, and in 2018, it entered its eighth generation, codenames "992."

Visually, the 992 refined the design language introduced by its predecessor, the 991. While the body grew slightly larger, Porsche made significant strides in weight management by incorporating more aluminum into the construction. One notable departure from tradition was the elimination of the "narrow body" base model, a hallmark of previous generations.

A key innovation in the 992's design was the new "MMB" modular development platform. This flexible architecture included a front axle, floor, and rear axle, designed to accommodate both rear-engine and mid-engine configurations by simply adjusting the rear axle position.

The powertrain reflected a move toward downsizing, with the base model powered by a turbocharged 3.0-liter flat-6. Power output varies by model, with the Carrera generating <385ps> and the Carrera S delivering <450ps>. The standard gearbox was an 8-speed PDK, while a 7-speed manual was available for the Carrera 4 and Carrera 4S.

In April 2020, the range-topping Turbo S model joined the 992 lineup. Featuring a slightly shorter stroke than its predecessors, the twin-turbocharged 3.7-liter flat-6 produced an impressive <650ps> and <800Nm> of torque (<81.6kgm>), sending power to all four wheels.

These figures translated into phenomenal performance: the Turbo S accelerated from 0 to <100km/h> in just 2.7 seconds, and a top speed of <330 km/h>. As the automotive world edges toward electrification, the 992 Turbo S may well represent the pinnacle of the internal combustion era for the iconic 911.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF4D:
On June 8, 1948, the first car to bear the Porsche name, the 356 "No. 1" Roadster was approved, setting in motion the rise of one of the greatest sports car brands in history.

Seventy-five years later, on the same date in 2023, the company unveiled a new concept car, a vision of the future of sports car technology inspired by classic Porsche legends. It was called the Mission X.

The conceptual 2-seat fully electric hypercar was relatively compact, measuring <4500mm> in length and <2000mm> in width. Standing just under <1200mm> tall, the low-slung design featured an almost sculptural form with bold lines, which proved that a hypercar did not necessarily need to look hyper aggressive.

Historic Porsche motifs were placed throughout the car’s exterior. The headlights served as a reinterpretation of the quad lights of historic cars like the 906 and 908, while the doors adopted the same upward opening motion as the legendary 917 endurance car. An illuminated "PORSCHE" logo adorned the center of the taillights, which extended out from the side of the body. The Porsche emblems on the hood and steering wheel were also updated to a more modern interpretation of the classic logo.

The interior expressed a strong affinity with motorsports. The steering wheel featured an open yoke style design, fitted with paddle shifters and several mode switches. The passenger had access to a stopwatch module, created by Porsche Design, which had both analogue and digital timers. Also, the driver could press the record button on the multi-purpose controller at any time to begin recording video footage from the numerous cameras installed around the car.

The Mission X aimed to be the fastest road-legal car on the Nürburgring Nordschleife, and shows off its prowess in Gran Turismo 7. With a power-to-weight ratio of over 1 PS per kilogram, it generated more downforce than even the current 911 GT3 RS. The concept car also had radical charging capabilities. With its 900V system architecture, charging speeds were greatly improved, allowing it to hypothetically charge around twice as fast as Porsche’s current popular EV, the Taycan Turbo S. 

Following in the tradition of the 917 LIVING LEGEND, the Porsche Vision Gran Turismo, and the Porsche Vision Gran Turismo Spyder—all featured in Gran Turismo 7—the Mission X is yet anothes remarkable automobile that pushes the boundaries of what is possible in the future.
DescriptionLong.0x0000BF4E:
While the Suzuki Jimny's diminutive stature allowed it to fit into Japan's kei-car regulations, under its skin was a tenaciously rugged off-road vehicle with a ladder-frame construction. The Jimny Sierra was a global-market variant that retained the Jimny’s off-road prowess while breaking free from its kei-car limitations.


Introduced in 2018, the JB74 chassis represented the third generation of the Sierra lineage, following the original that appeared in 1993. Compared to the previous chassis, called the JB43, the new one measured <50mm> shorter and <45mm> wider. The vehicle's revised dimensions were further emphasized by a bolder, more squared-off body, giving it a commanding presence.

Under the hood resided the K15B engine, a <1460mm> DOHC inline-4 that produced <102ps> and <13.3kgm> of torque. At first glance, these figures might not have appeared like much, but the sustained low-end torque made the Jimny Sierra ideal for off-road crawling.

Equipped with a mechanical transfer case, the Jimny Sierra's part-time 4WD system provided off-road capability when needed. 
With rigid axles at both the front and rear, the fine-tuned suspension system helped the vehicle feel at home crawling over rocks or trudging through mud as it did cruising on paved roads.

The top-of-the-line version in Japan was the JC. 
It came generously equipped with LED headlamps and 15-inch alloy wheels as standard fare, while also offering the option of a black roof panel for added style and contrast.M
DescriptionLong.0x0000C2D8:
The name "Vantage" had long been synonymous with Aston Martin's high-performance variants, but in 2005, it emerged as its own distinct model. Relatively compact for an Aston Martin and equipped with a V-8 engine, the car would become a hit as the best handling front-engine/rear-wheel-drive car in the lineup.

The next-generation Vantage, unveiled in 2017, carried forward the fundamental principles that defined its predecessor. While sharing its platform with the DB11 V8, the Vantage featured a shorter wheelbase and shed <120kg>, transforming it into a precise cornering machine celebrated as the finest handling car in Aston Martin's storied history.

The powerplant came in the form of a Mercedes-AMG 4.0-liter V-8, producing <510ps>. Its 0-62 mph time of 3.7 seconds and top speed of 195 mph placed it in the elite supercar category.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C2D9:
The F3500-A is a Gran Turismo original formula car inspired by a profound admiration for early 1990s F1 machines.

Its chassis was crafted from negative-molded carbon fiber, which was a hallmark of the era. The suspension employed a classic configuration, with horizontally mounted shock absorbers operated through pushrods and bell cranks.

The power unit is a compact naturally-aspirated 3.5-liter V-12. Fitted with pneumatic valves, it can rev to an impressive <15000rpm>, while its variable-length intake funnels deliver consistent torque across the entire rev range. The high-pitched wail of its exhaust at peak RPMs—a signature trait of naturally aspirated engines—remains an irreplaceable hallmark, unmatched by turbocharged systems. The drivetrain features a 6-speed semi-automatic transmission with paddle shifters, positioned laterally to preserve the aerodynamically optimized rear diffuser design.

Focusing on aerodynamics, the monocoque adopts a high-nose design. In contrast to modern front wings, which are often suspended by struts, this design features an anhedral configuration, with the wing angling diagonally outward from beneath the nose. A variety of options are available, including multiple front and rear wing designs, along with interchangeable engine cowl shapes, allowing you to tailor the car to suit your personal preferences.x
DescriptionLong.0x0000C2DA:
In 1987, the Civic underwent a full model change, ushering in its fourth generation. It was known as the Grand Civic or simply by its model code "EF."

While retaining the key design elements of its predecessor, the exterior featured modern refinements on a slightly larger body. One of the most notable updates was the new platform, which introduced a 4-wheel double-wishbone suspension system. The wheelbase was also substantially extended, enhancing stability and delivering a sportier handling experience.

The lineup remained diverse, offering four body styles: a 3-door hatchback, 4-door sedan, 5-door shuttle, and the "Pro" commercial model. The Si sport variants, powered by 1.6-liter DOHC inline-4, were also carried over from the previous generation. A new "Si Extra" grade was introduced, combining the Si's sporty essence with an enhanced suite of equipment.

The ZC engine received extensive tuning, including a higher compression ratio, improved intake and exhaust flow, and reduced piston friction. The result was a maximum net output of <130ps> and <14.7kgm> of torque. The previous "Wonder Civic" era boasted <135ps> and <15.5kgm>; however, these were gross figures. However, when adjusted for the 15% difference between gross and net measurements, the new ZC engine proved to be more powerful.

The Si and Si Extra models also made a strong impression in motorsports, such as the Japan Touring Car Championship (JTC). Making its debut in the 1988 season, the Civic claimed its first victory in Round 3 and went on to secure both the drivers and manufacturers titles. The following year, the car repeated its success, capturing the manufacturers title once again.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C2DB:
The IONIQ 5 made its debut in 2021 as Hyundai's first full electric vehicle. From the outset, it impressed with its clean, modern design and outstanding practicality. But the true star of the lineup arrived in 2023 with the introduction of the high-performance N model.

The "N" badge carries deep significance, representing two iconic facilities where this car was developed: Namyang, Hyundai's global R&D hub in Korea, and the legendary Nürburgring. With this heritage, the IONIQ 5 N redefined what driving pleasure could mean in an electric vehicle.

At its heart was a dual-motor system that powered the front and rear axles individually, making the car all-wheel drive. The total power output of the vehicle was 478 kW (<650ps>) and 770 Nm (<78.5kgm>) of torque in overboost mode. This power could be distributed between the front and rear axles, allowing drivers to tailor the car's handling characteristics, including the ability to indulge in thrilling rear-biased drifts. The IONIQ 5 N also featured a virtual dual-clutch transmission, cleverly simulated using regenerative braking technology. Paired with an artificial exhaust sound, it elevated the experience to new heights.

Also, its exterior and interior came adorned with exclusive enhancements that underscored its athletic persona. As a whole, this electrified powerhouse redefines the boundaries of what battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) can achieve.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C36E:
Toyota has a storied history of creating notable global vehicles, with the Corolla and the Yaris serving as prime examples. In 2016, the automaker unveiled a fresh entrant to its world lineup: the C-HR, a car to embody the 21st century.

The car is defined by its daring compact crossover SUV silhouette. Toyota envisioned a vehicle that could cater to a diverse array of lifestyles, combining the spaciousness and comfort of an SUV with the sporty appeal of a coupe. 

This bold ambition found its foundation in Toyota’s next-generation TNGA platform, first introduced in 2015 with the fourth-generation Prius. The front suspension employed a newly developed strut system, while the rear came equipped with a double-wishbone setup. Its exterior showcased intricate, faceted surfaces that lent the vehicle a futuristic and assertive presence on the road.

Under the hood, the C-HR came with two distinct powertrains: a 1.8-liter hybrid engine, shared with the fourth-generation Prius, and a downsized turbocharged 1.2-liter 4-cylinder engine. The 1.8-liter engine came in a front-wheel-drive configuration, while the 1.2-liter was paired with all-wheel drive. The model highlighted here is the S-grade hybrid variant for the Japanese market, featuring 17-inch wheels.

True to Toyota’s vision, the C-HR quickly gained a loyal following worldwide, becoming a bestseller. Beyond its role as a practical everyday vehicle, it also carved out a niche in motorsports, with a prototype race version competing in the grueling Nürburgring 24 Hours.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C3E3:
At the 2002 Paris Motor Show, BMW unveiled the convertible Z4 sports car, which replaced the Z3. At first, the engine lineup included a 2.5-liter and 3.0-liter inline-6, a step up in class in comparison to the Z3 which started out with only a 4-cylinder powerplant.

The design unmistakably showcased the distinctive styling philosophy of Chris Bangle, BMW's chief designer at the time. The flowing lines and the signature "Z"-shaped press line in front of the doors were design elements that instantly distinguished the car.

With an entirely new chassis and body developed from the platform level, the Z4 achieved near-perfect front/rear weight distribution of 50.3/49.7. What was also notable was that although it was <25kg> lighter, the Z4 boasted three times the twisting rigidity of its predecessor. 

The suspension setup—featuring struts at the front and a multilink configuration at the rear—was carried over from the E46 3 Series. This decision was driven by the fact that extensive testing had already been completed, ensuring a smoother and more efficient development process for the Z4. No compromises were made in incorporating cutting-edge technologies, including BMW's first electric power steering system, DTC (Dynamic Traction Control), an enhancement to the traction control system, and DDC (Dynamic Drive Control), which adjusted steering feel and throttle response to suit either sporty or normal driving modes. The Z4 offered a variety of transmission options: manual, automatic, and a semi-automatic gearbox called SMG.

Like the Z3, the Z4 was manufactured at BMW's Spartanburg plant in South Carolina, USA. The motorsport version of the Z4 has been participating in prestigious events, such as the 24 Hours of Nürburgring.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C3E5:
In 1983, after more than 15 years of production, the Peugeot 104 passed the torch as the brand's compact hatchback to the all-new 205.

Designed by Peugeot's in-house team, the 205 featured a transverse engine layout and quickly became a bestseller, thanks to its modern styling and comfortable interior.

But the story of the 205 doesn’t end there. Alongside its debut, Peugeot unveiled the 205 Turbo 16, a high-performance model developed specifically for competition in the World Rally Championship’s Group B category. Peugeot recognized the need for a road-going sports model that captured the spirit and capability of the 205 Turbo 16. This resulted in the creation of the iconic hot hatch, the 205 GTI.

Its greatest appeal lay in its high-performance engine. Although it only measured a mere <3.7m> long and weighed <900kg>, this compact car came powered by a high-revving 1.6-liter SOHC engine mated to a 5-speed manual gearbox.

In 1986, engine displacement was increased from 1.6 liters to 1.9, which resulted in a output of <130ps>. The car also featured an excellent suspension setup with struts on the front wheels and trailing arms at the rear. Through turns, the 205 GTI showcased exceptional performance, rivaling the reigning "king" of hot hatches at the time, the Golf GTI.

In Europe alone, sales of the Peugeot 205 GTI surpassed 300,000 units. This masterpiece of French engineering is one of the most important cars of 1980s-1990s automotive history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C485:
During the global sport utility vehicle (SUV) boom of the 2010s, Mazda introduced the CX-3 and CX-5, although a notable gap in size existed between the two. The C30 was conceived to bridge that divide, offering a well-balanced compact crossover SUV.

Measuring <4395mm> from front to rear, <1795mm> in width, and standing <1540mm> high, the CX-30's exterior was relatively compact while showcasing Mazda’s signature "KODO Design" philosophy. The signature wing on the front fascia seamlessly linked the grille to the headlights, while the undulations along the body's side panels artfully reflected shifting light.

Under the hood was a choice of three powertrains: the 2.0-liter gasoline direct-injection SKYACTIV-G, the 1.8-liter direct-injection diesel SKYACTIV-D, or the 2.0-liter SKYACTIV-X, which employed a groundbreaking Spark-Controlled Compression Ignition (SPCCI) system.

The CX-30 X Smart Edition, shown here, was introduced in 2021, based on the SKYACTIV-X model. This model grade emphasized comprehensive driver assistance features as standard, including the Active Driving Display, which projects key information onto the windshield, and the Smart Brake Support automatic emergency braking system. Also, the introduction of this model coincided with refinements to the SKYACTIV-X system, with automatic transmission models receiving enhanced throttle pedal resistance that improved driving response. 

Combining versatile dimensions with a dynamic driving character, the CX-30 stands out as an appealing option in Mazda's lineup.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C486:
In France, a long-standing affection for practical "fourgonnette" vehicles—small commercial vans—gave rise to several iconic models over the years. Among them was the Renault Kangoo, introduced in 1997, that left a lasting mark.

Renault designed the Kangoo not merely as a utilitarian workhorse but also gave it the versatility to serve as a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) for family and leisure use. It introduced sliding rear doors for easier access and individual rear seats that could be adjusted independently.

The Kangoo’s success effectively established the "ludospace" genre, combining van-like practicality with car-like comfort. Overall length was about <4m>, with generous cargo space that made it a favorite among those with outdoor pursuits.

Various powertrains were available to suit different needs, but the example highlighted here is powered by a 1.4-liter gasoline powerplant. Producing a modest <75ps>, this engine aligns with the spirit of classic French automobiles—prioritizing the pleasure of fully utilizing every ounce of available power. Combined with its soft, supple suspension, the Kangoo delivered an unexpectedly fun and engaging driving experience. w
DescriptionLong.0x0000C521:
Unveiled in 2017, the Ferrari 812 Superfast continued the marque’s proud lineage of front-engine V12 grand tourers. Its name—a combination of “800 PS, 12 cylinders”—paid tribute to the output of its naturally-aspirated 6.5-liter V12, while “Superfast” came from the legendary 500 Superfast of 1964.

The design was shaped by Ferrari’s in-house Styling Center. It exuded classical proportions with a long nose and short rear deck—hallmarks of a front-mid-engine V12 layout. Yet, its sculpted aerodynamics and refined detailing placed it in the realm of modern Ferrari elegance.

Producing <800ps> and 718Nm (<73.3kgm>) of torque, the V12 delivered its power to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch transaxle. The 812 also marked a technological milestone as the first Ferrari to feature electric power steering.

Its dynamics were further enhanced by the Virtual Short Wheelbase 2.0 system—an evolution of the 4-wheel steering setup from the F12berlinetta. The prime benefit of this system was that it resulted in razor-sharp turn-in even on tight, hairpin corners, despite its <2720mm> wheelbase.

With usable cargo space behind the seats and a generously sized rear luggage area, the 812 Superfast offered grand touring capabilities wrapped in pure supercar body.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C525:
In 1999, Chevrolet introduced a hardtop variant to the Corvette C5 lineup. It traded the coupe’s removable top and rear hatch for a fixed-roof design, increasing structural stiffness that translated into improved handling and driving dynamics. Further underscoring this intent, opting for the hardtop model automatically bundled the Z51 performance handling package and a 6-speed manual transmission. 

Remarkably, despite these upgrades, it was priced below the standard coupe. That's why it became a compelling choice for driving enthusiasts who were drawn to its niche appeal.

From 2001, the hardtop evolved into the Corvette Z06. It was fitted with a <390ps> LS6 engine—an enhanced version of the LS1. The Z06 revived a historic nameplate first used for a race-focused option on the second-generation Corvette. The new Z06 was distinguished not only by its reinforced suspension and track-tuned alignment, but also by its use of a full titanium exhaust system—an extraordinary feature for a production car. It was available only with a manual transmission.

However, these high-performance enhancements came at a significant increase in price.  The Z06 was the most expensive model in the C5 range, even surpassing the convertible, which made it beyond the reach of many, especially when compared to the more accessible fixed-roof model that preceded it.

Still, the Z06 continued to evolve. In 2002, power output rose to <411ps>. Delivering <400ps>-plus was unheard of for a small-block V-8 at the time. These milestones helped cement the C5 Z06 as one of the fastest and most formidable mass-production sports cars of its era.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C526:
In the 1990s, Honda embarked on creating vehicles tailored for leisure, coining the term “Creative Movers” to define this new category. The first of these was the Odyssey, launched in 1994 to widespread commercial acclaim. A year later, the Creative Movers concept expanded with the debut of a crossover SUV. This was the first-generation CR-V.

From that point onward, the CR-V established itself as a perennial favorite, particularly in the North American market. The model featured here is the 2021 iteration, an evolution of the fifth-generation CR-V that first appeared in 2016.

A defining feature of this generation was the introduction of a hybrid powertrain—the first such offering for the series. The system paired a 2.0-liter Atkinson-cycle engine with two electric motors, capable of operating in both series and parallel modes. Its efficiency shone particularly at cruising speeds, where the gasoline engine took over. The availability of 4-wheel drive further broadened its appeal, offering versatility across a wide range of driving conditions.

While the styling retained many cues from the previous generation, the body was slightly enlarged to enhance rear-seat legroom and passenger comfort. Practicality remained a hallmark of the CR-V, with more than 1,100 liters of cargo space available when the rear seats were folded down. A gasoline-powered variant also offered 3-row, 7-seat configuration.

Beyond its practicality and efficiency, the fifth-generation CR-V was equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver assistance features, including collision mitigation braking and adaptive cruise control. All of this made the CR-V an ideal companion for both weekend adventures and everyday life.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C527:
Japan’s micro-car segment, known domestically as kei-cars, has become an essential part of daily life across the country. While the category includes everything from passenger vehicles and mini-SUVs to sports cars, it also plays a critical role in supporting infrastructure through a wide range of commercial vans and trucks. The Suzuki Carry stands as a quintessential example of the commercial kei truck.

First introduced in 1961, the Carry boasts a long and storied history. The tenth generation was introduced in 1999 following a full model change to comply with revised kei-car regulations introduced the previous year. The model shown here is from 2012, marking the final iteration of the tenth-generation model.

Compared to its predecessor, the new Carry featured a slightly larger footprint, measuring <3395mm> in length and <1475mm> in width. Its semi-cabover design placed the engine beneath the occupants' feet. Displacement remained within the kei-class limit at <658cc>, with early variants even offering turbocharged options.

To accommodate a variety of needs, the Carry was offered in several trim levels. The KC—its most well-equipped—came standard with power steering and air conditioning. While rear-wheel drive was standard, a 4-wheel-drive variant ensured that it was at home on snowy roads and rugged terrain as it was on the highway.

Beyond its utilitarian function, the Carry’s charming design and remarkable practicality garnered international attention. In the United States, pre-owned Carrys—eligible for road use 25 years after their original release—have become increasingly popular among farmers and hobbyists alike. Compact yet capable, the Carry is a testament to the ingenuity of Japanese design and its ability to resonate around the world.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C7BD:
In 1976, Citroën began a new chapter under the Peugeot umbrella. It left many wondering what defined a Citroën in this new era. The answer came in bold form at the 1982 Paris Auto Salon with the debut of the BX.

The BX was infused with unmistakably Citroën DNA. Drawing inspiration from classics like the GS and CX, it combined their iconic character with clean, assertive lines. Inside, the BX offered a comfortable cabin with generous space for both passengers and luggage. Its striking design was the work of none other than Marcello Gandini, then with the famed Bertone design house.

Great care was also taken beneath the surface. While parts sharing with Peugeot had become common, the BX proudly retained Citroën’s hallmark hydropneumatic suspension. This innovative system replaces conventional coil springs and dampers with a combination of nitrogen gas and hydraulic fluid, allowing the ride height to be adjusted at will.

The BX was offered with a variety of engine options, but the 19 TRS featured here stands out as a grand tourer-style model powered by a 1.9-liter gasoline engine. Although not especially powerful on paper, the engine was well matched to the car’s relatively lightweight, aerodynamic body, making it an ideal companion for long-distance holiday drives.

The BX proved to be a resounding success for Citroën, enjoying a strong 12-year production run. More than just a commercial triumph, it reaffirmed Citroën’s place as a serious contender during a dynamic era of innovation in the French automotive world.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C7BE:
Following the end of the Group B era in the WRC, Lancia turned to the Delta as its weapon of choice for Group A competition. Transformed with a turbocharged engine and a newly developed 4-wheel-drive system, the high-performance Delta was rebranded as the HF 4WD and made its debut in the 1987 WRC.

Just a year later, it evolved into the legendary Delta Integrale, equipped with aggressive blistered wheel arches. In 1990, the Integrale received a significant upgrade with the addition of a 16-valve cylinder head, boosting its performance even further. However, it soon faced fierce competition. Despite Lancia’s continued efforts, the Drivers’ Championship slipped from the Delta’s grasp in both 1990 and 1991, claimed by Toyota's Celica. Thus, in 1992, Lancia unveiled what would be considered the final evolution of the Delta.

This new Integrale featured reinforced bodywork for enhanced rigidity and underwent extensive suspension revisions, including a widened track. In line with these upgrades, the blistered wheel arches grew even more pronounced. To enhance aerodynamic performance, a roof-mounted spoiler was added to generate more downforce, while the torque distribution of the 4-wheel-drive system was recalibrated to give the car a more rear-wheel-drive–like character.

Thanks to these comprehensive improvements, the Delta regained its competitive edge. Although Lancia’s factory team ceased official racing activities in 1992 due to a policy shift by parent company FIAT, Lancia partnered with the Jolly Club satellite team, providing full technical support. Juha Kankkunen and Didier Auriol competed in 11 of 14 rounds that season, with Auriol taking six victories, Kankkunen adding one more, and Andrea Aghini yet another. With eight wins total, Lancia clinched the constructors' championship for the sixth consecutive year.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C7BF:
Peugeot has long been known for crafting spirited compact cars. This legacy continues to shine in today’s SUV-dominated market. The brand found success in 2013 with the debut of the original 2008 compact SUV, and in 2019, Peugeot elevated the concept further with the launch of the next-generation 2008.

Peugeot’s traditional naming convention—three digits with a zero in the center—evolved with the rise of SUVs, expanding to four digits. The 2008 follows this format, sharing the same CMP platform as its hatchback sibling, the 208.

Measuring just <4.3m> in length, the 2008 may be compact in size, but it projects all the presence and stature expected of a true SUV. Its sharp, angular motifs evoke the image of a lion’s claws and fangs, a design language that has become a hallmark of Peugeot’s identity. 

Step inside, and you’re greeted by Peugeot’s distinctive 3D i-Cockpit, a driver-focused layout that sets the cabin apart. At its heart is a compact, flat-topped and -bottomed steering wheel. Just above it sits a head-up digital instrument cluster, cleverly elevated to fall within the driver’s natural line of sight.
DescriptionLong.0x0000C7D4:
The Qashqai is Nissan’s C-segment compact SUV, positioned as a cornerstone of the brand’s global lineup. It was launched in 2006 and followed by a second-generation model in 2013. The version featured here represents the third-generation Qashqai, which made its debut in 2021. 

With this latest incarnation, the Qashqai continued to evolve. It arrived with a striking redesign, complementing its larger body with a bold, angular aesthetic. Sharp character lines converged toward Nissan’s signature Vmotion grille, giving the front end a confident and modern presence. Underpinning the vehicle is the advanced CMF-C/D3 platform, which enhances both ride comfort and handling.

When it comes to the powertrain, the Qashqai offers more than just conventional gasoline options—it also features Nissan’s innovative "e-Power" series-hybrid system. This setup uses a gasoline engine solely to generate electricity, which then powers an electric motor that drives the wheels. What’s more, the engine at the heart of Nissan’s e-Power system is the world’s first mass-producible variable compression ratio engine. It delivers significantly improved thermal efficiency, resulting in reduced CO₂ emissions.

Tekna denotes one of the higher model grades in the lineup. This trim comes generously equipped, with larger alloy wheels, ambient lighting, and a head-up display—all included as standard.m
DescriptionLong.0x0000C859:
Sony Honda Mobility introduced the AFEELA brand at CES® 2023 and further developed it through CES 2024 as a bold new direction in mobility, aiming to transform transportation into a rich, engaging experience. At CES® 2025, the company pulled the wraps off its first production model: The AFEELA 1. The name signaled the start of a new chapter—one that represented the beginning of something revolutionary.

Much of the technology and design philosophy from the prototype was carried over to the production version. It boasts a clean and refined exterior, with a flowing shape that avoids any unnecessary styling elements. Even the door handles are gone, and all sensors—including LIDAR, radar, and cameras—have been neatly integrated into the bodywork.

Inside, the AFEELA 1 was designed as a creative entertainment space—a true mobility environment. Wide-format displays dominate the cabin, while each passenger seat has been fitted with its own sound system. Advanced noise-cancelling and spatial audio tech ensure an immersive experience for every passenger.

A standout feature is its built-in personal agent, capable of natural conversation. It learns user preferences over time, evolving into a smart companion that can assist with travel planning and engage in meaningful dialogue.

Of course, the AFEELA 1 did not forgotten that it is still a car. Electric motors, brakes, and suspension work together as one system, controlled through advanced robotics-based software to deliver a smooth and composed ride and sharp handling traits in any condition.

The vehicle is also equipped with Sony Honda Mobility’s proprietary ADAS system. The sensors of the ADAS system feed data to a high-performance ECU delivering 800 TOPS of processing power, enabling the car to assist from departure to parking with precision and confidence.

The AFEELA 1 will be available in two trims: the AFEELA 1 Origin and AFEELA 1 Signature. The AFEELA 1 Signature, shown here, comes standard with 21-inch wheels, a rear entertainment system, and a center camera monitoring setup.^
DescriptionLong.0x0000C85A:
The N-ONE was introduced as a new basic model, taking design cues from the original N360—Honda’s first kei-car. Launched in 2012, the first-generation N-ONE quickly earned praise for its charming looks and fun-to-drive nature.

By 2020, it had entered its second generation. Although the platform was redesigned, strong fan demand for continuity meant the body panels from the original model were carried over. Instead, Honda refined the shape of the grille and bumper, subtly signaling the model’s evolution. 

The second-generation sports variant was named the RS, short for Road Sailing. While the RS badge also appeared on the first-generation model, the new version introduced a key upgrade: a front-mounted turbocharged engine paired with front-wheel drive and a 6-speed manual gearbox—one that made it even more enjoyable to drive.

The RS also featured exclusive styling with black trim pieces, but the standout element remained the 6-speed manual transmission. Geared for enthusiasts, the transmission used close ratios similar to the S660. Second and third gears benefited from heavy-duty synchros, and the clutch system was similarly reinforced.

Despite its performance focus, the RS also included modern driving aids. A peak torque limiter smoothed out clutch engagement, while auto brake hold helped during hill starts—features that made the car more approachable in daily use.

Weighing in at under <1000kg> and with compact dimensions, the N-ONE RS delivered sharp, responsive handling not typically expected from a car in this class. The result was a well-balanced package that brought the fun and excitement of sports driving to the masses.l
DescriptionLong.0x0000C85B:
In 2004, Nismo—now known as Nissan Motorsports & Customizing—celebrated its 20th anniversary. To mark the milestone, the team set out to build the ultimate road car, a showcase of two decades of motorsports know-how. The result was the Nismo R34 GT-R Z-tune.

By then, however, production of the R34 Skyline GT-R had already ended. To overcome this, Nismo sourced 20 carefully selected used cars that met strict criteria, then stripped them down to bare shells for a complete, hand-built reconstruction.

Every component added was engineered to meet the high standards of the Z name. At the heart of it all was the RB26DETT Kai-Z2 engine. The engine was based on the same 2.8-liter setup used in the GT500 GT-R of that era. It featured strengthened internals, from the pistons and rods to the block, for maximum reliability under extreme use. The IHI turbochargers were proven in the 2004 Nürburgring 24-Hour race. And the titanium exhaust system helped improve catalytic performance and flow.

To enhance chassis rigidity, additional spot welds were applied in key areas like the door frames, while sections vulnerable to heat-related distortion were reinforced with molded CFRP parts. For suspension, Nismo worked with SACHS to develop specially tuned bolt-on dampers, drawing on SACHS's GT500 expertise. Bespoke brake components were co-developed with Brembo to achieve 1.6G of braking force on semi-slick tires. The exterior was also reworked with a focus on reducing weight, improving cooling, and enhancing aerodynamics. In particular, the front bumper, fenders, and hood were replaced with CFRP parts.

In the end, only 19 units were produced—including the original prototype—but the R34 GT-R Z-tune remains, without question, Nismo’s crowning achievement among the second wave of GT-R models.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CAEA:
The Corvette CX Concept remained unmistakably a Corvette to its core. Engineered for both street and circuit, the Corvette CX Concept represented a futuristic vision of an electrified Corvette hypercar.

From its athletic proportions and aggressive, lunging profile to the cockpit tucked between muscular haunches, every line and surface served a purpose. The design was clean yet purposeful, with refined surfaces flowing seamlessly into a visible structural framework, while the interior prioritized lightness and driver-focused functionality.

The CX Concept featured active aerodynamics, with movable front and rear elements and a finely sculpted underbody, which delivered efficiency on the open road and the race track. A fan-based downforce system with thrust vectoring enabled precise aerodynamic balance between the front and rear. As an all-wheel-drive machine, the CX Concept housed four e-motors integrated into the RESS understructure, delivering more than 2,000 horsepower.[
DescriptionLong.0x0000CAEB:
Designed purely for the racetrack, the Corvette CX.R Vision Gran Turismo Concept pushed the envelope even further. It offered a glimpse into the future of Corvette GT racing.

The Corvette CX.R Vision Gran Turismo Concept possessed a more aggressive aerodynamic package, lower stance, and a lighter build than the standard CX Concept. Underneath, it featured an advanced E-Fuel/Electric hybrid powertrain—two electric motors up front, one at the rear, and a compact, high-revving twin-turbo V-8, delivering both the performance and the efficiency needed for endurance racing.

The interior of the CX.R Vision Gran Turismo was purpose-built for the demands of the race track.  Its geometric layout and lightweight seat—with minimal foam trim—offered essential head and neck support to withstand the intense cornering forces expected at racing speeds. The steering wheel featured physical buttons and knobs, ensuring precise control even when wearing racing gloves.

Finished in a striking yellow and black livery, the CX.R Vision Gran Turismo paid tribute to 25 years of Corvette GT racing heritage.j
DescriptionLong.0x0000CAEC:
The Renault Avantime brought an unconventional twist to the widely praised Renault Espace, reimagining the European minivan. Conceived as a bold design study by Renault’s chief designer, Patrick Le Quément, the Avantime made its debut at the 1999 Geneva Motor Show. When Renault confirmed plans to launch it as a production model in 2001, the news was met with widespread disbelief.

At first glance, the Avantime resembled a minivan—but with a twist: it had only two doors. Inside, it featured a conventional layout with two rows of seats, accommodating up to five passengers in comfort. Renault’s reasoning for this unorthodox design was that it was intended to be a niche coupe.

This intent became clear the moment you stepped inside the Avantime. The luxury of enjoying the expansive cabin of a minivan, with only a handful of passengers, truly defined it as a niche creation. From the rear seats, the visibility was exceptional. With all the side windows lowered and the expansive sunroof fully open, the sense of openness was remarkable. It offered a feeling of freedom and airiness not unlike that of a convertible.

In its home market, the Avantime was also offered with a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine. But for Japan, it possessed a 3.0-liter DOHC 24-valve V-6, producing <207ps> at <6000rpm> and <28.5kgm> of torque at <3750rpm>. True to its character, the Avantime delivered a composed and confident ride. The generous torque and trademark Renault smoothness came together in perfect harmony. The driving quality was so refined, it surpassed that of many traditional sedans and coupes.

The Avantime embodied Renault’s unique spirit that proved the monoform silhouette wasn’t the sole domain of minivans.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB7F:
Since its debut in 1990, the Elantra had been a cornerstone of Hyundai’s lineup. In 2020, the seventh generation was introduced, earning wide acclaim for the bold “Parametric Dynamics” of its exterior design. At the top of this seventh-generation range stood the Elantra N.

Created to embody the N philosophy of “making cornering fun,” the Elantra N was powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter engine producing <280ps> and <40.0kgm> of torque. Despite its front-wheel-drive layout, it accelerated from 0 to <100km/h> in just 5.3 seconds.

The car was offered with either a 6-speed manual or an 8-speed DCT. The manual came equipped with rev-matching, while the DCT added advanced features such as N Grin Shift for overboost, N Power Shift to enhance shifting characteristics, and N Track Sense Shift, optimized for race-track driving.

The suspension featured electronically controlled dampers, an eLSD, and a large braking system, ensuring sharp handling and confidence at speed. With its reinforced chassis and Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires, it achieved a fine balance between cornering agility and stability. Inside, the Elantra N offered a custom steering wheel, supportive bucket seats, and the N Sound Equalizer, which allowed drivers to tailor the exhaust note to their liking for a heightened sports-driving experience.

Hyundai even developed a TCR touring car variant of the Elantra, a machine that earned respect on the track and underscored the car’s deep ties to motorsports."
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB80:
The Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo stands as the 2025 highlight in Opel’s long tradition of concept cars. The brand with the Blitz logo was the first European manufacturer to unveil a concept car in 1965—the Experimental GT. Now, 60 years later, Opel once again broke new ground with a “phygital” concept—a physical show car that could also be driven in Gran Turismo 7.

The Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo draws upon Opel’s deep motorsports and performance heritage, blending it with the iconic Corsa nameplate while offering a glimpse of future generations of sporty GSE models bearing the Blitz insignia. In short, it embodies the essence of Opel’s GSE sub-brand, wrapped in a compact, all-electric high-performance machine.

To captivate the gaming community, the Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo combines outstanding efficiency with pulse-quickening driving dynamics. It's powered by two 350 kW (<476ps>) electric motors, one on each axle, for a combined output of 588 kW (<800ps>) and 800 Nm (<81.6kgm>) of torque. Also, its permanent all-wheel drive sharpens grip, refines handling, and elevates overall stability. With a single-speed transmission, it accelerates from zero to <100km/h> in just two seconds and reaches a top speed of <320km/h>.

Its stunning performance is mirrored by a bold, muscular presence. The car's muscular exterior is defined by sharp lines and intricate mechanical details. Overall, the Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo offers a sharper expression of Opel’s bold and pure design philosophy, highlighted by the sleek evolution of the next-generation Opel Vizor. The illuminated Opel Blitz stands proudly at the center of the signature Opel Compass, the guiding element of the design and the car’s backbone. On either side, horizontal lighting bars flank it with precision. The vertical axis of the Compass extends from the front bumper into the aero-sculpted hood, reinforcing the design’s symmetry. At the rear, a broad taillamp integrates with the rear window, giving the car a bold, unmistakable presence.

To ensure that the Opel Corsa GSE Vision Gran Turismo remains firmly anchored at speed, Opel endowed it with a suite of finely tuned aerodynamic solutions. Air curtains channel flow across the pronounced fenders, aided by black aero blade flares that smoothen turbulence aod increase high-speed stability.
