DescriptionLong.0x0000CB81:
“MAZDA SPIRIT RACING” was an initiative launched by Mazda to cement the company’s place in motorsports and to cultivate new talent through racing. Competing in events such as the Super Endurance Series with a large crew made up of Mazda employees, it grew into a formidable presence in the sport.

From this foundation, the team created a car that embodied the skills and knowledge it had gained through years of competition. That car was unveiled as the “MAZDA SPIRIT RACING ROADSTER 12R” in early 2025 at the Tokyo Auto Salon.

As its name suggested, it was based on the ND Mazda Roadster. But beneath the familiar silhouette, it was packed with works-grade components.

The centerpiece was its engine, built on a 2.0-liter block not normally offered in the domestic soft-top model, enhanced with a specially tuned head, pistons, and exhaust manifold among other components, each unit painstakingly assembled by hand. The power had been pushed close to the very limit of what was achievable in a production car that also demanded durability, ultimately delivering <200ps>.

Its chassis reflected the lessons learned from the Super Endurance Series. Among them was the suspension that used height-adjustable Bilstein dampers, while the brakes were equipped with 4-piston calipers from Brembo. It featured forged Rays wheels, identical to those used on race cars.

Other special parts included Recaro seats and a Fujitsubo exhaust system. With production capped at just 200 units, the ROADSTER 12R stood as perhaps the ultimate works-tuned roadster._
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB82:
The Toyota Land Cruiser was first conceived as a vehicle for Japan’s National Police Reserve, but it evolved into a world-class off-roader renowned for its all-terrain ability and legendary reliability. More than 70 years later, the model that continued to hold a special place in the hearts of enthusiasts was the third-generation “40,” introduced in 1960.

Exports had begun earlier with the “20” series in 1955, establishing the Land Cruiser as a serious contender on the world stage. The “40” was designed to better meet the expectations of international customers. Beyond its refreshed exterior, it elevated the model’s already renowned off-road prowess with greater comfort on the highway, broadening its appeal.

The 40 series was available in short, medium, and long-wheelbase versions, each tailored to different needs. The 2-door hardtop variant, seen here, found extensive use in mountainous regions, where its short <2285mm> wheelbase proved invaluable.

Compact in size, it measured <3870mm> in length, <1690mm> in width, and <1930mm> in height. Originally equipped with a 3.9-liter “F” gasoline engine, the lineup gained even more popularity in 1974 with the addition of the 3.0-liter “B” diesel engine. Its part-time 4-wheel-drive system with a 2-speed transfer case only reinforced its reputation for toughness. This was the model that embodied the Land Cruiser philosophy of “go anywhere and come back alive.”

Alongside the 2-door hardtop, the 40 series as a whole became one of the Land Cruiser’s greatest successes, remaining in production for 24 years, until 1984. Its enduring popularity inspired the launch of the FJ Cruiser in 2006, a modern homage that revived many of the classic 40’s design cues.

And in 2021, Toyota announced the reproduction of 40-series parts through Gazoo Racing, proving that this iconic Land Cruiser was, and always will be, worth keeping alive on the road.L
DescriptionLong.0x0000CB83:
When it was introduced in 1994, the Toyota RAV4 pioneered an entirely new market segment, called the “crossover SUV.” Combining smooth off-road handling with a compact body, the first-generation model was widely praised for its ability to transcend the boundaries of on-road and off-road vehicles, and it continued to evolve with each successive generation. In 2018, the fifth-generation RAV4 was introduced on an all-new platform. Built on Toyota’s New Global Architecture (TNGA), it set new benchmarks for driving dynamics, safety, and comfort.

The Adventure grade, in particular, embodied the core spirit of an SUV. With its distinctive front grille, skid-plate bumper, and 19-inch tires, it projected rugged styling and a readiness to embrace the great outdoors. Its powertrain paired a 2.0-liter 4-cylinder Dynamic Force Engine with a Direct Shift-CVT, delivering smooth acceleration and impressive fuel efficiency.

Of special note was the newly developed Dynamic Torque Vectoring AWD system, which precisely controlled torque distribution between the left and right rear wheels, enhancing both traction and stability. A disconnect mechanism allowed the driver to disengage the rear-drive system entirely, improving fuel economy during everyday use.

On the safety front, Toyota Safety Sense came standard across the lineup, offering advanced features such as a pre-collision safety system, Lane Tracing Assist, and adaptive Radar Cruise Control. Additional amenities included a modern multimedia system with smartphone integration and a Panoramic View Monitor that provided a bird’s-eye view around the vehicle.

An ideal expression of the modern SUV, it excelled on city streets and natural terrain, infusing a sense of adventure into daily driving.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD03:
The Polestar 5 is the flagship model of the Scandinavian high-performance electric brand, Polestar. It represents the realization of ideas introduced by the Precept concept car in 2020, embodying pure Scandinavian design, advanced technology, and sustainability.

Its stretched form, measuring <5m> in length, draws inspiration from aircraft, while the panel structure and expansive glass roof, extending toward the rear, contribute to its aerodynamic efficiency. With a drag coefficient of just 0.24, the bonded aluminum body delivers a lightweight yet rigid structure, offering greater torsional rigidity than many sports cars.

The powertrain employs a dual-motor system built around an in-house developed electric rear motor. The Performance Edition is capable of a total system output of 650 kW (<884ps>) and runs from zero to <100km/h> in just 3.2 seconds. Its 800 V electric architecture enables 350 kW fast charging, replenishing the battery from 10 percent to 80 in only 22 minutes. Maximum range under WLTP testing reached <670km> for the Dual Motor edition.

The suspension consists of a specially designed double-wishbone layout. The Performance Edition features magnetorheological dampers that read the road surface up to 1,000 times per second, balancing agility with comfort. Driver assistance systems extend further, with automatic lane and speed control operating up to <150km/h>.

With futuristic design, remarkable electric performance, and a deep commitment to sustainability, the Polestar 5 stands as the ultimate grand tourer package.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD04:
Ferrari had long produced racing machines derived from its road-going super sports cars, achieving remarkable results in endurance and GT race championships. The 296 GT3 was one such car to carry on that tradition, developed from the 296 GTB.

As a pure racing machine, the 296 GT3 dispensed with the plug-in hybrid system of the road car, relying solely on a 600-horsepower twin-turbo V-6 engine. This unit employed a 3.0-liter 120-degree V-6, extensively modified for weight reduction and reliability. Drivetrain, cooling components, and aerodynamic parts were all replaced with dedicated race versions. 

Unlike earlier racing Ferraris, traditionally constructed by Michelotto, the 296 GT3 was built by legendary race-car specialists Oreca. From chassis construction to assembly and after-sales service, Oreca provided full end-to-end support. The car was first unveiled at the 2022 24 Hours of Spa in July, before making its racing debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona.

The 296 GT3 was not confined to the current international endurance championships; its design continued to evolve toward the future. An Evo version, with enhanced aerodynamic efficiency and improved endurance, had already been announced for the 2026 season. 

By blending the sophistication of its road-going sibling with the raw speed of a track machine, the 296 GT3 became the new standard-bearer of Ferrari’s motorsports strategy.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD05:
There is a long-standing tradition within the Ferrari line-up in which its super sports models have relied on a mid-mounted V-8s. With a lightweight, high-revving engine placed behind the driver, this layout delivered sharp response and agile maneuverability, and it became emblematic of the brand. The 296 GTB carried forward parts of that legacy while opening the door to new possibilities.

It was the first Ferrari to adopt a twin-turbo V-6 engine. And it was the first time in more than a half century that a V-6 block had been used by the marque—last seen on the 206 and 246 under the Dino name. With a displacement of <2992cc>, the engine employed a 120-degree bank angle with IHI turbochargers positioned within the vee.

One of the key reasons behind the move to a V-6 powertrain was the integration of a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) system. Combined with a 123kW electric motor, the system produced a total of 830 horsepower, allowing for blistering acceleration from zero to <100km/h> in just 2.9 seconds. With a top speed of <330km/h>, the 296 GTB offered performance truly worthy of the Ferrari name.

Its design paid homage to the legendary 250 LM of the 1960s, while also being the most compact model in the contemporary Ferrari line-up. The distinctive tunnel-back rear window enhanced both aerodynamics and elegance. Blending the classic mid-engine sports layout with groundbreaking technology, the 296 GTB stood as the epitome of Ferrari’s new generation.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD06:
In 1980, as demand for smaller cars rose in the wake of the oil shock, Fiat introduced a bold new compact to replace the aging 126. In a stark departure from its predecessor, the Panda was a front-wheel-drive hatchback with a transverse, front-mounted engine.

Although relatively simple, its design was both modern and practical. The packaging of the Panda was entrusted to design maestro Giorgetto Giugiaro. To reduce costs, the body panels were shaped with flat surfaces and straight lines, while the windows were made of flat glass. The seats followed suit, using a basic hammock layout with fabric stretched over a pipe frame. Yet the overall look of the car was fresh, and the interior proved surprisingly spacious.

At its debut, the Panda was powered by either a <652cc> 2-cylinder air-cooled engine or a <903cc> 4-cylinder water-cooled engine. At the time, Fiat named its engines according to output, with the former designated the 30 and the latter the 45. In 1983, a part-time 4-wheel-drive 4x4 version appeared. It marked a world first for a vehicle with a transverse-engine/front-wheel-drive layout.

The Panda became an immediate success upon release, quickly emerging as one of the driving forces behind Fiat's resurgence. Giugiaro himself declared at the time that this compact masterpiece was the greatest work of his career.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD07:
Mine’s is renowned as one of the stalwart tuners in the Nissan world, and its most iconic creation was without question the fully tuned BNR34 GT-R N1 base.

Born in 1999, this machine was a deep exploration into the beauty of the R34 GT-R, while remaining faithful to the spirit of a street car. From the meticulous tuning of the RB26DETT, to the low, balanced suspension, to the restrained yet purposeful exterior, every element was shaped by the vision of Mine’s CEO Michizo Niikura, whose goal was nothing less than a first-class street car.

Yet this car was equally at home on the race track. It breezed past the one-minute barrier at Tsukuba Circuit, proving its remarkable ability.

Thus, this particular car—revered among enthusiasts as the Hon-Demo—achieved the astonishing feat of recording more than <10000km> on its odometer through circuit driving alone.

But its story did not end there. In 2021, the car received a full restoration by Garage Yoshida, breathing new life into the legend. At Niikura’s request, the original front GT-R emblem remained unrestored, a nod to its history. Its value was underscored in Gran Turismo 7, where it was priced at 3 million Cr.—a figure echoed in the real world, as the owner declined a cash-equivalent offer of the same amount.

Thanks to the dedication of Japanese restomod specialists Built By Legends, the worth of the BNR34 GT-R N1 base was once again being reexamined across the globe. If fortune ever grants you the chance to witness one in person, consider yourself truly lucky.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD08:
The FTO, which made its debut in October 1994, marked the return of the nameplate 23 years after the original model first appeared. The first Galant-based FTO coupe had been the little brother to the Galant GTO, and the reborn version was once again positioned as a 2-door coupe following in the GTO’s footsteps.

While the first generation was an FR, the new car adopted an FF layout, sharing its platform with the Lancer and Mirage. Classified as a larger size Class 3 vehicle (Japanese regulations), it was unusual for its category, its wide body becoming a defining feature.

Its design, with sweeping curves and flowing lines, was in harmony with the GTO and Eclipse of the same era. The front fenders blended seamlessly into the hood, creating a bold form that carried its motion through to the rear fenders.

Power came from a 1.8-liter SOHC inline-4, the 4G93, producing <125ps> and <16.5kgm> of torque; a 2.0-liter DOHC V-6, the 6A12, producing <170ps> and <19.0kgm> (<180ps> and <19.5kgm> in later models); or a highly tuned 6A12 delivering <200ps> and <20.4kgm>. The <200ps> output of the high-spec engine was achieved with Mitsubishi’s MIVEC variable valve timing system.

Its transmission was also ahead of its time. In addition to the standard 5-speed manual, Mitsubishi offered the INVECS-II 4-speed automatic with a sports mode—the first of its kind in a Japanese car—paving the way for future sport automatics.

With its distinctive styling and engaging performance, the FTO earned Japan Car of the Year honors in 1994. By 1997, the INVECS-II had evolved into a 5-speed automatic. Sadly, as the market shifted away from coupes toward MPVs and SUVs, production of the FTO came to an end in 2000.\
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD09:
The Renault Espace made its debut in 1984 as Europe’s first minivan. Ten years later, in 1994, an extraordinary version of the Espace was revealed at the Paris Motor Show. This machine carried an F1 engine at its core and was christened the Espace F1.

The original concept came from Matra, which had first pitched the Espace to Renault and had crafted its fiberglass body panels. At the time, Renault was partnered with Williams, fresh from its triumph in Formula 1. Matra proposed installing the 3.5-liter V-10 RS4 engine from the 1992 championship-winning FW14B into the Espace, both as a tribute to the model’s tenth anniversary and as a statement of Renault’s success.

Built at Matra’s Romorantin plant in France, the Espace F1 stood as an entirely unconventional minivan. It shared part of its chassis with the second-generation model, yet most of the body was refashioned in aluminum and carbon fiber. The body’s width was expanded to house massive tires, while a giant rear wing adorned the roof, pressing the body downward.

The engine, the very heart of the beast, was mounted amidships between the front and rear axles. Inside, the three rows of seats gave way to four carbon-fiber buckets, while the engine’s intake funnels stood proudly on display between the rear seats. The Espace F1 produced <800ps>, accelerating from 0-<100km/h> in just 2.8 seconds and reaching a top speed of <316km/h>.

Legends like Alain Prost took the wheel of the Espace F1 on circuit, releasing the piercing whine of its race engine as it roared past enthralled crowds.
DescriptionLong.0x0000CD0A:
Gran Turismo introduced the F3500-A, an original formula machine created as a tribute to the golden age of early 1990s Formula 1. It captured the speed and technology of that era, giving players a breathtaking taste of top-level racing.

To continue that lineage, we now present the F3500-B. The most significant change lies in its power unit. Where the F3500-A was powered by a naturally-aspirated V-12, the F3500-B turns to a lighter, more compact V-8.

Although devoid of cutting-edge systems such as variable intakes or pneumatic valves, it retains the same electronic fly-by-wire throttle of its predecessor. This engine revs to <13800rpm>, and despite the inherent limitations of the V-8, it produces more than <710ps>. A transverse 6-speed gearbox ensures the best possible packaging. 

The body remains faithful to the F3500-A, but the front end has been refined. Three different high-nose wings are available, each with its own aerodynamic philosophy.

The sharp responses and direct feel of the F3500-A remain, but with the F3500-B, you will also discover the “lightness” of this V-8-powered machine.M
DescriptionLong.0x0000CF1F:
Xiaomi has achieved global success in the world of smart devices. Utilizing the same technologies and innovative spirit, Xiaomi has turned its attention to the electric mobility market. Its debut model, the SU7 sports sedan, quickly found success, but development of the car did not end there. It was followed by a monster variant designed to challenge the preconceptions of BEVs. That car was the SU7 Ultra.

The SU7 Ultra used a three-motor all-wheel-drive system, placing one motor on the front axle and two on the rear. This configuration delivered a total system output of up to <1548ps>, with the “V-8-type” electric motors capable of spinning up to <27200rpm>—an unprecedented feat for a production model. This translated into extraordinary performance, with a
0-<100km/h> acceleration time of just 1.98 seconds and a top speed of <350km/h>.

Xiaomi has also left no stone unturned when it came to body innovation. High rigidity and low weight were realized through extensive use of carbon-fiber body panels and cell-to-body construction, seamlessly integrating the battery and chassis. This introduced an entirely new era of passenger-car construction.

The exterior was engineered for maximum aerodynamic efficiency, with the carbon-fiber body kit generating up to <285kg> of downforce. Special attention has also been given to braking performance—its brakes enable the car to decelerate from <100km/h> to a complete stop in just <30.8m>.

With its luxurious interior, electronically controlled active suspension, and the latest in ADAS technology, the SU7 also delivered outstanding cost performance. This ultimate mobility solution marked a turning point in the history of BEVs.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D167:
The ELANTRA N is a high-performance sedan from Hyundai’s N brand. There was also a special edition of this car built specifically for motorsports, called the ELANTRA N TC.

The base-model ELANTRA N was already an excellent choice for the circuit, featuring a turbocharged 2.0-liter direct-injection engine producing <280ps> and <40.0kgm> of torque, and capable of accelerating from 0–<100km/h> in 5.3 seconds in a front-wheel-drive layout. With these strong fundamentals, the TC variant was specially modified to meet international touring-car regulations and was imbued with the capability to win.

The aerodynamic wide body, carbon-fiber splitter, and large rear wing generated substantial downforce, dramatically improving high-speed cornering stability. The drivetrain incorporated a sequential 6-speed gearbox, while the dedicated racing suspension and adjustable dampers allowed it to adapt instantly to varying track conditions. The braking and cooling systems were also upgraded with endurance-spec components.

Efforts to reduce weight and increase rigidity were evident throughout, with the cockpit featuring a regulation roll cage and racing seat. The steering and pedal layout were engineered for immediate response to driver inputs. Carefully crafted into a machine built for victory, the ELANTRA N TC carried the competitive spirit of its road-going counterpart while retaining its agility and reliability.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D18E:
Since the introduction of the original Porsche 911 more than half a century ago in 1963, the 911 had long been regarded as the epitome of the sports car on both public roads and race circuits around the world. With its unique rear-mounted flat-6 engine and highly tuned performance, the 911 series had claimed victory in countless races, cementing its position in automotive history.

This bloodline was continued by the eighth-generation "992" model 911, released in 2018. With features such as stretched rear fenders on all models, 4-point LED headlights, and intricate rear combination lamps, this car became the true embodiment of modern Porsche design philosophy. Built around a turbocharged 3.0-liter flat-6, technological upgrades like improved cooling and the 8-speed PDK transmission allowed for peak performance from everyday driving to spirited sports use.

The 992 model was also developed into a pure racing machine as the 911 GT3 R.

Introduced in 2022, this car housed a 4.2-liter flat-6 engine producing up to <565ps>. It featured carbon-fiber and aramid-woven components, along with the double-wishbone and multilink suspension from the 911 RSR.

The brakes featured AP Racing discs, while the driver controls were updated with new steering components and a 10.3-inch user display. The 911 GT3 R represented the culmination of all Porsche’s racing knowledge and technology—a single purpose-built car designed to dominate the circuit.u
DescriptionLong.0x0000D1B5:
Introduced in 1966, the Camaro was created as a pony car to take on Ford’s Mustang, with the high-performance Z28 model developed for homologation for the SCCA’s Trans-Am Series.

The Z28 was released as a hardcore motorsports base model, equipped with a high-revving 302 cubic-inch V-8 engine (approx. 4.9 liters), with no options available for automatic transmissions or air conditioning. One such car under Penske Racing claimed a championship victory in the Trans-Am Series. Such results helped create a new trend of small-displacement, high-revving American V-8s.

Created by Gran Turismo, this “Camaro 1969 Race-Mod” is a modern reinterpretation of the original Camaro Z28. The spirit of classic Trans-Am was carried on in the car’s low stance, with a number of elements added from the restomod movement that enjoyed widespread popularity at events like SEMA. All the chrome trim was stripped from the exterior and replaced with carbon black components. A wide-mouth bumper, large ducktail spoiler, and a center-exit exhaust were also added.

The spartan interior featured a sequential shifter, roll cage, and Alcantara bucket seats. Behind these classical stylings, however, lay the true identity of the beast: a supercharged V-8 engine producing <667ps>. The ultimate modern Trans-American race car rebuilt tradition through new technologies.m
DescriptionLong.0x0000D243:
The Captur is a compact crossover SUV produced by Renault. The first model appeared in 2013 and quickly gained popularity for its urban-friendly design and strong everyday utility. The second-generation model was released in 2019, built on an updated platform that improved driving performance and ride quality. It also introduced the C-shaped signature lighting that became a defining design element. 

Measuring <4.23m> in length, <1.8m> in width and <1.58m> in height, it balanced the agility of a compact car with the presence of an SUV. The extended wheelbase and folding rear seats also allowed for flexible use of the cargo area. 

Powertrain options varied by region and trim level, ranging from turbocharged 1.0- and 1.3-liter gasoline engines to diesel and hybrid configurations. Renault also offered its first plug-in hybrid in the Captur lineup, the E-TECH PHEV, which utilized hybrid technology derived in part from Renault’s Formula 1 experience, delivering quiet and efficient operation with electric assist.

Agile handling and a stable ride were complemented by a well-finished interior and a cutting-edge infotainment system, providing comfort for both driver and passengers. Its elevated driving position made maneuvering easy, allowing drivers to transition from daily commuting to winding rural roads with confidence and ease. As a result, the Captur emerged as a versatile all-rounder that pushed beyond the traditional boundaries of the compact SUV segment.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D314:
In 1990, Renault transitioned from the Super 5 to the Clio. The Clio’s increased size, however, left space in the lineup for a smaller model. The car developed to fill that role was the Twingo, an A-segment hatchback.

The Twingo became known for its 3-door monospace design, with a nearly continuous curve flowing from the truncated hood, over the roof and into the rear. This distinctive shape set it apart from contemporary rivals and made a strong impression at its 1992 debut. Its wheels were positioned at the extreme corners of the body, maximizing interior space despite compact dimensions of <3433mm> in length and <1423mm> in height.

At launch, the Twingo was equipped with a transversely mounted 1.2-liter inline-4 OHV engine. While modest in output, it complemented the lightweight body and delivered a lively, city-friendly driving experience. The car was also praised for bringing character to a practical design, with sliding rear seats that allowed for multiple seating and cargo configurations.

Over time, the first-generation Twingo received a series of mechanical and visual updates, remaining in production for 14 years until 2007. Practical yet distinctive, it remains one of the most influential models in A-segment history.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D315:
One electric motor on each of the four wheels. The Yangwang U9 is a revolutionary model that challenged conventional ideas of the electric supercar.

Released by Yangwang, BYD’s luxury brand, it used the proprietary e⁴ platform, featuring four electric motors and delivering a total system output of 960 kW, or roughly <1305ps>. It accelerated from 0-<100km/h> in 2.36 seconds. It boasted a level of performance that could easily mask its status as a heavyweight EV. 

But the U9’s appeal extended beyond raw power. The “DiSus-X” suspension system integrated hydraulic and pneumatic controls to manage body balance, at times lifting the tires off the ground and, at others, enabling dynamic movement. This system was not merely theatrical—it formed the technical core of the U9, with four-wheel independent control delivering exceptional stability and precision.

Designed by Wolfgang Egger, the scissor-door coupe presented a futuristic form while retaining the presence expected of a supercar.

In 2025, the high-performance U9 Xtreme variant attempted a world speed record, reaching <496.22km/h>. The Yangwang U9 stands as a clear expression of power and technology and a defining symbol of speed in the electrified era.q
DescriptionLong.0x0000D403:
The BMW M Hybrid V8 was a cutting-edge prototype car developed to the Le Mans Daytona h (LMDh) specifications. Its Dallara-built carbon-fiber monocoque came powered by a DTM-derived P66/3, a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 engine paired with a hybrid system. Producing a combined system output of <680ps>, this power unit blended the thunder of internal combustion with the instantaneous response of electric assistance, delivering performance worthy of the M badge.

The wide kidney grilles of the front fascia created an unmistakable presence, identifying it as a BMW at a single glance. Outlined with laser lighting, these grilles reflected the brand’s heritage and forward-thinking technology while also maximizing aerodynamics and cooling in a form of functional beauty.

During the 2025 season, the BMW M Hybrid V8 competed in both the IMSA SportsCar Championship and FIA World Endurance Championship wearing a distinctive digital mosaic livery. In the eighth round of the IMSA season at Road America, the car dominated the field with a one-two finish, further establishing BMW’s reputation in the GTP class. Meanwhile, in the WEC, it demonstrated strong pace at circuits such as Imola while competing at the very highest level of endurance racing.

Although it carried forward the spirit of celebrated prototypes like the V12 LMR, hybrid technology allowed this machine to become a flagship pointing toward a new era of performance. Tradition, innovation and the drive to win—this car brought them all together.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D404:
The 963 is Porsche’s latest-generation LMDh prototype, carrying on the concepts embodied by the legendary 962 and 919 Hybrid. Its Multimatic carbon-fiber monocoque is equipped with a twin-turbo 4.6-liter V-8 rooted in the RS Spyder and 918 Spyder, combined with a standardized hybrid system. It was a package that combined the efficiency, reliability and overwhelming performance demanded in top-level endurance racing.

The 963 made its race debut at the 2023 24 Hours of Daytona and went on to compete in both the World Endurance Championship and the IMSA Championship. Together with the esteemed Team Penske, it challenged for the very pinnacle of endurance racing.

The 963 truly came into its own in 2024. It won the IMSA season opener at Daytona, then followed with victories at Laguna Seca, Watkins Glen and Road America, results that helped it secure both the drivers’ and manufacturers’ championships.

Its WEC results also were highly impressive. The 963 showed consistent pace throughout the season, winning in Qatar, at Spa-Francorchamps and at Fuji, while Porsche Penske Motorsport clinched the 2024 drivers’ title.

Porsche withdrew the 963 from the WEC’s Hypercar class at the end of 2025, but the car continued to compete in the 2026 IMSA Championship. The 963 is something of a masterpiece, further burnishing Porsche’s reputation as the king of endurance racing.h
DescriptionLong.0x0000D405:
The 2023 edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans was a special one, marking the 100th anniversary of the world’s premier endurance race. With glory waiting for the winner, teams brought their most cutting-edge technology and their best cars to the Circuit de la Sarthe.

It was a high-powered showdown, but even in this storied field, most eyes were on Ferrari. After all, Ferrari was returning to the top category for the first time in 50 years, following the 312 P’s appearance in the 1973 race. The car tasked with carrying that legacy was the prototype 499P. The 499P was a hypercar developed to Le Mans Hypercar regulations for the World Endurance Championship’s top category. The “499” in its name referred to the displacement per cylinder, while the “P” stood for “prototype.” Its hybrid system combined a twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 with a front-mounted MGU, producing up to 500 kilowatts.

Its styling was shaped by more than pure speed. It is futuristic, but also unmistakably Ferrari. That is a large part of the 499P’s charm.

The race itself was closely fought, but in the end, car No. 51 came out on top. The 100th edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans saw Ferrari make a spectacular return to the Circuit de la Sarthe, claiming its first overall victory in 58 years.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D406:
The Peugeot 9X8 was a Le Mans Hypercar (LMH) developed by Peugeot Sport with the goal of returning the French manufacturer to Le Mans glory. After stepping away from top-class endurance competition in 2011, Peugeot returned in 2022 under LMH regulations with the arrival of the 9X8. The "9" referenced its lineage to prototypes such as the 905 and 908. The "X" denoted its status as an all-wheel-drive hybrid built for the electrified era. Finally, the "8" reflected its connection to Peugeot’s modern production car lineup.

Upon its debut, the 9X8 attracted widespread attention for its radical aerodynamic concept, which initially eliminated the need for a rear wing. Its bodywork was shaped through extensive calculations balancing downforce and drag, challenging conventional ideas surrounding prototype race car design.

However, regulation revisions introduced during the 2022 season required adjustments to aerodynamic freedom and tire dimensions. To comply with the updated rules, the 2024 version adopted staggered tire sizes along with major revisions to weight distribution and aerodynamic balance. This dramatic evolution resulted in a redesign of roughly 90 percent of the bodywork, including the addition of a large rear wing.

The 2025 specification further refined these developments, creating the most complete version of the 9X8. Built around a hybrid powertrain combining a twin-turbocharged 2.6-liter V-6 engine with a front-mounted MGU, the car was engineered for reliability and consistent performance. It demonstrated its potential during the fiercely contested 2025 FIA World Endurance Championship season, where Peugeot secured a podium finish with 2nd place at Fuji. Developed through relentless innovation and refinement, the 9X8 became a striking expression of Peugeot’s engineering ambition and racing identity.
DescriptionLong.0x0000D407:
This 992-generation 911 Turbo S was a virtual model created by Gran Turismo, reimagined as a safety car leading the pack in the event of an incident.

The original 992-generation 911 Turbo S was the top-performance model of the eighth-generation Porsche 911. Built on Porsche’s latest 911 architecture, the wide body used a high percentage of aluminum parts, blending tradition and innovation. The rear-mounted twin-turbo <3745cc> flat-6 engine produced <650ps> and 800 Nm (<81.6kgm>) of torque, sending power through an 8-speed PDK transmission and sophisticated four-wheel-drive system before reaching the track surface. It was able to accelerate from 0-<100km/h> in just 2.7 seconds and reach a top speed of <330km/h>, but that served as only a glimpse of its true potential.

Qualities such as excellent traction and stability made the 911 Turbo S ideal for leading the field as a safety car. Meanwhile, its ability to keep a pack of race cars in line without faltering came from its outstanding performance and high-level chassis control.E

The IONIQ 6 N is the second high-performance EV from Hyundai’s high-performance N brand. It carries on the brilliant precedent set by the IONIQ 5 N, which shook the world with its spectacular debut at the 2023 Goodwood Festival of Speed.

The IONIQ 6 N was named 2026 World Performance Car, marking the second time in three years that Hyundai’s N brand had secured the award, following the IONIQ 5 N in 2024.

One of its most attractive points is its elegant exterior, which embodied the aerodynamic flow of the wind. This uniquely supple silhouette was not developed just for aesthetics, as it boasted a drag coefficient of 0.27 while also producing downforce for high-speed stability.

In terms of performance, N offered a new dynamic standard for the electrification era. With a total system output of <650ps> and 770 Nm of torque, it could accelerate from zero to <100km/h> in just 3.2 seconds. However, the true value of this machine could not be found in its figures alone. The N Active Sound+ system recreates different sounds, including the roar of an internal combustion engine, while N e-Shift created the sensation of gear shifting in an EV, giving the driver direct feedback.

The car came packed with numerous other features as well, including N Grin Boost, which unlocked full power for 10 seconds, the proprietary N Drift Optimizer, which enabled controlled slides, and a ceiling-mounted action camera mount to capture it all.

From driving at the limit on track to the winding roads of daily life, the IONIQ 6 N set out to accelerate driving pleasure. Ultimately, this epoch-making model represented the future shape of the sports car.,

Originally released in 1968, the Toyota Mark II was Japan’s answer to the midsize sedan. The Tourer V was a performance trim grade that became available from the seventh-generation Mark II onward. The version shown here was the Tourer V from the eighth-generation Mark II, also known as the X100 series. The clean-cut, long-nose sedan body and wild driving character resulted in a very attractive car.

Its most notable feature was the power unit. The 2.5-liter inline-6 1JZ-GTE engine was a further-evolved, second-generation model with variable valve timing and a single turbocharger, producing <280ps>/<38.5kgm>. Also available with a 5-speed manual transmission, a push of the throttle pedal delivered a surge of boost and the sensuous growl of the inline-6.

While it boasted excellent performance, the interior focused instead on luxury and comfort, gently enveloping the driver and passengers.

This dichotomy was what made the Tourer V so attractive. It hid its teeth, presenting the image of a refined gentleman. Its discerning drivability sent many car enthusiasts wild.

The Chaser was a midsize sedan that shared the same basic construction as the Mark II but offered different exterior styling. Of the Mark II, Chaser and Cresta sister cars, the Chaser offered the sportiest character and became the favorite of driving enthusiasts. The Tourer V was a performance-grade Chaser model featuring a turbocharged engine. The Tourer V grade was also available on the Mark II.

The version shown here was a sixth-generation Chaser Tourer V, also known as the X100 series. The engine was a second-generation 1JZ-GTE with variable valve timing and a single-turbocharger system, producing a dramatic driving feel. Pressing the throttle pedal delivered a surge of boost and fierce acceleration, while the front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout delivered predictable control and responsive handling.

While the engine was obviously powerful, it also had excellent reliability, leading the Chaser to be lauded as a tuning base car. The more work you put into it, the more intense the driving experience this exceptional FR sedan provided.
